reviews.review_text: I liked the way this class is structured. Lectures are okay, but you learn more in the lab sessions. She is very knowledgeable in Python and knows what she is doing. The Labs are the more valuable parts in my opinion and sometimes she would pop into the labs. Overall a pretty good teacher.

Labeled as an introductory class though most assignments require you to have previous coding experience. She has a hard time teaching; she is full of knowledge but fails to express it to her students effectively. Her lectures are hard to follow and she tends to make several last minute changes to her assignments and their due dates.

Professor Najjar is pretty nice/calm overall, but it is hard to keep up during lectures as she stumbles over her words a lot, lots of pauses and stuttering. It is pretty frustrating trying to understand and follow along. She also makes lots of mistakes, typos and things. TAs also expect you to know the material when you need their help.
Barely made it out with a B. lucky to not have an F. massive difficulty jump from test 1 to 2. Her teaching is like a middle schoolers who can't teach.

Dr. Najjar makes computer science very accessible for beginners who want to learn. 60% of the grade comes from three exams and a final, the grading structure has enough flexibility that one bad test won't ruin your grade. There's a big jump in difficulty after test 2, so stay engaged. Attend labs, put in some effort, and an A is very achievable.

Take this class if you can self teach the concepts to yourself and rely only on the textbook. You go into the labs and the TA's expects you to know what you read on the textbook. If you are not good in coding  I do not recommend Prof. Najjar. It is not really an introductory course with this professor. No opportunities of extra credit or retakes.

This professor is awful and does not know how to organize the class and teach. I did not learn a single thing this semester and had to teach the challenging concepts myself, even though this is an introductory computer science course. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE HER.

It's understandable Professor Najjar can't attend all ITSC 1212/1213 labs for hundreds of students, but her TAs do a fantastic job. The negative feedback seems extreme. The class is easy until Exam 3 (around Week 12); after that, you need to read more. Otherwise, she's super chill; just use office hours.
She doesn't teach anything. Everything is done by the TA's all she does is lecture once a week on what you already learned the week before. The class is easy though.

I don't really know how to rate Professor Najjar, mainly because all of the labs are only run by her TAs. She teaches the lectures every Monday, which do not help, and are so drawn out. The TAs were infinitely more helpful. The actual work isn't hard, but if you don't have previous coding experience, it might be difficult to pick up.

The class isn't the problem it' the lecture/syllabus that is. Lectures are attendance mandatory and can bring ur grade down a lot but then they don't teach you how to code-. For the syllabus it has clear directions on how your grade is affected and then the final grade comes out and the grading is nowhere close to the syllabus. Very disorganized.

Dr. Najjar knows how to code, but doesn't know how to teach code effectively to beginners. She also struggled with technology repeatedly throughout the semester. She kept grades hidden the entire semester, insisting they were inaccurate. Mostly you will learn on your own or in labs, which are TA run. Hope that you get a good TA.

She has no idea how to teach a intro course, she knows how to code, she has a lecture on Monday and shes basically reading off of slides, the TA's were super ineffective and I was pretty much teaching myself the course, I recommend switching majors.. SHES AWFUL so save yourself and save your money instead of taking her class!!

This course was honestly awful. If you don't have experience in coding please find another major before taking this course. You're basically thrown the material and told to learn it. Lectures aren't a help at all, I learned more from other students and some Ta's. But some Ta's treat you as if you're supposed to know everything in an intro course.

In my experience, she was... okay... I really only passed the class because I taught myself pretty much 90% of the class material. Her lectures were bad too. Prepare to teach yourself. This being said, she was very nice and understanding!

Professor Najjar is an awful professor. This is an intro course, but she doesn't teach anything. Her lectures are useless, the TA's aren't helpful, and by the end of the semester I stopped going to lectures to instead study, contemplate life, and cry. The only reason I didn't fail this class is because I had former python experience.

I could tell Professor Najjar really knows her material but she has no idea how to teach beginners at all.For lectures we meet once a week on Mondays and you just sit there and watch her read things off the slides.The TA's are also extremely inefficient when it comes to help understanding the material and don't put in the effort to be involved.

Class is garbage. You see the professor on Mondays for the whole semester, that's it. Mondays are lectures and you watch your professor read from a PowerPoint slide for two hours. Then you are expected to teach yourself how to code by reading a textbook.
I had a good time with her, she wasn't bad and actually followed a course structure. I'm not to sure what is up with the bad reviews but she was great for me.
Do not take this class. Even if you absolutely have to. Just switch majors. Its not worth it. Why god why

where do i even start this review, for starters she's knows the code but HAS NO CLUE how to teach that towards students, grades are hidden until the end of the semester so you dont know how cooked you are until the end, would much rather drink bleach and walk the desert barefoot then take her class again.

Awful, horrible, terrible class. You are expected to teach yourself ALL the material for this course with the textbook, TA's (90% of which being sophomore's at UNCC NOT a grad student), and AI. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

oh professor Najjar where do I even began.. she is HORRENDOUS, she doesn't know what shes doing and the fact shes a college professor astounds me, why is the final on a saturday at 8 am?? and why should i be relying on TA's who don't have a clue how to ensure the class knows what they're doing. PLEASE AVOID HER!! AT ALL COSTS you've been warned..

I never interacted with this professor the whole semester. On mondays she would have mandatory lectures which were lowkey boring and not beneficial. The crux of the class was from TA run labs, so if you get good TA's, then your set. Textbook was online and free, but the main way I learned was by applying the theory in the labs.
Honestly if you take this course, drop it ASAP and take it at a different college.

DO NOT TAKE HER. She can't teach. Also the TA's don't teach and they just expect you to know everything. Also, her tests are unfair. She expects you to do double the amount of coding questions + mc questions in the same amount of time as one lab where you do half of the questions.

DO NOT TAKE HER. If you can take it at a Community College or a AP credit for this course. You don't know your course grade for literally 3/4 of the semester. Her lectures are so monotone they are sleepy.

Dr. Najjar's lectures can be informative if you pay attention, sometimes the lectures can be long and boring. I found Dr. Najjar's office hours very helpful. Please stay on top of your work, when the code got more complex, I fell behind and that's what got me this semester. For beginners, the content in this course can be challenging.

This one of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. You never really know your grade, have to teach yourself everything, and every single component of the course is unclear. She currently has all of our final exam grade in as a 0/100.

The lectures were very boring since it was just her reading a slideshow (that's provided), but she still takes attendance. The labs were great though. They were informative and exciting, and I learned a lot from them, however a group of TA's were in charge of all labs. Your grade won't be visible for a lot of the semester which is annoying

She has no idea what skill level her student are at and her lectures while mandatory don't help at all. If you want an a in the class it'll have to be because you self taught yourself because at least in my case the TAs were no help either

It's a Python class. I struggled at first, but consistent effort made it more interesting. To get a good grade, redo the labs, review the slides and videos, and go over the quizzes. For coding, practice repeatedly until the concepts feel natural for you. If TA or lectures don't work for you, just keep practising more and more! A or A+ is possible!

This course is not beginner friendly at ALL. Nothing is taught in this class, you're expected to figure things out and learn on your own. The weekly lectures were not helpful in any way. This class made me so miserable I actually ended up switching my major. Good luck.
Get ready to teach yourself

Prof. Najjar isn't the main focus of her classes. She only does the lectures which are mildly helpful at best. The TAs will be your guide for everything else. You'll be teaching yourself a lot of the concepts. Tests and quizzes are frequent, but not too bad. The TAs are pretty much always accessible though!

This class is not hard. My issue is this professor goes out of her way to make this class intentionally painful. The syllabus is like 30 pages and doesn't even clearly define the grading criteria which I find predatory towards the students. You also can't see your grade in canvas ever because her class is special I guess??? Avoid this professor.

The content was somewhat difficult but if youre putting in effort to learn the material it gets better. 3 checkpoints + a final, the checkpoints aren't bad if you STUDY. She curved my grade from a C to a B and let us retake 2/3 checkpoints and turn in any assignments without penalties, she was also very quick to respond, TAs were helpful too.

very rough start at the beginning of the semester because why were we going over python when this is a java class. made things incredibly more difficult for me as a student. i will say you can turn in things late and still get full credit and she also offered retakes this semester (i took her for 1212). she was okay. could've gotten a better grade.

She gives a good amount of extra credit, so take it seriously. The 3 checkpoints aren't like what you learn in class, so go beyond the basics. The final isn't hard if you study the checkpoints and module quizzes. Lectures are boring but count for attendance. Runestone isn't helpful—watch YouTube channels like “Bro Code” instead.

Her lectures are pretty bad, and the tests aren't great, but she provides a lot of opportunities to get your grade up. We had retakes for 2/3 of our checkpoints(exams) as well as an optional project. It's clear she wants her students to pass, and if you don't at least get a C with all the opportunities she provides then it's probably ur fault.
Nothing to say but if possible don't take class of this professor.

My favorite professor at UNCC! Super organized and cares about her students. DON'T fall behind, it's hard to catch up, it is a lot of material. Lots of help is available through office hours, TAs, and many opportunities for extra credit. Stay on top of things, you'll do well. She is a very caring person, I enjoyed her as a professor.
By far one of the best professors, she really cared about her students and wouldn't make you feel dumb if you didn't understand the concept.

She is very bad at giving proper explanations for the concepts she teaches. It is nearly impossible to get her to reexplain in simpler terms. She gives very few opportunities to practice and learn the material outside of the checkpoints, which are graded as midterms. Too bad you're stuck with her until they hire someone else to assist in teaching.

Its impossible to get a hold of her, what makes it worse is her TAs have no idea what is going on, I leave more confused than I came in.TAs are only good for checking u off on the missing assignments, so do not expect actual help from her or her TAs.Her lectures are awful and confusing if anything.

Does everything she can to make a difficult subject for most people understandable, offers retakes, extra credit, one on one tutoring, extended deadlines for homework, etc. everything she does is to benefit the student but it's gonna be a difficult subject no matter what.

the most difficult class I've ever taken. lots of coursework through out the semester but your final grade comes down to four tests, which are confusing and hard to understand what the questions are asking you. Only saw her once a week and the labs were led by the TA's. No curves either, even when over 500 students failed one of the tests.

Prf. Najjar really does care. Her TAs teach the two lab sessions each week, so that's a luck thing. She leads the lectures on Mondays. She does her best to make everything as painless as possible. Since its such a huge course, there's endless help available. I'd take her a million times over if I could. Not saying it was so easy, but its doable.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. If you want to waste your time, stress yourself out, and leave the class more confused than when you started, then by all means, take a class with Professor Najjar. She is disorganized, dismissive, and completely uninterested in actually teaching. Her lectures are incoherent, her grading is inconsistent

The ratings given are for the course, not Prof. herself. Almost everything is self-learning from her custom textbook. Her lectures in the big hall are pointless, and you only end up being there for attendance, not to learn. Labs are run by TAs and are sometimes hit-and-miss to understand or know the concept. Unfortunately, there is no other option.

Never went to a lecture after the 1st one, attendance wasn't taken, so honestly can't say much about her. The labs were all TA-run. You kind of teach yourself from runestone, then go show your work in the labs. I feel like it's impossible to do bad, you can make up work, retake the midterm, and she adds so many bonus points at end of the course.

The professor doesn't do much except the weekly lectures (which aren't mandatory), so be sure to get help from your TA's in your lab sessions (these are mandatory to attend) and go to office hours, it helps a ton. It's an easy class as long as you go to your lab sessions and do all of your work. The TA's will really help you do well in the class.

Her lectures are so unnecessary because you don't learn anything from them. All the concepts for the course are learned on your own in the online textbook or in the lab sessions. Her lead TA mainly "teaches" the course but only when going over the labs. The other TAs try to help but they often end up asking the lead TA for help.

Learned absolutely nothing about coding. Lectures were almost as useless as her TAs were, who bragged about "getting paid to do nothing." If you get good TAs, you might enjoy the class. If not, goodluck. You'll do fine if you have experience coding/learning to code independently. This was a pretty bad and unnecessarily stressful intro-level class.

The lectures a majority of the time are unorganized. Professor occasionally goes off-topic. T/As mainly run the course, as there are two lab sessions per week. Easy class, however you must independently learn from the class textbook and external resources if you want to succeed, as the lectures and lab sessions aren't really that helpful.

This class is taught by P. Najjar's TAs. We see her each Monday for lectures in the big hall, then labs are the other two days (ex: Tues/Thurs). I would say it depends what TAs you get, but this class requires you to be pretty independent and teach yourself a lot through trial and error. She makes sure to start from scratch assuming you don't code.

Her lectures are so unnecessary because you don't learn anything from them. All the concepts for the course are learned on your own in the online textbook or in the lab sessions. In her lectures she goes on and on. She isn't really monotone but she has no pauses and no change in pitch or tone when she speaks so it just sounds monotone.

She's a good professor and her lectures are enjoyable, but I personally wouldn't take this class again. Most TAs didn't provide much help in explaining concepts during labs, and it seems you have to study independently to grasp what you're doing in class. My experience was okay, but not the best.
The way the class is set up is terrible. Lecture on Monday, lab on w

DONT RECOMMEND. She gives chances to earn additional points but she's a lazy professor. she provides no other materials than the textbook and TAs to help. its understandable why people end up turning to ChatGPT or Stack overflow to learn. They also dock points if you use ChatGPT for some assignments. Lecture is not mandatory and not helpful.

I literally never saw Prof. Najjar the entire semester, the course was lead by TAs following Najjar's instructions. She did do an optional lecture every week that was also posted online, but I never needed to view it. Some instruction would be unclear, and therefore TAs either wouldn't know how to handle things or respond inconsistently.

The group projects will be a lot of work, and there will be multiple presentations. However, Dr. Najjar does what she can to help everyone. Even if the lectures are a bit disinteresting, it's really difficult to complain. You can expect a lot of writing, but Dr. Najjar actually gives lots of class time to allow you to work on things like that.

Honestly the easiest & most student friendly computer science class, I have ever had. Professor truly wants students to grow and will do anything to help the student ultimately. Honestly no one here should have reviews below a 3 here, but she makes sure she wants to help you. You might not get to see her at all, but the TAs are godsend & WONDERFULL

This class was TA lead. They were very approachable and the class was set up well. Every week you had a lab based on online textbook modules and then the second meeting was a quiz. As long as you keep up with the work and study the material you should do well.

She knows what she is talking about, but isn't engaging. Attendance isn't mandatory for the lecture but it is for the labs. She will address questions in lecture and do basic examples but in lab it truly depends on if your TA's are good. You use a free online textbook that she uses heavily. You get second attempts on non-final quizzes.

I absolutely loved having Dr. Najjar as a professor. She was really caring and concerned about any issues that I had, even whenever my mental state felt as if it was degrading into nothingness. She is an amazing professor, lecturer, and an all-around great person. She definitely made computer science more fun for me.

This class was incredibly easy, if you do the work on time you'll succeed. When in class you're allowed to work with others. Every quiz you take, excluding the final, has a second attempt where you can use any resource to get 100%. The professor is rarely present in person during lab; however, the TAs are helpful and understand the coursework.

The overall class is a decent amount of work, but its hard NOT to finish with a 100.

Final was difficult

very easy straightfoward class, learn a lot by doing the labs rather then from the lectures, very hands on learning. A lot of the labs require some trial and error, but thats the best way to learn coding.

I made an account just to write a rating here. The 3.6 I saw last semester was downright criminal. I took ITSC1212/13 in her class and it was fantastic. The class was very welcoming, with optional surveys throughout the semester to make sure that's the case. We were taught at a nice, understandable pace, and assignments had very forgiving due dates

I love Professor Najjar. When she is not teaching, she is an understanding human being that takes in outside factors when talking to you. She's an all around great professor and explains the concept of coding extremely well. 100% would take her again!

This woman is a blessing on the UNC Charlotte Computer Science department. If you care about the class, she will be more than happy to help you through any troubles you have. Very friendly, very organized, and understands what she needs to do to convey the material. Take her if you can!
Overall pretty good teacher and fairly easy class if you know what you are doing. There is a lot of assignments to do and labs can be somewhat confusing at times.

Avoid if possible. Practice quizzes don't align with actual exam material, making prep difficult. Feedback is extremely slow; grades went unposted for two months, leaving me unsure of my standing between an A or a C. It was a discouraging experience because the instructor provided very little helpful guidance throughout the term.

Dr. Wilson is the greatest professor I have ever taken at UNC Charlotte. She always does their best to support students wherever they can. Super often she (or her TAs) lets students turn assignments in late if they need to, and she's always super understanding. Labs are kinda unorganized but super helpful if you pay attention.

This class was not good. I couldn't find any time to focus on my other courses and most of the learning was conceptual, not practical. She mostly just shows you some slides, has you do a quiz, then sends you out to do code and projects without truly understanding it. The Course Canvas is also unorganized. I will say the TAs were good.
she great-kisses

Terrible. Time wasted in class forcing participation, no real study material for tests, no learning material(she posts two videos at the start of the week made by another professor) never reviews this material in class. Tests contain content never seen or discussed in class. TA's making a fraction of her salary are more beneficial to my learning.

Dr. Wilson is tough but a great professor. If you need help, she will help by visiting her office hours; she does wear many hats in her position; however, she will find a way to keep you on track. Dr. Wilson with the poll quizzes is a lot, and its mandatory you come to class. Exams on lockdown browser, and dont ever get caught copying her code!!!!!

A flipped classroom with prep work required, but lectures can be dry. The TAs are key - they provide great support. Leverage Unstuck ai and other study tools to excel. Overall, a manageable intro class.
Lectures are fine, just pay attention. 5 projects that are actually really easy. Tests were not bad if you studied. There are a lot of assignments/prep works but nothing bad.

Barely any explanation of the actual concepts covered. It was all covered by online videos of another professor that is barely understood. Class was all poll quizzes that count for accuracy and then you're on your own doing projects/homework. No rounding up at all even if you had 89.5(my case) Don't take…..

She grades heavy on tests, NO ROUND UPS for grades (89.9% is a B).   No extra/partial credit on tests. Tons of videos and readings.   Focused on people cheating instead of helping.  Barely answers questions or emails.

I think she did her job pretty well and she was a pretty nice teacher. I think her lectures could have been a bit more engaging but she still did a good job teaching the material. If you take this class you need to pay attention and do the pre-work or you will not do well. The one thing I will say is sometimes she doesn't respond to your emails.

Her class is a flipper classroom so she doesn't teach in class, just review on pollEV which is a grade. Has 5 projects, 4 in class quizzes(30%) - multiple choice 12; coding - 18. 2 at home(10%) - multiple choice, lockdown browser without camera. Class is honestly easy just basics of coding, if you took CSA in high school thats the first unit of 4.

The course is fairly easy, personally I don't think there is enough rigor in it. It is a flipped classroom and the lectures are very minimal. But the overall course isn't great and not very indepth, it is a very shallow look at dsa topic. The TAs are very helpful if you need it.

Not a fan of her overall, lots of outside of class self learning. Her lectures are incredibly boring and unengaging for a flipped classroom. TA's are your best friend, and most of them are alright. Coding portion of tests are nothing like the studyguide, but class is moslty graded by projects, not tests so not too much to worry about.

Definitely a kind teacher, but lectures aren't incredibly useful, especially if you do the prep work. I feel like there was the potential to learn so much more, but it's an intro class and does lay some very helpful foundational blocks. TAs are usually willing to help!

Overall the class was great, this is a flipped classroom course which means you read the material prior to coming to class. She cares about your grade, overall this class is  fairly easy but I wish the lectures were a bit more indepth. The TA,s do the heavy lifting helping students with projects,etc. Has group activities in class which is good.
She's a great professor but she can be very tough, just study and get any prep work done before cause its a pain if you don't

1213 is a hard class - much more difficult than 1212. I had Dr. Wilson for both classes. Be sure to complete the prep-work and start projects early so you have time to meet with the TA's or Dr. Wilson if needed. The in-class labs are difficult so completing the prep-work is a must! Speak to her after class - She is very enjoyable to talk to.

I enjoyed Dr. Wilson's class. She offers a lot of extra credit opportunities, usually in the form of bonuses on the quizzes and projects, and her class is not *too* difficult if you are willing to learn fast. She's a bit scatterbrained, and that is hard to deal with, but generally speaking she teaches well and I learned a lot in her class.

Class consists of doing prepwork (or bookwork) over the weekend, and reinforcing those topics in class. She doesn't do as good of a job as my 1212 professor, the lectures are kind of dry and there isn't much class involvement. When no one answers questions she just waits until someone answers. After the lectures there are group workshop activities

She's ok. Attending class is only mandatory because there are in person assignments. Her lectures are inoffensive but doesn't teach you really. Class isn't necessarily difficult, just attend class and go to the lab sessions and you should do fine.

Didn't even bother to show up to class somedays. Can't really remember any meaningful piece of information she gave over the entire course, the TA's do most of the heavy lifting and are there to help if you need them. Just know that you'll be expected to learn and do a lot of the work on your own, which isn't too difficult.

Dale-Marie Wilson is a great professor and person all around. If you go to class and engage it is very easy. The prep work can be turned in late. No textbooks to purchase. Once you get the hang of her schedule and how she does her tests and assignments it is very easy and predictable.

Her lectures are terrible and her ta's do most of the work for her. Luckily it's just an intro class so a good professor isn't necessary. She'll constantly threaten you with a "acedemic integrity violation", which gets old very fast. Try to find another professor, if you can't just know you'll be teaching yourself everything.
Best professor in computer science. Lectures are clear and easy to learn. Definitely the most wonderful class I have taken in Charlotte. Love her
I recommend this professor, she grades fairly well and the assignments/study guides prepare you well for the class. Attendance mandatory but small price to pay for a good grade. She's awesome.

Her lectures were clear, organized, and easy to follow. She explained the material well and made the course expectations straightforward. The grading criteria was clear, and the TAs were helpful whenever questions came up. Overall, this was a well-structured class with strong teaching and useful support.
Great class. Professor is great too
This capstone helps to stitch all pieces you learnt together. Need a lot of work. But, the professor is always helpful and sweet

3135 is a great class if you want to work in frontend. Ms. Sahoo class teaches from basic to react.js. Very hands on. Ms. Sahoo is an excellent professor. Her lectures are insightful, will help you learn fundamental skills
Prof. Sahoo is great. She went through each topic very detailed way. First time I've enjoyed a programming class.

My grandmother mother has been really sick. Dr. Sahoo has been really caring, helpful and supportive. I have 4 more classes this semester. No other professors has been such supportive. She is a great human being, listens to your problems and find out a way to help you succeed. She has deep command over the material. Great class

Very caring and understanding professor. I am having some personal issues, she has been consistently supportive. Lecture are brief and amazing. She mentions interview questions in classroom discussions which is really helpful. Take her if you can

I just had couple of classes with her, what an absolute pleasure to learn from her! In the first class of learning, I was not able to figure out few things, she sat with me, explaining me each steps patiently. I have never had such experience in CLT. Next class, again I observed her going over the steps with some folks diligently. Rare to find!

Honestly one of the better professors I've had. Explains concepts clearly and actually cares if students understand, not just memorize. Lectures are structured, organized, and make hard topics feel manageable.

Workload is fair . you have to put in effort, but it's never busywork. Exams are reasonable if you keep up with class and practice.

Very approachable and supportive. Will help if you ask questions and genuinely wants students to succeed. Also flexible and understanding when life happens (rare but appreciated).

If you show up for code review pay attention, and do the work, you'll be fine. Would recommend 100%.

Great professor. Explains concepts clearly and actually cares about students learning. Workload is fair, no busywork. Exams are reasonable if you keep up. Approachable, supportive, and understanding. Not an easy A, but a fair one. Would take again.

All in all, coming from someone with a terrible math background this class was pretty refreshing, I would say its a bit tougher than calculus 1, but she makes learning the material more seamless, the class was 65% tests and the rest was assignments and readings, do not miss any assignments because she does not allow late work
Outstanding professor, definitely my fav one until now. Course contents are organized and easy to follow. Classroom lectures are very easy to follow.

Prof is good, provides extra help and support if you need. The class has heavy workload and if you are in a team where few chose not to work , you will be screwed. But, over all great learning experience
I enjoyed the class. Fantastic teacher. Everything was great

This is a semester long project building class. You build a project from scratch, design it, develop it and finally deploy it. You also show it in your portfolio. Pretty hands on class. The prof is a great mentor. No lecture, just project work. Personally I enjoyed the class and the prof is great
Prof Sahoo is an awesome educator. She does an excellent job going over the zybook reading materials in class. As long as you attend lectures, you will get the hang of the subject.

She is an awesome teacher. She genuinely cares for students' success and growth. I had a wonderful experience learning from her. 

About the course: this course is a bit hard as there are lots of topics. Zybook (prep work) does not do a very good job of explaining. But, If you attend lectures, you will get it. Prof and TAs are very much accessible

Dr. Sahoo is a very good professor. Her lectures are easy to follow. Explains very difficult topics in a way that is easy to understand and grasp. Take her class for 2175 and 3135. I had her for both, definitely worth it. She is also grades very leniently

Cool professor. It's a math class, but a hard one. I am not a math person, so as contents I  didn't like much. Same times , prof Sahoo is an excellent teacher. She knows the material and got an amazing teaching skill.

Love her! Love her! Love her! She is kind and understanding. Due to my personal circumstances, I was not doing my best. She took care of it. I was 2% below passing grade. She helped me and pushed me. I did not lose my scholarship because of it. She is knowledgeable. Can not thank enough for what she has done for me.

Excellent course structure. Start with very basic HTML, CSS, then move to JS and REACT. Tutorials are very clear. The prof always helps to grasp concepts. The class has code reviews which motivates you to go through science behind what you are programming.

I want to take my past comments back about her being Awful. I was mad at her as I thought she did not give any leniency. But, once she got a doctors note she excused my assignments and agreed to replace my missed test score with final test. She is generous and kind

She does an awesome job in teaching. Some students who are interested to work or learn, might not find this class easy. You need to be interested to learn, then you will enjoy this course overall. I personally found her very caring and considerate.

She is one of the best prof I have had yet. Her lectures are amazing and thorough. She helps one to one if you ask any doubts. Also, if you have any questions, she explains many times without getting annoyed which most prof don't. Take her if you can

She is really bad at teaching, and the exams were nothing like the practice. Our class had different material from her other class, and the test average is almost 16 percent higher. She is just terrible

Do not pick this class, she has single handedly gave me a reason to not live. Her lectures did not help with any of the exams taken. Each of the practice problems given were easier than the actual test. take a better professor like ADAM NUR he is amazing compared to her.
Over all good class and good prof

This class covers HTML, CSS, JS, REACT and deployment. Every lab (each week) has a code review which consists of going over your code and doing something extra in class. Very kind and hands on  professor. I absolutely enjoyed the class and conversations with her

The professor has a very job focused teaching and learning. She asks to do few things in class every week, kind of simulation of how you will be interviewed. Take the class if you want to be a front end developer

Material gets harder as time goes but he is helpful, would recommend if you want to learn!

He was a nice professor and all of his exams were on paper open notes with 4 pages of handwritten notes. The tests were similar to the exercises and labs you would do for the class, so if you understood them the exam should be a breeze. I would like to warn you that when you are taking the exams it might feel like your hand is going to fall off.

He is a funny professor, and a good guy. But, he is basically inaccessibly via email. Other than that, he is a good professor. The class gets pretty tough at the end once you start to learn RISC-V stuff. We had to complete assembly language stuff for test 3 and most of the class didn't finish the test. He offered a grade replacement for it though!

Professor Yan is a good professor, but good luck trying to get in contact with him. He will never reply to your emails. Also, if you don't know anything about RISC-V, all I can say is have fun; he expects you to know RISC-V as if it was taught in other Comp Sci courses (Spoilers: it isn't)

This class itself is tough, but he tried his best to deliver the lecture. He also goes over lab questions, and most of his review before exams will be in the exam. Attendance is not mandatory, but you'd better come since he will randomly give extra credits for attendance.

The course material is very dense. Attend and pay attention in lectures and labs. Don't be afraid to ask the TAs for help, you'll need it. He has a rather heavy accent, but is willing to explain and answer any questions.

I really enjoyed this class and thought Professor Shin was an excellent teacher. Nothing about the class was particularly difficult, however there are a lot of assignments to keep up with every week. Seems like he cares about his students and really enjoys teaching cs.

Easy class with almost no work. All your work is done in assigned groups so if you get a group you don't like, it might be tougher. The professor is very laid back but he expects you to try. He genuinely wants you to succeed but expects you to put in a little work.

This professor was very engaging and wanted us to succeed since public speaking is an important skill to master. As for the work, it's not difficult since the majority of it is group work. You are graded on very few things, so make sure to submit the best version you have, since, in my case, a bad grade will bring your grade down.

Most of the work in the class is done in predetermined groups so if you get stuck with people who don't show up or care to participate you are screwed. Showing up on time and participating is the majority of the grade. If you get a bad group it will drag your grade down as he does group grades not individual.

The professor was very hands-off, didn't really teach anything, you just do discussions/papers/power points, which are based on a vague prompt you have to research on your own. It was a gen-ed, so I guess that's a good thing. Very easy class if you don't mind writing a lot.

His class is an interesting one . Be ready since attendance is mandatory 
The class is competitive and requires interaction with classmates since there's a project given to groups the beginning of the class so does what you do the whole semester.
It's a great class .

Took his 3688 class online during a hectic semester. I had a lot going on, and he was very understanding. he let me turn in a major project late, which honestly saved my grade. Without that flexibility, I could've failed, but thanks to him, I'm now holding a strong A. Super fair and supportive professor.

Most fun course I've ever taken. The course is built around a semester long team presentation project. There is an ungraded presentation that allows Karp to give you feedback to succeed in the 2nd graded one. Karp is very energetic and engaging and really creates a great atmosphere for you to better your skills and get graded for being yourself.

Professor Karp's class is largely focused on public speaking.  If you approach this class with an open mind and commitment, it provides an excellent opportunity to grow professional and networking skills.  He offers exceptional feedback, and keeps his students in mind for opportunities and references that he is actively seeking for them.

Dr. Karp is a super animated and caring man, and makes it clear right from the start he wants you to succeed. The class is structured around working in teams to give a shark tank style product presentation. I got to practice my professionalism skills in a safe, fun environment, with people I genuinely liked. Phenomenal experience, highly recommend.

Very chill professor. Assignments were incredibly easy and the quiz every week was 1 multiple choice question with 2 attempts (very straightforward). Chill class if you have tough schedules like me. Would take again 100%.
Great professor

For someone teaching a class that purports to be about professionalism, Dr. Karp is highly unprofessional. Please note that he will also take pictures of you without your consent on his personal cellphone. Otherwise, the class is fairly easy and primarily based on a single group project.

Great class, Great Professor, If you actually participate and take this class seriously you learn how to get over your anxiety when presenting, great class for building soft skills, which so many CS students lack.  Dr. Karp is one of my favorite professors at the university.

Lively personality, that felt like he wanted to be there. Helpful when you seek help, and cares about the students. Group project is almost the whole grade with easy discussion board posts as the other part of the grade.

Dr. Karp has a fun and eccentric personality that makes the morning trek bearable. He utilized a hands-off teaching style that allowed us to learn about relevant topics in computer science. His ITSC3688 class consisted of easy discussion board posts and a final group presentation on an imaginary piece of technology. If you try, you will get an A.

Dr. Karp was one of my favorite professors I had at UNCC, great lectures, makes you think, and makes class fun.  It may be because of my sales and entrepreneurial background but this class was very enjoyable for me.  It is an easy class as long as you participate and work good on a team, not too much work, huge focus on the final presentation.
Love this professor!! Very easy to talk to and easy-going. If you have any questions he is always there to answer them and very funny. Would definitely take this class again, I enjoyed it very much.

Extremely easy going class. The class is based off of "Shark Tank" in which you have the entire semester to come up with an idea to pitch to the rest of the class. The presentation, a final paper, and weekly discussions are what you are graded on. Easiest class I have taken thus yet, but, I also did participate. Great professor and would take again

Overall he was a good teacher. At least for my class If you didn't attend class, it would affect your overall grade towards the end of the semester. Get prepared for group projects. As a professor, he understands how this class isn't essential, so he's easygoing. This class doesn't have a lot of things to grade so by all means DO ALL THE WORK!!

If you're thinking about taking Phys. Computing, be prepared for an unrealistic amount of prep and project work. Professor Wilson's lectures are extremely uninteresting; he goes over content students are already expected to know via the prep. Course projects are time-consuming. Do not expect timely communication from him either. Avoid if possible.

online class but lots of group works and group projects. in-class and prep work is worth most of grade. assigns the same amount of readings and prep for grads and undergrads, so if your undergrad, it feels like this class is much more of my week then my other normal undergrad classes. Also only offered at night.

Physical Computing is probably my favorite course so far and Dr. Wilson is def 1 of my favorite profs! Take his class if you want to make neat stuff! There's a decent amount of work and it's hard to catch up if you fall behind, but Dr. Wilson is very helpful with questions if you struggle with a concept. Idk why the bad reviews, he's a great prof!

The professor was pleasant, but this class was effectively teaching you to use the worst possible tool for a given task. We would spend hours building low-fidelity, inefficient artifacts that would probably get you fired from a workplace if you got caught building on the clock. You complete dozens of assignments to produce unimpressive products.

Only thing I like about this class: During group assignments, you're only responsible for your portion. This week I have a project, quiz prep work 3x, and in-class work. It's the same thing EVERY week, besides the project and prep work is usually 2-1x. He hides your overall grade. Acting like I don't have 4 other classes. Very time-consuming :/

I absolutely loved this course and, though there is a lot of group projects and work, I felt like I learned a lot from it all that I'm still using today. His class is also very well-organized and was just a lot of fun. I would absolutely take a class with him again!

This class is one of the most organized classes I've ever been in. It is a bit lecture and prep work heavy, but it is very interesting. There is a lot of group work, and assignments can take time. I would recommend to take Professor Wilson because he makes the course super easy. He has a nice grace period on assignments.

I don't know why there are so many low reviews. Prof Wilson is pretty great. Yes, his class is super long, but have in mind its a night online 3 hour course. The class is super easy, just long. There is a lot of group work and prep work before class. But it is so easy. He is SUPER organized with his canvas and has a grace period with assignments.

Probably the worst class and professor I have ever taken. He makes such an interesting and creative topic into one of the most mundane and mind-numbing things imaginable. SO MUCH useless busy work under the guise of "prep work" and then goes over the exact same material in lecture. Stupid group projects that are hard to manage due to being online.

**NOTE: IN REGARDS TO ITIS 4358 PHYSICAL COMPUTING**
Overall the class is pretty straight forward, prep work is hands on when you start getting to the Arduino stage but it is very fun. Since this was cross listed with the master's course our final grade was hidden. Takes attendance for in class assignment credit. Manage your time with the projects.

Professor Wilson is a kind and approachable instructor who assigns a lot of homework. However, he offers a lenient grace period for submissions. The biggest downside of his course is that grades remain hidden on Canvas until the semester ends! The course is manageable as long as you turn in your assignment's on time and correctly .

I don't usually rate stuff but this professor makes this class so unnecessarily hard for no reason, he talks so much that he makes all the assignments way more confusing than they actually are. It is only one class a week that is 3 hours and every single time he will keep you late and he assigns so much work.

Not sure what all the bad reviews are on about. We're about halfway through this semester and he's been alright so far. He does talk A LOT. Prep work can sometimes be long, but he posts it a week before its due so you have enough time to get it done. Make sure to manage your time, it is very easy to fall behind but its also easy to recover.

Lots of prep work, but this class is so easy, you can finish the work in a maximum of 6 hours, which is fine for a grad course. Dr. Wilson is respectful, caring, and understanding from what I've seen so far

I don't typically post ratings but it really did get that bad. Lectures are only once a week, but leave me stressed  to the point I question going to class on that day altogether. This is definitely the worst class I've ever taken. There's hours of readings and sketching each week. There's group projects that are due every 2 weeks...there's no break. Souless and void of any personality, this professor runs the type of class that makes passionate students drop out and never come back.  Take this unblinking weirdo of a professor only if you love doing hours of repetitive, meaningless, and violently dull work. I am disheartened, exhausted, and disappointed with Unc Charlotte after this course.

Many hours of useless, tedious, and very repetitive busy work.  I thought this was going to be my easiest course but I spend all of my time on stupid busy work.  Very frustrating I have to doodle (this class requires lots of sketching) for many hours instead of learning cybersecurity. Take a different professor.

I love the content of this class. But he posts 3 hours of prepwork on the DAY OF class. I work in the morning so it's impossible to finish in time for class, where we do more sketching. Sketching IS a big part of prototyping, but drawing for 4 hours straight is exhausting. Also prepare to be given work in class while he talks the ENTIRE TIME.

The 8-week version of the class is pretty tough with a full schedule but the work is fun if you like design. There is a lot of work to be squeezed into 8 weeks (5 group design projects, prep work, and quizzes twice a week), however, the work isn't particularly hard and the grading from my TA was very lenient. He talks for hours at a time.

This class was a nightmare. The course is now a half-semester and is online (scheduled meeting times). There is way too much individual busy work due before class each week. That workload on top of a major group project, which requires 2-3 long meetings outside of class to complete successfully, leads to far too much stress. TAs graded very late.

I am going to try my best to write this rating without violating the guidlines. DO NOT TAKE HER AS A PROFESSOR. This is not an easy elective. You have to learn a lot of vocabulary and there are too many readings on ZyBooks that you must memorize for in-person quizzes. The teacher is alright, but it's just too much homework. Cheat sheets could make up for all the memorization though.

she was a good professor and gave great extra credit at the end of the semester. she has a few problems with her speech but it didn't matter too much. i think if i studied more i could've gotten a higher grade but i still ended with an A and didn't really put a lot of effort in.

She is flexible on attendance and grades but there are a lot of presentations and Labs she stutters a bit at times. As long as you complete the labs, discussion post, and final project on time this class will be fairly easy to understand The midterm and final were a bit long but she does give an option for a cheat sheet DONT skip a lab assignment

flexible. lots of presentations. lowkey had an annoying voice. the midterm and final were easy ! the project was fairly easy. just lots of really tedious labs and lectures weren't helpful. gave extensions if needed

Unstructured,and while the she is understanding with late work, she's hard to reach by email.TAs are awful slow to grade, misgrade often and sometimes put in 0s for no reason.didn't even get all exams graded before the final.She misprintsquestions w exams and sometimes teaches things incorrectly students have to correct her.always check everything.

Prof is very very knowledgeable in this class. Theres a lot of reading and online labs but she knows its new to everyone and doesn't expect you to become a master. Networks was online a-sync, with most assignments just sections from the Comp tia textbook, so it's hard to judge Prof. Powell. Pretty boring lecturer but attendance wasn't mandatory for my class. Lots of homework but if you do it and read a little it's not hard to understand. If the code doesn't compile you will get 0, but gives you practice tests and it is fairly similar to an actual test. She gives you lots of help when needed. She is nice, not a tough grader when it comes to projects. She has said learning how to code comes from practice so she gives homework, but I learned so much. Get ready to spend some time on it

If you want to take this class as an easy elective go ahead and pick something or someone different. This class was unbearable as she just repeated everything from the mounds of reading/videos she makes you do. A lot of memorization for tests and one group project at the end of the semester too

Mrs. Powell is okay, would prefer a better-rated professor, if possible. Wouldn't gripe about being in her class again. Not the most organized or engaging. Professor stumbles over words repeatedly during her her her lectures. She assigns homework so heavily that your canvas calendar will be unusable. Excellent Professor, highly recommend

Programming Tests are extremely difficult, 0 room for error, every inch of the material must known or you fail the test, you get an A or an F.

She does not understand lots of the material and its always a pain to ask a question or ask for help because she is very unprofessional on how she goes about the interaction.  Grades have taken a long time to go in but does offer extra credit but that may be due to the original grades that are made on the test due to lack of knowledge on material.
