You're supposed to be graded on how well you use scrum principles, but sometimes we lost points due to our code being incorrect, which was frustrating. Other than that, no real problems. SWE is gonna be group projects, so just prepare for that.

Professor Dobbs is knowledgeable of the industry, he has a drive to ensure all students leave his class with an understanding of how to work together as a software development team, to include tracking of milestones and the use of AGILE and Scrum principles.  He is dedicated to the student's success; I had no communication issues with him.

For ITCS 4155:

Professor Dobbs is a great instructor that has been in the industry and is very knowledgable about what he teaches. He is very flexible in how you do the semester-long project and gives good opportunities to work with actual companies as well!

You're better off learning by yourself than relying on Dobbs to teach. He doesn't teach at all. Assignments are confusing. He provides links to the website of whatever program is being used but those are not useful to a beginner. Each assignment weighs heavy but the only good thing is you get to make your grades up towards the end of the semester.

You are expected to teach yourself almost all topics in the course, which can be really complex. I would only recommend this class to someone who already has a good understanding of JavaScript, MongoDB, React, etc. Instructor is also unwilling to help settle issue within groups, such as group members not contributing.

Do not take this professor if you do not have previous knowledge of software development tools. I.E. MongoDB, REACT, java script, setting up databases and setting up webservers. He offers no lectures on the information and gives very little supplemental reading. You are expected to learn complex topics in a week or less on your own.

He doesn't teach anything, super vague with instructions and grading criteria. He doesn't do any lectures or assignments, just projects. He gives you answers for all the projects except the final one (which is 30% of the grade). He doesn't give you any instructions or provide any help. You are expected to know everything before you take this class.
Homework assignments are long, tedious, and don't really teach you anything.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! 

If you can wait another semester to take it or you have a second option take that and don't look back. 

His homework is extremely complicated (even his TAs get confused), he doesn't go over any of the coding in class - just rambles about unrelated stuff

This is easily the worst professor/class I have ever had at UNCC

Nice man. Terrible class. This was by far one of the worst and hardest classes I have ever taken. The material in this class is so unnecessary and so confusing. Instructions are unclear and confusing. This class is basically in a foreign language.

Professor Wartell is an awful professor, he left the class a halfway through the semester and had another professor teach his class. He had no TA and had trouble trying to grade our first assignments. We never received any of our grades for the assignments until we had to bombard the TA of the other professor for grades. This class is unnecessary

Very easy orientation class. Good lectures and brought in numerous speakers. Class grading criteria is very clear and simple to follow. Not really any tests and not many assignments too. Great teacher would recommend.

I took ITSC 2600 (Computing Professionals) as a transfer class. Professor Slane is very kind and understanding. There's one weekly reflection and occasional assignments. Guest speakers visit weekly and share useful resources and advice for student success. She also responds to emails quickly. Easy class with a good teacher who cares about students.

Ms. Slane's class is a great class to come in for 50 minutes to relax and listen to speakers from the multiple departments here on campus and from companies. Yes, sometimes the lectures can be boring, but for only 50 minutes they're not too bad. The work itself is easy, but make sure to do the assignments, so that you're not stuck with a B like me.

Lectures were basically ppl coming from different departments and talking. Attendance was taken thru pollev. Homework was light work, occasional discussion post or reflection. Had a final group project that we had plenty of time to work on and was fairly easy to do. Professor was nice and seemed to care about her students and their success.
She is the nicest teacher ever, and her class is very easy. Class can be a little boring, but only 50 mins.

ITSC 1600 is an easy course. The class mainly consists of different presenters from student organizations, companies, campus resources, etc. There are some interesting/useful lectures, but a majority of them are quite boring. The assignments are not based on any of the lectures but are relatively simple. Attendance was 10%, and there was no final.

Dr. Slane is an amazing professor, however 1600 is just a boring class. She brings in guest speakers who inform us on various topics relating to resources/possibilities within the school and in the workforce. It's an easy class, and it's great for freshmen to learn what their future could potentially hold going into comp sci here at Charlotte.

I took her class first semester of 2024. Her lectures are really good introduction to Computer Science. She brings in a lot of outside people to talk and you learn a lot about their opinions and they give you advice. Great class for freshman in CS. She also is very understanding and her assignments are short and easy, other than the last long essay
Great Teacher! Super nice

Very introductory class that offers many resources, but it's very boring and at the end of the day you can't take away much. Her TA's do a lot of the grading work but she is accessible outside of class and truly cares about you. Lots of guest speakers and filler assignments.

Everyone gets an A if they do the work. The lectures can be boring if you have no interest in the presenter's topic (attendance is taken). The hardest part is a short research paper you write regarding an ethical issue in technology/computing at the very end.
This class is very easy and pretty much everyone can get an A if they do all the assignments. But I felt this class is pretty boring and not really useful.

The class is a waste of time but Slane does really care about her students and I wouldn't mind taking a class taught by her as long as it's not 1600 again. The class seems to be for straight out of high school students which is not me. It was annoying when recruiters came in for a whole class because I already have a job. Slane is great, class isnt
good professor, super easy class.

Lectures consist almost entirely of guest speakers and the assignments are unrelated to these presentations. Polleverywhere is used for attendance, which is part of the final grade. The assignments are straightforward and simple but Slane is very strict with deadlines. Not very accommodating when it comes to personal circumstances / getting sick.

By far the easiest class I have taken at UNC Charlotte. It was very self-directed and self-taught but the content wasn't challenging. Because everything was online (including test + final) and attendance was not taken you could easily pass this class with an A without ever showing up.

Professor Jugan is easy-going, straightforward, and informative. Attendance is optional and he even takes the courtesy of recording the lectures. This course has few assignments that aren't difficult at all, but it still feels like I learned a lot. A big plus of professor Jugan is that he's easy to reach outside of class!

I took this class on Zoom, attendance is optional and lectures are recorded. This is a project based course, you get to decide what you make. Since you decide, he doesn't give much guidance but is available for questions during class or office hours. There is very minimal work with this class, it's an easy technical elective.

Professor Jugan is a really good professor. He helps you understand the concept of unity and how to code a game from scratch. He is a leineit grader and he is very helpful. We had 4 homework assignments that stacked each time and we had the final game to present as our final.

He's a good choice for intro to AI. Super knowledgeable in the games industry and talks a lot about his experience. The study guides he provides are extremely helpful for the midterm and the final. There are 3 projects in the course. Attend class or watch the class recordings to get good insight on how to do them.

I would highly recommend taking Prof. Jugan if you need a CS elective. All of the milestone requirements throughout the semester are very manageable. There's one final project due, he just tells you to keep it small.

This is THE ELECTIVE CLASS TO TAKE! Super easy, only graded by 10 things, the lowest of which gets dropped. Quiz answers are provided on his posted lecture slides and can be retaken if it wasn't 100% the first time. The final project is easy and he grades things really loosely. Finished this course with a 100% grade! Prof is super funny too, bonus!

10/10. Funny and charismatic and very light workload. He's great at explaining things. He makes the class as painless as possible. Take him as many times as you can. The low-pressure assignments, light workload, and interesting lectures make this class a breath of fresh air. Doesn't try to trick students.-

Don't recommend at all, especially online. Lectures are near incomprehensible and very difficult to follow, and usually never line up with the projects you are working on. You are expected to be good at C# and Unity, or have AI do all the coding. Midterm was set up to be near impossible. Not nearly enough time to complete any of it.

No clear instructions, difficulty in communication, terrible grading, no teaching, 0 understanding. 
You won't learn anything, arbitrary grading, no clear rubric followed while grading assignments. You will waste your time, better take difficult class than wasting your time on this. If the university is listening, please get rid of such classes.
An easy A at the cost of your sanity

I've taken Dr. Benedict for data mining and data visualizations, and she was my advising professor for my senior capstone project. Never in my life have I had a professor more relatable and understanding. Her classes have motivated me to change my career path towards data analytics, and as a student I could not recommend her enough.

She is very relaxed, no attendance. Her class felt like a youtube tutorial, there is very little content and everything can be easily found online for free. She speaks for about 15 minutes over some AI generated slides or the TAs will have a code demo, and the rest of the class you do whatever. This class was a waste of time and money.

She's young and fresh out of grad school, which means that she's really chill and understanding. It seems like she cares, but she doesn't actually have much control over the structure of the course. Typically generates assignments with AI. It seems like she's typically busy and doesn't devote much to the class. New to teaching and too slow.
Great for 2214, would recommend if you want a relaxed professor overall, go with graduate students over professors.

I've taken data structures under two other professors and she is by far the best.  If you get the chance this is the professor you want to teach you data structures if you truly want to understand what you're learning!

If you're taking 2214, take it with Aileen. She didn't design the class, but she listens to students, extends deadlines, and answers questions. When I took it, it was her first time teaching, and she didn't fully know the material, but she admitted that and did her best to find answers. She is by far one of the best professors I have had in CS.

I took ITSC 2214, which was a difficult class—but not because of her. She did her best to help us understand the material and was always open during office hours. The class is challenging because of the content, which is prepared by another professor, but she made it more enjoyable and less stressful. 100/100!

ITSC2214 had a large learning curve, but with ITSC1213 now teaching VSCode and WebCat(coding software/programs), it shouldn't be as much. She didn't have control over the coursework as it was chosen by the department, but she was very sweet and helpful with questions. She truly cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed.

4 projects. Discussion posts and multiple attempt quizzes. In person option has zoom for when you are sick or when you really don't feel like coming to class. No tests. She makes this class so much more focused on learning and coding than tests. GOAT prof
Great professor, always available for any questions and all assignments are manageable & clear. She's also easy to contact and is very understanding!
She's a great professor. I think this was her first sem teaching Machine Learning, but I learned a lot and she offers a lot of chances for students to do well and is very accessible outside of class.

Aileen is one of the best professors here. She is passionate about her work and genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. She is willing to answer any questions and spend extra time with you if you need it.

Aileen Benedict might be one of the greatest prof I've ever had. She a genuine kind person that wants her students to pass. She gives the freedom to work with any dataset for your projects & she assigns the projects & structures the class in a way where you can have a portfolio showcasing your work so you can use it later throughout your career.

The best professor I've ever had. Very relaxed on deadlines and allows you to re-submit any assignment you got a bad grade on. There are 4 projects and a final project, the lowest project grade gets replaced with the highest. Very accessible and always willing to help. You pick the topic for the projects and they really help to build a portfolio.

Aileen is the best! You will have 4 Projects to do, but you can pick the topic for each of them! She is often willing to move back deadlines and help students out. Very responsive in the Discord server. The projects can be a lot of work to do well, but if you do them right, they can be very fun! If you work hard this can be the best class you take.

She's the best! She's truly understands the student experience and wants to help us learn comfortably. There are 4 projects and one final project and no tests! There are unlimited attempts for all of the quizzes/non-project assignments. You learn python and it's a great class for the beginning part of your comp sci major.

He teaches material that can only be found in his research, making it extremely difficult to study for his tests. Additionally, he requires you to complete a project using software from 2007. Grades are based on 2 tests and 1 project. I think the content of this class needs to be updated to the modern era.

Dr. Ras is very knowledgeable and very kind to students. Unfortunately he is just not a good lecturer. Students used to pack the room when his TA showed up for exam reviews. He is accessible during office hours and will give you a chance to make up for mistakes if you participate regularly. Only 2-3 exams will make up your entire grade.

The Prof. was absent the entire semester. I feel like the TAs ran the class most of the time. The material was not too difficult to learn. If you don't have a good team, you will have to work extra hard to get an A. The class is writing intensive. You don't do front-end design in this class but you learn how/why you should design in certain ways.

I took 3 classes with him and his teaching is amazing. He's really good at explaining complex topics in a simple way with real-world examples. His classes and even recorded lectures are engaging. He encourages participation, invites industry speakers, and is very kind and supportive during class and exams. He is my favorite professor in uncc.

The professor receives more criticism than deserved. He is very knowledgeable about the material and has a great sense of humor that makes lectures engaging. He encourages students to ask questions and is happy to clarify concepts. The class is enjoyable and rewarding if you stay focused and put in the effort.

Overall class is on visual optics using AI. Homework and projects are all coded in Python. He gives plenty of extra credit, and chances to make up grades. Bonus points were on almost all quizes, and the ability to re-do assignments were always available. No final, but a final group project is assigned
Just avoid the class. Dr Das is knowledgeable but has weird sense of humor and god complex attitude.

A profoundly confusing structure that meets homework wholly unrelated to what's taught in class. If you have taken Intro to ML get ready to relearn it for half the course instead of what you signed up for. The class has no actual rigor and can easily be completed, but don't expect to actually get the intuition behind the topic from the classroom.

Amazing professor that really enjoys teaching students. He really cares about students understanding what he is teaching and makes complex topics really easy to understand. Above all he is really knowledgeable in computer vision and knows well beyond the course work. If you he the chance to take his class ignore all other reviews and go for it!
The professor thinks he is funny but he is not. Will not take this class again.
One of the greatest professor I had in UNC Charlotte.
If I ever have to take another class with him, I think I'll paint myself on the ceiling!
Who even appointed him as a professor, we should meet that person. Poor attitude towards students, I wish someone else taught the class. Not emphatic at all.
Worst professor in the history of UNC Charlotte, should not be allowed on campus. Entire attitude is wrong.

I wish I could have dropped the class in the first week. Professor forces you to use jupyter and the instructions are inherently unclear on how to use it. Hes a funny guy, but this class is extremely confusing and you basically have to teach yourself. For an elective course, it feels like a core course.

you are going to have to know how to do all of the homework with no resources.would rather you fail than get outside help. hours are always full where u cannot even meet with him .half the kids dropped the class in the first week. about 70 percent of the class got in trouble for 'plagiarism' which was them all getting help. in my senior yr btw.

I'm a senior with a 3.8 GPA and had to drop this class because he was such an awful professor. You have to teach yourself a lot of content, it is mixed undergrad and grad students all learning the same stuff, and he takes pride in students struggling in his course. First day of class he showed his 2.1 rating on here and laughed.

I would beware ITCS 4152 and especially this professor, the pre req are not just matricies and data structures. The homework assignments are through jupyter and python heavy. He gives slides but no back code at all. You have to try to find resources to understand how to even complete the assignments. Please do not take this class it is horrible
Amazing professor. All his classes are great. Take the foundational models course. Truly enjoyed it.

Dr. Zhang is very knowledgeable and a great professor. Definitely recommend taking any of his classes. Just finished the first foundational model course offered in NC. Highly recommend for anyone interested in computer science, or applying foundational models to another research field.

Had the class do a closed-note pop quiz with no prior notice, then cancelled the final project and replaced it with a math quiz based on the results of said pop quiz. You'll be shocked to know that students will tend to perform poorly on pop quizzes when given no indication that pop quizzes will be given. Just one of numerous issues.

If you want to actually learn ML, I would advise against this professor. He admits that he makes the class very easy so that students don't fail, with no exams or in-person quizzes, and labs that are basically fill-in-the-blank with no thinking required. He doesn't lecture very well and doesn't really understand how to answer questions.

He's a great professor. The class is very manageable as long as you keep up with the labs and the capstone project. The best part is that he uploads all the lab assignments at once, so you can work on them at your own pace instead of waiting week by week. Overall, very organized and easy to follow, and you'll do well if you put in the effort.
I really enjoyed taking this class, Lectures, assignments and labs were super straight forward and all the content of the lectures were on canvas day 1 of class so you can go at your own pace
Well paced assignments that keep you involved, good lectures. Not overly difficult, well balanced class.

Dr. Zhang is very knowledgeable and I think did a great job at teaching lots of the basics for the machine learning models he went over. The assignments have been very straightforward with the instructions being clear to understand. Although he did have an accent, I never found him hard to understand.

Dr. Zhang has been a great professor. His lecture notes are informative and break down the goals, intent, and equations into intuitive pieces. 

Labs assignments are long but were really helpful for understanding how to apply techniques. 

Accent is thick, but I find that he speaks clearly and at a speed that allows you to fill the blanks.

This class is exactly what is it, an intro to machine learning. His labs are straight forward and he is always willing to help you with errors in your code. 

10/10
Professor has very strong academically background, which provides student a wide range of techniques and advanced approaches.

1. I took this on 2025 fall semester
2. 5156 intro to ML
3. easy to understand
4. It's good for basic level, but if you want to study more about ML, please take 6000 something ML class.
5. Summary : Easy to understand, good course for student with no having knowledge about ML.

Good bless you.

I saw several bad ratings above from the Spring 2024 semester (I'm in the same class). It seems he really pissed someone off with the tough in-class quiz, haha. 

The professor is, in fact, nice, willing to help, and knowledgeable. Generous in grading.  Has an Asian accent, which is still understandable to me and many of my friends.

This is one of the worst classes I've taken. For one, most people I talked to including myself could not understand a word he said because his accent was too thick. Other than that, he changed the syllabus on multiple things through the semester. ex: he told us he won't take attendance, then changed that halfway through with no announcement.

This class is difficult. If you're interested in ML, you'll learn a LOT and have fun. If you're not interested, you'll have a hard time. His notes and labs are dense but they cover almost everything you need to know about each model. Class is structured in a way that some models have concepts built on previous ones, so reach out if you get stuck.

Heavy accent, really boring lectures, idk about other people but I thought the assignments were super difficult, they're done in jupyter notebook and if you get stuck on one part you can't finish it at all, screwed me over for multiple labs. His only saving grace is that he's actually pretty nice and willing to help outside class if you ask.
bro is the king of yapping, most poorly ran class i've ever been in, it was a joke

One of the worst course experiences I have ever had. It was so unorganized and basically run by the TAs. The teacher would come run a Pol everywhere quiz and leave or lecture in a super monotone hard to understand or comprehend voice than leave and have a TA do a lab or something. My final grade was also suited incorrectly and had to get it fixed.

I swear every positive review was written by him. Professor consistently posts materials last minute, didn't teach/lecture until after midterms when whole class complained, only give quizzes and yaps over them. Extra credit and open book open note means you can get an easy A, but he does not care about this class at all. Grades come out super late.

He does not cover any material in class, just posts a PowerPoint that you are expected to review before class for the in class quiz. Extremely disorganized and often does not post material in a time for students to review. The TAs did most of the actual teaching in this class.

We learned more from a TA during one zoom call than we did with the professor. He would be in class for the quiz and then leave before we started doing assignments. He would leave a TA's in charge and gave her no instructions. He posted the solution to the practice tests the day of the test leaving us no time to understand how to do the problems.

Assignments outside of class are extremely easy, while the in class quizzes take hours to complete and there were only 45 seconds for each question, with quizzes being worth 20%. Midterms often had questions that were not in the videos or slides. Professor is boring during lectures, stays on concepts for way too long, and is difficult to understand

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR. Class is extremely disorganized with frequent absences from Pu, delayed material postings (posted Friday/Sat night and supposed to be read Monday, etc), and prolonged, repetitive rambling during sessions. The substitute teacher was more effective in delivering lessons. Extra credit & tests being open-note is only saving grace

Hard to understand professor! Gives random grades on poll everywhere quizzes! It's about how fast you answer the questions not what place you're in.  Tests are not from learned material! safer to take anyone else for this class.

MANY opportunities for extra credit, mostly based on how good your projects are. The course is project heavy, with three presentations on your dashboards. There's a decent amount of homework toward the beginning but less as the semester goes on. Dr. Yang is lenient when grading projects, gives great feedback, and she's very caring. No tests.

This class is a lot; the difficulty rating is more for the class than Fu. Do not underestimate it, regardless of professor. Fu isn't great, but is knowledgeable and will assist students. But he does not respond to emails, is sometimes unprepared for lectures, difficult to understand via Zoom, and has office hours only once outside of class days.

Can be a lot of homework in my opinion. Not coming from a cybersecurity background made this class a little more intimidating and I think that 3200 should be the only pre req for this class to prepare students. I do think this is a useful class. Lectures could've been more engaging or maybe 1 session could've been a lab session instead.

This class is extremely hard the projects suck. You aren't given a lot of information to go off of so your doing tons of research. He uses HTB for homework and as your learning resource. Do not procrastinate in this class your grade will reflect it. However, he will push back deadlines because he knows the class is hard.

The work can be difficult so it's recommended to start on assignments early, but definitely one of the most useful class you can take. Professor Fu is very passionate about cybersecurity and caring regarding students. He also extends deadlines as necessary so students can get work done on time.

Dr. Fu is a caring and generous professor who wants his students to succeed. He's willing to work with you if you put in the effort. A minor drawback of his class is that some assignment instructions reused from past semesters can be outdated, and new assignments may feel a bit experimental. Overall, his class is fair, enjoyable, and worth taking.

This course was one of my hardest classes I had taken. He knew the class was struggling and decided to switch his teaching methods around to make sure students can succeed in this class. He also is very open to extending deadlines so students can do well on them! One of the best professors I've had and is very caring!

This is a hard class. Probably the hardest class and pain for the cyber security concentration. You better not have a Mac for this class because the VM will not work on there. The professor is good at helping students no matter what time.

Material is hard. Uses Hackthebox as textbook. He teaches and goes over the projects (5) and 1 final and midterm. Gives a lot of extra cred and will curve final and midterm. He will always give extensions if students need it. Extremely receptive to student feedback and always listens to the students. If you need help on the project, he gives hints

10/10 communicator. You can reach this guy at all times of the day. Ask anything anytime and he will respond in a minute. If he is busy he will say so and then tell you he will respond asap. Extremely clear when you ask questions. He will explain everything and listens to his students every time. If project needs more time, ask and you receive.

What a GOAT. we have 5 projects and he said we were allowed to resubmit even after grades near the end. Extensions based on student feedback. We have a textbook and it was quite difficult like the class and so was the midterm and final but everything is open notes. Content is extremely difficult but professor tries to make it as easy as possible.

The class itself is INCREDIBLY DIFFICULT, however I don't think this is because of Dr. Fu. He actually tried incredibly hard to help out all of the students, would give extra guidance on projects, and was also very understanding if you had any personal/life issues happen. But the course itself (based on Dr. Chu's material), is really difficult.

Terrible, just terrible, the hardest class I've taken at this University. The amount of work for all of the projects given is ridiculous. Have known others who have taken this course with other professors and the work load was less than half.
She will never respond to her emails, doesn't care about her students and you will not learn anything from her class. NEVER TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES
Awesome class, the professor and TA's walk everyone through the class with weekly checkpoints and essentially ensure a good grade. Lots of group work and class is discussion based.
Easy A, essentially just show up to class, but other than that she's a really good teacher.

Dr. Johnson is personable and intentional. She gives great feedback and inspires you (furthered by her own extreme endeavors in life). The course is easy as long as you participate in classes and do the assignments, but besides that, class with her is so rewarding that even if there were lots of difficult assignments it would be worth it. 10/10

The professor is extremely energetic, fun, and understanding. There is prep work before each class that takes no more than 30 minutes to finish, and a semester-long project. You will do frequent group assignments. This class was fun, and felt like talking with some friends more than an actual lecture. I cannot recommend her enough.

Well-organized and well-planned course, assignments felt well-spaced and clearly explained. All of the material covered important skills; nothing felt like it was just there to fill a time slot. 

The only point of criticism I have is that she could have been clearer/more specific with feedback on assignments.

Dr. Johnson is an incredible professor. You will learn a lot by taking any of her classes. She does everything to help you succeed. There were group projects, they were fun and easy. When taking her CTCM class, she heavily emphasizes the communication part. Also, be ready to be cold-called! An amazing professor that I would definitely take again.

Liz Johnson is my favorite professor at this school. She is amazing at teaching critical thinking skills and cares for her students. She gives you everything you need to succeed and more. We had two graduate students in class to help us with writing our papers and making presentations. Take her, you'd be doing yourself a disservice if you didn't!
Amazing Professor. Definitely would have her as a professor again.

One of the best professors here. Helped me publish my article. Honestly amazing and even though she rambles a lot she truly respects and admires her students. I learned a lot from her and had an amazing time this last semester.

Great prof if you're taking this for the gen ed credit. Homework and assignment guidelines can be weird at times, but as long as you follow directions and show up to class, you'll be fine. Lectures are entertaining and there's a lot of class engagement.

Objectively one of the best teachers of all time. Very engaging in the classroom; will meet you where you're at; cares strongly about ethics; has extensive experience in a variety of fields, and always interested to hear students' own perspectives; provides insightful feedback; exudes a contagious professional & positive attitude.

If you genuinely want to stand out and improve your confidence in your comp sci career, you have to take her. She will push you to improve but you grow so much as a result. Public speaking is so much easier now. There is a research paper, a final presentation, and group projects.

Hands down the best professor I have had at this school. You can tell she truly cares about the success of her students. If you have to take ITSC 3688 try your best to get in her class. Her class is very easy because if you turn in the weekly assignments you most likely get an A. She made the semester very enjoyable.
I took his course . Biggest mistake I have ever done

Srinivas cares about students understanding of and engagement with the content, however the Mob- Robotics content is a lot of long equations and math, and while the concepts aren't terrible, you will probably feel lost a lot. Be ready for pop quizzes. He is an understanding and reasonable professor, so always ask questions

I enjoyed the Analysis of Algorithms course under professor Akella. 

Most assignments were using pen & paper with the intent of writing good pseudocode/ expressing the solution well. That allowed for better focus on the intuition of algorithm analysis without getting caught up in language semantics.
oh yes Srinivas akella is the best!!!!!!

Entire class is confused. Total of 3 grace days for late assignments. That means if you submit one assignment 3 days late, you've used all your grace days, for the ENTIRE semester. The very first assignment had a mistake, forcing people to use their grace days. Pop quizzes count towards grade. Very tough homework. Bad accent. Lessons aren't helpful
I LOVE SRINIVAS AKELLA HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC CHARLOTTE
classes are long but very confusing, not really sure what he wants. Ambiguous concepts and unclear instructions. avoid it.

Overall if you can learn through powerpoints and know all 150 slides and the codes in c++ on the test...which is 60% of your grade... no notes,no study guide,no openbooks and the "Q&A" days he hosts to answer questions about the test just leads back to the powerpoints.... you will probably pass... otherwise you will fail...

Erik Saule is an awesome dude. Don't get me wrong. But OH MY GOD this class will eat you alive if you are not prepared for it. You will pretty much have to teach yourself everything and the tests are abosolutely brutal. His 3160 class is alos completely different than other professors who offer the same exact course. DO NOT take his section.

Definitely worth getting to know him during office hours. Tests were 50% of grade, no study guide or information about the tests given. He is SUPER knowledgeable about the subject, but you don't code at all in class, just learn concepts. Tests on paper, closed book, coding on paper that was a first. Lenient grader-ish, but you need to put in effort

She is very nice, but the RealizeIt taught me more than her. The TA also (shout out to Mark). Statistics is hard on its own. Poll everywhere is pretty much everyday. She is also really fast paced, so beware of that if you take her. Overall, she's an okay professor.

Dr. J is one of my most friendly professors I've had this semester. To do well in the class it is important to watch the videos before doing the realize-it assignments. Dr. J reviews the realize-it content during the class by doing poll-everywheres, quizzes, and other assignments. Beware of the 2nd exam, it was harder then the final exam!

alright? the preceptor was a lot more helpful than her actual teaching but u can tell she cares about her teacher. overall i did struggle to keep an A but i know most of my class struggled even more. definitely need to pay attention in class if u want a good grade

Professor Jutmaan may have a slight language barrier but I believe that she works extra hard to provide us with multiple resources to get our information (such as extra videos and RealizeIT). Her TA was incredibly nice (shoutout to Anthony- the man was a walking W) and was always willing to help with anything! Tests are hard so study for them!

Most of the learning will be done on your own, which can make it harder since its math. A lot of small group projects but they mostly feel like busywork. The way she explains things can be a little fast paced which can make things harder. She does hire preceptors to help the class which does help a lot (thank you Marc). Most work is online.

Takes her an hour to explain a simple in class assignment and then ten minutes to explain the actual information we need for the test. I recommend not taking her class. The work load is easy but class is 100% a waste of time. She also would never explain stuff only repeat the information

Literally loved Professor Jutmaan. She is a super sweet lady and will sit in class (or outside of class) and do your homework with you. She puts all of her lectures and notes on canvas. Just pay attention, put effort and time i to your work, and make notes you will be good

Overall the class was pretty easy. You basically teach yourself everything so I would take valuable notes from the online platform realize it. The teacher is very caring and would make sure that you receive credit on your assignments.if you do the homeworks and practice tests then you easily pass the class.

You get assigned a group at the start of the term. RealizeIt is the online platform you use for practice, and it will basically teach you how to do everything. She reviews the content in class but it's not helpful. She talks a lot when you're trying to work which is annoying. Practice tests are basically the same as the tests, even for the final.

Realizeit due weekly, 3 quizzes, 3 group projects and final. The quizzes are the same as the practice tests. Offers up to 6 pts extra credit for each quiz. You will be teaching yourself most of the material, but if you actually try you can do it easily. Accepts late work and grades leniently. Dr. J really cares about her students and their success.

You basically have to teach yourself for this one. She's not entirely understanding when you don't understand and will just tell you that you're wrong. She doesn't grade too harshly, but her tests are significantly different than homework and her quizzes so beware. She has a thick accent which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it can be difficult.
She was very hard to understand but the class was decently

Don't take her if you aren't naturally good at math. You will be teaching yourself using realize it, and if you come to class confused she will treat you like you're dumb/not trying. She doesn't make things clear and goes very fast, but she allows you to have your group help you which is cool.

a very caring woman who wants her students to succeed. stay on top of your assignments and you will be fine. I was lucky to have a good group of people to do group work. she pretty much allows you to help each other on everything besides tests, but her practice tests are usually the same as the actual test. just come to class and ask questions.

If you stay on top of your Realizeit assignments and do them until you understand then everything else is easy. Group work is really annoying when they give the bare minimum. The lectures are hectic because she tries to do multiple things at once including attendance through PollEverywhere. She has a thick accent, but she's pretty nice.

Attending class is a must because there are lots of graded activities, homework, poll everywhere etc that happens in class. Her lectures are incredible but you must follow through, without them you can lag behind a lot. She is very organized and the resources needed for this class are neatly presented in canvas.

Lots of homework and group assignments. Prepare for assigned seating which is the group you will be working with every class period. Not very approachable and can be demeaning when asking her a question, privately at least. Interactive and does give good comparisons from math to other subjects. No clear course plan though. Gives study guides.
Only downside is that she takes a long time to grade assignments.

At first I thought she was a bit scatter-brained but as the semester when on, I understood why she teaches the way she does. VERY BIG ON GROUP WORK!! Each month you will have an exam on the unit and you will do well if you take notes and study before each test, even if you're not the best at math.

Such a fun and easy math class. If you like realistic math that isn't super heavy on formulas and complex equations, this class is for you. Professor Birdsong is super sweet and there is lots of extra credit opportunities.

Pretty good professor, never really had problems with her, which says a lot considering how rude a lot of UNCC professors are. We had an easy course so I rarely had to ask for help. She provides plenty of resources and teaches the class pretty well

her class is easy but its literally not math, we learned about numeration systems, and voting methods, i think i only used my calc for simple addition, she is annoying to listen too but i sat there on my phone and ended with an A, she also is a slow grader and i mean you dont get a test until the day or two before the next one. id take her again

Honestly...TAKE THIS COURSE! if you need it. The material is super easy in itself, but she knows how to make it easier. It's very group activity heavy but its also easy. On the tests she literally gives you a reference sheet....There is extra credit, AND she gives partial credit too. Super sweet and kind I looooove her!!!
Very easy class, the teacher was a light grader and curved the test and exams quite heavily. Homework had extra credit points each week with an online textbook. Would recommend !!

Professor Birdsong was very friendly, knowledgeable and even funny. However this course in particular is HARD. It is very abstract, and has you jumping between concepts frequently. Regardless, she navigates it fairly well, I would recommend her for other courses, but maybe just not this course in particular.

Great professor, attend class and do her homework assignments and study guides, and the tests will be a breeze. Offers a lot of extra credit on tests and the finals to help you get your grade up. you have to earn your grade by studying but she's extremely clear with what'll be covered and gives you the resources to learn.

I took this class for my math minor and because it seemed the most interesting besides MATH 4109, but it was unbearably difficult and tedious. Everything taught in this course is abstract, and grading was so strict.
She has a great passion for geometry. The textbook is required but easy enough to find online.
Dr. Birdsong is super understanding and makes math fun for someone who is not a math person. I highly recommend her!

Professor Birdsong is a great professor. if you are having trouble understanding something go to her office hours, she will explain it in more details. Homework once a week, practice quizzes in class before test (which are helpful). Overall a pretty great class and professor.
Professor birdsong is great! She's nice, a fair grader, and a good teacher. Notes are clear. Slow at grading tests tho. Also, the math in this class is easy.

Prof Birdsong is a great person but this class is a nightmare for neurodivergent people. I've never felt more overwhelmed by a class; canvas page is unnecessarily verbose, main 2 txtbooks don't help AT ALL, homework solutions aren't posted until right before the test, weekly hw sets are unrealistic, not enough guidance on what a good proof is, etc.
Really nice but does not explain things well

Dr. Birdsong is great. 1165 with her was great. It was the first time learning new math concepts as an engineer, and she made it very easy to learn. Her lectures are not boring, and keep you engaged should you choose to do so. If you pay attention in class, and do the homework, this class will be easy.

Dr. Birdsong is great, but the class was rough. It's so much material, but she does a good job of making it digestible. Make sure you have access to the textbook, and don't let the homework catch you off guard.

Takes a very long time (up to a month) before grading all the homework / tests / projects, and it shows by the amount of homework you receive on a weekly basis. The canvas page is very neatly organized and her notes are very easy to understand. Attendance was mandatory. Responds to emails very fast. Tough class overall.

The class was structured around an interactive textbook, which was very useful because if you leave class without understanding the material, you can go do the readings and homework and it will help you learn. She was a good teacher in class and was generous with grading, with extra credit being built into tests

While I think Professor Birdsong is very nice on a personal level, I started losing all comprehension of the material about halfway through this class. I found that I mainly learned from the textbook, with lectures only serving as practice. There were also about a dozen assignments due the week of finals, so just be aware of that!

Honestly, he's not a bad professor. The only problem for real is his accent. It can be hard to understand, but he uses a doc cam for his note taking so I just copied everything he wrote down and that got me through the class. The exam was hard though.

His class was fine; he has a very thick accent, which makes the first couple of weeks of class an adjustment. He doesn't do homework, so your grade consists of the online quizzes and tests. The 3 tests are actually like the practice exams, so if you can do those, you will pass the class. I would not take STAT 1220 with him if given a choice.

His accent is hard to understand at first, but gets easier through the semester. All of his quizzes are online and the textbook is optional but recommended to be used like homework. He has 3 tests and a final that make up most of your grade.

Amazing Professor! Don't believe what anyone else writes (they didn't try), if you take the time to practice his practice exams you will always get an A. Practice exams are word for word what will be on the test. Don't be shy to talk to him! He cares about all the students and amazing to talk to!

I really enjoyed this class and he is an amazing teacher who sets you up for success. Only downside is the attendance policy, you can only have 4 absences. Other than that, if you study and reach out the the TA or professor then you can make it through with a pretty good grade.

Professor Bishwal is a smart guy, but has a thick indian accent. I ended up using YouTube and ChatGPT to learn the material. Grades are quizzes (10 attempts) and exams (identical to practice tests), so it's a fairly easy class. Prepare for pain with the final exam though, the average score was a 67. Attendance is mandatory, missing 4 classes = 0.

Professor Bishwal is not the worst math teacher I have had but definitely not the best. The main grades are quizzes and tests. If you mess up on a test, you could be in trouble. If you honestly do the work with him while you're in class, you will learn. I will say sometimes this is difficult due to the accent. Overall, not a horrible option.

Dr. Bishwal is a good professor, and tests are exactly like the practice exams. However, his final was extremely difficult and the average was a 55. There are also only quizzes and tests for grades, so I recommend getting a different professor if you can.

He's a really smart guy, but unfortunately I and many others could not understand him. No worries, since some practice outside of class can get you back on track. He cracks jokes sometimes which made the class a bit more bearable. Attendance is mandatory.

I suck at math so I was initially scared of taking this class. I ended up loving this class and it completely changed my perspective on how easy math could be. Dr. Bishwal sets you up for success by literally making the exams identical to the practice exams, and provides you with all of the formulas that you need on exams. An easy A!

Accent but u get used toit,he is overall a nice person. The class as a whole is one of the easiest classes I have taken, considering I am horrible at math/stats. The homework is not bad and you have lots of time, and the tests are literally copies of the practice exams, so they are very easy as long as you study it beforehand.

The thick accent made it very difficult to understand what he was saying but the quizzes and the textbooks made it easier to understand the material. He is very lenient on grades compared to other prof. which he would give 10 attempts on each quiz. The tests were relatively easy if you study the past tests, so if you study, you should be fine.

He knows what he's talking about, but it is very hard to understand him. I had an A in the class until the final because the questions were completely different from the ones we practice. I used YouTube and Google more than him. Attendance is mandatory; you get to miss four classes, and if you miss more, your grade is automatically a 0.

I'm not a math person at all and because of having difficulty in calculus 1 i took STAT 1220, with professor Bishwal he is very supportive and he does believe curving test grades and final exam grades, just try to keep 100% in quizzes and only 3 test in entire course and yes he does provide the previous semester test and the test solutions.

Overall just a terrible professor. He cares very little about his students and you cannot reach him outside of the classroom. The quizzes do not prepare you for the exam in the slightest, and his grading criteria for the quizzes are incredibly unclear. If you can take a different professor please do.

Honestly, he has such a thick accent it can be hard to understand him sometimes. But, he does write everything down that he is saying and doing and projects it onto the screen. The quizzes are allowed up to 10 attempts. If you pay attention in class and use the practice exams to your advantage, you will pass. Attendance matters.
DO NOT I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN!!!!! HE ONLY USES BLUE BOOKS AND TESTS ARE THE ONLY ASSIGNMENTS! DO NOT!!!!!!!

Its important you pay attention in class he has a heavy accent. Class consisted of 22 quizzes throughout the semester where you have 10 attempts. They're 4 test the review he post on canvas. He offers help if you dont understand.

All his notes from class is posted on canvas. Attendance is mandatory and you'll fail if you don't attend. Grades only come from quizzes and 4 exams including the final. he does review in class going over past exams which are the exact same with the exception of word and number changes. final is worth 30%. he is easy if u jus go to class and study.

He is a great math professor. He is passionate about statistics although he does have a thick accent, however, I never had trouble understanding him. He doesn't assign a lot of work at all just quizzes and exams. 10 attempts on each quiz. He works with students who put in effort, if you don't put in effort you will most likely do poorly.
I couldn't understand a word she was saying so I dropped the class
Very difficult to understand.

She doesn't care whether you do well or not. She has a very heavy accent, and is very hard to understand. Gets upset whenever no one responds to her question (even though it is answered, but she can't hear it. Would not recommend this professor for anyone.

This professor was extremely difficult to learn from due to her accent, its almost intelligible. She also auto grades based on the website homework is given, so if you were to answer a question correctly but it gets marked wrong due to a syntax error then you would be given that grade. I would never recommend this professor.

This professor does not allow any type of syntax error in home assignments, for example I would answer a question correctly but there would be a basic syntax error in the homework assignment, and she would not go over the work manually. Also has an extremely thick accent to a point where its almost intelligible.

I took her precalculus course for a summer class. She's responsive and offers plenty of materials to help you learn the subject, like past exams and study guides. Pros: Allows you to get extra credit from doing test corrections and all homework can be turned in late.
Cons: Professor wasn't good at explaining anything and not sympathetic towards students at all. Constantly told her classes as a whole that they were going to fail.

It was very hard to understand the way she taught. She would get frustrated when it took us a while to understand something. There is so much homework and the tests only have 12 questions. I had to teach myself everything the whole semester. She gives you a lot of resources for success; I just think her teaching style isn't very good.

She comes off as a very condescending as she constantly belittled the class when everyone is too nervous to speak up. I got through the class by going to tutors, who saved my grade.

She is a great person and a great teacher. I think many people judge her based on their first impression of her but I would recommend sitting in the front and engaging in class because it was an easy 100 on all of the tests. You can always go to her office hours and she is just really great and funny.

If you have trouble understanding word-heavy or cluttered lecture notes, do not take this class. He is frustratingly difficult to understand due to his accent and tendency to spend very little time on a topic. Be prepared to use the textbook because trying to follow his notes is fruitless. Avoid at all cost, or at least try to take another teacher.
Terrible lectures, weird grading, and a heavy accent with terrible take-home notes. Would not recommend to take unless you can learn the pretty difficult material from just the textbook

Difficult to understand in class. I've had very good teachers with thick accents but Sonin specifically mumbles and is hard to hear. Outside of class he provides no resources and says to solve problems on textbook which doesn't tell you the answers. Most of your grade is rare homework problems which you can only solve by looking up how to do them.
Was very hard to follow during lectures as his notes were structured differently and was very confusing. You are better off teaching yourself the textbook as to not get confused by his teaching.

Difficult to understand. His accent and handwriting are too difficult to follow. His lectures are printed out handwritten notes. I had to drop this class because he was too difficult to follow. He gave a lot of hw and a test each month. I then retook the class with a different professor and figured out this course was easy af.

This professor is ROUGH to say the least. There are 6 homeworks, 3 tests, and a final (which has a short or long version). Be prepared to basically learn fully on your own and do everything you can to do well on the homeworks. You will not know what is going on 95% of the time and the professor doesn't go over examples in class. Avoid if you can!!!

Dr. Sonin was not a good Professor. The lectures he gave were hard to follow because of how he presented the material as well as his accent. If you want to pass you need to read the textbook. There's extra credit on the tests and homework. He allows you to bring formula sheets for the tests.

Dr. Sonin was a terrible professor. He did not come prepared for class. He printed out old scribbled notes and projected them, which were incomprehensible. He spoke with such a thick accent that made it impossible to learn. You can easily pass if you just go through the textbook to learn, it is a very helpful book. There is lots of extra credit

This class was a confusing mess. His lectures are very confusing and not well-made. The material he gives out is different compared to the other classes so the pal sessions are no help at all. Do NOT let your pride get in place of your thinking, 32 1 star reviews, stories about how he messes up and doesn't give credit, heavy accent, horrible notes, lectures, and explanations. Look up General Shepherd from MW2 describing Makarov, it should give you a solid idea of what this professor is like. Genuinely the worst professor ever so far.

Not an easy course, but he tells you what to do to be successful: Read the textbook, do the daily homework problems, understand the homework set, and do well on the tests. Got an A, but at the cost of my sanity. If you mess up on the homework you pretty much mess up on the test as your HW contributes to your test grade. If you get 2 A's and a minimum of a C on whatever test you can take the short exam which is only 3 questions, and that short exam would replace the lowest exam grade. Short exam was not bad btw.

Lectures are handwritten and hard to understand. A LOT of people withdrew before the second exam. However, is a genuine guy and talks about other math topics a lot in class that are very cool if you like math. The textbook is easy to follow and very helpful, did 90% of my learning from it. Allows notes for exams and will help you during them.

Having an A be a 85-100 and having extra credit on the homeworks might sound like a plus, but there is a clear reason why they are there. The content is easy, watching other teachers lectures and tests, the content is a lot easier then Professor Sonin makes it. He also made a typo mid test with no compensation. Dont take him, wait for an open seat.

you can not understand him when he talks or writes. His lectures are just pre-written notes that you will not understand. His grading system is very confusing. He also has bad hearing so do not expect him to hear you.

Hands down the worst math professor I've ever had. Gave lectures that were super unorganized and made no sense most of the time. He knows the material well but doesn't appear to know how to teach it. He was willing to attempt to explain concepts that weren't understood, but those explanations weren't the best.

Prof. Sonin's class was difficult but if you put in some effort you will be fine. Lecture are not always clear but he is helpful in trying to explain topics to you again. Every hw and tests include extra credit. If he knows you put in effort and you are close to higher letter grade he may bump you up. Above average effort but its doable.
Dr. Sonin's class is hard, but he also assigns a lot of extra credit, so as long as you read the textbook, and get any help if you need, it should not be a problem to pass this class with an A.

Prof Sonin is a very intelligent professor but his lectures have no form of structure and are largely incomprehensible. There are 3 tests in which the 2 associated HW assignments contribute to your overall test grade. Not a tough grader. Be prepared to use external resources other than the lectures and the ineffective textbook given for the course.

I recommend Dr. Sonin's course because he is very kind and helpful. If you do the work on time, correctly, and ask questions or help, you will definitely pass the course. Make sure to stay after class for help. Tests are open note. Do very well on homework and you will be good.

You'll have to teach yourself most everything and the homework can be rough. Definitely recommend going to tutoring for the homework. The way he grades is pretty easy. If you get 100 on both the homeworks before the test then you have a 50 and only need a 25/50 on the test to get a 75 which is a B since he has a 15 point grading scale. Nice guy tho

Professor Sonin is probably one of the worse math professors I have had. He teaches via projector and his notes and some of the homeworks are illegible. He assigns home problems and spends over half of the 50 minute class to go over them leaving barely any time to go over the actual notes. Only way I passed was from his 5 point offset grading scale

Do not take this professor no matter what you do. You have to be an exceptional student to pass this course which of course most people are not. Unless you are ready to teach yourself the entire course material do not take this professor. He is very unclear in his teaching and his questions are vague and hard to understand.

The class is manageable if you are good at learning from textbooks. Sonin is pretty difficult to understand during lectures and also has a hard time understanding the questions that students ask. However there is extra credit on nearly every assignment and partial credit when grading.
Lessons with clear, understandable, thoughtful notes. Makes the content seem easy, though it is still difficult. Little grades: 3 HW, 3 Test. Final was a lot harder compared to midterms.
Best math professor there is. His ways of teaching are beyond this world. You are guaranteed to pass this class.
Super passionate about teaching dfq and was always straight to the point with practically everything. I would try my absolute best to take him out of anyone else.
Over all amazing professor, provides excellent practice tests. Very understanding, and provides a lot of leeway. I would love to take his class again.
The volume of 4 and 5 star reviews speaks for itself. He is a great teacher and you should absolutely take him given the opportunity.
BEST TEACHER!!!

No one is as straightforward when it comes to explaining problems as Dr. Safronov. Differential Equations is not an inherently easy class but Dr. Safronov makes it feel simple. Cannot recommend him enough.

Oleg is the goat when explaining how to do math equations. He will walk you through each step and explain why he is taking it. His tests are straightforward, and he will tell you what will be on them. He is extremely nice, but his only fault is his monotone voice, which put me to sleep once or twice.

He explains the topics clearly and goes over the problems in detail. He usually goes over what problems are going to be on the exam the lecture before the exam which is helpful. Three HW assignments, three exams, and one final. Truly one of the best math professors I've taken!

problems are done in immense detail to the point you forget the material is actually difficult. though it can be tough to sit through when you are advanced, i would not have wanted any other professor. fantastic job, sweet guy too

Professor Safronov is an easy professor. Attendance is not required and he posts his notes. Really, you only need to attend the 2 classes before the test because he reviews and its basically the exact same as the test.
The final is harder than the midterms. The average was a 70 smh.

Not much homework. Doesn't take attendance. He walks through the exact questions that will be on the test in the class before test day. Only three homework assignments the whole semester, and three tests, and a final.

Funny guy and explains topics clearly. He gives test reviews that go through most the questions you'll see on the exam. I was teetering between letter grades before the final and he explained everything I was confused about once I asked. Best diff eq professor ever he clearly cares about his material and students.

He was truly one of my favorite math professors and made the subject really easy, the tests are exactly like the review and he makes the concepts easy to understand. Only thing is he doesn't round up grades at the end of the year even if you ask, and my 89.5% ended up being a B.

Best math professor I have taken. He works through example problems step by step so you dont miss any details. This can be boring at times if you already know whats going on but it really helps you understand the material. Basically solves the tests the class before just different numbers. Only 3 homeworks and 3 tests in the whole year. The GOAT.
Practice problems with little concepts. Class was easy if you did the study exams. He is funny at times llol

Great prof; explained differential equations by solving problems in exhausting detail. Lectures could be boring at times, but Safronov was thorough and explains even basic concepts. Easy exams (works through the problems before the exam), fast grader. Not the most tech savvy (notes were chalk on chalkboard) but his handwriting was weirdly perfect.

Prof. Safronov is exceedingly kind and patient. DiffEq methods were taught via practice problems, solved via exhausting detail. No step was skipped and particular answers were usually single-digit integer. Lectures never released early; instead, next class's content was started. This resulted in some content being taught twice. Hard to stay engaged

His lectures are slow, unengaging but, I understood everything he was teaching. He gives study guides which make exams easy. However, after setting us up very well for success, he didn't set us up for the Final. Avg grade for the tests: 95. The avg for final: 68. Meaning the average student went from 95 to 87 from the final. Don't be too confident.

The worst math professor I've had at UNCC. His “sarcasm” is just an excuse to be rude to students, and he is borderline unapproachable outside of class. If you do take his class, it's not impossible but you will need to focus on acing the daily quizzes and go to PALS. You can pass, it will just be miserable.

He is a great professor whose ratings are tanked by freshman unable to pass calc1 having their dreams crushed. He is hilarious, caring, and an incredible teacher that makes the effort to learn your name. Calc3 is a test heavy class and conceptually challenging, but you can pass so long as you attend the lectures.10/10 professor

His lectures were okay. He's not mean but he's very dry and not particularly nice either. The worst thing are the daily quizzes for attendance which make things unnecessarily harder and will bring your grade down for no good reason. If you can avoid him do so there's no reason to make math harder for yourself by taking his class.

Very tough course, lots of homework. Attendance was not mandatory, but there was an understanding quiz for every class graded, so if you missed class, you missed a quiz. Dry speaker and every class is a lecture. There was extra credit, but the tests were very difficult. The final was not as hard but requires a lot of studying.

Not the worst option in the department but not the best. His lectures are really the only bright spot from my experience. With how many tests/quizzes are given keeping a good grade is definitely tough, especially since none are dropped.

Three rating because he isn't the worst but doesn't match my needs for learning. He is a very fast teacher, it's hard to keep up if you don't understand. He doesn't seem very welcoming, doesn't enforce a hand textbook or post videos for people to go back and watch. If you are good with Calc 2 then take his class, if not then I don't recommend him.

If you have this professor, try to make sure that you make friends in that class to help you study. He makes asking questions in his class a humiliation ritual. Don't get me wrong, he is nice and can be funny at time but I do not recommend taking him.

If you want a helpful professor that will use the entire time of his lectures to adequately prepare students for his course, look elsewhere. This professor will demean students who ask questions and not take adequate class time to go over difficult topics. Go with Bland instead save yourself a lot of trouble.

He's not a bad professor, he explains things well and stops to answer questions. But when it comes to the homework, grab a friend and start it early to take advantage of the 20% extra credit for each question.
If you do decide to take him, be prepared for a pop quiz on the second day of class and his sarcastic humor.
I would not recommend this professor if it is your first time taking Calculus. His lectures are not helpful, and his tests are tough. He also doesn't curve, do not take him.

Prime example of good person, bad professor and horrible class. Wanted to like him so much but the way he structures his classes is absolute trash. One of the only calc teachers who does pop quizzes, doesn't replace lowest test grade with the final and just sucks in general. I hate that I had to switch to his course instead of anyone else.
This guy sucks , if you're not a good test taker might as well drop. You fail a test and you're working all semester to work that grade back. GL

Wilde is a funny teacher and good at explaining. In class, it can be hard to tell when he is being sarcastic in a question response. His exams are pretty tough, so study hard for those,you will be good.

Calculus 2 is a tough class and he was good at communicating ideas. He was somewhat rude towards people who had genuine questions. One time in class I asked him when a certain exam was and he mocked me by saying "I don't know, when is that exam?" Meanwhile, people interrupted his class without him stopping them which created an annoying situation.

Calc 2 is challenging in general, but Wilde does a good job explaining most concepts. Some tests seemed more difficult than hw questions and were graded strictly, but you can recover from a bad exam grade like I did. Attendance isn't checked, but definitely show up to class because he gave hints about some test questions.

Dr. Eric is a great professor. If you have to take Chem do it with him!! He will work with you if you are struggling whether it's inside or outside of his class. Dr. E is great. He's so nice and makes you feel like you belong in the classroom. His lectures are amazing. Dr. Eric is amazing! I was very nervous about taking chem 1251 because of everything I had heard about it. He explains everything very well and at a nice pace (not too fast not too slow). Sometimes he does experiment in class which is interesting. Lots of participation points to help with grade. He is a really sweet professor, but the work he provides for us for the exams is NOTHING like the actual exams. Our class average on the exams is really low, and sadly, it seems like I must retake the class because of the exams.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN HELP IT. Not only is Professor Shelton rude and has an attitude when you ask questions, but he will not help in any way if you are trying to understand the material better. He's overall a good guy but your grade is really only determined on how you did for the exams. Lots and lots of homework that doesn't really go towards your grade at all. TA's don't go over how to solve problems rather than just give you the answer for problem sessions. Overall wouldn't recommend!

Hybrid course. Homework consists of discussions and problem sets that don't affect your grade. Tests are the only assignment that control your grade. Professor himself is very engaging and lenient. Overall not a bad class but it would've been nice if he was actually in class for questions. You bassically have to teach yourself and practice otherwise you will indeed fail!!!

The professor does not come in to lecture and is very hard to contact through email. Very difficult to follow this professor. Never clear on what content would be covered in lecture. Jumps around a lot. Assignments don't align with what's on the exam.

Prof Shelton is very smart and passionate about the subject, but some people are not meant to teach. He becomes super confusing. Only accessible through email.

Dr Walter was by far one of my favorite professors! He is fun, kind, respectful, responsive and very knowledgeable. He was always down to meet with students and answer questions and you could tell he really cared about your understanding. O chem king for real. If you can take him please.

This professor was ahh sss. I had technical issues and she did not give a f. Like she just gave me a zero. Crazy part is that I handed the lab in before it was due and time to fix it but she was like I already graded so she gave me a zero and did nolt let me resubmit.

This professor by far is the GEM of the chemistry department, even surpassing anyone at UNCC. The way she teaches and her dedication to the difficult subject and her effort to help them learn is MASSIVELY EXTRAORDINARY. Take this course with Prof. Pavel & YOU WILL SUCCEED. TAKE HER !!!!

I had a GREAT time! She may come across as harsh/cold, but DON'T take that personally. Very passionate about chemistry and willing to help. She is funny and will joke around with you. She is worth getting to know, and I would love to take all labs from her forever! She doesn't play favorites. Her pre-lab lectures run long.  Love her!

Great chem professor. Homework is hard but are very useful for tests. She gave extra credit so take advantage of that. Lectures are good and aren't the easiest to follow but will answer any questions thoroughly. Does not require a textbook and she says attendance is mandatory but it really isn't. Take her if you can.

She is passionate about Chemistry and will do her very best to ensure all students understand. ASK QUESTIONS! she will take as much time as needed to explain, she also gives guided notes (not for grades, just for personal use) to make sure you understand key topics from each chapter. She uses the extra practice questions on the tests, so do them.

Great professor! He's pretty tough and holds high standards, but he's also incredibly fair and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He pushes you to do your best and gives some of the most thoughtful advice, especially when it came to developing and refining our proposal documents. One of the most helpful and motivating instructors I've had.
One of the most engaging and supportive professors I've ever had. He cares about student learning and are always available to help!

Dr. Afonin has impressive knowledge and experience in grant/proposal writing. He uses real-life examples and teach you about what a real grant application look like. Speakers from academia, industry and gov lab are invited weekly to share their perspectives for career planning. He will push you hard but I find it very helpful for my career

I must say that Dr. Afonin's teaching style is very interactive and he is excellent in conveying the course materials that I like most. He is very knowledgeable and successful in his field, so he always tries to motivate the students to step out of their comfort zones and face challenges. He always provides constructive feedback on assignments.

Thanks to the intimate class size, we were able to receive incredibly constructive feedback on each of our proposals. The clear and challenging expectations pushed me to develop invaluable grant-writing skills that will be extremely beneficial as a Ph.D. student and in my future career.

The class was very small so there was a lot of discussion. The course is a writing-based class, so there were many writing assignments. Overall, I learned a lot from this course. There was fair grading throughout and I grew as a scientific writer.

Really nice guy, knows what he's talking about. He expects you to read the textbook before coming to lecture, and kind of goes over what was in the book. Uses a lot of example problems during lecture to teach the material. Only downside is he grades by a few things- quiz every friday, 3 exams + final, and one extra credit assignment.

Like any organic chemistry class, it's going to be extremely difficult. Quizzes every Friday, no homework to help boost grade, and 4 exams. Professor is great, easy to talk to, and truly does seem to care about your learning but the exams, in my opinion, are just so hard.

quizzes every week, which were given regardless of how prepared the class was. Tests were difficult and he provided little feedback. He taught the class as if we already know the material, and didn't help in office hours. other classes were insanely ahead of us.
The lecture is boring, I honestly learn more from the textbook. There are no homeworks, quiz every Friday, so exams and quizzes weigh a lot.

really friendly guy, but his lectures aren't helpful at all in terms of content on his tests. a quiz every friday, the way he lectures is not really teaching, more like just telling us what it is. also expects us to have prior knowledge on everything.

He was an amazing person, but he was terrible at thoroughly explaining concepts. Additionally, he gave no homework. He would tell us to use the book, but do we pay tuition to be taught or to rely on a book.

Dr. Bejger is awesome and super friendly. Organic 2 is a HARD class, but Dr. Bejger does a phenomenal job of breaking things down and explaining difficult concepts. Quizzes every other week that are fair, three lengthy exams + final, generous extra credit opportunity in latter half of semester. Only gripe is he can be a little softspoken sometimes.

Not only is he very rude to his students, The projects in this course are unbelievable and his expectations are insane. there is a special topics project, multiple exams, 2 presentations with 10 page reports, and a closed book final.
