I unfortunately couldn't attend all of his lectures due to biochemistry and had to devout a lot of time to it, but he is very genuine and I believe he doesn't want anyone to fail at all. Very funny guy and knows how to keep students engaged while delivering his point across.
Still no clue how to study for test. Getting good grades in all classes except this one. Teacher is not clear on what to study for the test that makes up majority of grade.

TBH only got an A in the class because of the extra credit. He is a really funny person and incredibly knowledgeable, but if you wanna meet him personally it gets really serious. Like a 180 on the personality, but his class wasn't bad but at times there were points where he would fly through lectures. Cool guy tho.

Dr. Chi is a really caring professor and very funny! He gives lots of bonus points, the final is not cumulative, and the homework and paper assignments are pretty easy! However he goes so fast in lectures and spends a lot of time talking about topics not aligned to exams. The study guides are useless, and this course is HARD

The class is hard but Dr. Chi makes it worth it. He is incredibly knowledgable, funny, and caring and really makes sure you understand the material. Attendance isn't mandatory but really helps with learning for the exams.

Personally, I learned nothing from Dr. Chi. His lectures were BAD! However, he sets up his students for success by his course format. If you can't keep up with him during lecture you can certainly catch up with the PP slides, HW, quizzes, discussions, & papers he gives. This all helped me actually learn he material. Not an easy A, but a feasible A.

Dr. Chi is an amazing professor who I highly recommend. He is really kind and funny. You can tell he really wants his students to do well. The tests are hard so I recommend not taking extensive notes during class and just listening. Then go home and look at the PowerPoint again. If you can take him..DO IT! Lots of extra credit too.

I would not recommend this professor. She is unable to grade assignments. Tonight she made a threat if you don't email me about a missing grade by tonight I'll give you a 0. She posted this at 4pm. Meanwhile it's her who can't keep track of submitted work. If you want to be penalized for turning in your work, you'd love her.

I really enjoyed having professor Ferdous. I took her class online and she was always quick to respond and helped with any issues that my group encountered. The class was challenging but she provided study materials to be prepared for each exam. I would really recommend this professor to anyone taking BIOL-1110 online.
Assessments weigh 60% of the grade... and they are hard as hell.

Group discussions that had to be presented, or an individual presentation/group presentation each week. Never had a real lecture, which sucked because the information in the course would have been super interesting.  Weekly group assignments in college is not ideal and is extremely difficult due to differences in schedules. Very unfortunate!!

Dr. Ferdous makes what could be a really neat class awful. The tests are EXTREMELY information heavy and you basically have to memorize everything on the slide sets to do good on the exams. The average exam grade throughout the semester was around a 60. She blamed the class for the bad exam grades after every exam. Do not recommend at all!

This course was more difficult than it needed to be bc of this professor. She seemed to want to help when the entire class was struggling, but made it feel condescending. No matter how much you can study, memorize, or learn, there is not enough time for the material to be fully understood before exams; which were short answer/MC.

This course was challenging due to a lack of communication, as emails often went unanswered. The tests were extremely difficult, inaccurate at times, and seemed to rely on other students' questions without proper review. The online structure lacked guidance and preparation, leaving me feeling unsupported and unprepared throughout.

It's a pretty easy class if you aren't lazy about studying and watching the lectures. Tests are pretty straightforward if you know how to apply the material. Many people complained about the lack of study guides, but it's not high school, so I don't know what they were expecting. Just study as you go.

A hard course because of this professor. The average for the 1st exam was a 50, she refuses to take any accountability for this. Several peers have asked for a study guide atleast for this course since its very information heavy, and she refuses to provide us with one bc its a senior level course & that other classes have far more info than this

I did not enjoy this course at all. You are split into groups and remain in that group for the whole semester. Each week there is a group project. If your group members do not participate you have to complete the assignment yourself so your grade does not suffer. The exams are taken using lockdown browser and are only open for one day.

Dr. Ferdous was very responsive and cares for her students. The class is mainly group assignments so pick your group carefully. As long as you keep up with the assignments and study for the assessments, it should be an easy A.
Weekly quizzes and homework with a group. Tests are 50% of your grade and come from the lectures posted online. Class is fairly easy as long as you keep up.

Very kind Professor who will understand and care if you have questions. DEFINITELY test-heavy as tests are worth 50% of the total grade, so make sure you study and read the lectures. Other than that, amazing class!

The professor is accommodating, caring and understanding. There are weekly group projects, assignments (due on Wednesdays) and Exams taken with Lock Down browser (due on Sunday's.) They aren't challenging more like busy work! The final assignment is a group project (there is no final exam.) Take her class if you want an easy A!

Dr. Ferdous is very nice and caring. The lectures are a bit hard to follow due to having lots of information and big, scientific words and some of the test are difficult but it is very manageable. The grading for the group projects is pretty straight forward and the first two grades are easy 100s but the last one is graded more harshly.

This course had only four exams, which focused on small details. The lectures were unfortunately not very engaging, presented in a monotone manner, with little enthusiasm, which made it difficult to stay focused. Most of my learning had to come from teaching myself the content outside of class, since lectures didn't offer much insight.
DO NOT TAKE 3166 in person with this professor! Only graded on exams and exams are difficult! Does not email back promptly. Please dont be dumb and take this class for credit with him. Reg

The grade is 100% based on exams with no study guides. He did provide extra credit for attending weekly review sessions, and a few practice quizzes. It is hard to understand what he is saying, and the lectures are not paced well or very helpful.

Exams are difficult and is your ONLY way of passing the class. You can get extra credit (it's not a lot) by attending the study session, but it was hard to attend because they were all during my class times. Everything he says in lectures is just word vomit of info. Unless his polices and teaching change, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS & SAVE YOUR MONEY.

Professor is so unengaging and shows little care about the class. He doesn't teach, he just talks. 4 exams make up your entire grade (and they are extremely difficult and specific). No resources other than unorganized slides, textbook, and practice quizzes that look nothing like the test. NOT OPEN NOTE (as of fall 2025).
hes not open note anymore :(

He completely changed his layout from the previous semesters. The only grades in the grade book are exams and one syllabus quiz. Exams are difficult, taken online but in class, and closed note and his lectures are very unengaging. Gives extra credit if you go to every single review session. If you bomb an exam, girl good luck.

yall i took him in the summer, and it was really good. open note tests, and EC for attending review sessions. I heard he has changed from that format to in-person exams without notes, so be aware if you are planning on taking him anytime soon. recorded lectures were ok, but not sure how he is irl. good luck

This class material is very difficult but I think the department understands that so all tests are open note, so make sure to take notes on lectures and you will be ok, also do your best on every test because there are only 3 grades.

If you don't get an A, you aren't trying. Only graded on 5 open-note tests. All the answers were in the PowerPoint. I never took notes, watched lectures, or read the text. Easiest bio class I've ever taken.
Online. 5 Exams, final is mandatory. All open note and open book. You cannot fail this class. Easy A, take him!!!!!!

Your only assignments in this class are tests but they are open note and most of the answers are right in his powerpoint. He also offers 2 extra credit sessions a week where you can get up to 5 points added to your final grade. If you are going to take genetics I would take it with him.
Great professor. Exams will be your only grades for the class though. His power points are easy to understand and he offers optional review sessions two times a week. Take him if you can.

Very receptive of class feedback and it is a bio class, come to class and don't leave early. She is such a wonderful person! There are group projects that the class could do without but good class, great teacher. Reading/explaining the textbook was useful for me, take detailed notes in class, she mentions things that aren't always on the slides.
Good luck teaching yourself everything!!

Prof Lassiter is SO RECEPTIVE of class feedback. After the class did bad on one of the exams, she changed teaching method & genuinely helped my grade & made me motivated to learn bio a lot more. She offers lots extra credit (I didn't get an A on a single exam, i got an A+ on the class) Gives credit for participating and showing up TAKE HER!!!

This teacher is the best she is so helpful and will listen to your questions and genuinely wants to help do better. She gives so much extra credit because she wants to help your grade. She makes to keep it engaging as well as interactive. Her tests are pretty simple as long as you go through the slides and review material.
This class is a class where you have to teach yourself.

Such a kind woman! She responds to emails quick! (30m-1day). Very lecture heavy, takes up a lot of time. Know the material before next classes, you can end up writing notes/looking over material a day after, but you'll be confused day of in class. Pop quiz type of teacher. On exams, theres small details you can miss from notes. Final can use notes!

Dr. L is super fun and kind and wants you to learn. As a lecturer for general biology, she's very detailed oriented. The material is somewhat difficult, especially for a bio I course. She does have slides that you can access but you have to really know the material to succeed in her class. Would recommend reading the textbook to be prepared.

I had Dr. L for two classes and enjoyed them. Attendance is not mandatory; sometimes she gives quizzes that can only be taken in class. She goes through slides quickly. You may need to review the material on your own. She doesn't assign much homework, and what she does assign is pretty easy. Overall, I enjoyed the classes and would take her again.

She is not a very helpful professer for the average student. Tests are heavily weighted with no chance for correction, and she goes through the content without truly making sure students understand. She also is very detail-oriented and asks for specifics that should not be asked for in a General Biology I class.

The professor does run by the slides fairly quickly however she will make sure that everyone understands what the main concepts are, she also helps prepare for tests by providing review sessions and giving out well oriented study guides.
lovely quick to respond

I can tell that she really does have a passion for teaching and she does want to her her students. I would email her constantly and she was always good at having a thoughtful and helpful response. Another comment summed up her lectures, she talks very fast and doesnt always go in depth with the topics until a couple of days before the test.

Not a great teacher, in my opinion. Speaks very quickly and asks questions for the class to answer instead of teaching the material. Seems to assume that we know all the material already and are already proficient in it, which I did not like since this is a beginner course. Slideshows for her lectures are also very long, often more than 30 slides.

Very interesting class. The material was fun to learn. Exams were long, free response only. No lockdown used. The homework assignments rarely aligned with the material we were doing in class. Not sure I cared for the format of the class but it wasn't very hard.

Will teach you a lot about molecular biology, introduce you to open source websites for analyzing genetics - stuff you can mess with on your own, useful if you are interested in graduate school/research. Highly recommend. Not much structure, req discipline. Exams short, know red ppt terms. Grades lenient. Tough around the edges, good prof.

You won't know where you stand in the class until a week before finals, she is terrible at grading!! Really rude and mean when you contact her in any way. Knows students are struggling in the class and refuses to change. Her tests are around 20 long answer questions and she only gives 1 hour to complete it. Fells like she wants people to fail.

Worst bio class I have ever taken. Super unorganized, a lot of assignments that are more related to Bioinformatics than Molecular Biology. Assignments do not relate to the lectures at all. Lectures are also just videos of her reading from slides that are super detail heavy so it feels as if I have not learned anything.

TERRIBLE TEACHER!! she only reads from the slides during her lectures. does not explain how to complete the hw assignments. gets annoyed when we ask questions. has 1 hour of office hours/ week, and sometimes she won't be in her office then and will not notify anyone. Worst professor I ever had. Acts like she hates teaching and her students.

does not give any support to full online classes. Does not have a schedule- just posted all the homework and assignments on the first day of classes and made them all due on 3 different dates. The homework is so long and based on very confusing websites which she gives no guidance on. Terrible at answering emails.

The course seemed interesting, but I ended up dropping/withdrawing. Seemed fun until she graded homework. She would claim she's not looking for a "perfect drawing," but was SUPER critical, would leave harsh feedback, and grade very harshly. Lectures were also unorganized and super fast. You would be better off finding another class.

such a fun class and great professor. goes over a LOT of topics, from all of arthropoda, to apiculture and med-vet. exams are straightforward with 20-30 ec available for memorizing families. hw is drawing NC insects, and grades fairly. very flexible, engaging lectures, and a professor committed to getting students interested in the world of insects

I absolutely recommend this class. Dr. Stellwagen is a very passionate professor. As much as I hate bugs, I loved this course and became fond of bugs. There's a lot of information to memorize, but it's definitely doable (took this course while taking biochemistry). She offers a lot of extra credit and sometimes extra credit for attending class.
Dont recommanded him!

Dr.Yan is a great professor, he made me interested in the field of dev. biology. the class content is TOUGH, with so many different concepts to shove into your brain, but it is still doable. His lectures are hard to follow at times, but he genuinely wants the best for his students. i would take this class again just for the content! nice prof!

Dr. Luo's class makes some of the mysteries of grad school clear. This course is extremely valuable for grad students and should be offered every semester, even pushed as a core course. We rarely get the chance to flush through our ideas and writing in this depth.
So inspirational! Really pushes you to think in a holistic point of view and think critically about the impact of your work.

You can definitely tell that she cares about her students, providing fast responses and useful feedback on class assignments. Can be a tough grader. Exam format was different from the norm and challenging, but overall interesting class.

Not very understanding. Textbook was given online - from an intro level class. Most info was severely outdated hypotheses. Quiz questions barely made sense. Final exam was 40% marine viruses, we had 4 slides. Harsh grader on participation, hurts you when others don't participate. Same answers got different scores.

The professor was great. Engaging, encouraged questions, treated everyone with respect, challenged the way we thinked and provided timely feedback. I enjoyed the course content and learned a lot from this class!

Took her for BIO-3111, nice professor but lectures are boring and the tests are INSANE. Quizzes are to be done at home and no homework otherwise so you can focus on studying, but even that won't be enough to be prepared for the tests.
I took her for BIOL 3111, but that's not an option to select. She's nice, but she mostly just reads off lecture slides. Tests are difficult so make sure you study.
She's amazing. Take her if you can!!!!

I think Dr. Johnson is a very lovely professor. She genuinely wants you to succeed. Her lecture slides are very informative, and she even does case studies to apply what you learn in class to the real world. She is very friendly and approachable both in and out of class. Would definitely take another course with this professor.

Dr. Johnson is kind and very enthusiastic w/ a dry sense of humor. Be aware that this class is extremely dense in material. To be successful, attend every class, do the reading beforehand, & don't procrastinate studying for exams! This class is fun but requires work!

I took her for both micro and another bacteria class. I like the layout of her class mainly being lectures and only 1 assignment before exams. Her exams aren't too bad you just need an understanding of the info more than just what her slides say. Overall she is not a bad professor, it's just a lot of info you need to take in which is normal!

Tests were 60% of our grades & rather tricky. We had a project due at the end of the semester (w/ an initial rubric). The wk before class ended, she updated the rubric w/ new requirements which was a huge inconvenient for those who completed the project. She changed our online tests to in-person randomly. Doing well in the class almost impossible.

This was an okay class. Dr. Johnson sometimes, especially near the end of the semester, would fly through the slides in class and not thoroughly explain those topics. The assignments we do outside of class have little to no benefit in helping us learn the material, it was just busy work, not about lecture material which added more stress.

This class was extremely difficult;one of the hardest I've taken. She's a tough grader, but also one of the best professors. She truly values student input and teaches critical thinking, not memorization. Lectures are fun, but exams (even open note/book) are brutal. Be ready to work outside.

Loved the topics explored in the class! Lecture-heavy, exams are about 70-80% written response. Still, they aren't really about memorization of lecture content but more about what is the bigger picture we can pull from the world of fungi. Weekly Perusall Reading and discussions are fairly simple just a bit long to read. Interesting course though!

Lectures are not helpful. He doesn't hand back tests. He literally makes you schedule an appointment with the TA to ensure grading was correct. He often answers questions by repeating the statement you asked about as if it's obvious. Tests are 3-5 questions. Don't expect them to be the same as homework questions- he always throws a curveball.

Attendance is not required. He talks more about the derivation of formulas/theories INSTEAD of doing practice problems with us/applying concepts. Answers emails enjoys his job, but is not the best at teaching us what we ACTUALLY NEED TO KNOW HOW TO DO for the exams. The EXAMS ARE 60% of your grade. (2 exams plus a final).
do NOT take this guy. take physics 2 at a community college and cheat, you will never use this again, unless you're a stinky Electrical Major
Lectures tended to be bland and unengaging. The TA's classes were much better and helped me out a lot. External sources were also very helpful for learning the material.
Bro made more mistakes than relevant points, if I didn't have a good TA I would've been cooked. He cares more about his drawings than the actual topics and is always screaming at his iPad.

Aktas handwriting is like chicken scratch. The physics department in uncc is the worst. The attendance on day 1 of lecture = 100%, day 2 = 50%, day 3 = 4% and very soon the physics department will only be teaching walls not human beings. Pathetic. Avoid him at all costs TAKE IT AT CPCC!

This class was horrible. I showed up to lecture the first day where he got sin and cos mixed up and proceeded to look at the board in confusion for 10 minutes. Never showed up again. The only reason I finished with 102 is because I studied hard outside of class, I asked my TA a lot of questions, and there was 8 extra credit points on 2nd midterm.

An example of a professor who acts like he is knowledgeable but ends being opposite of knowledgeable is Aktas. This guy comes to the class, yaps for 1.15 hours about some bullshit derivations that don't even show up on the exam. Only a psychopath can create a brutal grading structure with 90% of the grade just from 2 midterms and one final.DONTTAKE
Terrible, I was better off learning the subject on my own than going into the lectures

Dr. Aktas is a mediocre lecturer at best. He makes interesting topics boring and he skims over important nuance. We would consistently spend half of every lecture trying to figure out some mistake he made mid-class. The entire class is graded off of 2 tests and a final with 3-4 questions each
Easy class just look at practice problems before exam, if you can't do that I'm sorry

He frequently messes up on problems in lectures. You genuinely have no idea if you are solving things correctly, and neither does he. Solved exam reviews were consistently wrong and conflicted with other ones that the TAs did. To sum things up: 90% of our grade is on content he can't even get right. Just No! Don't take it at UNCC! Worst Prof. here.

very condescending. lectures are incredibly boring and hard to absorb anything from. he just sits and derives expressions. no intro to the new material, just straight in without explaining what anything means.
Watch the lecture videos, and understand the theory and you will be just fine. Other professors are the same but he makes the videos and he is a very nice man

I think that he know the topic very well but as far as teaching, he goes over more of the theory than the practical application for the homework and exams. Doesn't help that the final grade is composed of 90% tests

90% of your grade will be two tests and the final, the other 10% is weekly homework that takes hours every week to complete. All of his lectures explain the concepts behind everything, but he never really touches on how to apply those concepts to the problems he assigns. Be ready to have to teach yourself the whole course.

It was impossible to understand what this professor was saying and writing. He doesn't give examples, only goes over the theory and proofs while hardly explaining anything. There were 2 tests and a final, which were 90% of our grade overall. I had to teach myself everything and even then, I barely passed. I ended with a 75% that got counted as a B.

Unless you're very familiar with the content Dr. Aktas covers in class, his lectures are extremely hard to follow. He often makes mistakes during his derivations that go unnoticed, and he does not post any of his class notes online. To pass this class, study the homework and answer keys religiously. Expect a letter grade curve to your final grade.

Professor Aktas is a knowledgeable teacher and knows the subject very well. In my opinion the teaching could be made easier to understand. Learning outside of class was the key to succeeding and the TA recitations were a must attend. I do not think this is a bad class but it is taught at a higher level of difficulty than it needs to be.

I think the ratings are a bit harsh, he is okay as a professor. His lectures can be confusing but his TA's in recitation were incredible. He curved a bit at the end and offered opportunities for extra credit. Grading is very clear and partial credit is given on exams.

Aktas' PHY2102 class is notoriously challenging. Exams are tough with little partial credit, and his teaching style can be hit-or-miss. But Unstuck ai's practice tools helped me stay on top of the material and ultimately earn a decent grade. Not the easiest class, but manageable if you're willing to put in the work.

Take this class anywhere but at UNCC if you can. Aktas only derives formulas in his lectures and you'll be left trying to understand how to solve problems afterwards. Exams were 60% and the final was 30%. No curves on your exams either so if you mess up on the first one you're probably screwed. His only saving grace is he uses a 12 point scale.
Worse teacher I have ever had in my entire life, 80-90% of his students are failing. The class average on the 3 midterms are 60%, 55%, and 53% respectively.

Finally, it's time to shine on rating this prof/class. I took more than one class with him this semester (no other choice). Trust me, you will fail his classes. Classes are soul-sucking beyond your imagination. There are no assigned books, and his notes are useless. Don't think you're smart, you got it. You will get SMOKED.

One of the most pee pee bedsheets courses I've taken. Miserable during exams, when doing HW, and when thinking about the class. Exams are 4 or 5 questions and be prepared to receive a D if you dont write the equations and drawings exactly how baby daddy Aktas wants them. This class is balls

Took this class asynchronously over summer. Learning was ridiculously hard, and I ended up doing most of the learning myself. The videos are pretty uninteresting and not very engaging, and there were LOADS of homework, which was pretty stressful. The partial credit process for tests was also rather unnecessary.
This professor is impossible to follow, don't take him.

I can not give the full scoop on Dr. Leilabady because I did not attend the lectures. As for the course itself, please start studying early, get your hands on previous practice exams. There are only two midterms and a final. Your grade in the class is based of those 3 test, nothing else hardly. Studying past exams and the practice sets are vital!!

Do NOT treat this like any class you've treated before. The test averages are in the 50's year around. You WILL fail this class if you do not make it your top priority. Study WEEKS in advance. Leilabady is there to teach you the concepts, you must do the practice on your own. This is a massive weed out class so prepare yourself.

I was not used to Leilabady's lecturing style because his way of teaching would be coming up with example problems and showing the process of deriving answers. Most times there would be no numbers, just notation to follow, so it was hard for me to keep up with sometimes. Lecture is more supplemental than anything. Self learning helped me get an A.

Dr. Leilabady is not good, but you are basically forced to take him so get ready. Monotonous, poorly structured lectures that don't teach you anything for one of the hardest conceptual classes you will take. Will randomly call on you for pseudo-class participation, but everyone stops going to lectures after two weeks anyways.
Funny guy but his lectures are difficult to follow. The TA review sessions are more important than anything in this class, go to all of them if you can.

Was a decent professor who got you lost when getting into the details of the course. was very funny and could go into great detail when asked questions. The tests are brutal, but he is better off two evils for physics.

Professor Leilabady is knowledgeable but I found his class structure frustrating at times. His lectures were a hit or miss. I stopped attending lectures because I found it easier to self-learn. Exam 1 was easy. I struggled on Exam 2, 3, and Final. I wish I had put in more time to practice test problems than I did to understand concepts.

Leilabady handwriting is like chicken scratch. The physics department in uncc is the worst. The attendance on day 1 of lecture = 100%, day 2 = 50%, day 3 = 4% and very soon the physics department will only be teaching walls not human beings. Pathetic. Avoid him at all costs TAKE IT AT CPCC!

Physics 2 was a journey to say the least. Sometimes the lectures were hard to follow. Your grade is solely based on the 2 exams and final, with those making up 90% of your grade. The TA's were the sole reason on why I passed this class. They had review sessions before the exam on what to expect to be on there. TA's are your friend for this course!

Lots of partial credit on tests so pretty easy to get B's without studying. GO TO RECITATION!! I had an A, skipped recitation 4 times and dropped to a low B. Recitation was annoying, had to write about how socializing helped us...? Leilabady is funny and makes sure we are following along during lectures. Lab is easy.

Phys 2 is a lot to say the least. Barely squeezed by with an A, and I solely thank the TA's for helping us understand via reviews and insight on tests. The TA's are your friend lol. Honestly, lectures are not extremely helpful, and the review problems are sometimes unrelated to tests. 90% of the grade based off 2 tests and final (30 each) are crazy

Physics 2 can be rough but the TAs make it a lot easier. Do the test review packets they send out and attend the test reviews and you should be okay. Grade is 90% tests but the lowest test score could be replaced by final. Leilabady only really covers the theory so you have to learn most of it by yourself. Best professor for Physics2.

This is the worst professor in the physics department. The tests are way harder than they have to be. Doesn't respond to emails and doesn't help his students. This physics department should be in probation for making the tests very hard

Ive taken a physics class last semester and failed it horribly this semester the materiel was a step harder yet he made it easy to understand. He's funny and tries to get everyone involved. They dont require attendance BUT GO TO CLASS!!! The study guides for the tests are great but going to class and trying makes everything click.

Leilabady's lectures are not good. He often makes mistakes and is all over the place. I stopped going to class and solely learned off of the lectures on canvas made by another professor and I did well in the class. Exams are graded so easily with so much partial credit.

If you genuinely want to learn or care about learning take this course at cpcc. I was advised this but it was too late for me. Not sure why there are even lectures, you're only wasting time that could be used to learn on your own. Only way you'll learn or pass is from the textbook and your TA. Your TA is your best friend for this course lol.

Pretty easy class (if you know what you're doing) but the professor was just hard to hear sometimes and the lectures were kinda confusing. I only got through it because I have been in two previous physics classes in highschool. For attendance, lectures were not required, but every Friday there is a recitation that is required.

Physics 2 tested me in more ways than words can explain. Take it at a CC if possible. In hindsight, his lectures are good if you study the textbook before. Tons of partial credit. He can be entertaining but the class is brutal imo. *Study outside of class* HW ISN'T ENOUGH to understand PHYS 2.
Kind, caring, intelligent guy. Legible handwriting.

Skip class, spend that time watching the online lectures and practicing the practice problems in the textbook and that are on canvas and you'll make an A. Not a bad professor, physics is just something you have to teach yourself lowkey. If you fail his class reconsider college because his grading is lenient.

Dr.Leilabady is Okay, Had him for Phys1 and Phys2 and the biggest complaint is that the example problems ran through in class are frequently strictly conceptual and only use variables which can make understanding any math that is unclear very hard. But he is good at answering questions and making sure that he cleared up what you were asking.

He is the worst teacher I have ever had for PHY 2101 and 2102. He does not listen to students, and if you have problems with Canvas or quizzes, he will never help you; he will say it is not my problem. I have a hard time understanding his language.
Useless lectures, couldnt understand like 90% what he was saying.

Professor Leilbady has gotten more lenient than in past reviews. The practice problem sets are graded based on completion, and recitations on Friday are bonus % points. His exams were similar to practice problem sets and problems in the textbook. You will have to review a lot of information outside of class but overall, it is a good class.

Dr. Leilabady is a chill professor, but his class has some challenges. The lectures can be hit-or-miss, and the homework doesn't always align with what's taught. However, the tests have predictable formats, and unstuck AI is a great tool to prepare. With the textbook and TA sessions, you can do well.

The homework was so difficult and took forever to get graded, and the exams were short answer and you had to submit the work with it. To be honest, it is not structured will for a summer course because it is only 5 weeks. To do well you basically have to watch hours upon hours of blurry lectures he recorded from like 2017, and it isn't condensed.

Dr. Leilabady is a really nice and funny guy, but as a teacher I had some issues.  The lectures were hard to follow at times, the homework was not what was taught in class at all, the tests were hard and different than the review material, and the grading between TAs varied so badly that your grade was just based on luck.

Pretty run-of-the-mill professor. A kind and funny guy, can speak quietly but will respond to criticism and requests to slow down. Is accommodating and offers office hours. Everything is graded by TA's, results in a wide range of feedback and grades. Tests are similar to the homework, the textbook is not really required.

Dr. Leilabady gets way too much hate here. He is a very chill guy, funny, and extremely knowledgeable with all of the course material. Before each test, we were given the formulas needed for the test and the topic of each question. Test questions were mostly from past tests and practice problem sets. You need to do a lot wrong to fail the class.

I emailed him three times during the semester and he did not answer one. He's nice but I understand why his mother-in-law hates him. (you'll understand when you take him). Overall he's better than the other man.

This class is hard but not nearly as unfair and cruel as people say. Dr Leilabady was a pretty solid teacher, he told our class the general topic of each question on each exam which was extremely helpful on the exams. He drops the lowest test and im pretty sure he curves the tests. Just study before the tests and you'll be fine

Dr. Jacobs is an amazing professor. She's very candid with what you need to pass her class, and provided awesome recorded lectures. The practice exams are a great resource for the real thing, and were my primary source to study. If she sees you working hard and doing your assignments, she is incredibly compassionate and willing to accommodate you.

Dr. Farida is the best professor I had this semester. Even though the content of the course can be difficult to understand, she has a plethora of resources available. She offers study hall hours with herself or her TAs. She offers extra credit and bonus questions to help pat your grade.

Dr. Jacobs is great, gives extra credit and has lots of availability during the week for office hours on zoom led by her or one of the TAs. Do the homework, extra credit assignments, and go to review expos and you'll be fine.

She is such a kind professor, and offers plenty of partial/extra credit. I am not great at physics but she made it easier. One thing: you can skip lecture and rewatch the videos she posts, but do not skip recitation sessions since they are attendance based, have worksheets, and weekly quizzes. Quizzes aren't too bad. She drops your lowest.

I was originally very skeptical of this class because of all the low reviews, however, Dr. Jacobs is a wonderful professor who clearly cares about her students. She has several study halls that are easily accessible and provides numerous extra credit assignments throughout the semester.

I took her over the summer She is very nice but overall she is super strict so listen to her directions when taking test and do not look like your cheating!!! She does offer a lot of extra credit but please watch her lectures and practice the problems since they are similar to the test.

Dr. Jacobs can be a little condescending but she'll help you out. Problems on the lecture slides are fairly similar to exam questions, so do those and the worksheets and you should be good. Lectures are optional but workshop is mandatory — her pre-recorded lectures were a bit better than the live class ones imo. There's partial and extra credit.

Her class is hard to get used to at first, but she wants people to do well in her class, so there are lots of assignments to buffer grades. They're annoying, but they help keep grades up. In her lecture videos, she hints at what questions are on exams. Quizzes affect your grade more than you think.

This course is not for the weak. sample exams don't reflect the actual difficulty of the real tests. Her & her TAs are extremely strict when grading, even if you get the correct final answer, any discrepancy in your work can cost you points. she can come off as condescending and will make you feel dumb for forgetting middle school math concepts.

Dr. Jacobs calmly acts like you're stupid for not understanding material she can't explain clearly. She isn't strict — she's a quiet failure taking out her regrets on students. Exams barely match lectures, and the course feels designed to break you down. She's what happens when someone who should've retired clings to a job they were never good at.

Dr. Jacobs is a great professor and knows how to explain concepts extremely well. Attendance for online lecture is not mandatory, but it is mandatory for recitation. Recitation is really helpful and all the practice problems assigned throughout the week. The only issue I had was the way she tended to talk to people can be interpreted rudely.

Explained everything well. Very funny too! Recitation assignments and quizzes really helped me prepare for the exams. Review everything and do practice problems as you go and don't wait the night before exams to study everything and you should get a high grade in this course. Attend the review sessions if you need extra help!!

Agree with previous rating, class was easy, but there were definitely students struggling which is understandable. However, there was a clear discrimination for some odd reason. Maybe due to an assumption of who's going to put the effort or not? Weird. Cool class, odd superficial personality on teacher.

Complete honesty: every batch of students has that one person that will be picked on or degraded/looked down upon for some odd reason. I could never form a relationship with her and it was hard to approach after the petty nature she presented, even if I tried. The other reviews are clearly the better end of the batch, but be prepared. Good content.

Not an easy class but if you are willing to work for a good grade, she will help you get it. Not falling behind on watching lectures helps you do well on homework and quizzes. Practice problems and concept maps will help you master skills needed for exams. Go to office hours for help, makes sure you actually understand instead of doing it for you.

Dr. Jacob's is the best professor I have never met. She makes this class easier than it is . Her lectures are simple and very helpful for exams , just pay attention to each ‘very good' example she mentioned . Her recitations worksheets are helpful for understanding concept.She gives extra credit and she cares about students like a good mother .

Don't listen to the negative reviews on here. I loved Dr. Jacobs. The class is hard, but it's physics 2. It will be hard with any teacher you take. She is the most available teacher I have come across. Before exams, she will host a study hall on zoom until 11 pm! All of the exam and quiz questions are identical to questions she goes over in class.

Really great professor! Very helpful and responsive outside of class but my only warning is that it's a LOT of work for a summer class. 5-7 hour plus long lectures a week and 5-8 quizzes a week!! Does offer extra credit though and video lectures are helpful for tests!

Pretty good professor. Exams were not that hard and very similar to problems she went over in lecture. Watch all the videos and do the Rec. worksheets to do well. Her study hall ZOOM was helpful and she was always accessible outside of class. She liked to make jokes in class and understood that most of us don't care about physics. Overall solid!
Pretty good professor, good amount of homework without it being overwhelming, if you watch the lectures you'll do really well but they're all over an hour each so it takes a long time to get through.
Overall Great Instructor. She gives partial credit on exams, opportunities for extra credit, and the right amount of homework to be successful in the class.

Very good at articulating what is expected. Gives lots of practice resources. Real-life applications to physics which I appreciated. A lot of practice but if you do them you are ready for anything on tests. Great in office hours. Accessible and flexible with my situations.

She is an amazing professor! She has pre-recorded videos that are very helpful when you can't make it to class. If you want a good grade just make sure you put in the work. Do as many practice problems as you can. She also gives extra credit that can add 3 pts to your overall score. TAKE HER!!!!!!!
Farida is awful. She is partial to certain students, and acts like she cares about her students and wants to help but end up being extremely degrading to your and your questions. NEVER take her!

Dr. Jacobs is great. Lecture attendance is not required. You only have to attend recitation. No need to read the textbook. Just do the recitation worksheets, watch YouTube videos before recitation, watch the recorded lectures and you will do fine in the class. I like the freedom she provides in the course.

He is a decent lecturer that has an accent that sometimes makes things difficult to understand, and sometimes he does not explain concepts well.  He answers questions in a convoluted way.  I would recommend studying with friends or looking up supplemental content online to understand things clearly.   He does offer ec for attending all lectures.
Pretty funny dude, topics weren't very difficult, and lectures were pretty good and easy to understand definitely better than some of the other physics professors.

These bad reviews are mostly false. Dr. Gerges is a decent teacher. He does have an accent, but you can still understand what he's saying for the most part. As long as you study all the practice and recitation problems, you can definitely get an A, or a B+ at worst.

He was an okay professor I thought he was okay at teaching but honestly I just stopped going halfway through the year and instead watched the videos on canvas. Theres not really homework or anything so if you wanna do good u just gotta make sure you put in the effort to practice throughout the year

He is very bad at lecturing and explaining topics. He just reads from his notes every lecture but it's still confusing. He doesn't stay on a single topic and explain, he jumps from topic to topic because he gets distracted. Luckily attendance isn't mandatory but he does say he will curve your grade if you miss less than 3 lectures.

Thought he explained everything incredibly well, but you have to pay attention over the zoom. He's got a cool setup & very nice too. Ppl in my class that complained about him were doing it during class & texting the whole time. If you're not paying attention, you're not going to understand what's going on. He makes it easy, just pay attention.

Took him over the summer and it was kinda useless. His lectures were impossible to understand, you are better off watching YouTube videos on the topics. Tests were weird with a zoom setup and lockdown browser with a TA that didn't even pay attention to students that asked a question.

I just didn't like the class. The exams were set up weird like you had to be on Zoom and show your work space but I feel like the TA didn't care at all. The quizzes were confusing and communication was rough, overall I found it very hard to succeed in this class without outside help like YouTube videos and my friends explaining topics to me.
Don't believe the bad reviews. Put in the work and you will do fine. He is hilarious and very good at explaining things.
It is very hard to understand his accent. No extra credit opportunity. The grade is based on tests and quizzes only.
just attend zoom meetings for test reviews as tests are based off of them. not hard to get a B
PRAY TO GOD YOU PASS THIS COURSE!!!! Thats what I can say in 7 words. Good luck and you will need it.
Would have given a 2 but he rounded my D to a C so he's not so bad. Not the best at teaching either. Brutal final and expect to see "GOOD LUCK" written everywhere.

Made it clear what was expected of us. Tests were fair and were similar to the practice problems, study with those. Topic tests are difficult but doable. Explained things well to the class. I thought the student instructors were helpful as well. Class goes fast though, as long as you don't fall behind and practice semi-regularly you'll be ok.

Professor does a good job of lecturing; however a great deal of the lecture is recorded after class time has already concluded. Grading structure tries to help you out overall; with partial credit on most of the exams and lots of overall grades.

I'm not giving a 5 because that'd mean perfection; a 4 is the next best thing. People rate this class harshly, but it's just not an "easy A"—you have to do the work. Mr. Gerardy is incredibly patient and gives more chances than students probably deserve. He is a smart man who leads a great team. Highly recommend if you're willing to try.

Lectures online through zoom however they are hard to follow as this guy has the worst handwriting ever. the workshops and study halls are were you're really going to learn and understand the material. Exams sometimes take +2 weeks to get back.  The TA's are great and actually help so reach out to them

Gerardy is a kind guy; he genuinely wants to help but can go off on tangents. The content is difficult, the size of the class is big. Have a strong trig/algebra background before this class. If this class is the only option for you, PLEASE go to study halls and office hours. Him and his TAs are very kind and helpful and want you to succeed.
Get ready for a bunch of homework. The tests have random things on them. If you're not religious, find one and start praying.

This class had very many assignments. The grading criteria was very confusing. The class is test heavy. The professor himself is very good, nice, and he is a very good teacher. The professor gives every student time even with hundreds of students if you ask for help.

Worst of the worst. Attendance is mandatory. Group work. Placement test on the first day of class, which is graded and we haven't even learned anything yet. Rambles too long for a simple topic and gets off topic.

Very passionate and is great at explaining things in multiple ways if you don't understand. Knows the content very well and it's hard to do bad in his class. Grades fairly. Offers SO MUCH extra credit at the end of the semester, you just have to put in the effort. I finished his class with a 100. Final was worth 100 out of 112 possible.

Gerardy is a sweet guy- he's very personable, nerdy, & a bit quirky. Most physics courses require a lot of outside study time, and this one is no exception. It's best to stay on top of things, DO NOT fall behind on lecture & post-lecture material or you'll regret it. Try and avoid taking other time consuming courses w/ this one (orgo, genetics)

I can't read his handwriting ever, he rambles forever about random stuff, we are required to purchase a textbook which features incorrect answers/typos/offers no space to write. Our exams are extremely hard, and the first one which you take first day of class counts for credit… despite not being taught any of the information yet… Take someone else.

The online format is annoying for a subject like physics however in person workshop helps. Make sure to go in during study hall before exams as this is the only time you'll be able to ask for help in person directly with Dr. G. He explains very well (especially in person) so you must be willing to ask. Gives enough resources for success; use them!

Pretty good lecturer, and he records himself doing the entire workbook. If you can do all the workbook problems, you'll do good on exams. Pretty helpful during workshops too. Definitely refresh on sin/cos/tan in degrees, angles, and moving variables around. Decent amount of extra credit available.

He does a great job making a tough class as manageable as possible. He drops a good number of assignments and offers plenty of extra credit. The workbook has some errors, but that's not on him. I just wish he were teaching PHYS 1102, too.

Extremely slow paced, simply just spits information at you and tests you on a different language of topic for the exams. There is easy, weekly homework assignments. Lecture is requires as PollEverywhere takes attendance. Dont waste time going to exam review, no help given at all.

Has to be one of the worse professors I've had. He is terrible at explaining the subject and just rambles on about topics. He reads straight from a workbook that is required you buy because he grades completion of the pages. In the workbook itself half the answers are wrong and the questions have typos so you cant even use the booklet to study.

Gerardy is a personable guy. The schedule is weird but adaptable. You're given a workbook and everything is in it. He explains things well, but it's a hard class. It's manipulating word problems. Quiz every week, exam every 2. Equation sheet is given. He posts recordings of all lectures! Extra credit for every module- treat it like weekly homework!

The structure of PHYS1101 is very annoying. Workbook checks and weekly workshops which makes it feel like high school. Slow-paced online lectures, but they're recorded and posted online. If you do all the work, it's not too bad, but you might have to use youtube to learn. I wish this was just a regular lecture class.

allows regrading on tests. very understanding let me make up week 2 homework around the end of the semester for full credit. Allowed 6 points extra credit on the final. The only bad thing is the placement exam you take in week one of the class is 7% of your grade.

I enjoyed Dr. Gerardy as a professor. I found him to be very helpful and He took the time to explain every problem you had. I think the selection of TA's was phenomenal. I thought they too were very helpful. He does give a lot of extra credit so I would take advantage of that! 10/10 professor!

Dr. Gerardy was really great in workshops for PHYS 1101, he explained concepts arguably better than they were explained in lecture and he made difficult concepts a little easier by giving us real life examples. Physics is a very difficult course, but Dr. Gerardy made it a little easier to understand.

Currently taking 3220 and learning more from YouTube than this guy's lectures. Everyone who's taken Linear Algebra agrees that the way he teaches the subjects is weird, and that's not even a prerequisite for the class. In addition he teaches to the blackboard while body-blocking, once was an hour late and made a point about refusing to apologize

she was overall very sweet and the class was pretty easy. it felt more like a gpa booster than a good class for if you liked astronomy. I think the lab really aids in the experience considering its a fully asynchronous class. her lectures are alright and watching the videos are for a grade. overall she gives a lot of extra credit at the end

I didnt like that we had to purchase the book just to do Homeworks since there's no reading but her lecture videos are required for attendance.The project instructions made it seem that you could work independently but thats not the case, therefore most people will work on something they have no interest of. Overall good/caring professor.

Very unorganized canvas page, to the point where major assignments can be overlooked, and her video lectures are not the easiest to understand. I would recommend referencing the textbook over her for the work in the class. Class overall wasn't that hard, just seemed lazily put together, but she's very nice and generous with extra credit

EXTREMELY unorganized professor, assignment descriptions make little to no sense, group work is required in a fully asynchronous class, attendance was taking for watching the videos which had a constant noise in the background that gave me a headache, the syllabus is a mess, her answers to questions are incomplete most of the time.

Dr. PA is a nice professor. She seems to care about her students, and for the most part responded in a timely manner; which I respected. My only issue was the short time frame for our tests, as they were online so I expected them to be open for more than one day. Overall, though, she was sweet and the topics we learned were interesting.
Won't take again of there are other options to choose

Professor uses WebAssign for assignments and uses a paid online textbook. Tests are loosely based off of the hw. There is a final project at the end where you make a video answering an astronomy question you have. The recorded lectures are okay, it is hard to understand sometimes because she has an accent.

This professor has NO IDEA how to use Canvas properly. Tests would be locked after taking them, making you unable to figure out what you got wrong/how to improve. Same assignments had multiple due dates and you wouldn't know which one was right. The study guides she gave hardly covered the content on the tests. She's nice, but this class was awful.

On the first day of class, this professor will tell you that if you are uncomfortable or do not wish to be in class to learn, nothing will be held against you. All the professor does is talk quietly, never answers emails and grades unfairly, and also take away study guides without warning. Stay on top and don't be afraid to send emails!

Dr. Porras is so nice I feel bad saying this but her lectures are awful. She speaks so fast and without clarity, and the powerpoints she posts are unhelpful as it's only pictures. She locks homework assignments and there are NO extensions unless there was a genuine emergency. She's very sweet but I don't think I'd take her again

Did not use canvas so I didn't know my grade most of the time. He tries to explain things the best he can. Don't miss class because somethings get confusing. I used Radiology Tutorials on Youtube to understand the class.

Great guy, I thought he was super funny. Lots of great guest speakers, one of which inspired where I want to go in my career. The only hard part is the final project, which was hard because we had to research a physics topic and I don't know that much about physics yet lol

Dr. Fried is a condescending, disrespectful, empathy lacking individual. Picks on students in workshop, does not respond well to feed back, and is a nuisance to the learning environment. He needs to be removed from all physics departmental positions. Ruins peoples passions of grades and any motivation to succeed in their academic careers.
The class itself is difficult but he does his best to break it down and is very understanding if you need extra assistance or accommodations for any reason.

This class was hard! He rambles during most of his lectures, but he knows his stuff. The quizzes weren't horribly hard but did require lots of studying. He was a lenient grader and drops lowest grade in each category. He was always willing to answer questions and enjoyed participation. Brought real materials into class to demonstrate.

Dr. Fried was one of my first professors my freshman year & right off the bat you can tell how much he wants his students to succeed. This was a freshman seminar class so it was more abstract, but he gives great feedback and is very encouraging.

If you DO NOT have to take molecular biology, do not. This course was absolutely horrible. Class consist of just lecturing from the book, reading of the slides word for word. Very boring. And the exams are absolutely hard! He does not provide a clear understanding on what will be on the exam when more than 5-6 chapters are being covered.

Dr. Fried was very caring. he offered help outside of class if requested. physics in medicine was a difficult course. very lecture heavy, taking clean, organized notes is a must, as well as studying regularly. he wanted his students to pass and most of our assessments were curved. this is a class you must attend.

The lectures were extremely ponderous and pointless feeling, many people leave halfway through. Definitely would recommend skipping them and self-studying. Tests were fair, homework would sometimes be quite long. He is a nice guy but unfortunately myself and many others decided that we were better off teaching ourselves.

Lectures are not mandatory, but the Friday recitations are. To sum up my experience, I could not make it through a single lecture without falling asleep, which I never do. I would only reccomend taking this class if you can self study

He is a nice guy, but he makes physics so hard. The practice tests are nothing like the actual exams and I genuinely don't know how people do well in his class. The TAs are amazing, very passionate about physics, and so is Dr. Heindl, but he is very monotonous and it's easy to get lost in class.

Mr Heindl is a great professor. Always shows up with a positive attitude and even is humorous during technical difficulties. Replying to other ratings: lectures can get boring but Heindl does what he has to do: teach. His lecture notes are more than enough to understand a topic. 1 day is lecture, the second is practice problems.

In all honesty he's a good professor, the only harp on him goes to the difficulty of the class unfortunately. He genuinely wants to help people understand it, he typically has one day of lecture and the other with practice problems. I would 100% take him again over the other two available physics professors if I had the choice.
Just talks a lot during lectures and youll get lost everytime. I stopped going to lectures after a few weeks to save myself the time.

Prof. Heindl's lectures are not mandatory and sometimes felt confusing and disorganized, but I believe that he really cares about his students and he was always willing to answer questions or re-explain. If you are good at self study I would absolutely recommend Prof. Heindl, however if you need more structure this may not be the class for you.

Lectures were slow and attendance wasn't required. In class, he worked through problems much harder than those on the tests, which could feel intimidating. Weekly quizzes and unit tests were manageable, but the final was very difficult. He was nice and listened to student feedback

If it wasn't for the online lecture material from other profs, I wouldn't have passed. Lectures are basically pointless because it was a large class and he would stop to answer every question instead of office hours. He didn't explain important topics in detail but would spend the entire class on minute details that weren't ever brought up again.

Lectures are confusing and disorganized, skip them and use the time to study. He asked for student feedback on his teaching and applied some of it, which was good. No homework, weekly quizzes, and a couple exams with practice exams provided. If you study and work hard on quizzes, you will do well.

I took quantum mechanics with Dr. P. It is an incredibly difficult subject but he structured the class very well and so it was hard, but not frustrating. He made sure to teach the subject matter before the homework was due and went light on us the week before any exam so we could prepare.

13 Homework assignments, 0 graded by the time the final exam showed up. He does return your exam grades quick but actual exams only can be accessed in his office during office hours. Extremely boring lectures and is always behind schedule to the point that we had 2 exams on the final week of classes with the final while still missing 2 more exams.

Poor time management; consistently late and holds students past class. Lectures are repetitive with scattered notes. Feedback is nonexistent, with homework remaining ungraded for months. Assignments have short 3-day turnarounds. Grading is heavily weighted on exams (85%), and the professor speaks very quietly. Some online material is available.

Really nice professor, but can be boring at times. Asks a lot of questions during class to try an keep it engaging though. Assigns lots of homework, sometimes with 2-3 days till its due. Exams were fair and I never looked at them after the fact but im sure he's a lenient grader. He also came to my job and tipped me good, so he's my goat.

Tests aren't super hard. Beaman is a terrible teacher, so prepare to teach the course yourself. He runs over time on every class and comes to each class late. He doesn't really care about students doing well or understanding the course. He strictly abides by his syllabus and doesn't round. Personally would never take another class with him.

Beaman's Dynamics is interesting. He is probably the easiest Dynamics professor at the school. But on the other hand, his lectures were a snoozer. I thought his tests were very reasonable and on the easier side which is great. The homework was annoying, as he would randomly post them and have them due in 3 days. Take for 3121, but idk about 3122.

Always late to lecture and holds everyone up 5 minutes after every time. Extremely boring to sit through where you might fall asleep.  Randomly assigns homework's without warning. Exams are fair and graded decently but you cant access your exams unless you go to his office hours where he'll watch you down like a hawk for looking at your exam.

I would describe this class as disorderly. He often showed up 5 minutes late, assignments created Thurs/Fri and expected to be turned in by Monday, and held over class period. As I am writing this, not a single one of my HW assignments has been graded besides ones from the online program RealizeIt. Tests were fair. Overall, left much to be desired.

If you can stay awake long enough to process what he's saying, you'll learn a lot. Brevity is his arch nemesis. Generally caring and understanding of circumstances. Frequently late to class and ALWAYS went at least 2-5 minutes over. Allowed extra time on exams as necessary. 
Took several classes with him, would not take more.

At the start of the class, the pace may feel slow, but trust me, it's for your benefit. The professor approaches teaching as if you haven't taken any related courses before, which is fantastic, especially if you've had less-than-ideal professors in the past. I highly recommend taking his class—he's great at what he does!

A good guy, caring and understanding. Lectures can be tedious and always go ~5 minutes over, but subjects are explained thoroughly. Occasional attendance quiz (graded on your name being written). Assigns a good amount of homework but chooses good examples to practice. Takes hw questions from the textbook (get the right version or ask a friend!)
Beaman is a great lecturer, and he does a good job of explaining the course material.

If you want a professor who rambles incoherently about unrelated topics for 45 minutes, then keeps you 10 minutes late every class period, this is your guy. Excessive amounts of online homework, he lets online software do all the teaching, and never returns exams on anything remotely resembling a timely basis.

Dr. Beaman assigned two tests during the year worth 60% and had a comprehensive final worth another 30%. He also does not allow the use of a graphing calculator. Tests are pretty similar to the homework problems.
You get what you put in for her class. The tests so far have been based on what we do in class.

Professor Smith is genuinely one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is very transparent about expectations, grading, and what to expect on quizzes and tests. She genuinely cares about her students and by the end of the semester will have everyone's name memorized. I would highly recommend taking Professor Smith.

I'm currently taking MEGR 2141, and I have nothing but great things to say about Dr. Smith. She genuinely cares about how well the class is learning, always willing to answer questions, and takes the time to walk around and give individual help. Good energy, clear lessons, welcoming environment to participate. 10/10 would recommend.

Tough class but lecture was pretty easy to follow along, homework and additional study materials were all focused and helpful. If you were confused, she was good about going more into detail, and she's accessible outside of class.

Dr. Smith is the goat, if you have yet to take Statics you need to take it with her. All her presentations were thorough and comprehensible, which definitely helps in a class that can be challenging at times. She also made extra lecture videos which were extremely helpful, especially for practice. Great resources and the best professor I've had.
Very caring professor. spends a lot of time making videos and finding practice problems for studying. The best way I could describe this professor is that she is extremely fair yet challenging.

I loved this class she made it bearable and she was always open to helping us be better. The class is long about two hours but she tried to make it shorter now the class is ENGR1301 though for all freshman coming in Fall '25. She is also lowkey funny which I love and there are 5 tests in the class so a test was like every 2-3 wks. So study!

She is genuinely a great professor. Her lectures are designed for you to understand. She is more than happy to clarify things if you have questions. the quizzes and exams made up a large part of the grade but as long as you understand the material you should be fine. She is pretty forgiving on tiny errors on exams and quizzes. Overall GOAT.

This professor was the best I've had. When she missed class, she would post a lecture video. Always extremely helpful during the lecture. She always provided so many examples so we were always prepared for quizzes and tests. I've taken her twice for both MEGR 1100, and MEGR 2141. I would definitely take her if you get the chance.

Attendance is really important, is not like attendances everyday, the teacher gives out random in class assigment, and you don't know if you did not go in person. And this class teach stuff thats rally easy, bascilly high school stuff nothing is new, but somehow attdency is important, and no phone. NOT recommend, do not ever select this teacher.

This professor is great. She is very clear in her lectures and doesn't make you feel stupid for asking a question or to go over something again. She is very understanding and kind. The tests and quizzes are straightforward and similar to the examples given in class. You will do good in the class as long as you keep up and know trig pretty well.
One of the best professors I have ever had.

This woman deserves a raise! One of the best I have had here. I wish she could teach everything. She explains things in a way that makes complicated concepts easy. This class is easy to overthink but once you get passed that it isn't bad. Dr. Smith answers emails quickly and has effective office hours. She also cares about you understanding.

Dr. Smith is an amazing professor. She made statics simple and easy to understand. Class was structured mainly around solving practice problems. Homework was usually a single problem similar to class. Overall easy and manageable workload with an encouraging, kind prof. One of my favorites so far. Would recommend to everyone

Smith is probably one of the best teachers in the ME department. Statics is still tough but she can teach is so good that you won't want to die inside in her class. She is a bit picky on how you write final answers but it is very manageable. She only curved 1 test  but the other averages were good enough to not need one if you needed any more proof
This professor was excellent. She provided great feedback and was very easy to learn from. Made sure you were prepared for the tests, and was very accessible outside of class. 11/10 would recommend.

Dr Smith is great. I had her for both MEGR 1100 and MEGR 2141. She was my second attempt at statics and that was a huge benefit to me as she made the content so much easier for me to understand. She is very caring and helps you achieve the best grade possible if you attend her office hours. My only gripe is that she didn't round my 79.0 up to a B.

Dr. Smith is a really great professor.  She makes it very clear how to succeed in her class and does a lot to help her students both in and outside of class.  Every problem in class was thoroughly discussed, test and quiz material was all prefaced beforehand, and graded feedback was really good, overall a great professor for statics.

Overall great professor. 1100 is kind of a Frankenstein of a class with random but useful concepts stitched together, but Dr. Smith does a awesome job covering the variety of topics. I personally appreciate how the class period before every test was solely a unit review, which helped me a lot to do well on each unit test.

Does a great job explaining topics while making the class fun. I would take this class any day over chem 1251. A great class to get you into the foundations of engineering with a great professor. There was also no homework I think ever for this class. Just go to class.
