Here is your best advice: take this class online during the summer with her! All you need to do is read the textbook and sorta listen to her lectures. Really just pay attention to the stuff in her lectures that aren't in the textbook. Such an easy A. Make sure you do every packback and the quizzes. Quizzes are easy if you spend 20 min studying.

I have taken Mrs Gaultney for both research methods and senior seminar. Many say her canvas is unorganized, but give her the benefit of the doubt as she's older and is retiring soon. She is extremely knowledgeable about psychology and has done a lot of research on sleep. Her classes are fairly easy as long as you attend the lectures and read.

This class is as writing intensive as it gets. You will be writing a lot, conducting your own research, and basically writing your own journal article. Gaultney was sweet, but her Canvas is unorganized and confusing. The weekly assignments get confusing too but she does not grade them harshly. Attendance is graded and be prepared to use statistics!

The class itself is easy and it is nice that there isn't weekly homework. The only things that are graded are the exams and a few simple assignments. But the Powerpoints are horrendous. Going through the slides is a must, but they are often 80 slides with a 1-2 minute audio on each one. And she speaks so slowly and monotone. Would not recommend.

she had a rude tone every time I emailed her, and also CHANGED the syllabus in the MIDDLE of the semester. she had an "extra credit cap" for the course (odd). I missed ONE critical thinking question and many others missed the same one, but DIDN'T let us redo it, even though the syllabus implied she'd give us an extension.

Even though I got an A in the class I think that some of her policies were annoying. I did all the extra credit assignments and she took away 7 of my extra credit points because she said I reached the limit. Overall, if you just read the textbook and do the practice quizzes you should be fine on the exams.

While the class is kind of assignment heavy, if you put in the time, utilize the study guides, the extra credit assignments, and the unlimited quiz attempts, you'll do great. She gave me so many resources to build on and I honestly could've gotten an A if I didn't slack. She's great!! :)

I took this class fully online, and as long as you keep up with the weekly chapter readings, it is easy to do well on the exams. There are many extra credit opportunities, and she drops your lowest exam score. She is very understanding and kind. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

Amazing prof all around! Caring & knowledgeable. Enough extra credit to bump up a grade. Studying is a must. Study guides were not helpful, they were just the lectures in question form. My advice: handwrite all the lectures & study those for exams. Dr Levens is willing to listen and adjusts her approaches so material is easier to understand.

She is so scatterbrained it makes it impossible to follow along and learn in class lectures, where she reads off slides. Exams are hard, so much memorization,33 page study guides when fully answered. Yes there is lots of extra credit but your only allowed so much at the end. If you have to take the class fine but take time and prepare to study.

I have both taken and been a TA for Levens's B&B class, and Levens is great. There is no reason for you not to get an A; she offers up to 30 points extra credit, drops your lowest exam and your lowest writing assignment, and the TAs always hold in-person review sessions for upcoming exams. She is a tad scatterbrained, but brilliant and kind.

Dr. Levens is a great professor.  I took her course over the summer and am just finishing TA'ing for it.  She grades tough and the material is hard but she really does try her best to make it approachable to students.  Take her class over any of the other professors for B&B, and being her TA was a pleasure.  I would take her course again.
Overall this class gets a bad wrap, you just need to study for it.  Its a lot of information, come to class!

She is extremely intelligent, but I think she has a lot of stressful things going on in her personal life. She stumbles around her words a lot and it makes it a bit difficult to grasp important bits during lectures, but I know she is doing the best she can. I wish nothing but the best for her & her family. I think she should move to online courses!

Felt much more challenging than a 2000-level course. Dr. Levens is super passionate, intelligent, and kind. Unfortunately, teaching complex material is not her calling. I recommend relying on your textbook if you take this class. Her lectures are confusing and boring. Tests are memorization-heavy. Don't skip out on the reading like I did!!

Don't take this class. It is completely unproductive and unmotivating. She assigns everything at the last minute including the Final Portfolio which is approximately 12-20 pages long and only gave my class a week to complete it. She is unreasonable and all over the place. Half of the time she rants about stuff that is not pertaining to class. RUN.

Sara always forgets to prepare for class and needs reminders to turn in assignments. The course requires reading empirical articles, writing response papers (which are important for grading), and making social media posts, all due the next day. It's stressful to rely on her to turn in the assignments on time, which can make learning frustrating

Unprepared for class. Unclear instructions. Tends to ramble and sidetracked. Required to read 2 empirical articles, write response papers, comment, and do separate assignments. Due by the next day. Assignments took 6 hrs. Lacks understanding & compassion. Prefers quantity over quality. High expectations of students but does not meet them herself.

PSYC2113 is a hard course but Dr. Levens is a great professors. She is very knowledgeable and explains complex topics in a simple way. She also gives lots of extra credit. Class is very straight forward so long as you read the textbook, watch her lectures, take the quizzes, and study for the tests.

This class is hard and so are the tests. Dr. Levens gives study guides and tries to accommodate people if an emergency pops up. Do the extra credit it will boost your grade a lot. While the class is hard I recommend taking Dr. Levens for this class if possible.

An all-around wonderful professor! Her lectures are clear and understandable. She makes an effort to make the content as relevant as possible and takes time to explain. Very kind. Gives study guides and lots of assignments, but drops the lowest scores

Amazing professor. She is extremely helpful and responsive. Her lectures are very interesting and she always makes them relevant to our lives. Tough tests but she gives study guides that if you study really help. She also gives a lot of extra credit.

She is an incredible professor- her lectures are extremely organized and help so much for the tests. If you go to class everyday and stay up to date on assignments you are guaranteed to pass. She is very helpful and responds to emails in less than a week. She won't baby the class and can be a harsh grader, but it genuinely helped me to grow.

Her tests were extremely hard and the study guides were 40-50 page google docs, some of the information or topics not even being on the test. We met once a week and would often go off topic in class. You have to try extremely hard to get an A and I just barely made enough credit on the final to pull through. First exam average was like a 50%

I had a class with her for PSYC 2113, we would only meet once a week, and even then, she would cancel classes often. Her study guides would be 3 pages or even longer, but many would still fail the test. She seems nice, and when we did have lectures, I would enjoy them and learn many facts, but overall, I would not ever take a class with her again.

Dr. Berzins is a lovely woman. Her class however was one of the most dreadful ones i've had. We only had it once a week and most weeks she would cancel. The test material didn't match with the lecture most of the time, not to mention they're worth 60% of your grade. Plan on studying for days on end if you want to pass. You do get test cheat sheets!

She was okay. She seemed like she didn't care much for my class. The class was very independent. Many people in my class barely passed. She assigned weekly quizzes that you had to read 1 or 2 chapters for. The textbook is very hard to understand, which is what most of your teaching comes from bc she hardly lectures. She did give exam study guides.

I took Dr.Berzins for 2113 as well, and both classes were extremely hard, but she is so supportive and genuinely wants nothing more than for her students to succeed. she went above and beyond helping me in both classes throughout the semester. she gives insane extra credit opportunities throughout the whole course too!!

This class is difficult and requires a lot of reading, but she gives you lots opportunities to earn points outside of tests. We were allowed to take cheat sheets to the last 2 exams, and she creates exhaustive study guides for each test that the whole class can fill-out together. If you take brain/behavior with her you will pass.

Dr.Berzins did a fantastic job of setting the class up for success. If you read the assigned reading and stay on top of this class she takes a really difficult subject and makes it really easy. Lots of chances for extra credit and the materials were easy to follow.

This is for both Social Psych + Brain and behavior Pysch. Overall, I wouldn't recommend her at all. Her lecture style is unpleasant. Her lecture slides consist of some words and rambles for a few minutes so you don't know what's important and what's not. She wasn't there as often as she could have, Her exams are HARD, class averaging barely a 70.

Most stressful class I had, not only weekly homework, "weeklies"  and assignment's for a 20+ page literary review, then random days where we sometimes learned stuff, her teaching style wasn't for me. If you do the work on time then you will do fine but you definitely have to try and put in the work. no tests or quizzes tho. Final is open note.

She was kind and offered many extra credit opportunities. However, her lectures didn't match up to the content she wanted us to learn, neither of which  fully matched up to the study guides (often ~40 pages long), and all of which didn't match up to the exams. The assignments give a good background but aren't very useful.
Awful, terrible, how could she... (she overcomplicates everything and it honestly doesn't help at all). We all bombed the first test.

Class was once a week and she was never there. She lectures well if you forget about the content on the tests. Everything taught in class is not reflected on the tests. This class isn't hard because of the content its hard because of the lack of continuity between test and coursework. Take this class with someone else.

I found the lectures to be interesting as she's straight forward in explaining the content, and she's very clear about her expectations in general. She provides a study guide before each exam that I found very helpful. Overall I'd recommend because you can tell she really cares about what she's teaching.

Favorite professor I've ever had. She's incredibly clear about what she expects from her students, and she inspired me to seek a career in a similar field. She posts every slide on Canvas, is prompt with responding to emails, and gives very cohesive study guides before tests. If you do the reading and take notes, you'll be fine.

Very lecture heavy. You have to go to class to get a good grade. 4 exams, no final, weekly hw on the readings, occasional journal prompt hw. You have to read a lot in the hw. Her tests are very hard, class avg is a C. She does provide a study guide w/ feedback, but you have to study a lot to get a A or B on the tests. Take 2130 with someone else.

Overall a fine course, the material just gets really similar and hard to differentiate apart from other "theories" and definitions. Berzins lectures fine, but is slightly disorganized and often goes off the powerpoint to the point where she's going back and forth between 20 slides. Attendance is not required, however, you gain points going to class

Despite being a nice person, Berzins is not a good professor. She was absent every other week, and barely taught anything during her lectures. Tests are bad measures of what we learn in the week, and her TAs are incompetent. I have gotten all A's in every other class, I spend over 25 hours studying for tests in this class and still do poorly.

Dr. Berzins is a nice woman but I think she's a little overwhelmed and too busy to be a professor. She comes to class sick and unmotivated to teach. Her teaching style is talking and making us do activities that are useless because it's only like one question about the activity that took almost all of class. I regret taking her for TWO classes :(

This professors classes were one face to face and one asynchronous class. I signed up for this class because I wanted to take it in person and believed it was the best option. Though, we only met in person and actually had a lecture twice six weeks in. I think she is a brilliant person, but seemed busy with other more important things than class.

Objectively, her tests are a not good measure of the way these social psychology concepts are taught/exist. The questions are often ambiguous, she doesn't allow you to ask any questions so "she is impartial" which I think is silly. If majority of the class gets specific questions wrong, it is illogical to attribute to the students' misunderstanding

This class is hard, but Dr. Berzins did a phenomenal job preparing us for it. She made sure we had plenty of time to prepare for the literature review paper. She set a timeline through the semester, requiring us to finish an outline and 2 drafts for a grade. There are extra credit opportunities for the paper and exam. Plenty of resources. Take her!

The class is hard but Dr. Berzins makes sure that her students are prepared to succeed. Provided detailed study guides and was always accessible via email or through office hours. You NEED to do the readings and study for exams, or else you will struggle. If you want to pass brain & behavior, take it with Dr. Berzins.

Great lectures and provided countless opportunities for grades other than exams. Provided study guides that she helped fill out if the class struggled with certain concepts. She is clearly extremely passionate about what she teaches which makes lectures fun. Super accessible outside of class and very respectful! Highly recommend any of her classes.

I loved Dr. Berzins class. The material is challenging but she does a great job explaining it. You MUST study for exams but other grades are provided for some cushion. You will do good just GO TO CLASS and try your best. She is very understanding so ask questions and use TA's.
I couldn't rate her for social psychology for some reason but that is what I took.  The content was difficult but she was great at explaining the content and is extremely knowledgeable in the field.

Dr. Berzins is a new professor and I loved her class. This course in challenging in general and she did a great job making it easier to understand. You will cover a lot of material, be prepared to and and take advantage of TA's and tutoring center. She by far seems like this best option for this course. STUDY for Exams

I enjoyed this class. I'm not good with anything about the brain, so I did find tests very hard even though I studied. He drops your lowest test grade, including the final, which is great. He does random polls everywhere for an attendance grade and drops your lowest five. Lectures weren't boring, and I didn't mind the class at all. I recommend him!

Good teacher really enjoyed his class. Tests aren't hard as long as you study enough. Gives extra credit. Knows what he's talking about and lectures aren't boring. Lets you out of class early some days.

I took this class for credit as an elective but had a fun time during his classes. His lectures were enjoyable and took attendance by using PollEverywhere which also made it engaging. Chill, Friendly, Understanding person. Answers his emails fairly quickly. I recommend!

McMains is an awesome professor! I found his test to be very straight forward as long as you take notes and actually come to class which is simple! He gave very interesting lectures that made coming to class worth it and spoke about personal experiences as well. He's a very welcoming professor and was funny. His study guides were also the best.

The material was relatively hard, unless you have some biology background. Dr. McMains is very knowledgable about the material he teaches, easy to access outside of class, and will gladly answer questions. He has study guides for 5 total exams which are great to use to follow along during his lectures. Other workload done via Revel.

Professor McMains made taking this class so bearable. He uses slides to give all the information needed for his tests, and his lectures are very engaging. He also gives out the test study guides right after the previous test, so you have them while you are learning this material. I highly recommend taking his psych class; he is a great professor.

Dr. Mcmains is a great professor and is very knowledgable in the field of Psychology. I am not sure if this is a course thing, or just what he does as a professor... but this course is extremely exam heavy. Exams count for the majority of your grade. If you are a bad exam taker, I would not recommend this class. They are very hard tests.

This was a class that required studying, but he was an amazing professor. He clearly knows and loves psychology. He sends out "Study Guides", but they are just topics that will be on the exam, so you should know how to describe all of them. The tests are not easy, but they are simple. They are also each 60 questions. He drops 4 attendance grades.

I did drop his class since it wasn't the best fit for me. Even with this happening, he was super accommodating and caring for my situation going above and beyond recommending new classes I could take even from other professors. Absolute amazing guy I would highly recommend taking his classes. Even friends say he's amazing to work with.

he is a good teacher. Make sure to study everything on the slides and you should be good for the tests. U have to do a mini assignment before every chapter but it is easy and u can work ur way up to 100. The 2 journal assignments r also easy. Study in advance for the tests. the second sentence will be the key to ur success. He does drop 1 exam.

He is truly one of the best professors I have ever had. He is passionate about psychology and engages the class in fun activities and questions which helped me to truly understand the materials. I recommend him.

My favorite lecture professor by far. His lectures are great and he includes amazing explanations to all the information needed. Additionally, he tells you exactly whats going to be on the exams. The exams are difficult, but your grade doesn't heavily rely on them. Extra credit is offered along with plenty of time to get all your work done.

I took Dr. McMains for PSYC 1101 my freshman year. Dr. McMains has engaging lectures and a good sense of humor. Tests are the majority of your grade, but as long as you go to class and study, you'll be fine! Highly recommend this course and especially Dr. McMains!

I loved this class, harder material but the way he teaches forces you to pay attention. miss classes you WILL fall behind-the slides only show the vocab not the definition so you cant go back if you miss something he says. Study guides literally show exactly what will be on the exam, exams are fairly easy if you study. Absolutely recommend.

I did not care for this class. I am an A-B student and I found his test very difficult. They are very wordy and hard to understand. The test are a major weight to your grade, however the lowest test grade is dropped. Only one homework assignment a week, but it can be hard. I enjoyed most of his lectures, just be prepared for difficult test.

Great guy! Clearly knowledgeable. Tests are hard but not difficult as long as you know the material. Easy A if you put in a proportionate amount of work to the three credits. (For me, like 2-3 hrs/week). Just go to class and take notes and you'll be fine. He posts the exam study guides way in advance (usually like 2-2.5 weeks). Would take him again
Makes the lectures fun and entertaining. Easy at least A or B if you do the work and listen to him. Best professor I have had at Charlotte.

One of my favorite professors in the dept. Very organized lectures/slides, I truly looked forward to going to class. Fast pace and the material is dense but, McMains is sensitive to more difficult topics and doesn't "fly through". Very responsive and also publishes a study guide for the exam so you know what to expect. Heavily recommend him.

He makes it very easy to get a good grade. His lectures are very interesting and enjoyable. Although attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, there is participation graded in class, but you'll find yourself looking forward to class. He gives study guides before the tests which make it very easy to study what's on the test and get a good grade.

Despite the dense material, he is excellent at explaining abstract and difficult concepts and making them relatable and interesting. Attendance is not mandatory, but lectures are very worthwhile and you will fall behind if you miss them. It is mostly based on a few exams, but he gives a study guide for each.
His lectures are fun and interactive. He is really sweet and understanding, you can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching.

Dr. Gadaire is passionate and well-versed in his subject, and he provided me with valuable information for opportunities when I expressed an interest in this subject. Be ready to understand your material entirely and apply it to scenarios in and outside of class. This class is easy and Dr. Gadaire is approachable when experiencing difficulties.

Professor Gadaire himself is a really good professor who is incredibly kind and caring. However most of the actual work in the class was just textbook assignments that felt very much like busy work to me. The tests were not extremely hard but you definitely have to study. Overall a good experience.

This professor cares a lot, it seems. He just has no control over the classroom. Many classes were drowned out by people talking over him. If he gained a bit more control over the room, I think he would be an excellent professor. Be ready to read because there are 2 chapters per week, usually. But the actual tests aren't too hard.

He's honestly a 3.7, but the class was a lot.  Attendance is taken every day through polls. You have to read an entire assigned chapter reading or two in just a week, with graded questions. He also did not mention, nor did the syllabus, until the day before exam 1, that exams are multiple choice, 3 short essays, AND fill-in-the-blank.

We had lab homework every week and a semester long project as the final. I always recieved minor points off of all the labs (always 9.6 or 9.8 out of 10 points) and I would have to ask him in class why I recieved that grade. Overall, understanding professor and attendence was not graded but you will not pass without attending.

Dr. Gadaire very clearly cared about doing his best for his students. The material itself was difficult to learn but actually coming to class really helped me grasp the concepts. He made things fun when in class and helped us when we needed it. If I could take another one of his classes I 100% would.

I really liked this class as Dr. Ravyts as a professor. The tests are literally just the lecture slides so as long as you attend and take notes, you will pass. One paper and one group assignment, pretty slight class and he grades well.

The class is based around conducting a research project, which can be stressful to cram into one semester. However, Dr. Ravyts is a relatively generous grader and makes sure everyone understands the concepts. Be aware that the coursework is concentrated towards the end of the semester.

Dr. Ravyts is such a great professor and would recommend him to anyone. pretty lecture heavy class but his exams are simple and straightforward. You must take 3 out of the 4 exams given and the lowest grade gets dropped! No assignments other than a group debate and 3 pg paper towards the end of this semester. Loved this class and def recommend!
Very lecture heavy class, graded on 3 tests, a paper and a debate. However, tests were easy if you listened to the lecture. Ravyts was super kind and had interesting lectures.

Dr. Ravyts is a good professor and taught a really interesting class. Grades do depend on 3 tests, but if you attend class, take notes, and study you will be fine. The class isn't very difficult. I enjoyed his class a lot and would take another one from him again

Professor Ravyts was a really nice guy! My only complaint is that the majority of your grade depends on the three exams, and sometimes they consist of topics that weren't in the study guide. Besides that, it was a pretty easy class if you made sure to either pay attention to the lectures or review the slides afterward.

She's a good professor who obviously cares but her course lacks structure. Theres often no feedback on assignments, no clear grading criteria or lectures at all. The lecture part was nice, we would often just talk of real world issues in the class which was refreshing but it's juts stressful not having grades in until the end of the semester.

Mary is a great professor. She tailors her courses in a way that promotes real learning and understanding as well as a school-life balance. I've had her for two classes now, and she never gives her students more than they can handle. She's also very quick to respond to emails. She's kind of a slow grader, but she cares deeply about what she does.

there are a ton of assignments in this class, 5 exams and two final projects towards the end. Super sweet teacher but you just need to make sure you pay attention in her class you have to be dedicated in this course to learn everything! I would take her again

Dr. McKenzie is a passionate professor who fosters engaging class discussions. While grading can be slow, the class is manageable with active participation. unstuck study was a helpful study tool alongside the readings.

Really good professor teaching an interesting subject she is obviously passionate about. Class periods were all about free discussion of topics both presented in the material covered that week and in the news that related to it. The only drag was that grading was pretty slow for the big project we did all semester.
Good professor, only bad thing is she uses the lockdown browser.

Hybrid course. Dr. McKenzie is clearly passionate about her work but spends most of the lecture talking about her own experiences and beliefs, most of which rarely touch the topics in the textbook. Doesn't take attendance and you basically teach yourself at home. HUGE writing assignments and classwork assignments (which you can also do on your own)

He is a good teacher that really cares about what he does. He is super down to earth and genuinly a good person. His class is very reading heavy, but the books are on real life issues that are very informative and not a pain to read.

I participated in Prof Fitzgerald's study abroad program. He gives students space to contextualize and research ideas. He provides insight and feedback when needed to help guide students toward a clearer understanding. He is a wonderful and challenging professor

very harsh and subjective grader, which can be tough since his attendance assignments are a 5-minute time to handwrite an in-depth response to a basic and simple question from 7-9 chapters of a book, and half his tests are free-response. tests include sporadic content from videos to books to lectures. use his  extra credit to your advantage!

Pay attention in class, show up. The tests are based on the lectures and this makes it easier to succeed. This is a very lecture heavy class, sometimes he can get confusing but will reword if you ask him too. There was also many opportunities for extra credit! Very reading heavy class as well, pop quizzes on the readings as well. Make sure you read

I genuinely did not like this class at all. The exams barely covered the lectures and you had to study very hard and study extra material. You had to find everything through modules and I wish he put an assignment tabs. The amount of work you had to put into the assignments were definitely worth more than 5 points. Did not like this class at all.

Loved this class! I learned a lot through the lectures, discussions, and reading materials. Professor Fitzgerald explained the material perfectly and was very flexible when asked to change something, even if it was projects, reading, discussions, etc. The TAs were extremely nice as well. Very clear grading criteria. Get ready to read.

While Dr. Fitzgerald is very smart and passionate, he is a researcher, not a professor. He assigns an unreasonable amount of reading that are overall unneeded for what we are doing in class. He also believes that everyone in his class will be getting a graduate degree in sociology and that's the only valid path post undergrad, which is unhelpful.

Great professor, always made sure to keep the class engaged and was very open to just about any feedback. Might be a little difficult to get used to the readings, but I personally found them to be really interesting.

Professor Fitzgerald is a great professor. He is so understanding but does have pop quizzes on the reading. The test are fairly easy if you understand the material. He gives good lectures but sometimes he rambles on so it can get a bit confusing

Dr. Fitzgerald is overall a good professor. Three books are given throughout the semester and pop quizzes follow every reading. His lectures can be confusing and he does get slightly flustered with some questions. He gives several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester and is open to feedback. Put in a little effort and you will be fine

Very caring, really loved him as a person. Clear and fair grading, and also very open to feedback and criticism. Lots of reading, 3 books over the semester, but I enjoyed them for the most part. Sometimes, his lectures can get overwhelming; he tends to be a bit erratic when covering multiple topics. Overall easy A if you do the work and readings.

Dr. Fitzgerald has an inflated ego and assigns so much reading for no reason, and the books he assigns aren't engaging and are hard to follow. He's very intelligent, but he's hard to keep up with in lectures because he touches on five different topics in one minute. Do not take this class if you don't absolutely love sociology, you will hate it.
You'll do good if you do the reading. Love his teaching and would take another class with him!!

I like Dr. Fitzgerald as a person, but didn't care for his class too much. Ethics was not interesting to me, so it was hard to pay attention in class, especially since his lectures were very talkative. I would only take his class if it were a class that I was very interested in and passionate about.

I loved prof Fitz. He made class fun & really directed the course for his students. He'll change things if they don't work for his class. No textbooks, but required regular books (like $10 each, we had 3) I would recommend him and 2211 to everyone I know because he's the embodiment of what a great teacher looks like. Really cares about his students

Dr. Fitzgerald is one of the best professors I've ever had. As long as you complete the assignments on time, you'll have no problem getting a good grade in his class. He is also very open to meeting outside of class and provides meaningful feedback when it comes to essays and writing assignments!

Dr. Stearns was great- the class had clear grading, easy to make an A; only reason I've left off a single star is the TA. When I took 1511, the TA accused students of AI use on a few assignments after claiming to have left the country for good, evading backlash and throwing the situation on the new TA. Would take again.

Stearns was great. The class was light. Attendance/participation made up most grades other than the final group project. Lectures were interesting if you actually care about the subject. Just show up to class, participate, do the readings and you'll be good.
She's excellent, fav professor of the semester. Her class was an easy A and she just yaps but shes really funny.

I personally felt like the class was all over the place. There was NO proper structure whatsoever & she spoke in circles, often contradicting herself. It wasn't bad overall but I just didn't fancy her as a professor and HATED the group work we had to do (groups were assigned randomly). I constantly asked myself: "What even is this class?"
Very manageable class… easy grader

Dr. Stearns is also an enjoyable person to talk to and learn from! This class is easy and revolves around a semester long project in which you will present at the end of the sem. My advice is to show up to class (she does allow up to 5 absences), do the assigned reading, and make sure all of your work is turned in on time. I would take her again!
Easy class to get an A in. Show up and do the reading. Only tests were on Fridays, and related to the readings.

Great professor! I have never taken a sociology course but she made it very interesting. Not many assignments so if you show up and complete the work you should pass with an easy A. Friday group sessions are extremely easy too.

Dr. Stearns was a very nice and understanding professor. All she asked was to come to class and complete what little work was assigned. You have 4 free skips in this class. The main assignment was a group project that she gives 5 weeks to complete. Easy class if you are needing a themes course.
I can't imagine anyone having a problem with Dr. Stearns. She was clear about her policies, and it's impossible not to get an A if you attend class—possibly the easiest class I'll take here.
This professor is very nice and her class is overall easy. There are very few assignments throughout the semester and one group project at the end rather than a final.

She is probably the best professor at the school her classes are interesting and the class is based on a final project so that means there isn't a final exam in the class. also one of the easiest classes at the university.
The class is overall one of the easiest courses in UNC Charlotte. It is surrounded a main project. I recommend not to skip class attendance is crucial. She is a great professor!!
Amazing class, get ready to do group work. Will definitely take this class again

Did NOT enjoy this course. Great lectures, annoying semester-long projects instead of tests. Grading/feedback was slow & sparse. She lectured Mondays/Wednesdays and her TA led Friday sessions. Friday sessions were project-centered and the worst part. There was disorganization and miscommunication b/w the Professor & TA bc it was just too chaotic.
Overall just boring
she's the best!

I took him a few semesters ago, and my GPA is still hurting. All tests have questions about the book we have to read outside of class. He NEVER goes over content from the book in class, and if you ask him about the book, he doesn't directly answer your question. There are also pop-up group activities in class. He is very passive-aggressive as well.

Dr. Overton was very kind, he tried to help, but the effort fell very flat. His lectures were engaging but heavy, and there was so much he wanted you to remember from what he said but it was too much to write down. There were no examples for assignments so it was hard to judge what he wanted. The quizzes were lengthy; we needed more time.
Cares about his students. He moves very quickly through content, but he is receptive to feedback so make sure you vocalize any concerns you may have. Mandatory group projects.

Lecture heavy, and he's fast. Can be hard to get info he says that isn't on the slide. He doesn't tell you when there will be in class assignments, even tho attendance isn't taken. He expects you to read the textbook, but he does put study guides up on Canvas. Only two exams: midterm and final. Had a hard time reading the textbook for this class.

Gives tests solely based on his study guides, so just do those and you'll be fine. You have to be an extremely fast notetaker, which makes his lectures feel a bit overwhelming at first, but he's very friendly and sets you up with everything you need to succeed in his class as long as you pay attention.

You gotta learn how to be a fast note-taker to succeed here. He gives a study guide for the tests and the tests are very similar to them, but you have to come to class and take notes off what he says, he doesn't put a lot of info on the slides and a lot is just said verbally. Otherwise, he tries to be funny and goofy and he's an interesting dude.
Interesting lectures. Tests are easy if you do the study guides. He lets the last exam be optional and lets you replace your lowest test grade with it.

I really enjoyed this class even though it wasn't exactly what I thought I was going to be learning about. I took SOCY1511. If you had a question he was able to make a clear understanding for you. He gave feedback on short answers on tests. Attendance isn't mandatory but it is important for you to pass the class and to do well on the tests.

I took SOCY-1511. Attendance isn't mandatory, but go to class because he discusses points on the slides that probably won't make sense otherwise. If you participate in class he'll appreciate it a lot! Very open to help if you don't understand a concept.

SOCY 1511

Professor Overton did a great job. He's a fast lecturer but does a great job contextualizing the material. Tests are huge in the class but he provides relevant study materials and goes over the material in the week leading up to the test. He does a great job making the course valuable but "easy".

One of the best professors I have ever had! His assignments are very easy and all he really cares about is participation and attendance. He has very engaging and interesting lectures and the assignments pair perfectly. Grading is based off of attendance and class assignments. I definitely recommend taking Dr. Overton!
He was a great professor. Very laidback and easy to talk to. Don't talk over him during class. Group activities and projects were fun and actually taught me something.
The workload's no easy-A. But the guy offers pretty reasonabl ways to recover your grade. Classes are fairly interactive. I always found him eager to offer help. Friendly and approachable too.

At first, we had a few pop quizzes on the chapters at the beginning, but eventually, we just stopped doing them. He makes class fun when doing his presentations by giving group activities that are graded based on participation (sometimes even extra credit is given). Helpful when asked questions and is just a nice guy.

Love her. You can tell she truly loves teaching and Socy. Lectures can be a little tough to follow but she always asks if everyone understands before moving on. Super fair grader and admits when she makes a mistake. She insists on teaching "life skills" more than material. We did a lot of work with excel. Weekly assessments but she helps if needed

The entire semester is spent preparing a mock research proposal, each week is a different section before you finally put everything together at the end. Very easy grader, late points aren't going to hurt you as long as you put in genuine effort. You'll also present about 4 times to your group instead of the entire class.
quantitative. She made sure that we understood the material before moving on.  Many teachers move on regardless of whether i get it.  I finally feel like I understand statistics.
She was an amazing teacher and graded fairly. She is understanding if you need help or can not make class. She tries to be very interactive with her students and is well respected.

For quant analysis. Literally just STAT so it was really easy, but not a lot of people knew what was going on and I think if you did poorly in stats you wouldn't understand this material, and her teaching style wasn't effective. Between that and her constant canceling of class, we were always behind and the syllabus changed. Fair grader though.

I took SOCY1501 , but I didn't see that here. I'd give a 3.5 if I could, Ms. Walker is a completely fine teacher. She assigns one short paper a week (even on break week) and a long one after each unit, so be prepared for those. Class is otherwise pretty easy and didn't really engage me personally, but if you like sociology she's definitely good.
The class was very easy. This class was pretty much movies, one big presentation, and small debates. Some homework/project can have unclear instructions which made everyone confused.

Took this class fully online but I could tell Dr. Y cares about her students. Not too many assignments, just quizzes each week based on the readings/videos. Some papers which were very simple, and some exams based entirely on course concepts. Overall an extremely interesting class that was easy to pass. Definitely take if you have the chance.

super great professor, she's really sweet and responds to emails super fast. There were quizzes, 3 papers and 2 exams in this course but I found it to be super interesting. You do need to pay attention though since you're graded by so little assignment wise. Would 100% take her again

Dr. Yavorsky is very understanding. There is one book you get to choose from a list she has to do your paper on. I suggest getting a head start before classes start if you want to get a head start. There is also readings for each class so read at least two days before going to class.

Dr. Yavorsky has easily been my favorite professor I've taken at Charlotte thusfar. She's incredibly caring and respected, and is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject that she teaches. Her class is pretty difficult given that it's a level 4000 class, but Dr. Yavorsky is incredibly communicative and wants to see you succeed.

I can't stand this class. There are so many things that bother me with this course. Dr. Y gives you around 3-4 articles to read (most are at least 10 pages, not even kidding), a TED talk or documentary to watch, and a slideshow with notes. It's just too much, especially considering most of us are taking 5 classes. Read the textbook or else u fail.

I absolutely loved this class!! I am a biology student so this was my first time taking a sociology class at uncc and I loved it! She was so respectful and understanding some topics could be triggering or heavy and she did an amazing job in having a very comforting space for students. if you make sure to keep up with deadlines, its an easy A!
Dr. Jason is a very nice woman but is tough. She gives feedback on assignments but doesn't always make it super clear what she wants you to do.

Amazing professor, I have her for 3155 & 4112 and I enjoy her classes so much. She has a way of making the work come alive, never have i been so engaged and I have ADHD and a very short attention span. The class consists of lots of readings, but most are fairly short, you must read before class. We have pop up quizzes which are not bad. she cares!

She is one of my favorite professors I have had here - the discussions are fun! The hardest part of the course is preparing for pop quizzes and the papers. She is very helpful and cares, but if you do not read and prepare before class, the pop quizzes may affect your grade - though they are easy. I would happily take her course again!!

Kronberg is both a nice and informative professor. She has really good lectures, and explains topics very clearly; she definitely knows the material. If you watch the lectures and go to class, you will succeed very easily. Graded on: open-note prep. checks, labs, mid-term, and final exam. She responds to emails quickly and provides good feedback.

Dr. Kronberg is awesome. Passionate about the subject and clearly cares for her students. Pop quizzes and papers are sometimes difficult, but she is always willing to help and is accessible outside of class. I learned a lot not just about sociology, but what to do with my life after college as well. Take her if you can!
no. not cool. she's a lazy professor and makes you spend time doing her job outside of class.
The best professor ever! Super nice and if you attend class you will have no problem getting a good grade.

This teacher is amazing. All the lectures are interesting! Time flies in her class because she is really passionate about what she's teaching. She makes you want to actually participate in discussions even if you don't think you know the answer. All of the labs are simple and she goes over them in detail before they are due. 10/10 will take again.

Dr. Kronberg was the best teacher I have had in my entire academic career. She is extremely caring and engages with the class and allows class-wide discussions. I cannot recommend taking her classes enough and engaging with her. 10/10 love Professor Kronberg!

Professor Kronberg is so intelligent and is very open to help in any areas you feel like you might be lacking.
Pretty straight forward, just do the assignments and pay attention in class.

The small group discussions are sometimes awkward and confusing but the lectures are good and the notes are awesome. Her method is a flipped classroom so most of your work will be done outside of class.

Had her for American Democracy, Attendance is graded but if you miss a few classes you're good, quizzes on lecture every other week. Literally just take notes on the stuff in class and study it for a couple minutes day-of and you'll be fine. Easy Class!
Don't take her.
Difficult grader, assignments aren't clear, no structure, surprised I finished with an A.

She requires you to purchase a book that has nothing to do with our capstone project & spends her lecture times talking about irrelevant topics or her personal views. She is all over the place when she talks and will not directly answer your question. Her instructions are never clear and I could go about her. AVOID taking it with her at all costs!

I feel like if this class was in person it would have been better. She admits not liking the online format, and it made some classes difficult when she wanted discussion but no one would have their camera on. Her assignments are difficult to understand at first, but if you want help she is willing to further explain.

She doesn't do a very good job of explaining her assignments and she is kind of inconsistent with grading, but her assignments are never hard. Most of class was spent with her just talking about random stuff and you don't learn much but it is an easy A. She is a very nice professor though and does care about the class. I would take her again.
Dr. Potochnick is really well versed in her area and is truly interested in what she does. She is clear in her expectations and is very understanding. I highly recommend her!
Best professor ever! She really knows what shes doing! I would take her for another class!

This teacher is very strict and assigns insane amounts of work for a general ed class. She assigns a lot of readings for quizzes that make no sense. Attendance is mandatory, and you can not be late. She won't let you even go to the bathroom during class and makes you keep your phone and computer in your backpack. Do not take her unless you must.
do not take any of her classes, such a harsh grader, lectures make zero sense and very participation heavy with speaking in front of the class. also doesn't grade until end of semester

There were extensive reading assignments each week, sometimes an entire text of 40 pages but no less than 15. While I didn't mind the reading itself, the assessments felt mismatched. Dr. Flint gives different readings every week that are ~9 pages long and they are very boring. There are some pop quizzes every now and then, so it's better if you show up to class. There is also group work and study groups that meet on certain days. Overall, it's harder to fail than it is to pass, but I personally strongly disliked the class.

Not a very good teacher, her lectures were boring and confusing, if you miss one reading you are screwed. Readings are super lengthy and boring, her quizzes were confusing and if you didnt read the reading intensely the questions wont make sense

More difficult and time-consuming than my regular classes. Boring lectures and 40+ page readings given every week with occasional random quizzes that were difficult to do well on. Slides were never uploaded to Canvas despite grading us on our class notes. Weekly breakout sessions on Fridays that didn't help much. Wouldn't recommend to anyone ever.

The class was quite boring and the professor taught mainly from PowerPoints that were not uploaded to Canvas. She requires her students to take in-class notes in groups which are then later graded. LOTS of outside reading and pop quizzes this professor also uses packback weekly. I would not recommend it but it's not overly hard.

Overall I learned some really interesting things in this class HOWEVER, this is extremely heavy on readings (20-40 pages) for 5 question pop quizzes. She also doesn't believe in making incorrect answer choices so all the choices could be right but only one is actually right, these were my down fall. Weekly breakout sessions.

I had to take this as a freshman intro class, and it was my hardest class. The readings are extremely time-consuming and can be up to 5 each week. The lectures are just talking through slides, and you are graded on notes. Unless this class is related to your major, I do not recommend taking it.

Frankly insane class for a freshman to he expected to take. Flint is a nice person outside of class but her lessons are absolutely brutal. Long boring lectures that somehow still give you no time to write notes in time and 40 page readings for homework with random pop quizzes sprinkled in. There's a reason she's been getting 1 stars for 20 years!!!
In general is passive aggressive about absences, confusing phrasing for a lot of the work. On your own learning style But can gain some stuff from her experience.

There are long readings for every week, which will occasionally have pop quizzes on. Pop quizzes are difficult to get a good grade on even if you do the readings. There are graded notebook checks, checking for all lectures and readings. Tough grader and will change the instructions for assignments multiple times after they've already been assigned.

Overall, I enjoyed having Dr. Flint. She is very reading-heavy, you have to take thorough notes because she grades note-taking and even has notebook checks. She maybe a very nice person in real life but she is a very difficult professor to work with. This class was supposed to help you get warmed up to college but instead this course only made it harder for us freshman.

Avoid. Dr. Flint is nice, but she's an awful professor. DO NOT TAKE. This class involves lengthy reading of 45+ page PDF's every week for in class pop quizzes. The teacher takes offense to when no one cares for the boring topics that she rambles about. Dr.Flint was the absolute worst professor. She knew nothing about the material she was teaching. Her grading is ridiculous, all of her grading was insanely nitpicking, she does not give 100s. One of the worst professors I have had this semester. Her lectures are extremely boring and the homework is beyond extensive. WORST PROFESSOR EVER.

Dr. Dupre is a very kind professor; he is approachable and is willing to explain things from the lecture. If you are like me and aren't the best at writing, good luck in this course.

His class was honestly pretty easy. There is a lot of reading, but that's expected in a history course. Make sure you pay attention and take good notes because the only assignments are exams, but they're relatively easy.

Dr. Dupre is super respectful and always willing to help his students when they are stuck and confused about something. He does require a bit of writing but it should not be an issue if you get it done on time. Other than that, he's a good professor.

Professor Dupre was very nice and knowledgeable. He only teaches through lectures and class discussions, so taking notes and participating will help you do good. Grades on 6 pop quizzes that he bases off readings he gives you, 3 exams, and a final paper. Attendance is required but overall great class and great professor.

Dr. Dupre gave me hope in history again after having a terrible and harsh professor the semester before. He's extremely smart, he's super friendly, and makes an effort to get to know his students. He's easy to talk to and never makes you feel embarrassed for asking even the most simple questions in meetings with him. Attendance is key though!

Professor Dupre was one of my favorites! Great lectures, make sure to take lots of notes. Pop quizzes are usually on documents that he assigned to read before. He let us bring a flashcard with notes for the exams, which was really helpful. Be ready to write papers and read long documents. Overall, great professor and course.
He was hard to pay attention to, very boring. almost everyone I know had a d.

Dr. Dupre is a good professor, and I enjoyed this class. He is a tough grader but is very clear with his feedback and offers a lot of office hours and opportunities to get help. I also appreciated his meetings throughout the semester to make sure nobody fell behind. A difficult grader but a great professor and a nice person.

This is the first time I have written one of these for a professor. And I highly recommend him for HIST-4000. He gives clear and concise feedback. He will also work with you in order for you to pass or succeed in your field of study. Just communicate with him, because he will communicate with you :)

Don't do it. Takes participation seriously, understanding the readings are important, in-class pop quizzes are considered "quick and short (lies)." Definitely contradicts himself when grading. super critical, dont take his class

The class is lecture heavy, these lectures are kinda boring and it feels like youre shamed for not alreading knowing historical topics weve never learned. Class participation is really big. Weekly readings that he will assign sometimes at 5pm and its due the next day at 10am. Essay tests that are graded more citical then most english teachers.

Commuters with busy schedules do not take his in-person classes. Dr. Ferdinando requires you to schedule in-person meetings with TAs before every test and group project, and attendance is mandatory for a grade. These meetings are outside class hours, and I had to miss work to attend—super inconsiderate of students' schedules.

Does not provide good feedback keeps telling us to refer to the information without specifying what is wrong with the writing. A lot of reading initially. Does not post lecture slides on canvas. You will be in a group. He maybe needs to be more socially aware.  Although the final project is only two paragraphs.
All tests are in person essays, never left his class without multiple wrist cramps.

Dr. Ferdinando is the worst grader I've ever had, this is probably the first History class ever that I've received a grade lower than A-. Nothing is perfect to him.

Dr. Ferdinando is AMAZING!! By far one of my favorite professors. He gives excellent constructive criticism and genuinely wants his students to succeed and know the content. He released exam questions beforehand, and allowed you to bring a note sheet. If you can take him, DO!! HIST1160 (I took it in Fall '24) was my 1st of 3 classes taken with him.

I had 1512 course! He was very knowledgeable and during his lectures you need to take notes & PAY ATTENTION otherwise the exams and Term IDs will be hard to do.Very accessible out of class & has the drop policy.He will know if you use AI- and doc off loads of points. Kind and humble professor who's willing to help. All exam topics and essay prompts were given in advance, and note sheets were allowed. Minimal homework. He is a very unfair grader, I have always tried hard in school but he refused to give 100s even if it was deserved. I attended every class and he still managed to add negative help to my papers. If you follow all the criteria on assignments and it's clear you put effort into your work, you are sure to get a good grade. If you have good attendance he'll curve your final grade (he bumped my grade up from a B to an A).
Lots of lecture readings, homework but easy grader and easy class if u do read

Tough grader in the sense that he looks for very specific things, he tells you what they are you just have to figure out how to answer them. He gives good feedback on just about every graded assignment, he'll tell you what you did right or wrong, so it's easy to improve if you pay attention. I probably wouldn't take him for an elective.

Dr. F is a great professor but if you are looking for an easy class, this is NOT the class for you. Each week you will be expected to read 40-70 pages of the assigned textbook. Dr. F is also very specific on grading, you will get paragraphs worth of feedback and tough grades. Lastly, be ready to buy Microsoft Word and PowerPoint for this class. GL!

Dr. Ferdinando does a good job of making this class relate to non-history majors. He understands that not everyone cares about historical stuff, so he makes an effort to constantly connect this class to other stuff that's important to future non-history careers. He is a tough grader, but he is approachable for help if you need it.

Dr. Ferdinando is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and he tries to keep everything engaging. I enjoyed this class, but he is a tough grader so be prepared. He drops the lowest assignments and is accessible outside of class.
Lots of reading and extensive discussion. Lots of feedback to see improvement but is a tough grader

Dr. Ferdinando is obviously very well-educated and he cares deeply about his subject. That being said, he is an extremely critical grader and there is a lot of outside work to be done to be able to keep up with the class. Certainly helps students get prepared for further academia, but for my sake I hope I never have to take a similar class again.
Nothing is ever good enough for this man.

Dr. Ferdinando is a top professor if you're looking for a good 2600/3600 professor. He does an excellent job teaching the methodology skills needed for the final paper and is always available for questions after class or in office hours if you don't understand. He also gives good feedback on papers through comments and clarifies them at meetings.

Dr. Ferdinando is really helpful when it comes to writing. He has a clear rubric for every assignment and gives really helpful feedback for writing assignments. His class is really boring though, & attendance matters. Make sure not to procrastinate on the hard writing assignments. But I would not suggest taking him unless you really have to.

Dr. Ferdinando was a fantastic professor for HIST 2600. Despite the class itself being pretty daunting, he makes everything clear at the start of the semester, he's easy to work with, very approachable, and is a great storyteller, his lectures always had me invested. I loved Dr. Ferdinando and would take a class of his again.

Dr Cameron was great this semester! His lectures were pretty engaging to me, and the five-question comprehension quizzes afterwards were extremely simple. Weekly DBs, but they weren't difficult at all. The midterm and final are oral exams, but attending the review sessions and taking notes on the lecture will definitely prepare you!

This was an asynchronous class and a normal week would look like two quizzes due at 5pm on Mon/Wed then a discussion post due Fri. Lectures can be long and you have to actually pay attention and take notes since the quizzes are based off of them. My least favorite part about this class was the oral exam for mid term and final.

I was a senior in college, working on 2 publications, 2 jobs, and 18 credit hours. Cameron showed no sympathy and instead lectured me on time management after giving none for assignments submitted 1 hour after the due time at 5 PM. Very disrespectful in his response, and genuinely surprised that he is allowed to serve as a department chair.

Professor Cameron is a very chill, laid back professor with extensive knowledge in his field. I found his lectures interesting, and was impressed that he seems to be able to remember historical details with great accuracy, just off the dome. Almost all grades will be quizzes and tests, so make sure to read the textbook and attend class lectures.
Dr. Cameron could teach every single class in the History department and I'd eat them up.

This class is LONG. There are a series of readings you must complete, usually a 200ish-page book every week, followed by an in-class quiz to make sure you did the readings. I recommend doing the readings. There is also a final paper, but it is only 12 pages that you start working on in the middle of the semester. I would try taking another section.

Gives reading quizzes about once a week on a chapter reading. Usually about 30 pages so start EARLY! The quizzes are very say though, just do the reading and you will be fine. Besides that, just lectures and a midterm and final. Lectures are great, he is a very nice and easy-going professor. He cares too, will let students retake always. TAKE HIM!

He was a great professor and made the class very interesting. The class consisted mostly of quizzes, long readings, and the midterm. He is very nice, will answer your questions, and would frequently cancel class. Overall, he is a great professor, and it's an interesting class!
Easy going class. Quizzes every day but if you read the chapter it was super easy. It was an 8 week class so everything went fast but just stay on top of it and you'll pass.

Overall just a great professor. She really prioritizes learning instead of worrying about grades. She doesn't give you tests as well, just a few routine assignments and readings. Also, a very interesting class, probably one of the ones I've learned the most in. Highly recommend!

I loved her. Her teaching style was amazing and very interactive. I feel she is very passionate about her subject and even could make someone who is not and never has been a history buff enjoy it completely. She even pardoned the third test. No one I ever knew did that. She was always my best professor. Life-changing exp. Take her always! The GOAT!

Dr. Frat loves what she teaches and it shows in lectures. I only took this course for the graduation requirement but she made it bearable. Mostly busy work but very easy to pass. I do honestly feel like for an American Democracy course we spent half of it in the Middle East lol. You don't NEED the course reader, just borrow from a classmate
10/10 would take a class of hers again

very good class, she worked hard to make it a discussion class, even with about 50 students.  Learned everyone's name.   A fair amount of reading,  many times class time was small group discussion that was then summarized for whole class

Wonderful professor! I added this course last minute and I'm grateful that I did. Prof. Frat is an incredible lecturer and makes difficult topics much easier to understand. She calls on people a lot but she never makes you feel stupid and you are allowed to pass if you're too shy.

Dr. Frat is a stellar professor and person, and I'm sad the class is over! Her lectures were always interesting and engaging, and she treated sensitive material with lots of care. You can tell she loves and takes her job seriously. She is a very generous and understanding professor & I hope to take another class from her in the future.

Favorite professor at UNCC. I've taken all her courses. Down to Earth, funny, caring, and gives good feedback. Explains what she wants well and helps you to achieve what she expects. W Professor. If she is available as a History Maj Class (3600,4000,4600) get her you won't be disappointed. Took 3600 and 4003 with her, true shame I couldn't do 4600.
She's awesome. She's really interested in what she teaches and wants to teach you about it.

Very nice person and a caring professor. She is very helpful in feedback and accessible outside of class. She is a very difficult grader though. You really need all of your stuff in strict Chicago style otherwise she WILL catch it. Aside from that her class was interesting. Towards the end, it began to drag though.

As a professor, she is very caring, helpful and genuienly nice. Understands that some students have other stuff going on so she extends deadline and such. Her lectures were boring though and the content wasn't interesting for me. I don't recommend it if you're not into Middle eastern history like me. Took it only because I had to.

I took LBST 2301. Textbooks were referenced but I never needed to use mine. Great teacher with a fun personality who genuinely cares about improving your skills and knowledge. She does like to take up the whole class time but if you go to class and apply her advice to your writing, you will earn a good grade with very little issues.
chill professor will work with you but course load hevaing and boring lectures
Just show up and do the work and you will end with an A

Didn't show up for 1st 2 weeks of class. Only gives 5 grades total. Did not update grades the entire semester. Got the vibe he kinda only teaches because he has to the fund his digs. L Class

He can barely finish a sentence unless he reads directly from his presentation. He won't provide any grades on Canvas, he briefly gives feedback at midterm. Professor Gibson is a pretty good dude overall, but, he has some issues regarding him and the way he structures his course. Very little classwork overall but there is a 20-page final worth 50% of your grade

CONS: Worst Canvas user I've ever seen, only grade feedback is at the midterm and final, kinda boring lecture, takes attendance, + pop quizzes

Great professor; very low-cortisol class. There's no "textbook," but you will have to buy one or two actual books for the course (mine were included in the Niner Course Pack). Greg is an awesome professor. He doesn't make the class difficult at all, and his lectures are very helpful. He is friendly and funny sometimes too. Easy class, Greg is awesome.

I don't think the class was difficult, as long as you actually do the readings and pay attention in class. I LOVED this professor and class! The lecture does get a bit boring but honestly if you just do the reading and pay attention, it is so easy to pass. Greg knows what he's teaching, but that doesn't stop him from making the classroom absolutely dreadful. I felt as though I was in HIGH SCHOOL AGAIN...genuinely. WARNING!!! ATTENTION ALL STUDENTS LOOKING TO TAKE A PHILOSOPHY CLASS. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. SURE, HE KNOWS ABOUT THE SUBJECT. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!!!!
Good professor! the only thing is he has an assignment every class on the reading you did, you can miss up to 4 though. I would say overall easy class!

You need to read but it is not a lot and material is interesting. Great lectures I never dreaded attending class. He is also very funny love his teaching style. Would recommend to anyone, was my first PHIL class and a great intro overall.

Didn't read a word after the first few weeks and still made a 101 in the class. Just annotate the readings as he covers them in lecture. As long as you ask questions with big words in lecture he thinks ur smart. He literally told me I should change my major to philosophy lol
It was a fun class, too much to read for a P/F class though

Professor Ganapini just sums up the readings in class, though she explains them really well. Her only grades are quizzes, and she doesn't give much that actually makes you learn the material. yap yap yap yap yap

He was very sweet and passionate about what he was teaching! My only complaint would be the homework assignments; we had to read a lot and annotate the readings. Other than that, the class was pretty interesting and easy.

Only graded on 3-4 tests (I don't remember), so study! Tests are based on what she says in class and the notes. Avoid this class if you want an easy elective. The prof is passionate and knows her stuff, but tests are based on what she says in lectures and not what's on the slides, so attendance is a must. Grades come from 4 tests and 2 all-or-nothing extra credit assignments. Guest speakers and the documentaries were a highlight.

The teacher is nice and respectful, but I didn't like the class much, it was SK. There was 4 test and each has 2 points extra credit paragraph you can do. The presentation ar really disorganized and so hard to study.
Only has four grades. TESTS, I hate it but I like the professor. Shes respectful and knows what shes talking about. if you are a good test taker, you should take her!
Entire class based off of four tests. Only extra credit assignment seems to intentionally have a weird due date. Professor claims that class cannot be passed unless you attend every lecture.

This class is extremely challenging for what it's worth. This was supposed to be a free A elective, but instead, due to the 4 tests being the only grades, it wasn't. This professor seems to enjoy the failure of her students, and it's truly disheartening.

She is a sweet woman and is passionate about the class. You're graded on 4 tests alone. She provides 2 extra credit assignments but is a tough grader on them. No late work is accepted, and no partial credit is received either. Overall, the class is fairly easy, you just have to show up to class and take notes. Lots of memorization!!

Dr. Coston is a great professor! All her lectures were really interesting and she is passionate about what she teaches. My only complaint about this class is that it's graded based on the four tests you take throughout the semester with little to no extra credit and other assignments to back you up if you bomb one, hence why my grade dropped.

Dr. Coston is a great professor! Her lectures were very informative and she is very passionate about the subjects she teaches. My only complaint about this class is how your grade is based on only the 4 tests you have throughout the semester, with no other assignments to back you up if you bomb one of them like I did. Great class overall though!

Dr. Coston is a great professor. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but the tests are dependent on what she says in class. You will want to take a LOT of notes on essentially everything she says. However, as long as you study your notes, you will get an A in her class. She also brings some guest lecturers and puts on interesting documentaries.

If you attend class, it is very easy. While she does provide a copy of her slideshow, attending the lecture and taking notes is important to succeed, as she often "fills in" areas of the notes in class. You get a PDF copy of the textbook, but the questions are solely from the lectures.

Professor Coston is very knowledgeable and makes the lectures engaging. With only 4 exams as the grades, the class is manageable if you attend and take good notes. unstuck ai was super helpful for test prep.

Honestly, if your not good at tests, steer clear of this professor. I got a 74 on the first test and I was trying to get my grade up the entire semester. ONLY 4 TESTS, NOTHING ELSE. There was one extra credit assignment at 11:59 am instead of pm, and I missed it because I read the time wrong. Take a weekend to study for the test, u need the grade.

Good prof! I like that she doesn't use a txtbook & brings in guest speakers & shows films in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go to class bc your only grades are 4 exams. As long as you go to class and study the material you will do great. Dr. C is very knowledgeable. She will go over what you should study.

Only grades were the 4 unit tests. Every test had an extra credit question and she gave multiple other extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Many guest speakers spoke with the class that were very interesting. Professor heavily knows the information she is teaching and is very willing to answer all questions.

This class wasn't too difficult overall, but your grade is determined by just 4 tests. The test questions can be very specific, so make sure to pay attention closley during the lectures. She does review classes that tell you what will be on the test and goes over the entire unit in depth. The first few weeks, she will let you go early most classes.
She was a great teacher but the only grades for this class is tests. They are 100% off the slides which she goes over in class (they are also posted in canvas).

A very caring and nice prof, class is a lot of memorization but as long as you have notes the tests are pretty easy. She is a great teacher with lots of experience. Thought it would be a boring elec. class but was actually interested in what we learned. P good communication, and made mistakes with the tests a lot but she would fix it quick

Dr. Coston is an amazing professor that knows what she's talking about. She works in the criminal justice field and her lectures are interesting and keep you engaged. The class itself is not too hard but it's a lot of information to remember so pay attention during review. She also tends to make some mistakes on tests but gives points back for it.

Professor Coston was pretty good, she was thoughtful into all of her work and truly knew what she was talking about. The only down-side to this class is that we only have tests, there are no other assignments to boost your grade so you need to study, but as long as you review the presentations you should be good.

Online course that consist of four exams and one final presentation. The first exam will be due about a week and a half after the first day of class. You have to read two books for the first three exams and test four is an essay question. I managed to pass the class with a B and didn't do much of the reading but that might not work for you so......

Professor Coston is a phenomenal professor and an expert in the Criminal Justice field, her lectures are engaging and entertaining (also easy to understand). However, her notes are purely based on the lectures, and (given this was an online course), the test questions would be out of order (they were shuffled on each persons test). Overall, 8/10.

Very friendly and knowledgeable woman. Lectures could be boring sometimes, but overall they were entertaining, and the information was fascinating. The only graded things were tests, but an extra credit assignment was offered. Multiple guest speakers that had a lot to share and gave a lot of insight into CJUS.

Professor is engaging with some opportunists to go experience things haven't done before. I was nervous about assignment, but see why she made us do it. She does some cool easy class opportunities so u have to go to class. Prof Harmtna makes class easy to talk about hard topics. She does a good job of listening to all sides and knows her stuff.

The best professor in the CJUS Major. Incredibly helpful to all students. Class was organizes really easy to understand but still was challenging. I liked I could discuss things in more depth than other classes. I can recommend to go to the lectures there is participation grade and make note cards for exams. You will learn life long stuff.

I'm sure Hartman is great, but she should NOT be holding online classes.
