Prof Hartman is engaging and knowledgeable. While the class has a lot of work, she provides helpful feedback. I found Unstuck AI and the free textbook to be great study aids alongside the lectures. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course.

It took a bit for me to engage with Professor Hartman, but once I did I like her style. She is a good teacher who is VERY passionate about equal justice for all, especially marginalized communities. Goes over American histroy of how we got to today in the US. Also learned about masculinity and patriarchy. Online course w lots of content but was ok.

Its lots of material to cover. Online so recorded lectures and lots of powerpoints. Four exams, lots of quizzes and writing stuff.  Grading was fine. Best part is prof hartman made herself available to answer questions. Not an easy grade but i did learn some stuff.
Accessible outside of class and has been supportive

Took as summer class because I need class for my major. Don't like onine classes, but she made it ok. I guess. Prob would have given more stars if we were in person. Online did let me keep my job, so I did like this option. A few tests, but you drop worse one. Some writings but have had worse graders. I do like she gives written feedback.

Prof Hartmanis engaging and knowledgeable on the topic, Gender, Race & Justie. Great teacher, class should be required for all CJ majors. All of the books where pretty amazing. Best part was being encouraged to ask questions about race, gender issues that I would never bring up in another class. Class changed by mind on a lot of things. Take it!

He is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. I loved going to his class. He was knowledgeable and funny, and made lectures entertaining. Take good notes and make sure to read the book as tests come from the book but they are fairly easy. I would definitely recommend Dr. Mckee to anyone who wants to take Criminal Justice.

Genuinely one of, if not my favorite professor. He is funny in class, you get opportunities for extra credit, he is great at teaching the material, he fosters an open learning environment, and he tries to connect with his students. His office hours are also very productive.  DO NOT TAKE IF:  you hate fun,  you hate this review,  you are a bum
Great professor, always made the class very fun and interesting even at 9am! Attendance is not mandatory but he gives extra credit for attendance randomly so go to class.

Amazing professor. Lectures were very entertaining. Talked slowly enough to take notes on everything. Everything on the exams is from the lecture slideshows. He gives you a study guide that is exactly like the test. Gives random extra credit quizzes, and you get one extra credit point just for being there. 100% take this class.
Super funny and a great lecturer.
Not a bad teacher at all, just didn't have assignments, so if you do badly on your exams, you won't do well in the class.

Professor McKee is good. He keeps his lectures fun and engaging, and teaches well. However, the class only has 3 tests, the first being the worst. He doesn't post slides on canvas so attendance is needed but not mandatory. Pop quizzes are also very common, but only for extra credit
Great professor! Just make sure you show up to lectures as most of the information from notes are on exams. Probably one of my favorite professors. Course was super interesting too!

Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but you pretty much need to show up if you want a good grade. He keeps the class fun, interesting, and engaging. There are readings, but I never did them, prolly could've gotten an A if I had. Sometimes class is canceled so we can watch a short film or documentary, which is nice. PowerPoints are NOT posted.

Great professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but he doesn't post the slides on canvas so it is highly recommended to show up. He is really funny and I find the lectures interesting. In my opinion the tests were not hard, as long as you read the textbook and take notes during class.

A discussion every 3 weeks in person, three total tests, and a couple other grades. He gives a lot of extra credit. He also makes lectures very entertaining to the point that I don't even understand why people skip! This a need to take a professor especially for a gen ed.
He's absolutely hilarious! Great and interesting class! The only real grades are the tests and there aren't many of them. DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE FIRST TEST!

I truly enjoyed his class so much. He's very funny and it's easy to get a good grade in this class as long as you keep up with the lectures and textbook. He gives no assignments so if you do bad on the exams you're pretty screwed and have nothing to fall back on. If you are a good test taker you would be good but if not I don't recommend him.
really funny and cool professor ! 4 tests and 4 discussions, no assignments so you have to do really good on them. attendence isnt mandatory but his lectures are very very important to be there for.

Dr.Mckee is a good professor. His lectures are kind of boring but he does his best to make them funny and interesting. Professor McKee is a good professor. He gives great lectures and is pretty funny. This class is built up of 6 discussions, 3 tests, & 1 paper so each assignment is crucial.

Professor Mckee is a very cool teacher. Has a lot of stories about his life that relate back to Criminal Justice and is so laid back that he doesn't really care much if you study or not. Very simple rules in his classroom no disruption, don't ask for extra credit, and if you know that you can't show up don't. Very simple rules and cool to talk to.
Best professor in the department by far. His lectures are actually interesting and he's super chill. You'll learn a lot and have fun while in his class.

Very straightforward professor. Hard class, and you need to find your way of studying the material, or you will struggle. He is available to help, but you have to reach out. He is an amazing professor. The class is very interesting and he gives great lectures. Class consists of weekly 2-question quizzes and 1 major paper, along with exams throughout. The exams are an EXACT COPY of the lectures and the textbook. Whatever you do, make sure to read the textbook as it sneaks up on you on the exams. Professor McKee is hilarious and very engaging, so the lectures are entertaining at the very least.

Doesn't have many assignments to grade so if you mess up on a test your grade in this class will not be the best and if you have to miss an exam for whatever reason he will not care, Ego is thru the roof with this guy

The professor is super chill. Everything he talked about in the lecture was interesting. Had exams every quarter but he made a study guide. If you pay attention in class and take you will be fine. Great professor, made class fun. Does not have a lot of grades, end grade mainly reflects test grades.
This guy is awesome. He is super knowledgable, funny, and respectful. Your grade is primarily based on exams, but everything on the exams is clearly in your notes/readings. Highly recommend!

Professor McKee is like no other. He makes the lectures engaging and has great comedic timing. Really funny, pop quizzes and about 3 test during the whole semester, WHAT YOU LEARN IN CLASS WILL BE ON THE TEST, great and simple notes on power points, would take his class again.

He was a great and engaging professor. Mr. Mckee is an all around great guy. I really enjoyed his class. The tests were difficult for me, and with no study guide I struggled a lot even though I regularly attended class. I would've enjoyed it more had there been more graded assignments, and study guides for exams.

So the class is broken up into 4 tests and 1 essay. You also get extra credit if you come to all of the classes. Funny lectures with good dry humor. Sometimes there are “pop quizzes” solely to provide extra credit. Honestly a fantastic teacher, I wish I could take more of his classes, if only I wasn't an engineer.

10/10 would recommend, this is my 2nd time having Professor Mckee and he is easily one of my favorites. This class includes 3 test and 4 writing assignments which are super easy. Dr. Mckee is hilarious and engaging which makes the class really interesting despite it being mostly lectures and some videos. Dr. McKee is an amazing professor! If you do the reading and take notes, you will do very well on your exams. His exams are extremely straightforward and all questions are multiple choice. There is no work in this class. If you are not a good test taker, DONT TAKE HIM. your entire grade is based on 4 tests and one essay. I studied for them and took notes during every lecture but it does not matter because he puts the most random questions on the test.
This guy should be a comedian. He makes lectures entertaining and as long as you show up to class it's pretty easy. HIGHLY RECCOMEND.

He is such a good and funny guy, made class interesting and very engaging. But, if you don't do well on the test, good luck getting above a C. For a general education course, I thought it was kind of annoying that the test really affected our grades. We get a study guide, but it's hard to prepare how the question will be asked. Goodluck!

He is great , he interacts with the class and always plays devils advocate and his lectures are funny. Exam heavy becasue he doesnt give any homework so if you dont do great on the exam that might not be good but aslo the exam is bascially the notes he gives in class.
Easy to get along with awesome possum in my opinion.

thiHe won't help you and you risk losing 5 points OFF YOUR FINAL GRADE if you ask him for "extra credit" meaning you can't go to him with any concern about your grade. Prof McKee is super funny, one of the few college classes where I enjoyed the lectures. He does give pop "discussions" from time to time, so make sure to go to class. This has been my favorite professor I've had at UNCC despite it being the only B I've made so far. No homework besides a 2 page paper near the end. Lectures are interesting and he's really funny. Such a great professor! All you're graded on is 3 tests, 1 paper, and 5 easy discussions, You have to come to class, his powerpoints are not uploaded and a lot is on the tests. Read your chapters and make sure to finish any documentaries we start in class. Many small extra credit opportunities! He made class worth coming to, very funny person!

5 mini group assignments and 4 tests, you have to do good on the tests. Provides extra credit opportunities. Refers to the textbook a lot. Textbook questions, documentary questions, and anything mentioned in class will be on test. Got more strict at the end. Loves to debate anything when a student speaks.

Class is not mandatory but it's important to come for the notes, the tests include things he said in the lectures. Funny and very engaging. Professor Mckee is great! This is my second time taking his class and I'll definitely be taking classes with him in the future. One of my favorite professors. Plenty of extra credit (as long as you go to class). Not many assignments but tests are very easy. Take good notes, read the textbook, and go to class. That's all you need to do to get a good grade. Very funny & laid-back professor. I plan to take another class of his in the fall. Definitely recommend taking his class

Professor McKee is my favorite professor I've ever had. Every day is just lectures but he's super funny and engaging. You're graded on 4 tests, 5 discussions, and one paper(2 pages, no research). If you show up, pay attention, and take mediocre notes, you are VERY likely to do well. If you read the textbook you will get an A or B for sure.

Really awesome guy with plenty of extra credit opportunities. The tests are straightforward and his lectures are very interesting. He has a John Mulaney-type of humor that carries well in his class. Highly recommend taking his classes.

McKee is very enjoyable, he's funny and laid-back. Grades are just 4 tests, a 3-page paper, and very easy "discussions," with a nice smattering of free extra credit for attendance. Loved professor McKee, this class was very interesting and helpful. In order to succeed it's important you attend lectures, he doesn't post slides online. Really enjoyed taking this class because it was very interesting. I was not expecting the amount you had to read from the textbooks. Only gives exams, and discussion grades so study.

Professor McKee is a good professor who does a great job making a tough subject (domestic violence) much easier to learn about. He is very respectful of the seriousness of the topic while trying to keep the class light-hearted. He is willing to answer any question the best he can no matter the difficulty. He is also approachable. Highly recommend.

McKee Is a very fun professor. His lectures are interesting, he gives extra credit for attendance, and he likes to joke about Ethan, a student in my section, committing heinous crimes (Ethan was okay with this).

He was always engaging with students during class, lectures are interesting and easy to understand even if you arent a CJUS major. He's always cracking jokes and telling storys that relate to the course content. His tests are relativly easy if you pay attention in class and take key points from the textbook.

Honestly the best professor I have had. Makes his lectures funny and interesting and the content is relatively easy. Attendance is not mandatory but it really does help on all of your assignments
Phenomenal teacher, very funny as well. Very helpful if you go to his office hours. Only homework is reading the textbook which is very helpful.

Professor Mckee was an amazing professor for the first criminal justice class I took at UNCC. He was hilarious, gave extra credit, and specified what would be on the tests. The readings aren't bad and as long as you take lecture notes and do the readings, you'll be fine on the tests. Just don't start slacking off and you'll do great in it.

He's super chill and cracks jokes, but you have to go to class in order to pass the exam and get extra credit. for an elective class, i think hes still fine and material is comprehensible, but im a cjus major so i loved it. practically no assignments. study and put in the effort, especially for exams and you will pass with a B or better.

I love this man. He was easily the best criminal justice professor I have had thus far. Professor McKee was one of the best professors I have had at UNCC. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. His lectures were always entertaining and he is just an all around great professor. Most of your grade is based on tests and a few assignments but go to class and you will do just fine.

McKee does a great job of teaching material and also being entertaining. This class ends up being one that you actually want to go to. As long as you go to class, the assignments are easy and sometimes you can get extra credit for showing up.

His test questions are so random. Makes us watch a bunch videos and then grabs random questions out of those. Besides test we have writting assignments. His tests shouldn't be that complicated for an 1100 class.
Professor McKee us by far the best professor I've had so far. He made class so interested and when it came to tests, he told us what we needed to study.
I wish we had some more homework so the tests weren't the only things graded. And the two assignments we had were easy but don't do anything to your grade so it was useless.

fun guy & lectures were fun but there was no homework and tests were 60% of your grade. there was 1 extra credit option at the beginning of the semester but none after that. 3/5 because all his tests were on paper but they're multiple choice so thats good. super funny & nice guy. attendance is mandatory and always read ahead in the textbook.

Isabelle has got to be one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She is so caring and if you tell her you're struggling with anything she will support you in any way she can so you don't fall behind. She's hilarious and energetic and made learning a foreign language so much easier.
she's perfect

Madame Isabelle is hands down my favorite prof at UNCC. She's the sweetest lady ever. She's very understanding and forgiving with mistakes, and acknowledges that learning a language is difficult. Before every quiz/test, she tells us exactly what'll be on it and does practice problems beforehand that are almost identical. She's the absolute best!

Profe Cisneros is wonderful! It's been a while since I've taken a Spanish class, and I can say that she really helped me build my confidence. She cares deeply about her students and tries to encourage you to ask questions and try your best, even if you make mistakes. The VHL assignments were a bit much,  but they were good practice!

I passed the class and as long as I did all that was assigned I managed, but she does give sooo much homework the first half of the semester. I'll also say her approach and demeanor can give off passive aggression and rudeness, to the point where I felt hesitant even reaching out or asking a question. Not the worst but not the best :/

This professor goes above and beyond! I am very happy I took this class, I definitely learn a lot and I am able to apply these skills into my future career. This professor really cares for the students and wants them to be successful in their career.

Profesora Cisneros truly cares about her students and their wellbeing. She is tough on you but it is for your own benefit in the end. She is a wonderful profesor, she adds her own personal experiences in her lectures which makes you feel more connected with her and her topics she teaches, for a better understanding.

I loved this class with Profe Cisneros! She cares deeply about inspiring students and applies real world concepts to the class. The assignments not only practiced Spanish, but also genuinely had me reflecting on my identity. There are a couple of small presentation assignments and in class writing compositions that are graded fairly. I recommend!

She will assume everyone is on the same page and you should know everything from the previous classes (I took the placement test and did not take any previous classes). She teaches very fast. It's hard to keep up. There is heavy homework load and a lot of testing with exams and compositions. She doesn't teach the material well to keep up with it.

Prof. Cisneros gives you the attention you give her. if you don't care neither does she BUT if you care about the class and your grade she will stop at nothing to support you in whatever way necessary. I'm so bummed shes not teaching 2202, I will take whatever i can with her in the future!

Profesora Cisneros es fantastica! She upped my confidence in language learning. Her lectures were very engaging and easy to follow along and try the in-class activities. Her passion and enthusiasm encouraged me to work and it and learn and treat it like an activity and not a chore. I even excelled in the difficult presentation and Boomalang.

Profesora Cisneros made language learning easy and engaging. At first, I was worried about taking this class since I had not taken Spanish since high school. She built my confidence up and I ended up keeping an A for the duration of the class. She always responded to emails quickly and was eager to help.

Prof. Cisneros is so funny and truly cares about her students. There are many homework assignments but they do have a purpose and do help with upcoming tests. She has little patience for late assignments but due dates are fair. Put in effort and you should succeed.

Profesora Cisneros is awesome! She will definitely challenge you in this class but recognizes that people are coming in at different fluency levels and considers that when grading. She is such a caring person and is always willing to help you, whether in class or outside of class, and is very accommodating and considerate of her students' needs.

Overall a very sweet and caring teacher. She mentions every class that there is help provided and resources that are available to you if you are not doing well. I feel like when she writes stuff it could be more organized but that's it. Overall a really good teacher, the class is not bad, just study up.

I want to love her bc she is so lenient on due dates and cares about helping but her class is so beyond difficult especially for non native speakers. A seven minute presentation without notes or words on the slides is crazy. She is so intimidating, but so nice at the same time. I just wish I was actually learning and not scared of the class.

As a student speaking Spanish throughout all my years of school, I was worried that this environment wouldn't be reciprocated in college. Taking Profesora Cisneros my first semester of college was a great decision. She is so nice and positive. You can truly tell that she cares and her class topics are very deep/useful. I love her class
Definitely a very understanding professor as long as she knows you try in class and you actually attend! Sometimes she doesn't explain material or the exams enough, but it's still doable

Professor Cisneros is a kind soul. She is very sweet when it comes to extensions and helping with concepts you don't understand. I haven't had any issues with her at all. It was a little hard for me to adjust to her Argentinian dialect as opposed to past professors. Other than that, very good professor.

Honestly the best Professor at UNC Charlotte. I studied abroad with her in Sicily, and it was such an amazing time. Professor Daniela genuinely cares about her students. She also really cares about what she is teaching. I would take her again and again if I could. BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!

Had Professor Dal Pra for a study abroad and she was the best professor that Iv ever had. The assignments for the course went with everything that you would see in person. 10/10 would do it again. I highly recommend a study abroad experience with her.
All online responses that were graded on the grammer more than the content. Use a grammer check if you take her class.

I love Professor. Dal Pra so much. She is one of the best professors I've ever had, and she is super flexible. She likes to change the courses depending on what interests her students. She is an easy grader for the most part, but when people start taking advantage of her, she starts grading slightly more harshly.

Daniela is an amazing and caring professor. She is very fair and knowledgeable. I have taken multiple classes with her and her classes never disappoint; they are hidden gems. UNCC is very lucky to have this professor. Just show up, participate, ask questions, do the work and you will be fine.

Proff. is very passionate and talks about the topics in cinema with proper information but she is VERY repetitive. She will pause the films to talk about exactly what (and will) happen/ed. Participation is HUGE and even grades harshly if you don't praise the topic enough. You take class notes for everyone and even with that, you'll be graded harsh.

He is an awesome professor at his core, his classes are not hard nor are his assignments. I would however advise anyone considering taking him for an elective in addition to major requirements to look elsewhere. The amount of assignments is absurd and you will not keep up if you have other demanding courses that also have a ton of assignments.

Bledsoe's class was very easy, featuring online quizzes, discussion posts, journal entries, and papers tied to approximately 11 documentaries. The grading was lenient, allowing for three missed classes without penalty, and students often received extra points for quality assignments. While Bledsoe attempts humor, it can be cringeworthy at times.

Great professor! I took his anime class, JAPN-3140. Not sure if the code changed, but it wasn't listed. There are a lot of online assignments, but they really don't take long to complete. There are a couple of long lecture videos, but they were interesting. Mainly watched anime/documentaries in class.

Prof. Bledsoe is an okay professor. I took JAPN1502 (previously 1201 I think) a gen ed class. Its easy as long as you keep up with the 6+ weekly online assignments including 4 discussion videos and multiple quizzes based on lecture videos. He doesnt teach in class we just watch documentaries, all the actual learning comes from the online lectures.

I had him for JAPN 1502. There is a lot of homework in this class, however, if you do it while the class is going and do not wait until the last second, it does not seem like a lot. He is a great professor and cares about his classes that he teaches. I would 100% take him again. I do not have a problem with him at all.

Professor Bledsoe is an awesome professor who really cares about sharing japanese culture with students. The class I took was new so the curriculum may very well change but if i doesnt, expect a ton of easy assignments. He is also very lenient if you miss any as long as you communicate with him. Take his class if you want to relax and learn.

Professor Bledsoe is very chill and his lectures are fun. There are a lot of assignments, but they are super simple and do not take very long to complete. No tests, only a final project at the end of the semester. Attendance is required so show up. There a quite a bit of asynchronous days for the class, which was nice.

Amazing professor! Keeps class engaged and entertaining and is very lenient with homework. There is LOTS of homework, but at the end of the semester, he drops a lot of our lowest ones. Also no tests or quizzes, just assignments that are easy 100s.

Professor Bledsoe is great at explaining japanese and makes easy to learn! He does a "flipped" classroom where you watch videos first and practice in class. Attendance is required and you practice with classmates throughout the semester. He also gave us the opportunity to turn in certain assignments with no late penalty.  Definitely take him!

Lots of group work, but as long as you have good teammates, the class is super easy. This class would only be difficult if you don't try at all and think presenting in front of a class is the most difficult thing in the world. Very little investment outside of class is needed and overall it was a fun class, I learned a lot more than I expected.
Mori Sensei's stricter schedule makes it easier to stay on tract to learn Japanese but it's nothing impossible. It is a class that can be done at any reasonable pace you want to do.

I absolutely loved her class and teaching style. I felt challenged and extremely motivated throughout the semester. It's pretty fast-paced but you get used to it because it's very structured, and it didn't feel like we rushed over any lessons. Overall, one of my favorite classes I've ever taken!

This class was so much fun, it felt more like a group of people practicing Japanese together than a traditional class.  There is a lot of work to do but it genuinely does help you learn the material, I didn't have to study at all outside of the assigned work.

I loved Mori Sensei's Japanese course! She is very kind and genuinely cares about her students and their success. Japanese is hard (that's a given) and the course is fast-paced but grading isn't too harsh. Tons of homework but I found Genki work to be fun. The TA Yuki-san was great too! :)

I heard that Mori-sensei is intimidating but I didn't get that feeling with her. I would take her again if I could. She's caring and brought snacks closer to finals. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask her for clarification. My favorite class of the semester.
Sensei Mori made this class not only fun but challenging (in a good way). If you are wanting to get your Japanese skill up quick, I would recommend her.

Mori-sensei made me want to keep learning Japanese, since I nearly debated dropping the major. She's very joyful to be around and helps you understand the content one on one if needed in a clear manner. So easy to reach out to and teaches in a way that is helpful to everyone in the class. Still calls on you though lol so be prepared to study!

I was scared to take a class with her at first because she was known to be strict and fast paced. In a nutshell, Mori sensei ended up being one of my favorite profs. I once spent over half a class crying in the bathroom and she walked in on me by accident. She didn't say anything but she counted me present despite the fact I was absent for most-

Mori-sensei is an amazing lab professor to have, very engaging and reviews content efficiently. She does call on students a lot and participation is something that makes or break this class, but her feedback is extremely helpful and she is always ready for questions. Sometimes, she might misunderstand them though.

Lectures are super boring however he is a nice guy, lots of group discussion which is fine. I didnt really try in the class however if you put in a even a little bit of effort and show up to class youll be fine. He could be better but he isnt bad either, just meh

Professor Stone is as average as they come. I thought he did an okay job but didn't do much to prepare students for quizzes or exams. He would give pages of the textbook instead of taking the time to make a simple study guide. He's not a bad professor but I think there are better professors to take that will make the class way easier.
Professor Stone is an excellent professor. You have to really pay attention if you want to learn, but it's a super nice grader. Extremely understanding and cares about his students.

Prof. Stone is an amazing person and good teacher. I would definitely recommend taking him. The only reason I didn't do well was bc of personal circumstances and couldn't catch myself up. He did try to help me and work with me, but I just think Spanish wasn't my thing anymore. Anyway, DEFINITELY TAKE HIM!!!

He gives alot of homework, kind unorganized sometimes. One oral presentation but not infront of the class. He helps when it comes to compositions but test review "study" is just pages in the textbook. Slow grader. Final was cumulative.
Really kind professor, but be prepared to do lots of homework

SPAN 2202: He explains concepts well. I'd recommend taking him! Hw can be a lot since it's due every Mon/Wed, but as long as you stay on top of it, you'll be fine. Tests are fine just study and do the VHL hw!, and he goes over material beforehand, especially if he knows students don't understand something. He's really sweet/chill, you'll like him!

I have taken Professor Stone 3 times (1 3000 level class and 2 4000 level class), and I transferred here in my junior year. He is a fantastic teacher who really does help you. I really can't recommend him highly enough.
Is very kind and good at teaching. Only downside is that there is a lot of homework so be prepared for that.

Professor Stone is the nicest guy, his lectures are great, and he manages to make basic Spanish a lot of fun to learn. He prepared us for the test well, the homework wasn't too long and reinforced topics from class. He was always available if you need help.
Such a great professor

He's a respectable man but this class has been so difficult for no reason. He uses the textbook and there is no room for synonymous words as he will take points off if you don't use the direct translation for words from the textbook, direct wording for concepts and accent marks. On average 1-2 quizzes per week, can't miss class, final is cumulative

He takes a long time to grade assignments and doesn't give much feedback when he does. Study guides were just a list of all of the units we had been taught. Taught us lectures after being tested on the content already. Its finals now and still hasn't graded several assignments. He is nice, lectures well, and is helpful when you ask in class.
Easy class as long as you read and do the online homework, there are a few tests throughout the course and an oral exam professor stone is great

He genuinely cares about students and wants you to succeed. I am a spanish minor, and struggle to keep up with native spanish speakers, but this class was fun and I didn't find myself staring at the clock like usual. He's very understanding, and his lectures are actually helpful and taught me a lot.

An okay professor. He's super nice and understanding but he doesn't do too well at explaining. I can tell he tries his best tho. He's very soft spoken so sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. Long hw but that's every Spanish class. Lectures can get boring & interactions w/ classmates are required. Exams are okay bc half-point is allowed.

Really kind teacher and very easy to work with! I took this class online, but probably be better in person. There is a discussion board almost every week where you watch movies or read the textbook. One midterm, a mini project on an Arab country, and a final interview. Not difficult just follow the rubric. You must show your face for the project.
She is very nice and her class is relatively easy just a class where she talks and you listen.overall kind teacher.

If you are learning Arabic for the first time, Dr. Noha is the best professor. She perfectly explains everything and makes learning the language enjoyable. She annunciates letters very well and emphasizes where there might be any confusion. There is a lot of homework, but they are for your benefit. Plus, she drops 3 lowest HW and attendance grades.
she was terrible, NEVER take her class PLEASE.

You are expected to read textbook chapters before coming into class, gets disappointed if you do not. She is very cooperative- makes the deadlines favorable to the students. She is a tough grader with no clear rubric for discussion boards. Very heavy DB class.

Mrs ghali is truly kind and cares for the students this review is for her Arabic cultural studies class she's a very good explainer with easy assignments that just require effort make sure to attend and read the material provided and you will be fine she's a great teacher.
If you want an easy and enjoyable class, this one is a great choice! The material was straightforward, and the tests weren't difficult. I definitely recommend taking it.
Great Professor, very genuine and wants everyone to succeed in the course.

Dr Noha is a very good professor. If you are looking to learn Arabic, she is the right professor. Walking into the class, I had no knowledge of the Arabic alphabet or language. Now, I know the whole alphabet and can read decently with just one class. Overall, I learned a lot from her class and would highly recommend if wanting to learn Arabic.

This review is actually for her 1502 class. Professor Ghali is nice and caring. You will have a discussion board question every week and in class discussions. Attendance matters, not much but it can drop your grade if you miss say 6 classes. She sometimes makes you align with what she believes so when you post discussions, write notes in class.

One of the best teachers ive ever had. tries to make the work load as simple as possible for the students while still making sure we learn the information to do well. her teaching style is amazing, shes funny, pretty, and nice. only thing that people may not like is that attendance is mandatory.
A very good professor, she makes a point to really hear her students and gather their opinions. However If you don't like participating don't take her. She is an amazing professor though.
n

Dr. Ghali is really nice, and answers emails promptly. I liked this class, and it taught me a lot about Arab culture. However, towards the end just about every assignment had a movie that you had to pay for in order to do your homework. Not that it was expensive, we just already pay so much for college in general and we paid for a textbook.

Took ARBC-3211 over the summer. For a 3 credit hour class the work involved should have warranted at least 4. Three discussions per week, each requiring no less than 500 words. Lengthy lecture videos, excessive amount of resources required. Watched several films, read books, wrote way too many papers for a non-major class. Not worth the headache.

the TA's teach the class, I had Miriam, she was a sweet girl but she made the class soo boring that it felt really long. easy work but it was textbook heavy. the TA would also be so mad at us if she spoke and no one answered, understandable tho. You do have to meet with David one time for a grade (zoom call) hes sweet tho just boring class.

Attendance is mandatory, but I missed a few classes, and it only hurt me a little. He answers emails quickly and is always willing to help. You literally just watch movies about Latin American history and do some quizzes and canvas/discussion posts. Very easy general education course.
This class almost made me start a therapy that I've been denying for years. Do not recommend.
class was overall pretty easy, mostly graded on movie and textbook quizzes. midterm and final were both online but had lockdown browsers and had essay prompts.

Amazing professor, only saw him once or twice tho. The TA Diana was beyond amazing as well. The class does have a weekly discussion board which you have to answer to two classmates, two quizzes, and watching a film + reading textbook. There's two exams, pretty easy but both include short and long essays. Overall great experience!

Dr. Dalton appeared in class for the first two weeks of the semester. I was excited for this class; I wanted to learn more. And I feel like I did, but I could've interacted more if there had been someone actively talking and explaining. The TA did a great job with what she had to work with. The workload can be heavy, so stay on track.

I saw Dr. Dalton maybe twice in the semester and the rest was taught by a TA which I was quite disappointed in because I was really excited for this course and I feel like I was not pushed as much as I could've been if he was there because I find the material interesting and he seemed very passionate about all of the material before he left.

Professor Dalton I saw maybe twice throughout the semester, but overall the LTAM 1502 course was disappointing. Being asynchronous, you only met once a week in class with a TA who did a very boring lecture. The movies were long and difficult to follow sometimes. I did not retain much of what I learned because it was so uninteresting.

Very boring lectures which are mainly taught by the TA. I've only ever seen Dr. Dalton twice and homework can be overbearing sometimes. Just pay attention in class and make sure to prepare for tests outside of class.

Professor himself is a great person and passionate about Latin American studies but due to his schedule he is not necessarily there for classes. My course is a one day class and the rest online so I can't say much about him. LTAM course is fairly easy but easy to procrastinate if you don't like to read or sit through a movie to then discuss on both
Good Goood Good

Overall, Professor Dalton is very knowledgeable and passionate about everything Latin America. I did find that the homework was pretty heavy, and the old-fashioned approach to exams (writing essays by hand, etc) isn't the most practical. Despite this, I am definitely a lot more interested in Latin American culture than ever before :)

I have taken Dr Dalton in LTAM 1502 and two higher level summer courses. He is great and helps you out whenever you ask him. He is the sole reason that I added an LTAM major to my degree and it has been a great decision.
David  David David DAvid

Do NOT take unless it's required. This class meets once a week & the rest is online. You're required to read a chapter, watch a film (which is between 1-2 hours long), participate in an online discussion based on both and discuss what was read and watched in class all in one week. Also, exams have mc & an essay, which is due at the end of class..
Good is a great person, really good, the best.

He knows a lot about the text, but he is an unorganized professor. Idk if he's new at teaching, but he clearly struggles. The formatting is lazy and he seems to not know how to teach. Also a bad grader, he'll grade on a writing assignment and not give back any feedback and will just expect u to fix it in next essay. He's lazy and I don't recommend
for a 1000 level course it is quite rigorous, he assigns 2 quizzes and a discussion board every week. Be ready to read and participate in his class.

Dr.Dalton is a good teacher, he's very passionate on what he teaches. There's movies you have to watch every week and read the assigned textbook, with that you will have a discussion board every week. There's two quizzes one specifically from the textbook, and one from the movie. I found them pretty easy to do.If you do your readings you'll be fine

For an online class, it wasn't bad. You have work each week that doesn't take too much time and you meet once a week with a TA. As long as you do your work, you'll be fine. You do have to do a group paper though

For a summer class, this class was quite rigorous. You watch 2 films a week and have to write some mini or full essay each week. You do have the opportunity to peer review for credit, but overall this was quite the difficult class. If you get behind at all, then you're totally screwed. I don't know how people could handle more than just this class.
Do not take this class w this professor

Worst Spanish professor I have had at UNC Charlotte. The class had no engagement, no interaction, and it was hard to learn because she spoke so quietly. There was clear favoritism, and if you were not one of the preferred students, you received little to no support.
The sweetest professor i've ever had. She's great at teaching, repetition and practice is key to the class. Quizzes and exams were very similar to the homework.
Very sweet and caring. Explains everything in depth and repetition is key for this course. She's very understanding, homework is a lot but it's not hard.

Homework is due every night before class. They will tank your grade if you don't do them. Accessible outside of class and is very Spanish beginner-friendly. Super sweet and only wants her students to succeed. Take her if you can.

Amazing professor! The sweetest person and passionate about teaching. Willing to explain concepts, accessible outside of class, and welcomes questions. Grades fairly and wants her students to succeed. Homework due every night before class. Stay on top of assignments and prepare for exams and you will do well. Highly recommend her!
Everything we did went along with the tests and homework.

Absolutely the sweetest Spanish professor at UNCC. She genuinely cares about everyone and tries her best to make sure you understand the material. Learning a new language is definitely challenging, but as long as you do the homework and attend the lecture then you will be ok. Lectures are a bit of repeating whatever the homework was however

Padilla was a great professor; however, you do your homework before class, and then go to class, and she is going over everything you taught yourself. But as long as you're okay with teaching yourself the material, everything is super easy. Her tests are exactly what was on the previous quiz + some extra information. Overall easy credits.

Very nice lady and very understanding. Only complaint is that attendance is mandatory, and the assignments are a lot for a beginner level course. I don't think that 15 assignments per week is necessary for an elective class. Other than that, she is very kind and will help you in areas that you are struggling.

I'm not sure why her ratings are so low. She is probably one of the sweetest professors I've had at UNCC. She is very understanding and as long as you pay attention and actually learn the material you should be fine. Not alot of work at all. Only thing I struggled with was attending class which is a grade!

Class only met once a week which I found to be very unhelpful. Class was quite neutral, felt like we did the same thing every week. Not too sure if I would take her again, as I didn't find class very exciting or inspiring. However, she is an easy grader - at least for the lower levels.

This class was challenging but if you do your work you should be fine. She only teaches in spanish in this class (4233) so if you honestly aren't good at speaking and listening do not take this class. However, if you are take it. There is a final written project, 3 exams, and only 1 homework assignment per week. It is definitely doable.

This was the easiest class I have taken all semester, I really enjoyed Ms.Padilla-Falta. We only met once per week and the work was online, you only came to class for lectures and exams she gives you amazing study guides for every exam so all you really have to do is pay attention during the lecture, study your notes, and or the textbook.

Terrible rambles in a monotoned voice you could go to sleep to the entire semester. Never gives you a grading scale on anything her grading is done entirely on her opinion and can fluctuate greatly between projects so good luck trying to plan out what you need to make on your next test. She will refuse to show you why you got a question wrong.

Professor Padilla-Falto is probably one of the best language teachers I've ever had. She doesn't demand much outside of class except for a couple quick homework assignments. I plan to stick with her as my Spanish professor for as long as I can.

Professor Padilla-Falto is a wonderful professor who clearly enjoys what she teaches and does an amazing job at it. It is a 4000-level course so there is a lot of material to take in, but tests are open book and her canvas page is meticulously outlined with for the class material. Incredibly lovely lady from all of my interactions with her!
Really easy going semester, profesora makes learning really accessible and she is super kind and understanding!

She is a very good person, but by far the worst professor I've had at UNCC. I can't recall a time she was fully prepared; she's a super tough grader, and she's quick to throw out accusations towards students about using AI or translation. Again, really nice person, but that does not make a good professor. This class was the worst class I've taken

She graded rough drafts of papers as if they were final drafts, which made things difficult. Even some of the native speakers struggled with the grammar in this class. Overall, I just think the grading was too tough. It wasn't too much work, though, and I really enjoyed being in class with her. She made things super fun!

I had a hard semester in regard to mental health, and she was incredibly supportive. I opened up to her and she gave me ample time to make up assignments and gave me grace for late work. She is a very understanding and kind woman whose care for her course and love for teaching shines through.
Professor Lawson was amazing. She made learning and coming to class fun. Homework was completed online and class was used for practice. Tests were easy and fairly graded.
Professor Lawson is super sweet and makes it very easy to learn the material. I highly recommend taking her class!
She made learning Spanish so much easier. Her PowerPoints helped a lot. She is also very helpful when you have questions and is easy to reach over email if needed.

My favorite Spanish Professor! She is super kind and clear when explaining things. If you do not understand something she is very willing to stop and help. It helps a lot if you are willing to participate in class, and that could just mean occassionally answering questions!

Super sweet professor. You do have to interact with other classmates in this class (as most Spanish classes do). Explains in a way you can understand. Homework is on McGraw Hill and can be long sometimes. Consists of 3 exams and an oral exam. Allows half point for exams and that really helped keep my grade up. Overall nice and understanding!

Accuracy is essential, and translating into Spanish is not an easy task. As a native speaker, he has been very helpful in improving my skills in the discipline. Translation requires a level of precision that goes beyond simply speaking Spanish.
The worst professor I have experienced at UNC Charlotte. Very rude, tough grader and does not care about his students. Avoid this professor at all costs.

actually one of the worst professors I have ever had. first B I have received here after previously getting all As, and Ive taken multiple other spanish classes with other professors and I was fine. he does not teach, the only thing you will learn on is the class work book which quizzes take forever to read for and do. DO NOT take him.

He is the worst professor in languages . Like he is so rude when you ask questions. He thinks he knows everything and his Spanish sounds broken , his Spanish grammar is awful. He grades so late and gives unclear instructions. He makes no sense in his assignments. avoid him and take native speaking teachers:) they know what they are talking about.
He is the worst in the translation depa

Nagano sensei FTW!! She is so funny, sweet and a great instructor. Has great energy and will help you when you ask, no matter the question. TA Akari was very nice as well. Both graded work within a 2-3 week window. Only downside was a classmate, Mr. Tristan, whom we all tolerated but Nagano made sure to silence him if he got too rowdy.

To be fair, a lot of my experience in actually learning in this class came from the homework. Lectures are mostly just review but still very helpful for retaining what you learn during personal study. Professor is very sweet and helpful in correcting your mistakes.

Lectures heavily and grades tough. One thing I did not like was how she did not give us any links to her slides or any sort of study guide for her exams (there are two exams). Would not recommend anyone who thinks its a easy class.

Nagano Sensei was super sweet. She was really sympathetic towards my situation and really tried to help me get back on track and made sure to keep checking in on me while I had a NIGHTMARE of a sem. And btw, Japanese is one of the hardest languages to learn for native english speakers-- FSI category 5 (didn't know that until it was too late lmfao)

Super nice and chill. There is a lot of work but I mean it's learning a language.
Obviously there's a slight issue with accent and occasionally mispronouncing or forgetting a word in English but her accent is relatively easy to understand.

I absolutely loved this class and this professor! Lectures are amazing - especially if you're already interested in Japanese culture - and were very engaging. Homework was manageable, there were regular readings, a few group projects, and a bigger project towards the end of the semester. I would highly recommend taking this class if you can!
Amazing professor. One of the most enjoyable classes I've ever taken.

Nagano sensei was not a bad instructor and had clear grading expectations, however, it was clear she displayed favoritism to certain students and helped them out more. Her teaching style and explanations are thorough and she is pretty chill but, I personally would not take her again.
