Be ready to learn the whole class on your own because he talks to himself in circles the whole class. Its not a hard class, but  you have to self teach it all

Class is going to depend very much on your client/project, but it's probably not going to be that hard. Stotts does great and yes, Friday lectures are usually excluded. Great for gen ed requirements and also to get actual programming experience. Try to go in with friends, or you might be playing Russian roulette with whatever group you get.

523 is my favorite COMP class, though there's a lot of variance in terms of the project you're assigned and the teammates you choose. We had class MWF, but Stotts cancelled nearly all F lectures and several M/W lectures. Lectures are ineffective when everyone is working on a distinct project. Different from a normal class but can be a great time.

Stotts is a good professor and is very quietly funny. The class was structured with one midterm, several assignments, participation, and the final. So there were not a whole lot of opportunities to get points. Nice guy and definitely knows what he is teaching about. I liked the class and would probably take one with Stotts again.

Very easy class if you do exactly what the assignments ask. The grading on assignments is very lenient as long as you know what you are talking about. He takes attendance on random days. Only a midterm and a final, and you can make a cheatsheet.

Not a great class, but not too hard. I skipped a lot of lectures because I found them boring and not helpful. There weren't too many assignments and they all built off of each other. Everything in the class is graded by an in-person demo. Super stressful and annoying for me personally. The exams were not very hard.
Nothing in this class is difficult besides the exams, but even those don't make up a large portion of the overall grade.

Most of the complaints on this professor are from students who likely ChatGPT'd their way through the course and couldn't explain what they did during demos. Also he posted lectures and videos for the topics. If you understood what you were doing in your assignments and projects then this class is ridiculously easy. Nirjon is great professor!

Don't really understand what all this hate is about. This professor was better than others in the CS department and his expectations were really clear. I mean if you just read his announcement, he practically told you each question on the final. His tests weren't bad. His expectations were clear and the class was easy if you study and do your work.
OK class not considering exams which are extremely difficult for no reason.

Don't recommend to take this class. People who had taken this class told me that it would be a good elective, but it wasn't -- exam questions are tricky and professor doesn't know how to design exams.

Poorly designed quizzes and midterm. Otherwise, the class is worse than mediocre. The problem is that professor doesn't teach you anything during lectures and then asks you questions on midterms that are not even doable in an hour. No clue what the quizzes are for for each assignment. 6 assignments, 6 class works, 6 quizzes, midterm, final - bad!!!

This is my first time writing a review on RMP because it's the first class I've taken where the material wasn't actually taught. The midterm and quizzes are poorly written, and with Tarik essentially running the class, it's no surprise it has turned out so lackluster.

If you do an assignment perfectly you get an 80 + your score on the quiz. Quizzes are way too hard and the midterm was super specific trivia/gotcha questions that barely applied what we learned. Instead of applying the android dev skills we are learning, we are expected to memorize tiny specific details for quizzes and exams. Don't take this class.
Painfully difficult class to succeed in.

Assignments are straightforward at times, but sometimes they require knowledge beyond the scope of what is taught in the class. Midterms and quizzes are tough. My guess is that the TAs, not Professor Nijorn himself, create the midterm and quiz questions. This might explain why many students perform poorly on these assessments.

Exams and quizzes are made by Tarik and other TAs, but Tarik can't create effective midterm questions. Many students did poorly on the midterm, and having a quiz for each assignment feels excessive, especially given the poorly crafted questions. Avoid this class if possible; it's frustrating to pay tuition for a class that isn't properly taught.

Not an easier elective as it used to be. He made the class more difficult, and I don't think he really knows the stuff he's teaching well. Midterm was very difficult, and I can't imagine how difficult the final is going to be.

Nirjon was good, no complaints. His lectures could be boring but they basically give you a walkthrough for the assignments which build off the last.  Class is easy if you attend lecture and complete the "Class Works".  As stated below grading was a little frustrating as it took all of class period for the TA to get to you. Overall great class

programming assignments were fair and not very difficult, they are pretty much cumulative and so is the final project. Dry lectures, but nice fella. the grading system for the assignments was pretty frustrating b/c they need to be manually checked off but the prof or TA and you end up sitting around waiting. exam questions try to trip you up though

This is an easy class if you put in the work. And you will be learning more on your own than from the professor. But don't be mistaken, you will get a lot out of this. 

By the end I had a functional mobile application that I am very proud of.

Despite the deteriorating CS faculty at UNC, this class is one of the few that is truly amazing. It's the hardest class I've taken, but it genuinely teaches you. Saba is generous with grading, and there's a TA for every schedule. It gets much harder after the first midterm, so reconsider if you're very busy. Otherwise, this class is a masterpiece.
Amazing class and genuinely learned so much. Nicest professor ever. I love that guy!

This will probably be the hardest class you ever take (content-wise; passing isn't as hard). You may understand very little because the content is super theoretical and might not even exist. Saba lectures fast, so LOCK IN and go to every one! Homework's hard and graded harshly but exams are easier and curved by free points. Take 455,550,M381 first!

While the content was difficult, Saba and TAs are more than willing to explain throughly during office hours. The problem sets always require a bit of ingenuity, but the programming assignments are almost always very straightforward. The exams were challenging but the final grade cutoffs are rather generous. I really enjoyed his class.

Agreed with other reviews there was a great opportunity to learn through this course; however, grading was at times punitive or ambiguous. Rubrics were never posted before assignments or projects. Verbal explanations of grading often felt vague, and quizzes were quite difficult, with some questions ambiguous or asking for material not covered.

Amazing prof. Very difficult class, but tried his best to respond to any confusion you may have (during or after class). Good homework and clear grading scheme. Not a tough grader. Accessible after class, and many oh offered by him and TAs. Strongly recommend to anyone who's interested.

Probably the best professor I've had from the COMP department. Yes the content is difficult, but him and the TAs are always willing to help and the structure of the psets really do make you think and maybe even learn something. Taking COMP455 (or any abstract math classes) before this will make the class easier to digest for sure

Cryptography is a challenging and interesting class that Saba teaches well. The class is structured  predictably, the TAs are helpful (thanks David), and the programming assignments are very cool applications. The midterm was hard but his letter grade ranges were forgiving in return. Overall a great class and a very cool niche in CS.
Amazing lecturer! Hard concepts but he makes them interesting

Dr. Saba is very passionate about cryptography. He brings the same enthusiasm to teaching students. I took COMP537-Cryptography. A difficult course for sure, with lots of assignments, and very little to start from. He makes up for this through his and TA's office hours. He's very kind and understanding when it comes to both assignments and exams.

Saba is a great lecturer, and I found all the material accessible for someone with few privacy knowledge. He clearly shows that he is interested in providing a good class curriculum by asking for feedback and hearing back from students on implemented feedback. He encourages students to be more involved in the department as well. Great guy

One of the best additions to the UNC CS department, Saba is kind, caring, chill, and funny while being able to teach advanced cryptography and privacy-related courses with incredible effectiveness. He motivates students very well in pursuing the material and is super receptive to feedback. One of the best professors I've ever had!

Saba is a great professor with a true passion for the subject he teaches. I learned more in his cryptography class than I've ever learned in another class, but it was simultaneously the most difficult class I've ever taken.

Saba's classes have been my favorite ones at UNC but also probably the hardest. He is very accessible and wants people to do well! Has tons of office hours if you don't understand. The class policies are very collaborative and designed for people to learn the material well.
I had 0 formal coding experience and this class was tough.

Has an incredible industry background, and is always happy to talk about what he's done and how he got there. A great lecturer in all the material we covered, from applied linear algebra to concepts on virtual reality hardware. Homeworks are long, but feel really useful towards your own skills and what you'll need for the final project. Awesome guy

I took the honors class and it was a nightmare. His lectures were poorly executed, as he would often rush past important details; i had to teach myself everything. He also had a propensity to only call on the male students in the classroom. I often felt like he was talking down to many of the other female students and didn't take us as seriously.
Great person and professor. If you do assignments and go to class, you'll do well

This course is pretty easy if you have previous coding experience and it is structured very clearly. There are a few homework assignments and required labs, but the attendance is not mandatory and he posts all of the lecture slides on canvas. He also allows cheat sheets for exams, so you don't really have to study at all. Overall good prof!

Attendance matters for Lab but not for lecture! Professor Marks is a really cool professor. He has extensive experience with the tech field like Sony, Google, and others he might say. Easy class if you have coding experience, but even without it just make sure to ask a lot of questions to your TA's or on Piazza.

Rick as a professor is fine, he incorporates his experience into lectures and gives extra credit, but flies through concepts. The class itself is tough without coding experience- I had to rely on experienced classmates to help me, and comp110 helped some. The homeworks and tests can be long and challenging, but the final project is pretty enjoyable

Marks' lectures are AWESOME! Super engaging lectures. The course work was perfect for an intro course. As someone who has 0 coding experience it was a little more difficult, but if you have taken a coding class before it will be easy.
Overall, he's super mellow and chill. The difficulty level is very reasonable for an intro level class, and you grade is dependent on a lot of factors.

He was very nice and approachable inside and outside of class. There is a group project at the end of the semester that felt very rushed, but he seemed to grade pretty leniently because it is a first-year class. The midterm was straightforward if you study the slides

Rick's lectures were interesting and pretty easy to follow. I enjoyed the concepts in this class and learned a lot from it. Final project was good experience and he grades very leniently. The midterm also was very easy with basic straight forward questions. Overall, he is a really cool guy and makes the class fun and simple. Definitely recommend.
Overall kind of boring lecturer, but the class wasn't too difficult. I did find hard to get help from him outside of class though and ended up having to get help from other professors.
He was an ok professor, I just didn't enjoy the class very much and found him to be kinda boring.
he's a really nice guy who is clearly passionate about the subject and cares for his students
Insanely knowledgable and respected professor in the AR/VR space. Taking COMP 590 (VR & 3D Graphics) – although extremely challenging – was my favorite class at UNC.

The lectures were informative, and he was readily available for office hours. The 1st half of the class (3D Graphics) was more mathematical, requiring linear algebra. The 2nd half (VR) was more conceptual. The lectures fairly prepared me for the midterm, and the exam itself was fair. The final project's grading could have been more detailed.

Pretty good for a first-time professor! We had multiple quizzes, HWs, midterm, & a final project made in VR. The workload was manageable & fair overall. There was a lot of math involved in the 1st part of the class about graphics, but the topics got more conceptual after that. If you're interested in VR/graphics, he can provide a lot of expertise!

Interesting class and the prof was pretty funny sometimes. Very knowledgeable. Barely anyone ever showed up to class which is probably why the other reviews didn't get a good grade. If you go to class, you learn a lot. If you get a good group for HW and final project you can easily get an A. Generous grading and a good guy.

Waste of a semester. unengaging lectures. 4 grades TOTAL. hw required to be done in groups-easier to grade ig, yet grades werent returned until end of semester & was limited to single letter grades rather than question-by-question score breakdown (including midterm). too little feedback far too late. didnt learn much. better off reading a textbook

I have no clue what to say, I don't even know what is going on in this class. Avoid at ALL COSTS. He's too busy working his job at SAS to teach us. 

But... that's just my opinion.

This was probably the worst class i have taken at UNC. Throughout the semester, we had 2 hw assignments, one midterm, and one final project. The midterm was hard, worth 30%, fully written by chatgpt, and we didn't get our grade back until finals season. his grading criteria sucks and his lectures are disorganized and he uses someone else's slides.
Hes the GOAT. DA GOAT

He's clearly passionate about the content and does a great job answering questions after class. Great overview of various topics in AI and fair/lenient grading. Definitely go to lectures and make sure you get a good group for your HW and final project. Slides are usually the same as previous years.

The course is very insightful and you have the opportunity to learn a lot. Jorge doesnt do well in teaching the content, most of them are tangents on a slideshow, which is not engaging whatsoever. Theres also no practical experience, as the course believes in learning the theory behind ML. Grading and assignments were easy, online exams.

The 5pm lectures are kind of rough. He is actually a pretty good lecturer and clearly very knowledge. The course is adapted from the graduate version so if you just look at the slides you will be very confused, as he cuts out some of the out of scope math. THERE IS NO MORE EC, so likely harder than the older reviews suggest, but u learn a lot.

If you do the homework and understand the lectures, you're good. The exams are difficult (worth 90% of your grade) but he is an understanding person, and curves generously at the end. He drops your lowest midterm.

Lectures were unpassionate, filled with technical jargon, with little explanation. All homework was graded for participation, making it very hard to correct wrong strategies. Zero study resources were ever provided, and class averages on midterms were squarely in the 50-60 range. He obviously cares very little about teaching or any of his students.

Lectures are extremely boring. He is literally an automatic text-to-speech reader and does nothing except for reading his slides word for word. You are better off not going to class. Exams are not the most difficult, and there is a curve at the end.
Good lecturer, fair tests, I didn't have any real complaints.

Not very much homework, lecture attendance is not mandatory nor needed. His policy on makeups is extreme, without my UAA I would have been forced to drop due to missing the first midterm. Otherwise very nice and humorous guy.

Overall a pretty solid professor. The class was quite difficult and after the first midterm, the teaching felt slow and sometimes not as engaging as it used to be. However, the homework was insightful, the exams were perfectly fair and the curve was generous. Thiagu is very intelligent and there is a lot of valuable theory being taught.

He was a superb professor! Very intelligent it was an honor to learn from him. 

People complaining because you have to learn difficult material are Lazy Bums LOL!

Not much to say about him. Fairly dull lecturer but nonetheless taught the content well. Has detailed slides so you can just rely on those if you need to. Homeworks and midterms are doable as long as you study.

Worst professor I have ever had. Gave my group a failing grade on our paper because we asked for a one day extension (religious holiday). He holds grudges if you ask for an extension because he has to give them under certain circumstances (other groups who got an extension also failed in prev semesters). He makes up his own rules so you cant argue.

Good sense of humor, but lecture material was pretty dry. He did explain the concepts well though. Homework was fair and had questions that were relatively similar to exam questions. Exams were tough (especially the length), but our overall grades were curved. Lots of material to learn, practice, and remember, but very doable.

The Slides were ok. The lectures were boring and I felt like sleeping. The homeworks were ok, you would need to go through the slides and go to office hours early. The HW were doable. The midterm and final exams were very hard. One thing I wish I did: Reading the book and practicing from the book for being competent for exams.

Absolute favorite! Personality reminds me of Carl from Up; Class is hard, but he really makes you fall in love with learning (I am not a math fan or coding whiz). As long as you make a sincere effort, your grade will be fine. UNC CS needs more talented individuals who excel at CS and teaching instead of department politics.
You can just rely on the lecture slides for the material. Tests were more difficult than the homework but they weren't that bad. Solid lecturer and welcomes questions.

He's not bad, but nothing really stands out about him -- all he really does is read slides in his lectures, which can be pretty boring, but they do help you understand the material enough to do well on the homework assignments and exams. Grades do take a long time to get back, though, and I'm not really sure what my final grade is going to be.

He is very accessible outside of class and makes things digestible in class (so make sure to go). Directions for term paper were a little unclear. Fair grader on homeworks and tests (which were not difficult). Sometimes he would omit problems and leave them as extra credit (leaving most of the class with a 150% for one of the homework assignments).
don't take if you haven't taken a coding class before, you will be confused.

No required attendance and slideshows posted so you can teach content to yourself if you like. Cheatsheet allowed on the three quizzes and final is a group project that isn't too bad. Overall recommend, pretty easy especially if you have previous cs or stat knowledge.

I took data 110 with professor lee and the class overall was very easy, we were allowed a cheat sheet during exams and the final was a pretty fun project that could be added to your resume. Overall, was a great insightful class that was not too challenging.

She doesn't care about her students and is extremely rude. Ive seen other students come to her with personal matters and instead of being understanding she refuses to give extensions or any type of understanding for a 100 level class.  Her grading is also all over the place, lectures are boring, and her TA's are accusatory.

Harlin is a great person and very caring of her students. The class is not hard to do well in at all, but her lectures tend to be really boring and I found myself not able to pay attention. Her lecture slides are also not very clear and can be really confusing. I had to teach myself most of the course content, but it wasn't hard.

Harlin was a great professor to have in Data 110! She is easy to reach and very accommodating. Attendance is optional, but you have the opportunity for extra credit if you attend a certain number of lectures, and her slides are posted on Canvas. The material is easy to learn if you put in the effort for the quizzes.
Very kind, down-to-earth, and caring professor. The class was easy if you paid attention in lecture or had stats/coding experience. TAs and the professor were accessible outside of class.
Chiller. The difficulty doesn't represent the class though, it's not that easy if you aren't computer science or data science.

Extremely kind person, and was a blast to have as a professor. Would highly recommend this as an intro to anyone even dabbling in the idea of Data Science, she makes things very easy to understand. She's down to earth, and is actively working towards our sucess. We were allowed cheatsheets on both of our midterms. Highly recommend!

Professor Lee is an incredibly kind and caring professor. She knows the material well and clearly gets excited by it. The homework can be time-consuming sometimes but there's not many and they really help you understand the different concepts. The class is very statistics heavy, but the exams are pretty easy. Professor Lee is also very accessible.
Very kind professor! She is easy to reach outside of class, incredibly helpful, organized, and gives lots of extra credit opportunities.

Easy class if you have experience with stats and coding. Only challenging thing can be the coding HW, but they aren't bad if you pay attention to lectures - TAs and Lee are accessible for help. Really comfortable class and a great intro if you're considering Data Science.

extremely easy if you have any background in stats/data science. The 4 HWs, 11 recitation labs, midterm, and final project were all free 100s. this class taught less than one semester of AP stats I'm ngl. recitation is mandatory, lecture is not (and slides are on canvas). gave tons of extra credit. lee is very kind and a good lecturer.

Harlin is absolutely amazing. She is genuinely so caring, and for the first time this class is being offered, she did an absolutely amazing job. Graded by 4 HWs, Labs, Final Project, and One Midterm. Veryyyy easy if you pay attention and have experience in Data Science (ex. STOR 120, STOR 320, etc.)
goat. super chill, derives ideas bottom up. dense but well organized lectures
The exams for this course are difficult if you don't have a very strong math foundation. However, the assignments and teamwork are very helpful. You can learn a lot from them.
Do not take this class.

Prof. Oliva is fantastic. Amazingly intelligent, articulate, and he stands out as one of my favorite professors at Carolina. That being said, he teaches a difficult course—be prepared to work. There will not be much hand holding and lectures will focus on key theoretical concepts instead of implementation.

Junier Oliva is by far one the best professors I have ever had. The class itself (Machine Learning) was extremely difficult, requiring somewhere about 5-10 hours per lecture to supplement, understand, and digest the material, especially for some later lectures. However Oliva makes sure to teach the nuance and it makes for a very eye-opening course.

He covered a good number of introductory ML topics but I don't think I took away much from the course in terms of understanding. Inconsistent grading criteria and a large gap in knowledge expected between class and the final project and exam. Other than bits of theory and derivations, I almost feel like self-study would be more productive.

The professor is passionate about the subject but he doesn't realize it is under the CS department. The only coding component is Google Colab assignments you'll figure out on your own. Lectures and the midterm are entirely math-based with no programming instruction. Avoid if you want to learn practical Python skills for building and training models

Definitely not an undergrad level course. You need a good foundation in stats, cal, and linear algebra to take this course. Otherwise, I don't think you would understand much of what he is saying. So I rec you don't take this class if you don't have enough prerequisites. Otherwise, he is nice and passionate about ML.

What's the probability of this professor understanding that the students taking the class have other things to do? Probably another annoyingly long mathematical equation involving various interpretations that would be infinitely easier to understand if the professor actually taught the class instead of dumping random equations every lecture.

He's nice and enjoys his specialization but he's teaching this course to undergrads at a grad level. Lectures filled with formulas that nobody understands how to work with. Idk how to actually train a model, what a tensor is, or how to use tensorflow. Only take this if you wanna research. Don't take if you wanna be an ML engineer, Udemy is better.

One of those classes where you go to lecture and watch as 1 person understands everything, and the professor takes this to mean that everybody gets it. 

This is a MATH/STOR course, not a COMP course. Heavy on the symbols, low on connections to real life. Little programming. 

Strong assumption that you memorized all of LA, Probability, and Calc 3.

Homework and tests could be stressful for this course but the teacher is very approachable and responsive to students' questions and concerns. He seems to be very passionate about his field and is an excellent resource for anyone who really wants to learn

This is a GRAD level class not undergrad. He taught the exact same material as his COMP 755. Possibly the worst comp class I have had at UNC. In order to do well on exams/HW you have to already know ML/LinAlg well. He has no problem assigning an exam, project, presentation, and homework all the same week. He curves but not worth the stress at all
goat. don't listen to 560 reviews. knows and teaches material extremely well

Shashank is the most brilliant professor in the university. He is also one of the best instructors in the CS department. The course is very math-heavy, but he cares deeply about the students' learning, and has an extraordinary knack to explain complex math concepts and equations in English.

There are homework and quizzes almost every week, and the classes are pure math calculations, and the homework after class is all code. 
But I understand some of the knowledge of deep learning by learning to derive these formulas. These are somewhat useful for my job search because I will be asked these questions in written tests and interviews.

At the beginning of class he said that lectures wouldnt be recorded, and there would be no practice midterm. But students kept on asking him for it, and he finally started recording classes and gave a practice midterm which was not useful at all in preparation for the exam. Overall, a pretty difficult course.

There was only 1 TA with 1 hour office hours a week. The professor had an appointment based 1 hour weekly office hour. There was Piazza for unlimited questions. If you are taking more than 12 credit hours and taking this course, I would advise not to. Make sure that you have a good foundation in Probability before taking this course.

I think because this is a 500 level and artificial intelligence course, and hence the professor made the course challenging. I think its not the professors fault, but I think that the department makes these rules. I think the course should have been made easier since it was the professors first time teaching this course.

This is a hard course, labeled as "Higher Level Course". 30% got A/A-, 55% got B+/B/B-, 15% got remaining. He teaches theory in class and did not type/write even one line of programming in class. In the assignments you had to do programming. The midterm was hard, he used chatGPT to make the midterm question.
AI is a buzzword. If for some reason you are not able to get in this course, because too many students want to take it. Do UC Berkeley's CS188, which is freely available online.

Very heavy curve which is a bit stressful since you don't really know what you'll get until the end.

Course content wise, I thought it was good overall. There were 3 units (search, probability/bayesian stuff, and ML). I thought search and ML were nice, but the bayesian/probability unit wasn't the best.

pretty good class for first offering, lectures could get difficult to follow at times. professor is clearly smart and knowledgeable. hard assignments and exam but grade was curved and nobody failed. learned a lot

A very nice guy who wants you to learn but grading was much more difficult than it needed to be. Only one midterm that accounted for 40% of the grade and that was unreasonably difficult and lengthy. Class was meant to be curved but it barely helped the grade in the end. The final project/homework were not given enough weightage to make any impact.

Shashank was clearly new to teaching, and there were times when he wasn't the greatest teacher, but he cared about students and learning and was pretty funny and generous with grading. He improved as the semester passed and would probably be a good choice for this class in the future. Overall a solid person and teacher.

Shashank is the smartest man in the computer science department. His lectures were amazing and you will learn a ton. One of the best classes I took. There is only one midterm, so study hard. The homework can get tricky. There was a curve at the end, however you still need to do well.

This is a review for COMP 581 - Intro to Robotics
Great class with hands-on group projects where you build your lego robot and program it to complete tasks. The material covered in the lectures and exams is relevant to help you build your robot.

My only complaint is that sometimes the lectures move slowly covering basic introductions for too long.

Why are there negative reviews? Because there were no quizes or exams, and no one studied regularly. When professor asked students questions, no one answered because they did not study. Because of this, Professor would never offer a course again where there is no quiz or exams. And its the students fault.
Definitely one of the few professors who really care about students.
A hidden gem in the CS department!

One major project over the course of an entire semester was a bit underwhelming.  We wasted a lot of time doing nothing really besides talking and spinning our wheels. The class was easy, so it gets some points from me on that side, but the course wasn't good.  I had harder classes as a freshmen.  Dan is a nice guy though. All around average.
Awesome professor. Learned a lot about research from this course. Doing the research project was fun.

Human Robot Interaction course. A research based course. Awesome Professor, good as a Kris Jordan. No midterms, quizes or exams. Projects, discussions, papers and presentations. If you are interested in an intro to research course and research related to Robotics, this course is for you.

This review is actually for COMP 581 which was not listed. Professor Szafir was an excellent intro to robotics professor. The most challenging part about the course was the robotics assignments in which you have to design your own controller for a robot. However, pay attention in class and you will be fine as he gives EC and allows retakes.

Mike Reed is an amazing professor. Lectures were so good and genuinely taught me so much about graphics, different ways in mathematics to do the same thing, and how to write very performative code. Take this class if you wanna learn from one of the best in this field and have it lectured to you in a very clear and intuitive way. I love that guy!

I dont think people realize that Reed is a graphics legend. We are talking about the same dude that made skia (and sold it to Google). You won't learn cool 3D techniques (hence the course name) but for people interested in graphics it builds a solid grasp of techniques used in the field. Taking this class is not even negotiable if you like graphics
This guy would teach you how to do your finals.

Reed is a great lecturer and professor. His passion for graphics and teaching couldn't be more clear. His lectures are easy to follow and informative. Assignments are difficult, so start early and follow along. Very clear grading scheme, most of final grade is from 6 projects. You will learn a ton about programming skills, graphics, and c++.
Mike clocks in as the greatest graphics professor I've ever had.

I quite enjoyed this class. Honestly, I don't care about graphics that much; I mostly enjoyed the performance/software engineering aspects. Mike was very good at explaining things, though it was a hard class. All labs. Final (10% of grade) was basically a lab you had to do quick.

Mike is a great instructor; he goes over the implementations for the 6 labs in lecture. Grade is composed of 6 labs, each worth 15% and they build off eachother so its important you keep up with them. Final is basically like another lab where you implement 2/4 methods. Class is tough but fun, felt like I learned alot.

Best and clearest lecture slides in the COMP department. Labs were only hard because the sensors were not reliable but tests were pretty easy. Content is very interesting and I learned a lot. Would definitely recommend taking this class. But remember, there is a lot of unpredictability and a lot of uncertainty in robotics...

There wasn't too much homework, but there is a group project where you build a robot and design it for the given lab days. The labs get progressively harder and make up the bulk of the class grade, and took my group anywhere from 5 - 10 hours a week outside of class to prepare. The assignments/exams were fairly challenging (mostly trigonometry).

I took COMP 89 with professor Alterovitz. SUPER easy class. 3 assignments and 2 projects for the entire semester, no homework. Class can be boring sometimes but Professor Alterovitz is super passionate about what he researches and studies. He does not take attendance. I highly recommend taking this class for a FC and easy freshman launch.

He's very passionate about tech., only talked about robots, AI, & internet instead of many topics. Grade based on a few assignments and 2 presentations (7 & 15 minutes). Attendance policy is unclear but as far as I know, he did not record attendance (syllabus said he would take it 3 random days). Lectures are somewhat boring but the class is easy

Dr. Arguello is patient and cares about his students! The material could be confusing, but he explained assignments clearly in class. You can even replace a bad take-home midterm with a take-home final. He's passionate and lets you choose your own project topics and groups, making it more enjoyable.

Nice guy and interesting content but does not seem qualified to teach this course. Seemed like he was relearning the material as he looked at the slides. Exams are harder than other calc 3 midterms, just harder exams overall.
844/15pi as answer? wtf?
Exams are drier than a camel butt in Sahara desert, the numbers are insane, you'll see 3124pi/15 on the final. Dont take her.

From what I have heard, she is the best teacher in terms of explaining the material. The others are more of a learn-it-outside-of-class. However, she is very nitpicky about certain things on the tests. This semester we were the only class to have graded recitation quizzes and 3 midterms. (She doesn't tell you what the quiz is on week to week).

She is incredibly passive aggressive and evil. Doesn't curve and is dismissive to students. Each exam was a battle waged with pen and paper that I the student could not win. She writes textbook definitions on the black board so itty bitty that you can't see. You should just open up Khan academy, he will get you right.

Dr. Burkhead is a solid lecturer, with good notes released afterward. Unfortunately, every assignment or test is brutally difficult, she does not curve, and she is not flexible on any policy. I was unable to get out of bed for a week, and she did not allow any extensions or makeup. I do not recommend taking her class.

The instructor sometimes forgets her notes and stucks in front of the blackboard with no words to say, then the whole class waiting for her to continue; Her notes on board are in a mess. The HW grading criterions are harsh, and no lowest HW drop allowed. 3 midterms with each takes up 16%, maybe no policy to use final replace the lowest one. Regret.

Classes are pretty fast paced, so if you miss one thing she says in lecture, you could be lost for the rest of the class. She tries to describe concepts using analogies that just don't work. Carefully assess your abilities. There's no curve for this class at all. It's the only one among 233 courses that requires a weekly exam. Also, I've seen exams from other sections that had only five simple questions in 50 minutes, but Professor Burkhead's test contained more than 20 challenging and time-consuming problems, with no extra time given.

Dr. Burkhead's midterms were nearly impossible to finish within a 50-minute period which made them tough. She prepared us well for the final though. Sometimes it was more useful to focus on learning how to earn partial credit than getting the answers right. Not always the easiest to approach with questions but very accessible outside of class.

Lectures were ok, she was a fair grader and gave some partial credit but it was her teaching which was not great. It was mostly a flipped classroom and although other professors may not have taught as well or have been as organized, they at least curved their tests unlike her. I would take another professor if you want a good grade.
Professor's lectures are verbatim recitations from the textbook; tests prioritize memorization and are graded with a hint of autism.

Decent lectures but does not care or take time to help students even when they come to office hours. 
Extremely tough grader especially compared to other professors of same class, who give you opportunities to increase grades outside of tests. 
Full grade lower on average compared to other professors of same class.

Dr. Burkhead is very nice and is helpful in office hours. However, tests and homework are graded extremely harsh, and many times I felt like the lectures was just writing the textbook onto the board. Needed to memorize tons of information for tests. Class will be difficult no matter the professor.

Grades harshly on exams, which are mostly memorization. She barely curved at the end of the class but replaced the midterm with a final without mention in the syllabus, intended as a curve, punishing students who performed relatively consistently on exams. Lectures are usually straight out of the textbook.
Grades super hard and the grading guidelines make no sense at all. Even if you put the answer key word for word, you'd probably get an 80 on an assignment.

Lectures were unhelpful and the flipped classroom didn't work well. Homework was confusing, and even ULAs struggled with some questions. The professor helps if you ask but can be belittling. No curve when the class average was ~50, we were only allowed to retake 2 questions for half credit.

Worst prof I've ever had. Other Calc II classes were SO much easier: They had curves, extra credit, easier tests, and their professors were nicer and more accessible. burkhead doesnt care if the test avg is a 40, she will never curve or give extra credit. calc is inherently hard but she makes it so much harder than it needs to be. AVOID AT ALL COST

She uses a flipped classroom style, so you kinda have to teach yourself the content. Mandatory reading responses before lectures count towards your grade. She uses no notes and sometimes has a hard time making concepts easy to understand. Relies too much on you understanding the textbook before class. Take someone else if you can. Hard midterms.

Worst prof for calc 3. Take literally any other prof. Class averages for exams in her section were 20 points lower compared to other sections, yet there was no curve. For some reason she likes having 40-minute exams and then 35-minute lectures right after. The common final exam was much easier compared to her midterms.

this class had me questioning if i was cut out for math in general. don't take, no chance for improvement. i worked super hard too, never have i studied this much... did all the practice problems, read the textbook, maybe i really am not cut out for it lol :(

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

This is a really hard class and Burkhead does not make it easier. She spend the entire lecture doing proofs instead of teaching us how to apply the content to questions we will be seeing on the exam. The exams she writes are significantly harder than that of other professors. Nice person, unhelpful professor. Take literally anyone else.

Incredibly caring towards students and easy to access. Really emphasized the reasoning behind concepts! Tests matched the material decently well but homework felt a little off. Hosted a final review session which I really appreciated :) Hard class but I loved having her as a prof!

Please don't. Your life will be actually horrible with her - she is so hard compared to other calc 3 profs for no reason. 4 tests + recitation quizzes + she writes a horrendous final. Take with literally any one else it will be better.
Don't take pls. So hard for no reason compared to other calc 2 profs

Very solid Calc 3 professor; very willing to answer questions during lecture. Tests are generally in line with review packets and probably easier than them. Dr. Burkhead is fairly good at explaining the "why" behind things, so you'll be fine if you have a good mind for math and did decently in Calc 1 and 2.

Don't take this professor IF YOU CANNOT HANDLE THE FLIPPED CLASSROOM MODEL because she barely teaches anything in class. Your grade is completely dependent of the practice and the reading you do outside of class. There are no lectures, no slides, no notes, so if you are someone who needs those resources, don't take it with her. She doesn't teach.

Prof. Burkhead is very smart and a good teacher. However, the lectures are very fast-paced. You have to read the textbook before the classes to get the most out of them. The tests are not easy, but they are fair. Expectations for the class are very clear, and she drops a generous amount of assignments from your grade. I would recommend!

Her lectures are barely helpful and I had to teach myself this entire course because I learned nothing in the lecture. She is very kind and offers plenty of resources. The lectures, homework, and tests do not match each other making it hard to study.

My choice for calc 2 was either between Compton or Burkhead and I'm thrilled I chose Burkhead. Compton is an amazing professor but I believe Burkhead really tried to make connections with her students whether in class or outside.  She sometimes curves but tries not to if possible. Her homework consists of like 10-20 questions depending on the unit.

Words can not express how unnecessarily difficult she makes everything. My roomate was taking calc 2 but with a different prof and her tests were a million times easier. She's also just kind of patronizing. Don't take her.

A hard class for sure. Objectively she is a tough grader, and you should expect to put in a lot of time for this class, but she is organized, fair, and provides a lot of resources to help you learn. 

Also, knew all students by name after the couple of weeks.

I feel bad saying this because Dr. Burkhead is genuinely really nice lady but this class just wasn't it. I'm bad at math so I won't talk about how well things were explained but: 
-Recitations were graded by quizzes that, in my opinion, were harder than the exams. 
-Our exams were not curved, where other calc professors gave curves

In honor of everyone just bombing their finals I can say with absolute confidence: worst teacher at UNC.  I studied more than I ever have in the entirety of my life and have nothing to show for it. No one I know did well. She's not a bad person, just a bad teacher.

Why this professor is so against students succeeding, I'll never know. I'm a junior and have never had a teacher so woefully underprepared to assist students during lectures or office hours. Going genuinely was a waste of time, and no one would show up by the end of the semester. The tests are insanely difficult, and the majority of people fail.

DO NOT TAKE HER PLEASE!!!! Genuinely take any other professor. Lectures, homework, and recitations never align with the textbook material AND tests. She makes the tests far more difficult than necessary. The averages were always shockingly horrid and she straight up refuses to curve (first midterm had mean of 61) She wants her students to fail!

Very hard tests and content compared to other profs. Test questions are overly complicated and not enough time is given. She is nothing special as an educator and can be intimidating. I have not had a great experience with UNC math profs, I thought she would be good teacher thats hard. I was wrong. Just take it with another prof she kinda blows.

Very bad professor, a very fast-paced class does not care if you know the material or not. She does not curve tests and she expects you to know everything before class. I would not take this professor again since she grades harshly and does not give you opportunities to show improvement and improve your grade.

Easily the worst teacher I've had at UNC. Acts like she has something to prove and in doing so constantly uses the hardest examples during lectures, for homework, etc. Considering that Calc 2 is arguably the toughest class at UNC by itself, this really doesn't help. Take anyone else.

Flipped class which makes an already difficult subject that much harder. Test heavy, and she doesn't shy away from making questions more difficult than needed--Be ready to master the material, not just know it well. It is evident that she cares and will try to help you if you're struggling, but just take it with a better prof
This class is very difficult and the instructor taught the material poorly, but Dr. Burkhead had a great ULA that greatly assisted in my course journey.

Average tough prof—you get out what you put in. Grading is rough and slightly unclear since TA grades hw, but she grades midterms—small things, but she's reasonable overall. Her office hours are key for homework but do textbook problems to prep for the midterms. We had a final project and an exam, so get feedback early on the former.

This discrete math course has been challenging due to the teaching style. The flipped classroom approach often lacks clear in-class explanations, and questions are met with condescending or rhetorical responses, making it hard to seek help. Office hours haven't been helpful, and un-curved tests feel overly strict.

Flipped classroom format worked well, as lectures were used primarily to clarify content from the readings, demonstrate proof structure, and work through examples. Dr. Burkhead is definitely one of the harder discrete professors, but she's good at explaining things, gives lots of practice, and writes tests fairly with plenty of partial credit.
The exams are just unnecessarily hard, compared to other MATH 233 professor her class is just hell. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS! Take 233 with the other professors.

The professor didn't explain everything clearly in class. The lecture is fast paced, the recitations are graded according to correctness instead of participation. The final is severely tough with no curve. Dr. Burkhead doesn't want her student to complete the class with descent grade.

she is so nice and caring she explains the topics really well. however there was no curve while other professors had a curve and her midterms were significantly harder than the other professors. if you want to understand the content would HIGHLY recommend her just be willing to do homework

Dr.Burkhead is such a loving human being, but an AWFUL PROFESSOR. Her exams are tough, and homework is tedious and extremely difficult. 4 exams, none dropped. The Final exam determines your whole grade. HER EXAMS ARE TOUGH. The exams are only 45 minutes each. She continues to teach right after the exam time is over. That is inhumane activity.

I took her math 110 class two years ago, and I still have flashbacks about how awful she was at teaching. I had friends in math 110 who took it with other teachers, and their tests were flat out easier. She made this class unnecessarily hard.

Burkhead definitely prepares students the best for the common final, even though her midterms tend to be harder and have lower averages. While her lectures are optional, they tend to be very useful given the difficulty of the material.

I thought that Dr, Burkhead was excellent! Don't get me wrong, this was absolutely the hardest class I have taken to this date. Lectures can be confusing but this is not due to Dr. Burkhead, but rather the raw complexity of multivariable calculus. If you're confused, GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!! She gives great explanations and is always happy to help!

Class is fast paced. Personally, I think she doesn't explain concepts clearly or just goes over it too fast, so read your textbook before class. Her notes also unclear at times. Majority of grades from midterms & final. Midterms usually harder than class examples, average scores around 70s. This, however, does make you more prepared for the final.

Dr. Burkhead is the perfect example of good person, terrible professor. Lectures were too rigorous and even continued after exams. Expected students to complete homework on a daily basis. Homework was nothing like the exams. Did not drop enough assignments considering the workload.

One of the cases where flipped classroom style worked well. Investing the time to understand the textbook before she goes over it in class is helpful. Her test reviews are a notch harder than the actual tests (being slightly overprepared = helpful), and she gives a lot of partial credit. Go to office hours and do the HW even if it's not collected.

Dr. Burkhead is a super nice, caring, and sweet person. You can tell that she genuinely cares about teaching the topics and will try her hardest to help you understand. Still, its Multi, calculus is super hard and there is alot of homework which ends up being harder than the tests. Overall, this multi section is the most optimal and forgiving.

Class is very fast-paced, but Dr. Burkhead does her best to help you understand. She is very kind and utilizing office hours is probably the best shot you have at getting a good grade in the class if algebra isn't your strong suit (I'm terrible at math). The grading is harsh and the extra credit offered does not help you a lot. No curves either.

Dr. Burkhead is caring, engaging, and good at explaining tough concepts. You'll spend a lot of time reading the book and doing exercises in groups. Tests are hard but fairly graded, and there is a 5-6 page group paper at the end of the class on a topic of your choice. I found the topics fascinating and would highly recommend Dr. Burkhead.

MATH 233 is a difficult class and you're going to have to read the textbook and do the exercises if you want an A, no matter the professor. This isn't your high school calculus class.

Midterms were tough but fair. No curve but tests are well-written and the final replaces your lowest midterm.

Burkhead is a sweet, understanding, and helpful prof.

Professor Burkhead is amazing at teaching Discrete Math. She's friendly, easy to communicate with, knowledgeable, and brings a lot of charisma to the class to keep it interesting. Her grading structure has a lot of midterms (3) that are worth 13% each, and she gives a lot of partial credit so they are useful to learn from. Beware the final project.

Professor Burkhead is a very good mathematical communicator. She is an amazing person and professor, however, her grading style was slightly harsh. She has 4 midterms each being 10% of your grade as opposed to other professors who only do 2 midterms. Her tests are very conceptual and are easy to loose points on for small mistakes.

Burkhead is a kind and energetic professor, she really tries to get students passionate about the subject. However, save your GPA. She has 4 midterms, of which she has a 70% average compared to other professors' 90% average, and with HALF the time. After midterms, she goes right back to lecturing. I learned everything through the textbook.

Dr. Burkhead is an extremely nice professor, however, this class for me was very difficult, given that her lectures consist of mainly working practice problems and briefly reviewing textbook contents, as opposed to spending more time teaching the fundamentals of the course contents (which is most conducive for my learning style).

Dr. Burkhead knows what she's talking about. Discrete math is difficult regardless of who teaches it, but I think Dr. Burkhead is truly a passionate, enthusiastic, helpful professor if you seek her out. She covers topics very briefly and only goes in-depth if you show up to office hours or ask during class. She grades relatively easy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! Her lectures are just practice examples and she barely talks about the concepts. You need to read the textbook before coming to class to get a proper understanding. The tests were unnecessarily hard. Our last test average was a 71 while other classes averaged higher. She is really nice, but REALLY hard. SAVE YOUR GPA!

Nice person and good lecturer, but tests were insanely hard for no reason. Our class was averaging low to mid 70s on all midterms, while other classes like Kumar's were averaging 90s. also, we had 4 midterms with 40 minutes each, giving us barely any time. every midterm was a speedrun

Calc III is just a hard class in general, but Burkhead does her best to help. She is very accessible outside and inside of class and always has great energy in lecture. Exams are tougher than other sections, but when you leave this class you will learn the material in great detail. Be prepared to make this class a main priority though.

Taking Calculus 3 with this professor was the worst experience of my life. Studying for her exams brought me to tears. The test study guides are an extremely poor representation of the exams and she wrote most of the final so her students did bad on that too. Her class average is a C, while others are an A. Do not take this class! Save your GPA!!!

Dr. Burkhead is an amazing professor, but she is definitely not for everyone. If you are willing to do a lot of textbook problems and reading outside of class, and enjoy being in a very fast paced class, I would highly recommend Dr. Burkhead. Her office hours are very helpful, and she makes herself very available to answer online Piazza questions.

This class was a lot of work but I found it enjoyable and Dr. Burkhead made it even better. She is very forgiving regarding grading, which is helpful because the class is high-speed and requires a lot of deep thinking to understand. The homework questions are harder than anything else in the class but make sure to prepare for every test and quiz.

Burkhead is kind and caring, but lectures move very fast. The textbook was abysmal, and I started showing improvement in the class when I stopped wasting time with it. If you are fresh on calc 1 and 2 concepts, you'll be fine. If not, it's a fight to keep up in this class. I attended every class and paid attention, and just barely scraped by.

A good lecturer who gives very fair tests. Throughly explains concepts and examples in class so I never found myself having to consult the textbook or Youtube. I found the tests to be very predictable-- if you study all the concepts she goes over in class, there should be no surprises. I never felt like I was "cheated" out of a good grade in class.

The tests are not like the lectures or homework. Her office hours help for class content but don't prepare you for the test content. If you're no the greatest at math, like me, be prepared to get outside help like peer tutoring. Overall, Dr. Burkhead was very nice but the lectures are quite different from what you are being tested on.

Good lecturer that starts with theory & proof then does worked examples. Lectures were definitely held back by the 50 minute limit but she managed to get most of the content in despite the week of lectures we lost due to the shootings. While her exams are difficult, there are no surprises. Just do her practice problems and you will be fine.

Personally, I didn't get much from Dr. Burkhead's lectures and chose to self-teach myself the course since attendance isn't required. Tests are cumulatively worth about 70% of your grade, with recitation quizzes and homework making up the rest. Tough class but if you put in the work you can do ok.

She is very nice, accommodating, and explains things fairly well. She does go into theory and proofs a lot which leaves me a bit confused, but it's never on a test. Filled in notes are provided for every chapter which are colored and detailed. Homework harder than tests, but they are pretty easy 100s since you have multiple attempts per question.

This is a hard class. The homework is nothing like the lectures/tests and take hours to complete. No curve and very little extra credit on top of over 60 percent of your grade being tests. Lectures were hard to follow.

Professor Burkhead comes off as intimidating but she cares about her students. The content of Math 110 was much harder than I expected, but I don't think that is her fault (fast paced lectures). Homework is long and takes a long time! Extra credit is not easy to come by, but tests are manageable (just do the study guides). She does not curve.

She is a nice prof, and her teaching is great. However, it seems that using online textbook she provides is more helpful than the lecture . That understandable because cal 3 is so difficult and covers so many things that she can't manage to go in depth for every concept.

Personally, I would never take a class with Emily Burkhead again. She continued lecturing during an active shooter on campus and was unaccommodating with moving deadlines for homeworks and piled them with the other due assignments the following week, instead of taking the time to rearrange the schedule (which UNC is advising teachers to do).

Calculus is going to be difficult regardless of the teacher. The class can feel fast paced and typically the tests are on questions that are more advanced then the problems we did in class. It's very important that you do the homework and look over non-graded problems as well. Professor Burkhead always did her best to answer all questions.

Her lectures do a poor job covering all the concepts, so A LOT of learning was done in recitation or by doing the homework instead (making the up to 50-problem HW's take even longer). 4 midterms with just a 40 minute time limit, and having all the class/recitation notes + doing the homework does not guarantee you understand everything on the tests.

Burkhead is very clear on the concepts. ppl hate on her just bc the class is hard but that has nothing to do with her. You really need to practice a lot outside of class though. Exams were pretty straightforward if you did problems outside of the homework.

Dr. Burkhead was AWESOME for 233. She was very good with linking theory to examples and walked around the class clearing confusion during example problems. Sure it was a lot of homework, but with calculus doing practice is how you learn it. 4 tests which were all extremely fair (and if you study a bit honestly easy) and a final which was also easy.
David's lecutres were all over the place and made learning the material very difficult. His office was also a mess, so I can see why he never responded to his emails.

Lectures were very disorganized and he procrastinated until a couple days before finals to post notes. Just understanding the concepts is not enough. The online HW is no help but the HW worksheets and in-class worksheets should be studied for exams. The third exam was easy but everything else was a mess. Did not give partial credit on the final.

The class is very test heavy (80%) and test difficulty varies a lot (but questions are pretty consistent with HW and worksheet content). Lessons are quite hard to follow and participation worksheets are part of the grade. May still be a easier class than other MATH347 professors due to less weightage on proofs and a pretty easy grading scale/curve.

David is a really sweet guy, and wants his students to succeed. However, his lectures are incomprehensible, and slides are hard to follow. It's possible to self-teach, since it's mostly computation. ULAs/TAs are helpful, especially for hw--tricky hw problems often were tested. Most proofs were pulled from slides. Check grading--often has errors.

Easily the worst instructor in the school. Attendance mandatory but lectures are incoherent. Attendance mandatory too. Still got an A, so IDGAF. Philippians 4:13 innit.

Hands down the worst professor at UNC, but i got an A so IDGAF. Didn't learn a thing from him in class, exams were next to impossible to be finished in time, and no amount of studying can save you. At the end of the day some people aint cut out for ts like me and Simeon. But If I can do it then why can't you? Get up and make it Work!

Linear isn't hard material, but this class was nearly impossible. Only grading criteria shared was the floor for an A, so no way to anticipate your grade. Exam scores are consistently lower than he expects, but he blames students and will not curve. Very arbitrary grading on exams and unclear instructions. Unreachable via email.

Chill class. Tests were straight forward and very similar to HWs and were graded fairly. Proofs were from slides/HW. Besides the questionable lectures, I think this class was decent. People complaining about it just don't put in the time to study and think their 60 on the midterm/final is the professor's fault.

70% of your grade is tests. Lectures are convoluted and confusing; you'd be better off self-studying but attendance is required. Unreachable via email even with in class follow-ups. Material isn't too hard, the teaching and expectations are what make this class so difficult. David is very sweet, just not a great professor.

Don't take 347 with him unless you're already confident you'll get an A. Tangents during lectures and graded questions and homeworks that are much harder than what's discussed in class. Proofs and examples are confusing, and exams are difficult and account for 80% of your grade. Stay away if you can.

DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. There are others who offer MATH 347, just take theirs later if you have to or join a waitlist. David makes the class so much harder than it needs to be with useless proofs and derivations while simultaneously making no sense and not explaining anything. A little bit on Youtube taught me more than him the entire semester. His slides are like a stream of consciousness that makes no sense to anybody but him. Just don't take him.

This has been the hardest class I have ever taken at UNC. He wants you to fail. There is no study guide only past tests and there is no answer sheet so you better hope you're doing it right. He expects you to just memorize all "short" proofs from the slide. Good luck even interpreting his slides. I would avoid this class at all costs.
Worst class I've taken at UNC. Made me question my sanity. If I could afford therapy I'd go because of him. Don't take, idc how much you think you can handle it. Listen to the reviews. Run! RUN!

Super fun class…if you're a masochist. Brutal class all around made worse by ambiguous teaching and prof's insistence on making you memorize useless proofs. Avoid at literally all costs, I'd rather get curb stomped than take this class again.

Very very bad experience. He doesn't post any answers to any of the assignments/midterms (despite saying he will) and this makes it soo hard to study especially when the slides he posts and uses in lecture don't make any sense. Very hard class made way harder by poor teaching and zero recourses.
Awful, awful class. Unorganized, unhelpful, uninteresting. Stay away at all costs, he makes it needlessly complex and it's brutal. Studying for this final will kill me.

So, so bad. So bad. Prof doesn't respond to emails, uses outdated/ambiguous slides to teach, and generally is very confusing. Take with someone else, this class isn't easy and he makes it way harder than need be.
Not a good prof, and an even worse class. Don't take with him if you can help it

Studying for exams right now and ready to just...be done with this class. A really, really painful class to take. Couple that with subpar instruction from David and it's a recipe for disaster. Please take with someone else if you value your sanity and are not a math prodigy. Thankful for the TAs/ULAs who helped me not get 0's on every test.

Took this class for Econ BS thinking it couldn't be that bad, and it has been even worse. This is by far the worst taught class I've ever been in...the class is unorganized, lecture notes are incomprehensible, and homework is long, tedious, and constant. I would strongly recommend against this class, and if you HAVE to take, take with someone else.

Contrary to other reviews, professor isn't terrible. Lectures feel a bit disorganized, but homework is straightforward and tests mimic the homework. All proofs on the tests can be found on the lecture slides.

Probably not the best 347 instructor, but very fair and not as bad as reviews would say. Just put in time outside of class to things.

Would not recommend taking this class...David is a great guy but his lectures are confusing and his teaching style is frustrating. Tests are 80% of your grade in this class and for some odd reason he loves to throw in questions that look nothing like the work you do in class/homework. Take someone else and save yourself the stress.

Just an awful class...David doesn't explain anything in an understandable manner, so you WILL be teaching yourself everything. Sitting in class for 2.5 hours every week just being talked at gets exhausting quick, and he makes zero effort to either help you understand or make class even remotely entertaining. Take with someone else, bc I hated this.
Very nice guy. He has an extremely cute dog named Mia, and he explains things pretty clearly.
he teaches it pretty confusingly, tests are incredibly accurate to homeworks and practice, is available for office hours, willing to answer questions but not the best at doing so.

If you have the option, find someone else. His lectures really don't make sense and his attendance policy is brain-dead. Won't curve prior to the end of class, and midterm averages hover around a 60. His tests always take longer than the allotted amount of time, and it is your fault for not being a professional in the sector.

Genuinely awful professor. His lectures are outdated, incorrect, and incomprehensible. He is unhelpful, boring, and just when you think you understand the material, he confuses you at the last second. Homework is tedious/unhelpful. Class averages for exams hover around 60, and he curves nothing. Take another teacher and save yourself the stress.

Everyone complaining just did not put the time into learning the material lol. His lectures can definitely be confusing if you sit in silence and don't ask questions, but he is always willing to re explain things. He also does make mistakes but quickly corrects himself. If you put the time and actually participate in class you'll be fine.

don't waste time going to class, get someone else to do the in class assignments for you. one of the worst teachers at the school and literally impossible to learn from. the first and third midterms are easy if you have old ones. don't take this teacher if you can avoid it but it's not the end of world if you do

This class is a nightmare... he is hilariously bad at lecturing. Material is overwhelming, undigestible, and you had better be prepared to teach yourself everything. UNC Math department needs an overhaul, I have not taken a single good class with them yet.
Very nice and intelligent professor but completely incomprehensible lectures, which would be fine if attendance was not mandatory but it was.

Unlike many reviews here, I found the class itself to be good. There's a practical approach to various problems, and if you follow the content well, you should be able to take the exam with only a little self-study. However, there are many errors in his grading, so check it carefully.

Yes, maybe David is not that good at talking about abstract concepts, but I found it extremely helpful in his office hours. A lot of examples similar to the ones in final were presented, and he explained what you should know. You need to figure out something yourself, that's part of college. It's helpful if you bring questions to him. Nice guy.

Professor Adalsteinsson's lectures are pretty confusing but the midterms are easy. There is a good bit of homework every week (which is similar to the test questions) and a worksheet every class (which I think was graded for completion). The final was hard and very calc heavy, but the grading of it was chill and it was easy to get partial credit.

Dr. Adalsteinsson is a really nice dude but an awful lecturer, he spent the majority of the class scrawling barely legible proofs/definitions and would switch slides so fast it was impossible to both pay attention to what he was doing, and write all of it down. Grading criteria was unclear and made it impossible to know your grade in the class.

Linear is a hard class no matter what, but his lectures are horrible and impossible to follow. You have to teach everything to yourself. You have a worksheet you have to turn it every class and it's very difficult to understand how to do it by the end of. Homeworks take a long time to complete and require hours of learning.

David is very smart but doesn't know how to communicate abstract thoughts, which is unfortunate since linear algebra is a pretty abstract class. I spent most lectures figuring stuff out by watching youtube videos or using GPT. He also went outside the scope of the required content while making it an important part of the final.

Class structure with the worksheets, edfinity and gradescope helped solidify understanding but the lectures weren't the greatest. midterms are 40% final is another 40%. midterms are fairly straightforward and reflect what we learn. adalsteinsson is a cool guy just not the greatest lecturer. grading criteria is also a little confusing

Most lectures were written minutes before the class. The syllabus contained multiple errors and very odd grading criteria. Some of the lectures we're extremely confusing, but only because of unnecessary proofs. The final grade was given in connect carolina with no clear criteria or announcement on canvas. Only giving a 2 is because he's a nice guy.

Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken (others not even close). Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given straight away without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.

Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about himself. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken. Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given straight away without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.

Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about himself. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken. Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.
he doesn't explain concepts well and lectures are a mess. he's a strict grader and doesn't curve in the slightest. please do not take him.

This class ruined my 4.0. Linear is such an easy subject but you cannot self study this class because of all the little things he makes you do his way on the exam. Final was 40%, midterms were another 40%. Honestly I've learned from this class not to take the insanely lower rated professors. I thought I'd give him the benefit of a doubt but rip.

Setup of the class forces you to participate. Do not plan on skipping a class. Content is easy for math oriented people but the way he explains it makes it seem harder than it is. The only way you could fail this class is if you try too hard to understand what he's saying. Exams resemble homework and both are typical style for a math class.

Lectures are SO confusing, I don't think he even knows what he's talking about. Homework was helpful, but expect to spend a lot of time learning on your own. Exams are not bad, just understanding of the basics but so different from lectures.

I stopped attending lectures after the first month because they were honestly confusing and unhelpful—it felt like the professor didn't fully understand the material himself. The midterms were manageable, but the final literally destroyed me. Thanks to him, I am going to say goodbye to my 4.0 GPA.

Never again. NEVER explained what was covered on the final exam, the lectures were awful- so basically, teach yourself. I am a math major and David made several errors during most of his lectures- showing incompetence. Take someone who has respect for his students too, he denied my accommodations for an exam.

High rating bc he deserves a higher average imo. Other comments nailed it. The textbook he assigned was the best teaching he has done. I crammed the nights before and got A on every midterm (60% of grade). Textbook and online video walkthroughs are your best bet. Brings up confusing stuff in lec but only really tests whats on worksheets.

The lectures were useless. He doesn't respond to emails. Fortunately, the class is pretty easy. You're best off going to class, grabbing the in-class assignment, then leaving class and studying for a few minutes a day rather than wasting your time. It's a shame he's a bad professor, because I actually kind of like him on a personal level.

As everyone else said, the lectures are awful but still consider taking David due to the fact that he drops a midterm, the tests are pretty fair, and he's generally a lot nice and approachable than a lot of your other options in the math dept. Basically, trade-off between nicer grading vs having to teach yourself. Be ready to self study EVERYTHING

Do not. While admittedly this has been a tough semester for me due to some other outside circumstances, this guy did NOT help at all. Lectures are plainly incomprehensible -- not even because of the accent, he just says things and expects you to understand. Doesn't go through problem solving in class. Assigns an ungodly amount of homework.

Despite attending the lectures, I found it very difficult to do the worksheet given to us to have completed by the end of lecture. I found myself learning most of the content outside of class and my emails to the professor sent with no reply. It was difficult to get a straight answer out of the professor as he would ramble about unrelated topics.

This class is atrocious to say the least. I have learned ZILCH from the lectures—and trust me, I've been to all of them. If you want a chance at passing the exams, I would read the textbook and review the worksheets. The homework problems sometimes include topics we haven't even covered in class yet, but he keeps them on their for some reason.
Professor Adalsteinsson cares deeply about his students, and attending his office hours is very helpful.

Dr. Adalsteinsson's lectures are extremely difficult to understand especially the posted slides themselves. Gives way too much homework every week with a P-set and Edfinity. Midterm 1 and 3 were pretty easy but midterm 2 was a PAIN with the amount of computation. Content is easier to learn compared to other math courses but extremely error-prone.

Anyone giving him more than a 1 is generous. Save yourself and DONT. His lectures are incomprehensible, and you'll have to teach yourself everything—no exaggeration. I thought his lectures couldn't be as bad as reviews said—trust me, they are. Exams are okay, but he as a professor is truly abominable and the worst ever. The homework is ridiculous.
Do not take this guy. He has no idea how to teach and does not care about the students. Tests are 80% of the grade and are inconsistently graded. Does not even tell you what will be on the final.

Make sure to have taken MATH381 or some proofs class before this. His lectures are mainly theoretical. However exams were mainly computation with about 10-15% being about proofs, except for the 2nd midterm. The computational aren't difficult but heavily error proned. Re-read lecture notes and go over proofs he discussed as some will be on exams.

Passionate professor, but the lectures are like hieroglyphics—extremely hard to understand and follow. The professor's focus on theory with little practical examples in class made it very challenging to grasp the concepts. I had to self-study everything. No answers or solutions were provided for homework assignments or lecture sheets.

His lectures are like a pizza with so many unnecessary toppings that it's hard to digest. He spent like four lectures talking about SVD but sprinkles in random side topics (like ODEs, exponential matrices, image space, Fibonacci numbers, permutations) that just make it overwhelming. He posts lecture slides but sometimes there's so much jargon.
