He has extremely disorganized lectures and his explanations are REALLY bad. Homework is never posted when it is supposed to be, and tests make up 80% of the final grade. He is a nice man and you can see he enjoys teaching, but he is not a great instructor, at all.

He is a very passionate and smart prof, but hard to follow in lecture. He does not make the material intuitive and goes off on crazy tangents. Take the free A on the first midterm, because material gets harder after that. Hammer computational stuff, so you can afford to struggle with the proofs. Second midterm is brutal. TAs were useless.

Dr. A does not give any care to his students and expects us to treat Linear Algebra like its our passion. Extremely disorganized lectures, notes, and resources. He rarely gave solutions to work and even if he did they could be wrong. Don't take this class.

He is very disorganized in class structure. He tries to teach students not only application but also the reason behind, but is not doing it very well. He rushes through complicated proofs and thinks these scattering shots are enough. If any professor wants to give a hint on analysis in an application class that is not how they should do it.

You can tell he knows a lot and there are many ways to approach this subject that he doesn't fully flesh out thoughts, making lecture confusing at times. There are daily attendance worksheets that I recommend taking your notes on to stay organized. You can tell he wants you to learn and gets excited when people ask questions, but expect self-study.
Awful professor, extremely bad lectures and very strict and unfair grading. Requires you to do things “his way” and goes down a rabbit hole every time he teaches something

This dude's lectures are mysterious. Don't try to decipher his slides. Watch some linear algebra on Youtube to save yourself (linear algebra in this class is pretty self-studyable). Gave him a 2 because at least he is a nice guy. Exams are 80% of your final grade so beware of that.

Don't read any other review. This one is the only one you need. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Students in class audibly laugh when this guy tries to explain the material. He's a nice guy, but he's the worst instructor of any sort I have ever seen. You will leave class more and more confused than from where you start. Avoid him please.

If you walked in on one of his lectures and looked around, half the people would be on their phones/laptops watching something, and the other half would be staring blankly in confusion. He ALWAYS went over on time and his lectures were extremely hard to follow. Use TA's and ULA office hours, and avoid his. He will take up hours of your time

He is a nice guy and clearly very smart and knowledgeable. However, I often left lectures more confused on the material than when I started. Grading scheme/curve was never revealed, nor were our grades on the final exam. Despite being the applications class, there were very few applications mentioned, and there were proofs on multiple of our exams.

Professor Adalsteinsson's lectures are definitely hard to comprehend. He doesn't explain the material well and sometimes he will dive into what seems like random topics. Overall, he is a really nice guy, just not a great professor. His tests are not hard, with them being mostly computational, they feel like hw questions with different numbers.

David is not a good lecturer. Confusing, hard to follow, and difficult to contact. Office hours are a big help if you can manage to corral him into actually helping and staying directly on topic. David dropped our course grade in Connect Carolina with no message, no access to our final grades, no grade breakdown, no regrades, no curve description.

The class is not taught well. The upsides of the class is that there isn't much homework and that he is lenient with the curve at the end. 3 midterms and 1 final exam are worth 80% of your grade, so be careful of that. The first and third midterms were easy, but the second one was extremely difficult.

Very poor time management during lectures; you will have to learn a lot on your own. Said that we did too well on the first midterm, so he made the next one much harder (the median score for one of the questions was a 0). Made us learn Julia but we weren't allowed to use it on exams. Would avoid this professor if possible.

Great guy. Lectures can be confusing, but that's just how linear algebra is. If you study the worksheets and homeworks that he gives, you'll do well on the midterms and final because it's basically just doing the same techniques with different numbers. Personally, I don't think the reviews on here are an acccuarete representation of professor Adal.
W prof

genuinely the worst professor ive ever had at unc. he always talks about things for 30 mins of our 50 min class that are completely irrelevant to the worksheets or homeworks or exams that we are given and then im left trying to figure it out for myself before turning in the 3 assignments we have due every friday. run. do not take.
Lectures are very, very hard to understand. The material isn't too bad so you can definitely teach yourself if you need to, but I would avoid this professor if you can. Super nice guy, though.
fluent in yappanese....

His exams are easy that most students get 100 on the first, 40% on the third. The second one might be bad but he "curved." I do recommend math majors taking his class, since the proofs he covered will increase your mathematical maturity. I don't think he recommended Strang's lecture in class so I guess people below are just finding excuses...

Prof Adalsteinsson is probably the worst professor I've ever had at UNC. He is super nice and obviously super smart, but his lectures are terrible. Lectures are confusing, scattered and read off his own poorly handwritten notes. He doesn't provide solutions for classwork and actually RECOMMENDS you watch other professors' lectures online.

David doesn't reveal his grading scheme ahead of final grades being posted so beware. Also, he tends to teach the class in a much more abstract manner than any of the other linear algebra professors. With that being said, he has done some interesting research and work in the field so talk to him about it if you get the chance.
this guy blows, don't take him

Here I am thinking I won't have a worse professor than the past ones I've had here. Then comes this dude. My GOD is he confusing and hard to follow. It's useless to come to lectures because he never explains anything and instead recommends WATCHING OTHER PROFESSOR'S LECTURES. The entire semester I had to self-teach EVERYTHING. DO NOT TAKE HIM EVER

Nice guy, horrible teacher. I have never felt more confused in my life than after leaving one of his lectures. Gives no context to the content you are learning, goes at a rapid pace, does not explain content, and just does problems on the board in a confusing way. Terrible slides that dont help at all

Again, super smart dude, abysmal professor.

Professor Adalsteinsson is a fair grader who has great lectures. he explains concepts very well and the tests are a good reflection of what we go over in class and practice. He also drops the lowest exam which definitely helps.

A lot of people do not say good things about professor adalsteinsson, but he is not bad at all. You just need to come to class and he is great at explaining concepts. Tests are fair and I would definitely take this class with him again.

David's lectures are all over the place and he is not responsive to emails/messages outside of class. Even when asking for solutions to practice he's given us, he doesn't provide any because he says he doesn't have them written up. This semester was incredibly difficult due to his unreliability and confusing lectures -- I had to teach myself.

He's better than his rating suggests, although sometimes it can be hard to follow when he proves things in lectures. The homework is also a bit tedious sometimes, but the homework and textbook prepare you well for tests. There's not a huge curve, but the tests are just practicing each of the techniques from the course.

Had him for MATH 347, but couldn't select it. The best part of the way Adalsteinsson teaches linear is following along with worksheets, so it's not just a complicated lecture that you have to practice on homework. Sometimes lectures became a bit too complicated to follow, but he was friendly and did a lot to make sure you followed.

I thought he lectured well, but the main thing which prospective students should takeaway is that he often gives practice tests which are very representative of the actual test, which I would say from a teaching perspective in a 500 level math course is a rarity
The lectures are not up to standard and content covered in class is nowhere comparable to what is tested on the exams. 100% of your grade comes from 2 midterms and a final.

Rozansky is really funny and you can tell he cares about his students, but his lectures are extremely disorganized and hard to follow. Not a bad class if you can self teach. There's 2 midterms worth 30% and a common final. His midterms aren't difficult, but 381 is pretty hard so the common final was rough.

Entire grade was from the tests. He did curve a lot but that says more about his teaching than anything. Basically, you're better off learning this from youtube videos and the textbook than him. Tests were very reasonable and easy, however. So, if you're confident in your self studying skills, he may be a good teacher for you.

Extremely disorganized and sometimes hard to follow lecturing. Despite this, he's so disorganized it's insanely funny. He also gives problem-by-problem breakdowns of exams which are immensely helpful. Don't schedule a class 15 minutes after because he will 100% run overtime every single class. Outside of this, he isn't too bad for UNC math profs.

this review is for math 529. honestly i had him for dif eq as well and he is a bit disorganized and its hard to know how you're doing in the class but he really wants you to succeed, is very helpful in office hours, and even gives you a list of topics for the final as well. you will have to be motivated and do a lot of self studying.

The class is EXTREMELY DISORGANIZED. Syllabus is barebones and we have no idea what to expect. Homework was on Pearson and did not sync with class material. He's terrible at explaining concepts and uses unnecessarily difficult Math jargon without explaining it. The only things I learned form this course was from youtube and self-study.

Really nice guy who cares about his students a lot and curves pretty generously. Watched the lectures a day or two before the exam and barely did any practice problems. I think his lectures are quite good, just need to rewind occasionally. Homework and attendance are optional.

The lectures were kind of confusing but basically all of the material can be self taught through the textbook. His tests are really fair because he releases the exact 5 topics before every exam. A pretty chill guy.

I didn't go to a single class, not even the first day, and not the last day either, or any day in between, yet I still got an A. I will not tell the you the strategy, but just knows its possible. The hardest part of the course was the very last concept (8.2). Otherwise, W Lev.

Dr. Rozansky is pretty funny, but he has no idea how to teach people who don't already know the content. The class midterm averages were almost always around 50%. He does curve the class a lot at the end, but it was not enough to really save my grade.

You can tell Lev is a really smart guy, but he just isn't a good teacher. Very disorganized. For example, after my second midterm grade, I asked him what my current overall grade was in the course, and he said he couldn't tell me because he computes curves at the end.

Teaches at a very high level, useful for some future classes but extremely confusing in the moment. The clarity of his note-taking and lessons is below average, but he is a very kind person. He expects a lot of his students and truly wants them to do well. Weird, quirky, funny guy.

DO take him if you are good at learning math yourself. Tests are manageable, just go through some YouTube lectures and his class notes, where he designs midterms from. You can even skip homework.
DO NOT take him if you only learn in lectures.

Lev is a quirky professor, but his class can be a real challenge. While the tests aren't too difficult, his teaching style is disorganized and he often skips steps. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for me - it helped fill in the gaps. Overall, a decent option, but be prepared to put in the work.

The lectures are disorganized, so I ended up skipping most of them and learning through YouTube videos. The exams are simple and straightforward. The only challenge is the amount of questions—you need to be very familiar with the material to finish on time. Overall, if you're just looking for an easy GPA boost, I'd recommend taking his class.

Professor Rozansky is very knowledgeable and has good teaching ability. However, he seems to care more about the material than the students: class is very disorganized, graded by 3 exams, and overall is set up without the interest of the students in mind. He is clearly forced to teach but just goes through the motions and doesn't care enough to try

DO NOT TAKE! Grades are 25% midterm 1, 25% midterm 2, 50% final. Silly guy, but terrible teacher -- I did not learn anything in class. Not clear on grading, says he "may" curve but not up front about it. We didn't know what our grade is at ANY point, and still will not know what we have in the class until the grades are final.

The teaching style and setup of the class is outdated and unfit for the modern student. His lectures are proofs of complex physical concepts that are not prerequisites. He is unorganized, often digressing, and it is hard to believe he prepares for the lectures beforehand. Exams are the entire grade, and his lectures will not prepare for them.

I enjoyed Professor Rozansky's enthusiasm but lectures were very theoretical. Difficult to understand. The class was essentially 100% test graded. Each midterm was 25%, and the final was 40-50%. Doesn't respond to emails, changed due dates and exam dates often. Don't recommend taking him. So much more difficult than the other 233 profs.

If you have no previous exposure to calc, do NOT take him. Even if you have previous exposure to calc, I would still take almost any other professor before taking him again. His lectures are unorganized and he speaks in theoreticals. This class was genuinely miserable. I had to teach myself all of the material. 100% of the grade was exams. Avoid.

I took Calc BC in high school. Wanted to retake calc because I felt like I didn't learn it very well the first time around in high school. Roz is great if you have exposure to calc already. If you don't have previous exposure, he may too theoretical, and you will need to rely on youtube or textbooks. Clearly very caring and sweet. Tests were fair.

I think he is actually fine. He is very nice and patient to answer questions in class. He also answers questions about homework on piazza. The exam is not too hard, and he gave enough materials to review. He does sometimes mess things up, but that actually does not matter too much in terms of learning

Man I know so many people who took AP Calc and did fine, this man complicates things for no good reason. I'm a good student, but once you do poorly on one test its over. He is rude to students, and assigns four times the amount of hw as other profs. Our syllabus said ~86% of our grade was tests, at the end he threw out the 14% and it was only tests

Professor Rozansky is definitely a character- funny, a bit rude, not very clear or organized. I can safely say I only understood about half of what was discussed during lecture, but they were always entertaining. Tests weren't hard, even without previous calc experience. He will bump your grade up a lot if you do well on the final. Decent option.

Funny guy, but really disorganized. Rescheduled each exam multiple times on short notices and had the wrong final exam date on the syallbus the entire semester. Also prone to assigning multiple homework assignments due within 24-48 hours.

Rozansky's linear class is really easy. His tests were directly the same problems as homeworks. He doesn't always explain things extremely clearly but overall a good guy. Pretty funny. It may require some independent learning if you do not understand him, and his office hours are not always very forgiving as he can be a bit critical.

I took AP Calc in high school and still did awful. 40/50 is the average for midterms (he doesn't curve). He does not explain anything well, insulted my friend's intelligence, and conducts the class different from all other 231 classes. I didn't listen to his reviews, but please for your mental sake take this class with anyone else.
Professor held a zoom class during the August lockdown. Do not take this class.

He is a chill professor, very understand for student and somewhat easy grader. He aslo record lecture. However his class is very unorganized. Syllabus doesnt include the grading percentage of exams, hw, etc. He didnt post grade for a whole semester and never reply to email.

Prof. Rozansky is a nice person and helpful if you meet him outside of class. However, lectures are confusing, it's more like him just doing problems and theory rather than teaching. He doesn't respond to emails and doesn't put anything in the gradebook, so I didn't know what my grade was until it was put in Connect Carolina.

He is a good person but please do not take his class. Though he's passionate about the subjects the lectures are poorly structured and very difficult to understand. Exams are extraordinarily hard and worth basically the entire grade. A "decent" level of understanding that could get you a B+ with another professor may not even let you pass with him.

Please don't take him, this will make you a hundred times better. Unless you have a few credit hours or you are a math genius. He teaches a lot of linear algebra, so if you want to learn two classes in one, go for it. The final is worth 60 percent of your grade and it was extremely difficult.

To whoever this may concern, 

I would rather swim with man-eating sharks than take this class again. Do not take this class if do not have experience. It will feel so hopeless that you would want to choke on your own intestines. Exams: 5 questions. No mic. Never tells you grades. Teaches at a high level. Skips steps. 

Pray if you get him

RIP

Lev is a great person, but the worst teacher. Like he is so into math, and should be like a researcher or something, but I had to read the textbook to learn. I did not learn anything the entire semester from him. I stopped showing up to class because it honestly confused me even though the topics are easy. Also 84% of the grade comes from the exams

Lev shows up late on midterm days, his exams are only 5ish questions long, doesn't really give partial credit, references the online textbook during class because he has no lesson plan, his syllabus is barely a page long with practically no info, didn't give a five day warning before an exam, AND HAD HOMEWORK DUE THANKSGIVING DAY DURING BREAK.

Lev is a very smart mathmetician, but he lacks effective communication with the students. He is often confusing in his lectures as he skips steps and expects you to understand terms that he has not yet defined. His tests are not overly difficult, but they are short and if you get one question wrong it drastically drops your grade.

While I do love his personality, his teaching style is horrendous. Grading scale: Two exams each worth 21%, final 42%, HW 16%. If you are redoing calc he may be good, but for newbies, he is not good. He hasn't answered a single one of my emails this entire semester. I have to teach myself everything for this class, which is very time-consuming.

Take Calc 1 with anybody other than him. Lev has two tests and you cannot drop or replace either (unlike other Calc 1 teachers). Questions on his test will be something entirely different than lecture or homework. Avoid.

He doesn't clearly give guidelines about what will be on the test and his lectures and homeworks are on two completely different things. Also, he is hard to access outside of class and often struggles with technology making it hard to keep track of what's happening and he has SUCH BAD handwriting.

Lectures are horrible, material is way overcomplicated and extremely theoretical while exams and homework are applications. Just learn on your own by watching other professors on YouTube. Exams are difficult as there aren't many questions, mess up one question and you're at a 75%. Entire grade is based off exams as well.

Lev is clearly an gifted mathematician, but he just cannot run a classroom. Exams resemble the practice problems but we never received answer keys to the midterms so we couldn't review or determine if we needed a regrade. Gave very few practice problems, and had a TA proctor a midterm for him who was late and he himself was late to the final exam.

His lectures were SO confusing (like seriously) and I literally didn't learn a single thing attending class. I had to teach myself the entire class from the textbook, which fortunately was very clear and understandable. The reason he's a 2 instead of a 1 is that his exams were almost the same as the HW problems he would give.

Prof. Rozansky is a knowledgable and funny professor. However, the lectures are difficult to understand for the average student who has not been previously introduced to linear algebra. After watching some Khan Academy videos, I realized linear algebra should not be as complicated as Rozansky portrays it to be.

There is no need to show up for this class; he makes everything more confusing than it needs to be. I did all the Pearson homework, redoing it until I got a 100% because why wouldn't you. I taught myself with the textbook as I went through the homework and understood it so much better than from his lectures. And PLEASE, go to the Math Help Center!

You can breeze through this class with little preparation if you've taken 347 before; however, make sure you study hard for the final (which was non-cumulative, and he sent the topics one day before). He is pretty funny but don't get too confident if you do well on the midterms (which are pretty fair) because the final makes or breaks your grade.

A really nice person but not as great as a professor. He clearly knows what he's teaching, but his explanation aren't very easy to follow. Also, there weren't weekly deadlines for homework, which incentivised me to end up doing all of them at the end of the semester.
However, following his schemes and exercises in lectures was quite helpful for me.

She did a good job teaching and her midterms were pretty easy. However, she is almost impossible to reach out to. Her grading doesn't make sense and is often hypocritical, she said she would give me points back for something, then never did and later refused to. Also, her class and midterms do not at all prepare you for the insane final.

Her time management skills are not that great. There appears to be no communication between her and the TAs, as we were often asked during recitation what we were supposed to be doing, and apparently, even the department can't properly communicate what they want on the final. Overall, would not take Calc. here if you want to actually learn.

Thomas is a fine professor. Her tests were fair and very similar to the notes, not the homework. Her lectures are clear, and she answers questions. That being said, she fell behind often due to snow days and other things. The catch-up was very stressful, and she's not accessible outside of class, which caused a lot more stress.

Overall this one was a good class. The slides she went over in class were similar in difficulty to the 3 mid term exams. What neither me, nor the students I talked to after the semester ended, were prepared for was the final. The final was unreasonably hard for what we had been previously tested on. My grade dropped 12 points due to the final.

Dr. Thomas was, overall, a great professor- her expectations were clear and fair. The HW was harder than the exams, but it prepared you well. The kicker of this class was the final- made by the overall math department was way harder than the other exams and honestly, completely unreasonable. No hate to Dr. Thomas but def hate towards the department

Dr. Thomas is a pretty good professor! She is a good lecturer, her tests were fairly easy, and she is genuinely such a sweet human being. The only things I would comment on are that she did not prepare us too well for the final exam, but I don't think any calc 1 teacher did. Also, sometimes she falls behind on notes. Besides that, she is great!

She is a really good professor. However, this poor rating stems from how terribly she underprepared the entire class for the final. I had a 94 going into the final and began following her guidelines 2 weeks prior. Suffice to say, I do not know anyone who scored over a 90 (after what was likely a 20+ point curve). My grade dropped from an A to a B+.

second time taking her. very clear lectures and grading criteria. literally just follow the class notes for exams and you'll be okay. she is very kind and patient and never made you feel dumb. attendance is only really a thing for the 2nd/3rd part of semester

Dr. Thomas is great, very understanding, and an excellent teacher. Not an easy class. Tests are huge and end up being close to 85% of your grade. 

I will say, just because this class says it's "business calc" does not mean it's easy. It's very similar to normal calculus, but with a few business-related word problems and formulas thrown in.

I realize she hasn't been teaching business calc for very long, but this class was difficult and I feel as though it was built for students who already have a strong understanding of calculus. DONT take this class unless you already have a good grasp of calculus concepts.

As someone who doesn't love math and hadn't taken calc in high school, Dr. Thomas made success very achievable. She posts all lecture notes/slides and gives many resources for exams which was super helpful. Overall solid class and great prof for 231

She got behind the course timeline at times but caught up and was really amazing. One of the best calc 1 professors. Posts notes online and does them on her iPad in front of the class which was really helpful. Her tests were fair and she gave a lot of partial credit which helps everyone. Super understanding and is prepared to answer any questions.

Teaching to a large lecture class can be very difficult, but she does a great job of ensuring everyone is caught up.  We got behind at times, but she is a super understanding person and is willing to work with you. You can tell that she wants everyone to succeed. She goes a little fast at times just to make sure the material is covered.

Definitely take MATH231 with Professor Thomas! She's great at breaking down concepts and providing clear explanations. The homework is more challenging than the tests, but using resources like the textbook, practice problems, and unstuck ai can really help you succeed in the class.

Super great lecturer but we got behind a little bit at times. Takes time to clear up confusion but when that puts us behind it makes for some days that are very quick and a little hectic to catch up to the course plan.

flipped style classroom so she didn't really teach the content. we watched videos for homework and then did practice during class. as long as you did the homework and studied a few days in advance, the midterms were fair. she was super understanding though and ended up randomly giving back a lot of extra credit.

This is literally the worst class I've taken at Carolina. Dr.Thomas made the exams very difficult. She hardly taught and was overall not a good professor. If you can, take it with another professor and save yourself the trouble.

I really liked Dr. Thomas. She wrote out her notes during the lectures which made it easy to follow along and learn. Her tests were hard and so were some of the homeworks but she did give lots of resources to help you understand the information. I would also say that the TAs were really great for this class and really helped me with the content.

Dr. Thomas was a super nice person and she was willing to help a lot, however this class is difficult and in my opinion she didn't really teach the class. She was very scatter-brained and seems to just have too much on her plate, which came out in classes. She also never actually taught, the video lessons were from another professor at UNC.

Retook this after being in it with McCombs last spring-- Thomas is significantly better. She writes out each step clearly during class with iPad and is very clear about what you need to know for exams. Do her practice problems-- then you'll have no surprises on the very fair exams. Homework unnecessarily harder than exams. Very kind prof, loved her
This class is super hard but if you're going to take it with anyone make sure it's miranda thomas.

Dr. Thomas was a great professor when she was there. We had a sub one too many times and she failed to post homework/class notes on time repeatedly. She is a very nice person but I think she has way too much on her plate and it reflects in class.
Great lecturer. very clear grading criteria.

i loveeee dr thomas. She is so caring, and she takes the time to reexplain any pre-calc/algebra concepts that people may have forgotten instead of just assuming we remember high school math. her tests are pretty easy, and she sets people up to succeed in her class. definitely take her class

Dr. Thomas's lectures were really organized and easy to follow, and she posts the notes of canvas.The homework was more complicated than the tests but manageable. This class is very manageable if you do the assigned textbook readings before class, do homework, and use the test reviews and practice tests. The test reviews prepare you well!

Math 231 is hard, but if you have to take it, take it with her. Homework is much harder than tests, but I think that's more of a math department thing. Tests are worth much more anyway, so if you can figure out the homework, you'll do great :) She's also very kind and definitely wants students to succeed.

Moves very slow in class and offers very few example problems during class hours and expects complete mastery of subject for homework problem sets, which are 10x more difficult than examples in class. She clearly cares about her students and the subject itself, I just wish she gave us harder problems/more examples in class, kind of frustrating.

I would take this professor for 231. Her tests are easier compared to the other sections. We do worksheets in recitation and our TA is very helpful. The other sections take graded quizzes during recitation. Her lectures can be unclear, but as long as you're willing to put in the work and take advantage of the math help center you should be ok.

Lectures are from skeleton notes, which is incredibly helpful. Final replaces lowest of 3 quizzes if higher, and homework is slightly curved. Made some mistakes during lectures and some concepts were better explained by outside sources. Class is fast paced, but if you're willing to finish learning concepts outside of class, you'll be fine.

Professor Thomas did a really good job of explaining concepts and was always willing to go back if a student didn't understand something. I had a hard time with the homework at first, we were allowed multiple attempts on problems, which helped. The tests aren't too hard, but make sure you study because they cover a lot of content.

Professor Thomas is definitely the professor to take 232 from. She is caring and understanding. Her tests are easier than the other professors, and her tests are very similar to problems done in the class. If you study the slides and her old practice exams for each test, you will be on the right track.

The lectures were okay. She kinda skips around during her work after the first example so its hard to keep up sometimes. The homework was super hard, way harder than the lecture practice and test. The test are doable if you study a lot. Not my favorite.

Professor Thomas teaches ONLY by doing problems. She will only briefly review concepts. If you are not willing to put time into learning outside of class then don't take this course. If you want to do well in this course, go to your TA's office hours. Tests are worth a lot, but if the grade on your final is higher it will replace one test grade.

Not only is she a very qualified math teacher, but she is genuinely such a nice person. I think her tests are easier than the other sections are she makes it very clear what will be on them...she doesn't try to trick you. She moves fast in lectures but that's every STEM class tbh. Super awesome and totally recommend for any calc class

I had previously taken AP Calc in high school, so I had some background knowledge coming into the class. You have to pay attention in class if you want to do well (she doesn't record her lectures), even if you have taken calc before. The final was worth 35% of our grade, so it is important you understand concepts because they build on each other.

Dr. Thomas was an amazing professor, really kind and caring! Her notes were fill in the blank, making them easy to print or follow along with as a PDF. There was a lot of hw and it was difficult, but the tests were similar to the notes in class for the most part. Tests made up most of the grade, & the final dropped the lowest test too! Recommend!!

Best Advice: If you are good at math generally, go for her. If you have issues with math, she is not a bad choice, just have friend in the class. I felt that calc 2 is easier than calc 1. It is straight to the point, no words. 
She gives partial credit for multiple choice. That is amazing.

If you put in the work, you have nothing to worry about taking her class - I took this class first semester freshman year and I heard awful things about Math 232. But Dr. Thomas made this class super fun - and she's so so sweet!
Not a very good teacher, and makes lots of mistakes. Regardless she makes exams very easy and she's the best option so take her class.

Calc 2 is a hard class by itself, but she makes it even harder to understand. She also gives a lot of homework compared to the rest of the Calc 2 classes. I always had to refer to other calc classes' notes to understand the material. Additionally, her tests are considerably more complex in comparison to the other sections. Take it with McLaughlin!!

Tests (final plus 3 exams) are worth 80% of final grade. Tests can be pretty challenging and require lots of prep (especially if you are new to calculus.) Makes frequent errors and justifies them, which can be confusing. Drops some homework and Pollev. You can replace a test with the final if it is higher. Office hours ONLY on Zoom, which sucks.

Professor Thomas is a great fit for non-math majors. The courseload itself is demanding regardless of who you take it with, but she makes it very digestible. Her syllabus is lenient, with attendance drops, homework drops, and the opportunity to replace your lowest midterm with your final exam grade.

Dr Thomas' form of teaching is based on reading off of . She expects you to already know complex topics before the class. She is not accessible outside of class. She is also a slow grader. Even after you teach yourself, succeeding in this class is very hard. Due to this class, im questioning my abilities to be successful.

She put in an A for my grade in connect carolina and then on the final day of grades being due, sent me a message telling me that she messed up my grade and lowered it to an A-. Talk about giving out false hope. Not cool.
The class is tough and many of the topics needed to be learned by yourself. Expect a hard class but if you put in the effort, you should come out with a decent grade.

Don't take her. She's not a mean person, but you will often find yourself scrambling to finish notes as she moves through slides quickly with little explanation. She makes mistakes in class and typos on exams. Our final was written by a different professor and recieved no curve. 10% of the final was a unit we covered the last two days of class.

I have taken Professor Thomas for calc 1 and 2 and thoroughly enjoyed her. Her exams are the easiest by far and she does genuinely care about teaching. She is difficult to access outside of class, and beware that every exam I have taken included a grading mistake, but the class rewards diligent effort, and she is by far the best calc prof.

I took her for calc 1 and 2 and I like her teaching style. However, at the end of calc 2 she taught us two new units in the last week where the other sections were taught them early in the semester. We had no practice with the material and it was heavy on the final. So it was very frustrating and my final grade suffered because of that.
I personally thought she was a really good teacher and explained things in depth well. She was really understanding with deadlines and I don't think the class was that difficult.

Prof Thomas was a very good 232 teacher up until halfway through the semester. After the first midterm, her lectures almost being impossible to follow along with. Ended up watching youtube videos to teach myself all new content instead.

Professor Thomas' teaching style is very unorganized and confusing. There were multiple classes where she wrote down work on slides, but then it would all be wrong. During tests, she would make announcements about there being multiple typos and incorrect values on questions. If you can take this class with another professor I would recommend it.

Dr. Thomas is great! She has a really good style of teaching and is very charismatic. I'm not at all a calc person, so I struggled a lot with the content, but it's absolutely not a result of her teaching. I didn't talk to her much, but the times I did she was super nice. If you have to take calc, I'd definitely recommend taking her class!

Dr. Thomas truly is a professor who wants to teach, she got her degree in teaching math and it shows. Her lectures are a little slow, but her tests are easy compared to lectures and recitation, and she does everything she can to prepare you. She is very kind and understanding, and if you just communicate she is happy to help. Best prof for calc 1!!

She was a very mid-professor. The one thing that was nice was that she did her lectures on fill-in-the-blank notes. Otherwise, the class is test-heavy, and tests only had a few questions. TAs do a lot of the grading and recitations were difficult. Homework was long and often didn't pertain to lectures.

Great lecturer, class material is clear. Linear algebra is normally difficult, as is this class. The main concern comes in the exams. The exams have proof questions which are very difficult, demanding abstract thinking of newly learned concepts. Memorize definitions to death and practice how they can be used to answer different questions. Big curve

Best math professor! His lecture is pretty good, although I missed some of his class because of the first class in the morning. You can still learn it by yourself.  He explains the concept easily. I did not know how to solve a question in the final, but I still got an A grade. Many similar questions to homework and written homework. A huge curve!
Exams were really hard and didn't accurately represent material learned in the course. Be warned
It was a difficult class but I felt that I learned a great deal. Professor Rimanyi is very knowledgeable but can be slightly terse on occasion.

This dude is so knowledgeable! I should have went to his office hours (he is active on Piazza as well), but AI is getting so good at clearing up computational/theory questions. Prof. Rimanyi is great at explaining the theory (I highly recommend watching 3Blue1Brown alongside his lectures!) behind linear algebra. He's a tough love kind of guy.

Rimanyi is no-nonsense & 347 is hard. However, he also tries his best to ensure students thoroughly understand the material & is an extremely fair grader. You'll have to work for your grade, but will appreciate lin-alg a lot more. If you like math, this is a VERY rewarding class & the curve is massive. Tons of respect for Prof. Rimanyi.

The professor is not kind to students! He responds with attitude and his lectures are soooo boring. He graded my midterms extremely harshly. Luckily, the homework was incredibly easy, and he curves grades at the end. For reference, I got 60s on both midterms and ended up with a B in the class.

Awesome professor, great teaching style, very caring
- Exams were tough and 80% of grade, I got a 48% and 68% on midterms and likely bombed final but received a C+ (never got final score back)
- Generous, generous curve
- Content is interesting and useful
- Take 347 with him

Very lecture heavy and he doesn't post class recordings nor any sort of slides (except his class notes which are often illegible). You will be fine if you attend lectures and do the textbook problems. Entire grade is dependent on 2 midterms (both of which I failed) and the final, yet I still passed the class thanks to his curve.

Rimanyi is just amazing. He explains concepts of all difficulties clearly and teaches real-life applications of linear algebra which is really cool. Not very lenient with partial credit and tests are proof-heavy but the curve makes up for it. Definitely the most rewarding class I've taken so far at UNC. If you have the option, take him!

Really intelligent guy, kind of intimidating but not unkind and sometimes drops a rare unexpected joke. More "proofs"/theory than others. MTs avgd 66, 71 but the curve was phenomenal. If u have any inclination/intuition for math and do the textbook problems you'll pass. I recommend taking it in a lighter sem so u can get the most out of it!

One of the best professors I have ever had. He genuinely cares for his students and will take time to answer any questions. Exams are no joke, you will need to really study to do well, but he is not trying to trick you. The curve at the end of the class goes crazy, it was at least 10 points. If you have to take 347, take it with Rimanyi.

Crazy curve-- had a 50% average on midterms, ended up with a B. Very good lecturer, but can be a little condescending when answering questions about grades/tests-- if you ask how to prepare he'll just say read the textbook, but you have to trust him on that because that is genuinely all you have to do

A lot more conceptual than other linear sections. If you wanna do well on the exams you have to really study the theory/proofs imo. Awesome lectures. Definitely take Rimanyi if you're a math major or just very interested in the subject!
Good prof and lecturer, but his tests are awful. He does curve a LOT though. If you like math you will probably appreciate this class.

Great honestly clearcut professor. Class characterized by "give it respect and respect will be returned" format. Lectures are at times proof heavy, but greatly contribute to understanding. Useful if you are a math major/someone with genuine interest to learn Linear all around (if so you will be GREATLY rewarded) but if not you will have to study
Was condescending in office hours and on Piazza
One of, if not the best teacher in the math department

He is an incredible professor. This is a hard class, especially over the summer session, but he made it so interesting and even though I almost failed it I would take another class with him because he teaches in such a way that it forces you to have an incredibly deep understanding of the material which is incredibly valuable

Rimanyi is the best math lecturer I've had at UNC. He teaches the material in an extremely approachable way without sacrificing any rigor. You can tell by the way he explains proofs and guides you through the course content that he wants you to understand. Very tough class, but was by far the best math class I have taken here.

I usually don't rate professors but i need to get this out of my chest. He is the best teacher I've ever had. MATH521 is a challenging class but he made it truly enjoyable. He made everything so intuitive and was so helpful in office hours. He truly cares about teaching and makes us appreciate the BEAUTY of theoretical math. Make sure to study HWs.

Rimanyi is probably the best professor that you can have for a course like MATH 521. His lectures are very well organized and I really think he cares that the students learn the concepts. The tests were also fair, just make sure to study all the homework problems that he assigns before the exams. I would highly recommend him for MATH 521!

Professor Rimanyi is a knowledgeable professor. He will give you the main ingredients you to need to be aware of (i.e. definitions and theorems) for the types of proof questions you will encounter on homework assignments and tests. Do not assume lectures will give you all the answers. You will have to put in the work and effort outside of class.

Prof. Rimanyi is a great instructor who never hesitates to answer any student questions or confusions. However, although I enjoyed his class, even given the short time frame of the summer semester, expect fairly difficult exams that may or may not cover weekly material. Don't get me wrong, Prof. Rimanyi's class was great, but be aware of his exams.

Rimanyi was solid as a math major but if you're not into pure math and want pure computational linear algebra take it with someone else. Big curve, fair homework, but lots of proofs that can be tricky.

As a math major, I would 10/10 recommend another math major to take linear algebra with Professor Rimanyi. He taught the course the right way by including the theory behind the computation. Professor Rimanyi teaches in a way that respects the beauty of mathematics, and his lectures were great. The exams are tough, but there is a fair curve.

Rimanyi is the best lecturer Ive ever had at UNC. He is accessible and extremely intelligent. You understand his material well. His section is very much proof based compared to others. The exams are rough tbh. But he's fair because he curved us A LOT. For reference I had a 94 hw avg, 55 mid1, 76 mid2, (didnt release final grade), and got a B.
Such a nice guy but can get too into theory. The tests were so hard. Thought I failed the final but I guess so did everyone else. Other profs had easier tests.

Professor Rimanyi is a unique linear instructor on campus in that he emphasizes the importance of understanding concepts rather than simply computing problems. He does a very good job of explaining concepts in lecture, and has supplemental videos uploaded to Canvas for personal review. Tests are proof-heavy, but not bad if you do problem practice.

His lectures are great, and I learned a lot. I am awful at proofs, and did no better in this class at them than in others. They make up large majority of test and homework problems. He also never released our final exam grades so idk what I got. But he must have placed a large curve because I ended up with a B. Hes a nice guy, but tests are hard.

If you are reading this, and if your not a math major, please do not take this class with this guy. He's not a bad person, he's lectures are not bad, however, the midterms are really hard. There is only 5 questions in midterms, and 9 in the final. Almost all of the questions are proof based. Really hard class. I got better in my discrete class.

Great professor. First of his lectures were great. He would connect the math to the real world which was cool. His first exam was hard, but I would say the second exam and the final were definitely better. I would say really study the textbook! The proofs are not bad, the textbook is really helpful to solve them.

Dr. Rimanyi was amazing. This class is very proof/concept heavy (more so than other linear sections). But he does a great job relating theory to computation.
Tests are pretty difficult imo; combination of proofs/computation/TF.
He's a really nice guy and made linear algebra so interesting.
Good curve at the end that makes up for hard tests.

Very smart guy but this course covers more theory than other sections. Linear algebra is very easy computationally but this class requires computations done by hand on exams and are also a lot of proofs / theory based questions as well. You'll learn a lot but a less in depth course would still have been adequate for most majors

Absolute GOAT, best prof I've had at UNC. Great lecturer, explains concepts clearly, entertaining guy, tells jokes and funny stories in class. Cares a lot about student learning and very helpful in office hours. Has reasonable expectations for this course and is fair to students in terms of grades. Char limit is too short to say enough good things.

Very nice person and is extremely intelligent, delivering very interesting and in depth lectures. You are certain to learn a lot in his class. That being said, his exams are extremely difficult and the final was horrendous. He gives proofs and really vague true or false on the exam that are very hard and just not fair at all.
I have scarcely felt melancholy after the conclusion of a course.

Rimanyi is definitely a great professor and explains concepts very clearly. However, tests are HARD and the proof-based homework problems are tricky as well. It is a more difficult math 347 section, especially if you have never had exposure to the topic or this is your first college math class. Rimanyi is great though and pretty accessible.

Any reviews negative towards Rimanyi are reviewing the class, not the professor. Rimanyi is an understanding, funny, and clearly intelligent professor. He explains difficult concepts in great depth and tries his best not to leave any student behind. He is VERY strict on test grades, but our period constantly outscores others. Take 233 with Rimanyi.

Very good in comparison to all math professors at UNC. Did lots of practice problems in class and his lectures were very clear. Midterms were very short and can be easy if you study. Would highly recommend.

He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. He tries his best to ensure students understand the material and gives everyone extensions on homework. This class was hard for me since I'm not used to lecture-based classes and I got a D on the first exam. I ended up mostly teaching myself with Khan Academy but his lectures were helpful

It's calc, so the class sucks, but he was a nice lecturer. Not sure why other reviews say he didn't do practice problems in class because a lot of the midterm/final questions directly mirror class examples. Recitation topics don't always line up, which is annoying, but if you review those problems as well, you should be prepared for the exams.
It's a math class. It was my fault for the grade. Amazing professor. He's very funny and super into math. He recently graduated from UNC, so he knows a lot of the newer jokes and whatnot.

Professor Compton is a very good teacher, but the homework and tests just ruin it for me. The grading is unfair for how difficult the homework and tests are, and the difficulty did not help me learn more. You need to teach yourself all the homework and make this class a very high priority. Terrifying grader and hardest class in my life.

Go to office hours, do the homework, and ask questions. The class is very hard and requires significant study time. The first test is manageable, but the second is much more difficult. Dr. Compton is super nice and explains the material very well; just be prepared to put in the work. Im on track to get a B.

I love Dr. Compton! He was an absolutely amazing professor. His tests are hard but are always fair, if you study the materials he gives you you'll do great. Make sure you study, you cant pass this class without doing so!
This is a super hard class. other sections easier

Professor Compton was a great teacher! He really cares about students and whether they understand the material. Calc is test-heavy, but he always offered at least one freebie on each exam (apart from the final). The final was hard, but the entire department made that final. Overall, a great teacher, and arguably the best one for Calc at UNC.
Had a very hard time taking this class. Did not end well
Really hard class in comparison to other sections. Only if you really want a big challenge
His test are way harder than the level he teaches.
There HAS to be better teachers to take this class with...

Professor Compton was able to make us laugh and make good connections while teaching. He recognizes which students attend every class. He's very clear in his explanations and tries to provide help outside of class. His exams are difficult but he also tries to give extra credit. No matter the professor, calc 3 is going to be hard.
Great in office hours but lectures felt a little fast and kind of jumpy at times.

Good at explaining content in class but the homework is completely different and challenging. Be prepared to go to office hours if you want to understand it. Even though lecture is not required, not everything he talks about is on the posted notes so I would recommend attending most.
Way harder than other teachers…

He is a silly and entertaining professor. His lectures were very clear and understandable. The tests were difficult, but expected with this class. He did randomly call on students, which was terrifying. Also, I had university-approved absences, and he took points off for them.
He is super funny and made learning fun, but has a bit of an ego. Made tests super hard for no reason and just graded harshly
Just not a great person to take any class with. Hard class to begin with, tests are hard and unfair

He is super accessible and presents the information in a way that is easy to understand. He is a very nice guy, and enjoys teaching. However, the tests were really hard and we didn't have many resources outside of homework and recitations to study for them. Lowest midterm is replaced with the final, making the final theoretically 48% of your grade.
I really enjoyed the class and his lectures were very informative. He is a very hard grader so it's hard to justify taking any class with him

He is able to teach the material well, but everything is so much more difficult than what is learned in class. Definitely pay attention to what you did on the homework and if you don't understand something ask in office hours because test questions are often similar to homeworks. Look at book practice problems, they are sometimes on tests too.

He is a nice professor and is clearly passionate about the subject, but his exams are incredibly difficult with no review material or practice exams given. I took Calc 2 with him and liked his teaching style, so I took 381 with him. But compared to the other sections of this course, Compton makes it unnecessarily difficult.

Dr. Joe is a solid option for 233. He's caring towards students and encourages you to come to office hours. Lectures are clear, but some topics are only covered in recitation so make sure your recitation TA is good. His exams are no walk in the park, but they prepare you very well for the department-created final.

great lecturer and very funny! unfortunately his exams are insanely hard, and he provides zero study materials.  he pulls from recitation, HW and lecture notes, so to prepare for the exams you need to practice everything. I still suggest him if you actually plan on learning calc 3, because i doubt youll find a better or kinder teacher then him
He is so funny. Overall really great person to take a class with. The only issue is that he will destroy you with his grading...

He seems like a nice guy, but his lectures were pointless. He spent half of every class trying to develop analogies that were unhelpful and sometimes inappropriate. Once we got to the actual material he would breeze through it. Tests were fair though and the class itself isn't too hard if you put in the work to study and do practice problems.
Would rec that you consider other options. Good teacher incredibly hard grading for no reason espescialy for first semester of college.

Dr.Compton is a great professor if you attend lectures. I found him to be very accessible outside of class and helpful. However, I found his exams to be quite difficult they are nothing compared to recitation or lecture. He does drop lowest homework and replaces one test with final. P.S. This was my first semester at UNC
Half the class did horribly other did fine. He didn't seem to be too upset about how poorly some of us were doing.

Lectures don't match the difficulty of exams/hw. Midterms and final exam decide your grade, and the 5% project is hours of work with strict grading. No practice tests or guides, and Edfinity isn't aligned. Many with strong calc backgrounds struggled (class stats shared only on first midterm, and it was a 67%). ONLY take if you can FULLY commit.
Very good lecturer and a very nice prof. Also very helpful in office hours. The class and tests are tough, but if you are willing to put in lots of effort it is possible to do well
Don't take if there are other options.

Difficult and time consuming homework, no practice exams or study guide, not clear on what he puts on midterms. Grading was harsh and unfair. He's fine in lecture, but makes the class entirely more difficult than it needs to be. Random quizzes to count for attendance & only drops one to account for sickness, so if you have to miss more you're SOL.
Very harsh grader. Terrifying.

I'm not sure why he has good ratings on here... He is very condescending, which is not a productive enviornment for learning difficult subjects like math. He doesn't give any practice for exams. Also, you can do great and understand all the topics on midterms, but then do slightly bad on the final and it will tank your grade.

Took him for Calc 2 and really liked him, so decided to take for discrete and regretted it. I know discrete is supposed to be hard, but not this hard. Homework is impossible to do with going to office hours and/or using AI/internet (and even then still incredibly hard). Test questions are also unnecessarily difficult. Don't recommend taking him.
Great lecturer. Tests were so hard I had to start therapy.
Great teacher. Do not rec taking unless you are very strong at math. Think deeply before taking this class.

I loved dr. Compton's lectures, he really teaches the concepts in a way which makes them easy to understand. My one big problem with this class is the tests.From what I saw with friends in other sections, our tests were more difficult and had way less study materials.

I love Dr. Compton! He's a great lecturer and truly cares about his students. I'd def recommend showing up to lecture and doing your homework w/out ai. Also go to office hours! He is super accessible and helpful in smaller group settings. For exams I go over his worksheets and I use my friends' old exams for practice. Exams are fair imo.

Super nice guy and definitely a good teacher. The only thing is the exams are nothing like any of the practice you do in class, homework or recitation and he refuses to give practice tests. Also can be unorganized as multiple times we have had homework for topics we need to know on a test due weeks after the test.

Dr. Compton is an amazing lecturer and strives to ensure that his students truly understand the content. If you don't show up to class, you're cooked, but if you do an actively take notes, you'll be fine. Make sure to study before midterms though! Midterms are a hefty portion of the grade, but he replaces your lowest midterm with the final.

Great lecturer and super funny but the exams are very hard and it's kind of hard to determine what you need to know for these exams. He will make questions based on things outside of lecture that you practiced in recitation or on the homework. Wish he was more clear on exam topics and expectations

I took this class with him over the summer after not doing so well on Calc 3 the semester before. He made the concepts easier to understand, and would help so much during office hours, and was very approachable. For this class, it seemed like the class had a structure, and the guided notes were very helpful in following along.

Haven't finished the course yet, but I am a big fan of Dr. Joe. He comes from teaching high school and it's very obvious. He goes very slowly in class and explicitly outlines instructions and the mathematical intuition that is very hard to teach. However, examples in class r nothing like the exam. prepare to do a lil self study.

Really great professor. I took this class during summer, so I don't know if a smaller class size makes a difference, but Joseph made sure to try to keep every student engaged. He also had prepared notes that you filled out in class, so it made it easy to follow along.

Class pacing was poor (his first time teaching the course), but the content was quite easy. Some homework questions were deeper topics than what we learned in class which sucked. I thought he was funny. People say he was condescending: he was sassy when you asked a question 10 minutes after he asked if the class had questions about that topic.. lol

He was an alright teacher and was very nice. Homework took a while but nothing insane. Midterms were very hard and did not give study material. I do not feel like he prepared us well for the final. A lot of it was just the class, it was by far my least favorite class. Midterms + Final were 75% of the grade, and no drops which others teach's offered

Curved 2 midterms, then told us we were “cooked” right before starting the final, then dropped the curve entirely. No grading scale, no clear policy, and final scores hidden until grades were locked. Some secret points added to the final after complaints. Grading felt arbitrary, dismissive, and shady. If you value fairness, avoid this professor.

He was very full of himself and often skipped steps that seemed "easy" to him. The first few units weren't terrible but the semester went down. He favors power series and put them on every exam where as other sections only had 1 exam on them. Class structure is super random and not linear. He has a great attitude tho!

It was the attitude that got me. He's a fine professor and the class wasn't too hard if you showed up. He said that he used to be a high school teacher and would bring those methods which could've been helpful without the condescending tone. Not hard but I definitely wouldn't take a class with him again.

Chill professor overall. not sure if this is a him thing but grading for this course was super unclear and people often didn't know where they stood. he grades homework unnecessarily hard too, but his lecture style is pretty good. don't like how hard his exams are especially compared to other sections.

I'm not very good at math, and the first unit was honestly incredibly easy. Everything went downhill from there. Pacing was awful, lots of homework, no curves, no extra credit, 3 midterms, a 3-part final research project, and a cumulative final exam. One of the worst 100 level classes I've taken. Compton is rude, condescending, and hard to talk to.

Not a horrible class to take, but he spent so much time on the first unit that we didn't get enough time for the other units and it screwed us over during midterms. He got a bit rude to us and would ask us to ask questions but then gave attitude if we did. I would still give him a chance though!

Very tough class compared to other 100-level classes. No extra credit, no make-up exams, no curve. Lots of homework. And he is not very nice to change the grades when you forgot to sign up during class.   And there is no review session before the exams. Time for preparing the exam is limited.

Very condescending and not great when you have to ask questions or for help. Often times the homework was not things he taught us, and he tries to shove a lot of information into a unit test that should've been spread out across a few units. Four units, 14 homework assignments, final was a project and a cumulative exam.

Compton was a great lecturer and made himself available during office hours. 232 is a difficult course but the tests were made fairly based on the problems seen in class. I would recommend reviewing in-class notes if you have him before the exam, those are the kinds of questions you will be tested on, not whatever is on Edfinity.

he chill imo
does a good job explaining stuff in class and during office hours
Very hard grader, take a grad student

Overall, I really enjoyed taking Math 232 with Joe this semester, and I would totally take another class with him in the future. I'm not a big fan of calculus, but I really like Joe's personality and he is super approachable outside of class! You definitely can't go wrong with him for 232.
Professor Compton is excellent at explaining concepts, and his classes are great!

Compton is a great professor. His lectures are easy to understand, and he always stops before and after class to answer any questions that people have. His tests are fair, and he hosts office hours that are very helpful to figuring out the homework and studying for exams. If you need to take math at UNC I highly recommend!

I would highly recommend Dr. Compton for any math class, especially 110. He does a great job simplifying topics and making sure everyone understands the class concepts. He is kind, funny, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Algebra should not be a difficult class, and Dr. Compton makes sure of it.

Dr. Compton was my favorite teacher so far at UNC. He was so helpful and easily accessible when having trouble in class. Lectures went through how to do everything we needed to learn and was open to answering questions. He also hosted review sessions before exams. I 100% recommend him.

Dr. Joe is an amazing lecturer. He taught high school previously, and I found he was really able to connect with the students in a more down-to-earth and approachable manor. Tests were manageable, however, homework didn't always align with what was taught in class. If you pay attention in class and do the study guides you will get a good grade.

As most math courses, this was very heavily weighted on midterms and the final. Tests were difficult and long for the amount of time we got. Despite the difficulty of the class, Compton made the content as clear as possible. He was very accessible and good at answering questions. I highly recommend!

Dr. Compton is an excellent teacher. He is friendly, funny, accessible, and has a knack for breaking down tricky concepts very well. Midterms were not easy, and class averages tended to reflect that (~70%), but Calc 2 is hard in and of itself. Irregardless, I highly recommend Dr. Compton.

Prof Compton is easily the best math teacher I've had. He explains content thoroughly and makes the lectures rly engaging. The homework can be difficult but if you can understand it then midterms shouldn't be too bad. Although the timing of the midterms wasn't ideal, he curved the final, which boosted my grade from an A- to an A. Def recommend!
Overall really good professor, homework was tough at times and not always related to test materials, exams were all fair, replaces lowest midterm grade with final.

Given how difficult Calc 2 is, Compton made it seem very straightforward and easy to understand. He explained concepts so in-depth, and his lectures were super easy to follow. He was also very funny and caring towards his students. Calc 2 is hard af no matter who you have but he was great.

I've heard a rumor that math 232 is the most failed class at the school (no idea if that's actually true) but Dr. Compton is peak. Exams make up almost 80% of your grade but he replaces your lowest midterm with your final. Tests are fair and homework is hard. Dr. Compton is overall a cool guy and checked all of the boxes and more. Engaging lectures

Dr. Compton is an amazing person! The class was tough but he did his best to help us on the midterms and the final! He drops a few homework assignments, which were online and more difficult than the exams, and also replaced our lowest midterm with the final. Overall, great professor just get ready to study a lot!

If you have to take a math class at UNC, take it with Dr. Compton. He made harder concepts easily understandable and really took the time to slow down if needed. He was very reachable outside of class and there were a few extra credit opportunities. Truly one of the best professors at UNC.

Notes during class presents the new topic with easy-to-do examples. Homework is quite a bit more difficult so the notes don't prepare you all too well. Midterms and final make up most your grade and the averages are in the low 70s. Tricky to prepare for the tests well since resources are scarce. Final was difficult.

Lectures are very clear, but the pace of the class makes it hard to keep up at times. The midterms created by him were much harder than the final, but the class never felt horribly unfair. The only unfair feeling part of the class was the midterms and final being worth 78% of your grade in total. Pay attention and you should be good.

Joe is the math prof i've ever had. takes a hard class and makes it enjoyable. knows most of his students by name.   lectures are so good and he posts all completed notes. midterms are hard and worth a lot of your grade, but if you pay attention in class and go to office hours you'll be fine. homework way harder than the test but good practice.

I really like Professor Compton because he is very caring and shows so much passion for teaching math. However, this class was the most difficult class I have ever taken and the exams were extremely hard. The class averages were never too great for these exams, but you genuinely learn a lot in this class. Also, make sure to go to class.

Great professor!! I had Dr. Compton for college algebra b/c of have no foundational math skills haha. He was a phenomenal teacher and introduced a conversational style in his lectures, as he used to be a high school teacher. He does a great job explaining concepts and always takes questions. I purposefully signed up to take math 130 w him next sem!

I loved him I had him for math 110!!!! So funny and caring!! He is so sweet attendance was mandatory sometimes (we did in-class assignments). I would so take his class again. after hearing what other math 110 teachers are like I think he is one of the better ones.
Hard class, but a good teacher. He wants to help you. Clear information.
I love Calc 232 with Dr. Compton! He is readily available, wants us to succeed, and funny in class. Clearly explains information and his teaching style is very explicative. Very very good teacher!

He is very good at communicating information and helping you understand how to utilize the theoretical knowledge taught in class on questions. Exam questions are very straightforward and reasonable. The final was pretty challenging and you can lose significant points for small mistakes on the homework. Overall, he is a very good professor to have.

Joe is the best. I've heard of much easier 381 teachers, but Joe is an amazing teacher even if his exams can be difficult. He explained everything very well and is super accessible, and we learned a lot more than other sections. He encourages participation, attending office hours, and working in groups all of which made the class great

Great class! He wrote me recs for some summer programs which I really appreciated. He teaches almost directly by the textbook (which you could find online), so reading outside of class isn't really necessary but it can help if you don't understand something from in class.

Dr. Huang is a kind and respectful professor. However, his lectures are not the primary way to learn the material, so independent study is essential. Attendance is tracked through in class worksheets. Midterms are manageable with practice questions. The final is harder. Best suited for self directed learners. Learn from Professor Leonard.

He is genuinely terribl at teaching, attendance is mandatory and that is the only reason I went. I try to follow along since I'm there but there just is no lesson planning at all. The exams aren't bad, but you do need to teach yourself everything for them.
He basically cannot teach. The class is very disorganized, and everyone in class is sleepy and distracted by sth else, doing their own things.

For math majors who are taking math 528 as a degree requirement, it is truly a waste of time to come to class, since you cannot learn anything useful immediately in class. You always need to do extra work after it. He is always trying to cover up the fact that he teaches very poorly by treating students with pleasing.

The lectures aren't very helpful, so I just went to class for participation. You're going to have to self study a lot, but the topics covered on the tests are VERY clear, he tells us exactly what kind of questions to know how to do. I basically taught myself everything with the textbook, but the class is really easy to get a good grade in.

MATH 528: This guy is nice, but sometimes he will go off on tangents talking about his research or loosely related topics.. like please just get back to the lesson. Also, that second midterm was extremely difficult since it involved proofs, computer output, and sum/difference trig identities.

Never understood any of his lectures. Rambles a lot, and his class notes are not useful for tests only the homeworks are which he doesn't teach us how to do. Has in-class worksheets so attendence is mandatory but chooses the easiest questions for them. Midterms are strange and not what we do in class.

The syllabus of his 235 is unreasonable. Too many concepts he wants to cover, and there's even not one main textbook but only his OneNote, which is sometimes super confusing. He always wants to focus on something comprehensive, but it IS the instructor's job to lead students to dive into details all the time. Y'all should take 233 with another Prof

For M528. There are two sections for this course this semester. I was on the waitlist of another section for two months, from November until the waitlist was purged in January. So he was the only option left for me to take 528 with. He couldn't rephrase the concepts taught in 383 clearly. Thankfully this course has a tb, otherwise you'll get lost.
I am very surprised he is allowed to be a professor. The two lectures I went to were agony. Disorganized, confusing, and not at all conductive to learning. Swapped to a different section.

I dropped this class on the first day to switch to a different section. I had a very hard time understanding him. I was confused the entire class period. It took me an hour to realize he was trying to explain how to multiply vectors, a relatively easy concept. He also danced around questions when asked, instead of just giving a straight answer.

His class is super disorganized and boring. Though he makes the exams reasonable and easy, the contents of 235 are still heavy. He always emphasized on 'big picture', which sometimes confusing and useless. Overall, good teacher but not fitting to teach.

Professor Huang is caring and kind, however, the class was extremely disorganized. Attendance isn't mandatory, but all the answers to the worksheets are in the lecture. I think we spent barely a week on the last few topics, and it made up a good amount of the final. Be ready to learn things on your own and go to tutoring/office hours.
Nice professor and very willing to provide help.

Advantages: fast grading, cheat sheets, extra credit, and quick responses on Piazza. The instructor offered insights into the practical application of concepts in research or hints about future advanced courses. While the class was disorganized, keeping up with lectures made the exams manageable. The concepts were challenging but explained easily.

Caring and intelligent man. But I'm not sure, with his level of intelligence, that he quite grasps what an undergrad is capable of. First exam average was ~95, next two and the final average were around 50-70. There were topics that were on the final that we never discussed in class. Prepare to self-teach (though office hours can also be helpful).
I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR HE IS AWESOME AND SUCH A COOOL DUDE LOVE THE PIAZZA. THE GOAT OF THE MATH DEPARTMENT.
He is so sweet and caring. Highly recommended.

He's a kind, smart guy. However this class is pretty difficult, and very exam heavy. He graded the final really kindly, but there were also questions that didn't resemble anything we did in class. Not the most organized class, and you may have no clue what is going on. Fantastic dude, difficult class. Achievable for a 500 level math, but hard.

Super nice teacher! Though his lecture might be somewhat disorganised, he gave us many chance to improve our grades (i.e. replace the lowest midterm and 2 extra credits). Math235 is mixed by Math232/233/347/383, therefore it is not easy to catch up everything at first. But if you put some effort you should get at least an A- (this semester >40%)

Professor Huang is extremely knowledgeable and willing to help. However, his lectures are disorganized and hard to follow. He often assumed prior knowledge of material from courses that were not formal prerequisites. The difficulty of the final exam did not reflect that of the Midterm and HW's (which he told us would adequately prepare us).

Professor Huang is one of the nicest and smartest people I've met. However, he does not know how to teach. His lectures are disorganized and impossible to follow. You can get a good grade since homework, lab, and attendance combine for 40%. If you want to learn anything though do not take this class. You will have to teach yourself everything.

SUPER SWEET!! Really kind professor who cares about his students and wants to ensure they understand the material. His lectures are slightly unorganized but going to office hours and tutoring helps a bunch. Replaces the lowest midterm with final and drops lowest worksheet/lab/hw grade!!

You have to review heavily outside of class and hope for the best going into exams since his lectures and notes make absolutely no sense. But, he is a very kind professor and is accessible and willing to help.

Very very nice guy. cares about his student. unfortunately a bad teacher. his intellect is too high to dumb down his steps down for us undergrads. Doesn't write down all the steps and does all problems in general terms. no concrete examples done with numbers (aside from some worksheet/HW problems) until the midterm.

Best professor ever! lecture is a bit unorganized but just go to his oh, large curve and easy homework, drop the lowest midterm replaced by final, he will explain questions patiently after class, choose him without doubt

Although attendance isn't mandatory you kinda have to go to every lecture to understand what was going on. The lecture notes are not very helpful and often make no sense.
