best professor, just take his class

Extremely disorganized. Lectures were confusing and unhelpful in learning course content--he spent a lot of time going over course topics at a high level but didn't know how to explain many concepts. He made simple concepts more complex than they should've been. Tests were pretty fair. There's definitely worse out there in the math department.

Take Linear with Jingfang. TRUST. Adeslsteinson is so hard and everyone in know in that class is struggling. jinfang exams are really fair and he is overall a sweet dude. he also curved the second exam. TAKE IT WITH HIM

Huang was a decent enough professor. It was the first time this class was offered so it was a little bit disjointed, but the class in and of itself was not too bad, and office hours were very helpful especially before exams. Generous curve and opportuninities to get free points/extra credit. Most of the content can be studies using online resources

Professor Huang is one of the nicest professors I've had at UNC. He really wants you to do well. MATH235 was unorganized and confusing at times, because he wasn't following a set curriculum, and it was new. Overall good experience.

First time this course was offered at UNC and was very disorganized. Professor Huang is very caring and accessible outside of class, fast grader, but uses a lot of technical language off the bat and it could be difficult at times to understand him in lecture. Allowed students to have 10 hand-written cheat sheets per midterm and 30 on final.

I didn't think he was the best at teaching things and it lead me to teach myself almost all the concepts outside of class through online videos. His tests were hard IMO and I've heard from friends and people around me the other linear professor is better, adalstein or something.

Professor Huang is one of nicest professor that I've had at UNC. He was always available outside of class though the piazza and office hours, and is very quick to reply. He is however, incredibly unorganized. It might be because the class was new this semester, but the lectures and notes were almost impossible to follow. Tests hard.

Prof. Huang is a very nice guy and he really cares about his students' success; his exams had generous curves and all of his grading was very fair. However, he was extremely unorganized, both logistically and in the classroom. It was near impossible to understand what was going on in his lectures and assignment deadlines were changed constantly.
Best of the best, the only thing is the lectures are either 8 or 9 AM and that's TOOOOOO early!

Very good prof, give alot of help, reply to email and piazza really fast!!!!! Super fast grader!!!!!(our finals finish at 7pm, he gave the exam back to us at 3am the next day, which is like 8hrs later) really care about his student. Alot of curves on exams as well!

Dr. Huang does his best to make sure every student succeeds. 2 of the 3 midterms were "curved" (more like test corrections), and he would do his best to answer every question. Responsive on Piazza. Recitation focused on Python application of concepts. Learn how to "drive the car" and apply mathematical concepts, as he says.
The best, kindest, and most accessible math professor you can ever have at UNC. The course is an easy A and super inspirational. Office Hour is brilliant. Take him!

He is very nice, but he is extremely unorganized. No one ever knows what's going on and his lectures make no sense. One of our midterms average was a 50 and he barely curved it. The homework is very difficult and his lectures don't prepare you at all for the homework or tests.

Professor Huang is a kind-hearted person more than willing to assist you when you have questions. The exams are not horrible. In fact, a majority of the exam questions are related to the homework assignments. There are also 3 group projects that may or may not be time-consuming depending on your previous programming experience. Take him!

Kindest professor at UNC in terms of attitude, responsiveness to Piazza questions, test difficulty, and grading. Helpful and patient in OH. Fastest grader at UNC (final released in 9 hours). Homework questions feel different from other classes' but you do learn a lot. Highly recommend Prof. Huang for any class.
Very smart professor, office hours can help a lot. Getting the big picture idea is very important in class.

Professor Huang is really a great guy. He is friendly and caring. His tests are not hard, and he didn't give us too much homework to do. But make sure to understand the worksheets and check if there is anything you don't understand. The only thing is that he didn't explain things well enough. However, his office hour is useful.

A solid choice for 521. Final was hard but he curved it and has a generous grading scale. Soft spoken lecturer but his lectures are organized and his handwriting is really clear for a math prof. Read the textbook and prepare to study.
Very nice. Not a great professor to teach lower level math, he expects a lot from you and does not explain clearly. You'll need to learn a lot on your own.
He does not reply to email. He will tell you he will respond within 24 hours on Piazza but he doesn't. Does not submit grades on time.

Prof Assani cares about his students. His lectures make 521 like learning a new way of thinking. Go to office hours and ask for help, he wants you to succeed, so he will help. My sole complaint was the disparity in difficulty between this year's final and the material we had seen all semester/last year's final, but he does challenge you to think.
GOAT of a professor. Super awesome guy and really cares about the material and about his students. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He will help you. Super great guy, really recommend.

I would like to preface this by saying I am a math major, so hopefully this review strikes your perspective more than the negativity I've seen for Assani. Assani is genuinely one of the best math professors: he's funny, very helpful in office hours, and makes sure you understand the concepts that are going on- all you have to do is ask for help.

While professor seems knowledgeable, accent creates understanding challenges. Classroom experience feels scattered, making learning difficult. Tests feel overwhelming compared to material covered. Tech problems slow us down. May want to explore other section options.

Communication barriers due to accent significantly impact lecture comprehension. Course lacks structured organization and clear learning objectives. Assessment difficulty exceeds course level. Recurring technical difficulties with course materials affect learning experience. Alternative instructor recommended.

AVOID! Professor's heavy accent makes lectures incomprehensible. Teaching style is completely chaotic with zero organization. Exams are impossibly difficult and seem designed for failure. Can't handle basic technology - constant issues with uploads and course materials. Save your GPA and sanity - pick another professor!

Dr. Assani was a good professor. The material is obviously not straightforward but his exams generally were right out of class. I felt I learned a lot and was not too overwhelmed so I recommend Dr. Assani.
I could not understand him or/and the course material for the life of me.

Prof. Assani is definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. His philosophy is that learning MATH 521 is like learning a new language, so he really cares about you learning the material well. He answers questions thoroughly and patiently, and lectures are super engaging. 521 is difficult but you absolutely should take it with Assani.

Don't be afraid of Assani, he is nicer than you think. Attendance isn't mandatory but good luck keeping up if you don't attend. Homework was due weekly on friday and group quizzes on Saturday - timing sucks but often nicer than in the middle of the week. Start HW early and attend office hours.

Math 521 is hard no matter what professor you get. Assani is nice, his office hours are helpful, and his TA graded super fast. Exams were fair, homework was due every friday, and group quizzes were due on Saturdays. Definitely start homeworks early. Overall good class.

Assani was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was hilarious and kind and I looked forward to going to class every day. His lectures are a little bit hard to follow sometimes, but he answers every question very patiently and never makes you feel stupid for not understanding. I felt like he wanted me to learn and understand the material.

Assani was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was hilarious and kind and I looked forward to going to class every day. His lectures are a little bit hard to follow sometimes, but he answers every question very patiently and never makes you feel stupid for not understanding. I felt like he wanted me to learn and understand the material.

Couldn't understand a word he said. He has a fairly heavy accent but that was not even the problem. He was practically whispering and no one is the class could hear him. When asked to speak up he straight up said no. I dropped the class and switched to a diff prof for 521 and am so glad. From the days I was there his teaching was all over the place

The most lovely man, extremely intelligent, like the smartest person I've ever met (and probably will ever meet). 521 is a super hard class that I struggled a lot in but he was so kind and really did everything to help me understand during office hours.

521 is a very hard class in general, but Assani does his best to make it better. Weekly group quizzes that he offers a lot of help on, and exams are hard but manageable. The smartest person you'll ever meet, and answers every question superbly, but has a french accent so it may be hard to understand. Overall, the best prof. for 521 (15 pt. grading)

For MATH383: If you want to actually learn material in class do not take this professor. Extremely unorganized, 8am office hours, and only covered half the material we were supposed to learn. For 383. She is accessible. But you will lose a lot of points in the exam if she doesn't like the format you write. The class is highly disorganized and homeworks are graded harsh.

This is for MATH383: Just wanted to recommend people to not take this prof if you want to learn. I was taking 383 though. Course was very disorganized and she basically cannot finish the syllabus by the end of the semester. Midterms are graded pretty harsh. Your points always get unexpectedly deducted.
NOT A GOOD TEACHER! SOMETIMES A GOOD GRADER!
Don't be afraid to take her, she has improved as a professor and she's very nice. Lenient grader and is often understanding of circumstances.
I don't understand all the animosity towards Professor Dumitrescu. Yes, her lectures weren't the best but she was nice and curved our grades and was willing to help us whenever she could.
Actually do not take. Maybe the worst lecturer I've ever had. Shames people for asking questions.

Her lectures were terrible. They made no sense and even the TAs did not know what was going on some of the times. If I did not have a tutor, I would have definitely failed the class. She does not answer emails or consistently show up to office hours. However, she grades exams very easily.
Easy grading however lectures were completely useless. Uses homework often for midterms and exam. Would recommend another professor if possible though.
Horrible teacher, barely speaks english, i learned the entire course mylself and stopped going to lectures

I think if your main goal is to do well in Discrete, you should take this course. Her tests are very easy to BS because of the amount of partial and extra credit she gives. Horrible lecturer, commonly changes homework due dates at last minute, not accessible at all outside of class

Prof Dumitrescu is… a mixed bag. Some concepts she made moderately understandable, others not so much. Doing the homework as practice and putting in lots of work can help a ton tho.
confusing lectures yet super loose grading, definitely take her for credit. Also amazing fashion taste.

Very caring and thoughtful; Tests and grading are very fair. Sometimes HW deadlines are unreasonable, but she will change them if you talk to her and explain your concern. Would definitely recommend taking discrete with her.
BEST bonus questions and very thoughtful tests.

Do not recommend her for a class like Calc 1. Very disorganized and hard to understand. Often was confused by her own notes. Recommend taking a different professor.

Prof. Dumitrescu was very knowledgeable about her field, however, she was so incredibly intelligent to the point that her teaching a beginner level calc course was not the best fit. Lectures were disorganized, but she gave a lot of partial credit. Final was easy, not sure how I bagged an A.

I would suggest everyone take this 381! Her lectures definitely aren't the best, will require some amount of self-studying for homework. The homework grades don't have clear comments/feedback. She has disorganized lectures. VERY EASY grader. She gives so much partial credit and gave 10 extra points on the first exam. Legitimately so great. Professor Dumitrescu is very knowledgeable about calculus, but she teaches the class like the students already know the material. Dr. Dumitrescu should not be teaching an introductory calculus course. She doesn't follow the syllabus and often forgets what calculus is supposed to cover. It is also weird that students can negotiate grades by going to her office hours and everything is subjective.

One of the worst professors at UNC to teach Calculus. She will not follow the syllabus and go over whatever she wants. She is extremely disorganized and does not have clear grading criteria. NO MATTER WHAT YOU DO, DO NOT TAKE THIS 231 WITH HER! THIS CLASS RUINED MY GPA, AND I WILL NEVER RECOVER. TAKE IT WITH ANYBODY ELSE AND IF YOU CANNOT, TAKE IT DURING IN SS
Get ready to teach yourself all of calc 1. You should not take this course unless you have a background in calculus from hs. She is a nice person but her teachings make no sense what so ever

Such a sweet and brilliant professor, but I unfortunately had to teach myself the entire semester due to her lectures being disorganized and incomprehensible. if exam 2 average was a 64, and everyone i know got a sub 70 on the final, that is the professor's fault not the students. i showed up to her office hours but she confused me even more :( i wish i was smarter and passed the ap exam in hs because this class was a living hell

I think she is one of the most attractive professors here :) her jokes are funny to. sad I did bad in calc 100% recommend

Absolutely the worst math professor to ever exist at UNC. Nothing is clear to us whether it is what she's talking about or what she is expecting from her students. Her exams are extremely hard, and although I studied with people it was not enough to pass this course.

Nice, funny, extremely smart, but just not good at teaching Calculus 1 to people who don't know Calculus already.

I am outraged by the fact that she had TAs who allowed students to take home their weekly recitation quizzes and TAs who only allowed their students 10 minutes in class to complete quizzes. Dumitrescu was a difficult professor. She rarely explains topics to their full extent and rather expects you to understand concepts by looking at examples of them in context. This learning technique, while some may find it effective, was not helpful to me. The tests were extremely difficult and she seems uninterested in her students' success.

Pretty disorganized, but brilliant. If you've taken calc in hs and have a strong math background, you'll prob be fine, but if not, it'll suck. i thought she was funny, but without khan academy and my hs calc notes i would have been sol. make sure you understand the homework assignments and refer to the (free! online!) textbook if necessary.

The only way to get an A or B in this course is if you sit next to the smartest dude during exams. And that's what many people did in our section, as it is impossible to comprehend her lectures. Good thing that she was the only one proctoring exams and it is easy to cheat.

Do not take! She is very disorganized and each lecture topic is a mystery until halfway through. I had no idea what was going on all semester. The exams are worth 60% of your grade and have nearly impossible questions. Despite this, she is very caring and gives partial credit on exams and will work conflicts out with you. Still don't recommend.

If there is another professor, take Calc 1 with them. She will overcomplicate things because she is way too advanced for this course. I agree with the girl who yelled at her before exam 2 saying that if it took her 40 minutes to solve a practice exam problem, she shouldn't expect us to solve it.
She goes off topic way too much and covers content outside the scope of this course. The only reason I didn't give her a 1 is because she seems nice and her grading is not too bad.

DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU HAVE NOT TAKEN CALCULUS BEFORE! She is very disorganized when teaching. While she gives partial credit on exams even that isn't enough to help you pass. I have studied but none of the homework problems or practice problem prepare you for the tests. Even the UNC videos for calculus do not cover all of the content on the tests.
She is a good professor but the way she teaches is all over the place. She gets off topic during class and acts as we already know the topic.
Exam 2 in her class was one of the hardest exams I've ever taken. She gave us questions that we did not cover during the lecture. She is a passionate professor, but often goes off-topic.

She is a brilliant professor but I don't think her expertise is for a beginner calc class. The way she teaches topics is very complicated and it is tough to understand. She jumps around topics and skipped some that we need for the final and she does go in the proper order like the other professors. The exams were really hard too.

His lecture is better than other professors in the department but still overcomplicated concepts. Test worth 80% of the grade but exam preparation materials from TA doesn't match the difficulty. Lagging on feedbacks of the worksheet from TA. He teaches 233 without any graphs but all written words on slides. Promised a curve but never gave.

Prof.Christianson is great and his lectures are fun. 
Previewing some content would be nice if you want to understand the proofs and some extra content (not covered in exams). However, I'd say it's really not hard to succeed in his exams, as they are quite calculation-based. Go to his office hour for some great extra knowledge=)

Not my favorite prof in the math department. His tests asked easy questions but too many of them. Lectures were of poor quality. He lowk can't explain math to save his life. He did not release final grades or curve like he said he would. Made me sad.

Homework often went ungraded for months, while curves and score cutoffs were unclear, making it difficult to know where you stood. This is common in the Math Dept, as well as 80% of your grade being determined by 3 exams. Grading was extremely harsh, and lectures consistently overcomplicated already difficult material instead of providing clarity.

Love Dr. Christianson! Beyond being a great teacher, he's also a really nice guy and super helpful during office hours. I will say that his grading criteria isn't very clear on the syllabus, and with your grade being 80% exams it's important that you do pretty well on all of them (so you don't need to rely on potential curves at the end).
Hans is an incredible teacher if you are passionate about math. I was in his 233H and he lectures clearly. He covers a lot of content but keeps the midterms easy enough.

Professor Hans is an amazing professor with very clear lectures. His exams are a bit long, but very fair and based on the HW. Grades come back a bit slow, and the final exam scores and breakdown were not released.

3 tests counted for 80% of our grade, the rest was homework. He promised a curve and never gave it. Grade thresholds were also not on the syllabus. He is good at teaching the material, just wish we'd been graded more fairly.

Professor Hans is an exceptional professor that explains all the content in immense detail. He was quite repetitive, with over half of the next lecture being a review of the previous lecture. The exams were fair, but do not expect grades to come back quickly. I got my week 3 homework grade back week 12. Overall it was an easy class and I recommend.
So understanding and helpful! Exams and homeworks were very fair.

Great professor. Tried his best to get us to understand the very complicated material. Extremely understanding of students. However his grading policy is a little crazy with 20% for each midterm and 40% for the final. The rest is based on homework. He also does not share how he curves the tests and only applies curves at the end of the semester.

Genuinely amazing professor that made me want to go further in math despite struggling with the course materials. He answers every question thoroughly, no matter how simple it is. I really wish I had gone to more of his office hours so I could get to know him better. He makes hard tests but they are on the topics discussed and graded fairly.

Overall, he's an okay math professor for 347, but he overcomplicates his lectures entirely. His exams aren't too bad, but he gives you absolutely no study materials or even guides. It feels like he wants to be difficult. His lectures, exams, and hws are very different from each other so it's hard to figure out what is important.

Tends to overcomplicate explanations and not be clear when explaining concepts. Lecturers consists of only theorems and proofs which are difficult to understand, and I found his lecture style to be so overcomplicated. The exams are more application based and fair, but it felt like the lectures were useless.

Go to office hours! Linear algebra is just a hard topic but Hans truly does care about his students and wants to make sure you understand what you're doing and why you're doing it. I also think his exams are super reasonable like he won't throw anything wild at you. I def recommend him for 347.

Solid choice to take 521 with. Super accessible outside class, and explains concepts really well. Make sure you go to office hours, as they are really helpful! Homework loads are pretty fair. Midterms and finals are hard but doable. TAKE HIM!!!

Hans is phenomenal lecturer and 1 of the best profs u'll find in math dep. He is the only prof I would take this class with. 1 hw/week and 3 midterms. Go 2 office hrs! It is basically mini-lecture + he gives hw solutions. Exams r hard but doable. 5 proofs/test. Go over all proofs from class, at least 2 will b from notes. He sets u up for success
Reignited my love for math. I think most people find 521 to be terribly difficult, but I loved this man and this class so much that it was a joy to take.

Hans is great. I don't get the complaints about the workload — it's similar to other 5xx math classes. He barely used notes in lectures and still explained everything clearly. He's also very accessible outside class and chill to talk to. Yes, exams are tough and graded harshly, but they are fair. My only issue is that we covered too little topics.
Don't know what the other reviews are talking about. Assigns unnecessary homework and grades very harshly. Avoid.

Hands down the greatest professor I have had here at UNC. Amazing lecturer in class with exceptional pacing and color coding on the chalkboard. I never felt as if the class was dragging, and analysis was intuitive with his help! Very forgiving with grading and gives clear criteria for exams. Also very accessible for office hours.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He made this class so fun and made the content much more intuitive than I ever thought possible. He explains things so well and is very accessible outside of class. Office hours were incredibly helpful and got me through the class tbh. He's also super transparent about what will be on tests!
Great professor (taken 2 course with him as instructor)

Professor Mitran was the best math teacher I have ever had. He lectures incredibly well, and clearly has deep knowledge and passion for linear algebra. The class is very difficult, but the extra credit opportunities are ample and if you put in the work you'll be rewarded. The concepts in the class will stick with you.

Mitran is a solid professor, but very uptight. Thinks very highly of himself for sure. He does go very in depth to the content you are learning, and tries to connect it to applications. I feel as though he would likely be better off teaching a higher level course as opposed to more introductory courses. Prepare to work hard if you want to do well.

I'm a math person. My worst grade in a math class before this was 89. The first time we got real feedback on our understanding of anything was the midterm. He showed us a chart of everyone's scores, where 70% of the class had gotten less than 6/10, and more than 1/3 got less than 2/10.
At that point it's not the students' faults.
Awful professor. don't take this class. doesn't reply to emails. extremely rude and condescending and grades really hard.

Mitran is an OK teacher. Lectures can be somewhat dull and he's definitely a critical person. The class itself is very easy, especially if you read the textbook. 50% of the grade is homework, which he gives a lot of time to complete. The final was similar to practice tests he gave, so if you put in the effort you can definitely get an A.

Gives 10 pts of extra credit that act as 10% of your grade on top of 100% allocated to HW and Exams (so 110% in total). This allowed for a learning opportunity on the midterm, which many people did not take advantage of. In the end it was easy to see he just wants his students to learn, and id be surprised if anyone failed the final exam.

He might seem scary but if you are putting in effort i.e. doing all the homework, showing up to class and taking all extra credit opportunities your grade will be just fine. He definitely wants you to think about the material on a deeper level which is difficult but keep in mind you're taking an upper level math class it isn't meant to be easy.

Wow, where do I begin. Quite literally the worst math professor at UNC. Provides hardly any resources, ignores Canvas, grading policy shifts without notice. Unapproachable, so help is nonexistent.
Homework is difficult and takes a lot of time. Courses are disorganized
Worst professor I've ever had at UNC

Homework took forever and he only gave ~2-3 days to do it. Requires you to defend 3 HWs in office hours and made people cry w/ how rude and condescending he was. Look, Sorin is on purpose and doesn't want to teach to people that don't want to learn. Gave an extremely difficult midterm, most of the class failed (14 zeroes), no curve. Admitted to a mistake on the first question but gave no credit. Displayed students' exams on the board. Took off full points for formatting issues. This guy is so rude and condescending please avoid him at all costs.

Awful. The only saving grace is the numerous extra credit opportunities, but they are necessary to have any amount of success in the class. Only one midterm, but he is also rude, and his lectures are confusing and unorganized. The midterm is very unfair, with questions testing niche topics not covered enough in class. Homework is important.

i am writing this rn studying for the midterm tomorrow and lowk think im cooked. One of the worst professors I've ever had.He is extremely rude, condescending and doesn't  put much effort into his students, took 2 months to readjust the class schedule/dates.He even made a girl cry once and embarrassed her for eating an apple during an 8am lecture(in a large lecture hall),not to mention he locks the door when your late to class
Extremely rude

Professor Mitran is a very good professor he just has a very hard class. With that being said he is very generous with points and has a lenient grading system with extra credit. I walked out of the final thinking I would have to retake the class and ending up getting a B. The class is defiantly hard but you learn a lot and he does his best to help.

Dr. Mitran is the best math teacher at this school. LOTS of extra credit, I'm not complaining though

First class I've ever considered dropping out of but I'm very glad I didn't. You can't bs your way through this class and it gets HARD. Very likeable despite making fun of students in class. He makes the class very real-life applicable and if you put in the work, you will learn a lot. It's hard to explain but the class is worth the challenge 100%.
Although I like a lot of things about him, he is not approachable and is very unorganized due to lack of care for students (or at least that is the impression I got).

Dr Mitran, while intelligent and accomplished in his field is a poor lecturer. He assumes you know more than you do, and when you ask questions he is exceptionally patronizing. I used the opportunity to go to office hours and he was exceptionally rude and disrespectful to me. Grading on tests is also harsh..
I am in Math 347 Linear Algebra. This is a hard class but man is horrible. He mumbles through lectures and assumes you know more than you do. His tests are impossible. PLEASE DONT TAKE HIM.

Pros:

HORRIBLE PROF. I WOULD NOT TAKE ANOTHER CLASS WITH HIM IF MY COLLEGE DEGREE DEPENDED ON IT. And I truly mean that. So condescending. So rude. So impatient. Does not care about his students. 0/10.

Genuinely the worst professor I'VE EVER HAD! If you have another choice, DO NOT TAKE HIM! DO NOT TAKE! Worst lecturer i've ever had. Unclear about the syllabus and weight of assignments. Diffeq is easy material but he makes it 100x harder than it should be.

Midterms and Homework were simple and open note. Final was actually impossible and nothing like what was taught/what was on the homework or midterms. One of the hardest finals I have ever taken. Incredibly unprofessional. Did not provide any syllabus until a week into the semester, and when he did, it was only a schedule with his contact info. Lectures were not very clear, and self-studying is very necessary. Professor Camassa is very intelligent, but it can make the class more difficult.

0 lecture notes online, made us pay $100 for a book so he wouldn't have to grade homework, exams take weeks to be graded, final grade will be the last one I get by atleast a week. no idea what bro is saying half the time

Midterms are just like the practices, but lectures are impossible to understand and it is hard to ask questions. Getting a tutor outside of class is strongly advised, but if you understand the practice exams you will be fine. Midterms are open note (including digital notes) with calculator allowed.
Dr. Camassa explains concepts thoroughly in lectures. Exams were directly from practice midterms and homeworks.

You can hardly call him a professor. His lectures are disorganized and hard to follow and it's impossible to reach him for help. Hard to reach, and the materials are unclear, unorganized. I wish he could at least give us a schedule of what we are gonna learn. Professor Camassa's fluid teaching style and story-like approach to mathematics teaching elucidate a profound beauty in the subject material. Sometimes, a confused student will try to interrupt his beautiful lessons, and thankfully, he quickly shuts down these awkward intrusions.
Do not take his section for MATH231. He makes his lectures too complicated and barely anyone is able to follow what he's doing.

If you have already learnt the AP Calculus BC before, the lecture taught by Professor Camassa gonna be very interesting. However, Professor Camassa is too smart to become the professor of basic calculus. Thus, most of students cannot afford the pressure of his lecture.

He was very passionate for math but acted like it was the students fault that they didn't grasp the concepts that he made way more complicated than they needed to be. Be ready to teach yourself pretty much everything in the class because the lectures didn't help me at all. Only reason I got an A was because I had already taken calc. Dont take.

He gave out his midterms ahead so I had an A- before the final. After the final, I had a C+ as my final grade because a professor who could teach set the questions. I somehow got 10/35 in the final even with all the work shown, also he uploaded exam materials 2 days before the finals. The other classes got it a week before us.

Most likely the worst professor/teacher I have ever had. Do not take this class with him. His lectures are vague and very difficult to understand. Homework was unrelated to the topics and no solutions provided. He barely gave any practice material, and the best way to learn for me was other sources or the math help center.
He provides very little materials for review and lectures are near impossible to understand. Honestly it is just better to self teach and hope all goes well.

Do not take with him. I tested out of this class from AP credits in high school, I just need a refresher of calculus for my major but that's the only way I did good in the class. If you do not know calculus from previous experience do not take this, you will learn nothing from him. I didn't look at his RMP before taking and I should've.
We took the final a week ago and still have not received our grades. Also, he does not teach.

If you really want to succeed in the class, memorize his midterm theoretical answers word by word, skip all the lectures (because you'll learn nothing) and watch Prof Linda Green and the orgo chem tutor on YouTube! He cannot teach, hope this helps!

His teaching style is very inaccessible; we have no notes, and if we miss classes, there are no resources. He gave us the answers to the midterm questions (tweaked slightly by a few numbers). If you don't memorize MATH and write exactly what he writes, word by word aka the simplified version bec his answer is long and goes in circles about the same thing, you'll only get half credit.

He cannot teach at all and we have to teach ourselves. He gives you the midterm papers in advance so you think you're doing well in class. Then, you realize Mccombs, a prof who can teach, is writing the paper. And then you realize: wow, we did not even learn this and we're getting tested on this! Hoping for a curve because it is unfair for us.

Goes through lectures really fast without giving students time to digest bc assumes everything is self explanatory. Isn't very reachable and not consistent in when we get our tests back or what the tests are on or other criteria. Very nitpicky on tests. He is passionate about his work for sure, but isn't very good at teaching. Stressful class.
One of the smartest professors I've had at uni so far, very captivating lectures. Has a tendency to go on tangents to prove interesting stuff not required for the class.

Perhaps the kindest professor I've had. He approached each lecture with enthusiasm and clearly loves math. However, he is just way too smart to be teaching entry level calc. Granted, I went straight from high school calc to 231 but it was not just me. I taught myself everything and barely managed a B. Shoutout organic chemistry tutor on YouTube.

He was too smart to be teaching this Math class. He was clearly knowledgeable on the subject, but to him what he was teaching was too obvious. Classes were often silent when he asked if anyone had questions because everyone was too lost to even know what to ask. I would recommend NOT being in this class with Camassa. Also inaccessable.

Horrible class. He lectures by reading out of the textbook and nothing else. No slides, notes, nada. Inaccessible outside of class -TAs will respond for him, or you can post on piazza with no response. He is a brilliant man, but is too smart for this class. If you get lost on a topic, you need to catch up as quickly as possible or else you're lost.

He is a very sweet man and obviously loves math, but my friends and I left class everyday more confused than when we entered. He is wayyy too overqualified to be teaching this course, so he thinks everything is "intuitive." There are many professors that teach this course, and every section takes the final, so DO NOT TAKE

Super nice and funny professor, really liked him as a person, but he was extremely overqualified to teach Math 231. In-Class Lectures didn't really cover anything except for proofs and theorems, and tests were usually pretty hard. No curve but tests are definitely easier than other sections.

The other reviews also say this but I'll echo it. Camassa is an incredibly smart professor but not a good teacher. Most simply, he's too smart for us. He goes really fast and unless you know the material before the class, you won't understand anything. He wants to answer questions during lectures but everyone is too confused to know what to ask.

He is absolutely brilliant; however, because of this, he doesn't recognize that you don't already know what he is teaching. Because of that, he skips over much of what is being taught which makes tests difficult and lectures extremely confusing. He does try to be funny though, so that's something.

Professor Camassa is a very funny and smart guy, but when it comes to teaching, he's absolutely horrible at it. He assumes you know what he's talking about, gives extremely vague lectures and example problems, doesn't explain step by step, he talks fast and it's hard to understand. Never know what to study for and I wouldn't take him again.

Although I bombed my final exam, Shahar is still the goat of math department. His lectures are truly amazing and he really helps a lot. Convex optimization is a difficult course, but he is good at making these abstract concepts clear. 50% of the grades are exams. Easy to get at least B+. You should really take Shahar's 560 for math and -- fun!

This class prepares me well for my second thesis project as a PhD student. I want to model biological questions, and the lectures give me a strong foundation. The two-week homework schedule gives me time to think on my own. Shahar is very supportive, and his office hours help me see where I get stuck and how to improve. Take this course if you can!

Could not recommend him more for MATH231. He is hilarious and genuinely cares about his students. His exams are fair, and he will actually answer your questions thoroughly if you are confused about anything. Edfinity homeworks during the week and quizzes, with 2 midterms and a final. The final can replace the lowest exam, and he gives extra credit!

He did not perform his duties as instructor at all. He never puts himself in others' shoes. When students are in great need of help, he always chooses to ignore it, which is such a blow to the students. He is indeed kind to this course, but he is definitely not an understanding and caring prof.

He always uses the excuse of having a lot of classes to teach and being very busy to not fulfill the necessary duties of instructor, such as providing support to students in need of special assistance, which he basically completely ignores. It's basically impossible to reach out to him by email. Don't want to take any classes with him anymore.
Hilarious, fun, and easily approachable.
absolute goat
Amazing teacher! Super understanding and will work with you. Make sure to show up and participate. Definitely reccomend taking a class with him!

I think Shahar is a great professor but only for the more advanced math lectures. This was his first time teaching MATH 231 and it does show. If I needed to take another more advanced math class I would definitely take it with him. Just not Calculus 1.

Kovalsky is super nice and a good lecturer. After the first midterm the exams are open note/open internet. It was a super reasonable lin alg class (I've heard other professors are a lot more difficult). Def recommend taking his class!
Best professor in the department by far, take a class with him if you can!
Very chill guy, open note midterms and final. Homeworks were tedious but prepare you well. Take him!!!

Goated professor. In class worksheets used as participation grade, fairly weighted midterms and exams, lots of homework on Edfinity (usually weekly). Best choice for 347, hands down. In-class work and homework focuses more on application, and it's helpful to have some experience with proofs for tests. EXTREMELY open note exams but may change after this semester so don't count on it.

Shahar is such a gem in the math department. I'm not a math major and have previously struggled in other math classes required from my major. His lectures are engaging and I genuinely looked forward to going to his class. He doesn't overcomplicate concepts and is very clear about expectations. All around fantastic teacher.

The best thing to happen to the UNC math department. Keeps lectures clear and entertaining, makes sure he takes every measure for students to understand the content. G

He is the best professor in the department. Very funny and knowledgable. You really can't learn anything like this in the department as well. Not an overly difficult class, as he is a somewhat slow lecturer and the class is not too proof oriented. I would take any class taught by Kovalsky. Favorite math professor. Very nice guy and very great lecturer, I think every math undergrad should have one class with him. For a 500 level class, not too difficult and very fair.

Great professor I agree with most other reviews. The content of the class can be difficult but the way the class is structured makes it one of the easiest math electives. Many people who did well in this class would not last a day in MATH 521.

I had him for Linear and was super excited to see that he was teaching 560 this semester. If Professor Kovalsky only has 10 fans, I'm one of them. If Professor Kovalsky has no fans, then I must be dead. Great professor with engaging lectures and friendly grading with finals!
I didn't understand anything and I made it take it!

Prof Kovalsky is hilarious and a great lecturer. There are no midterms in 560 and the class is mostly graded on homework - which is challenging but doable and relevant. I really, really enjoyed this class.

He is a great professor that really cares about his students. The exams were kinda hard but he reused most questions from practice exams and if you study the slides well you'll do fine. I really liked shahar! He's super accommodating when it comes to exams and genuinely wants people to do well in his class. As long as you work additional problems, you should be fine for exams. He's also great w answering questions in and out of class

Excellent class, excellent teacher. He gives more of a theoretical background rather than testing strictly computational abilities, which is great for long-term learning and higher level math-classes. Everything is very straightforward, and he makes lectures very enjoyable. Highly recommend.

Great guy, this class was not nearly as difficult as advertised thanks to Shahar. He is very kind and funny and his lectures were enjoyable. Lectures were incredibly engaging and transparent -- Kovalsky was an absolute gem to have in my last semester at Carolina. The class was tough, but fair (as higher-level math should be) and truly, truly enjoyable.
man was awesome. he was pretty funny and really wanted everyone to get an A. he dropped a lot of our lowest grades and also rounded my grade up without me asking. 10/10 great guy

Shahar is the best. As someone who normally struggles with math, linear algebra with him was very doable, and he was funny as well. I particularly liked the in-class assignments (worksheets) and found them, along with the lectures, to be very clear and helpful. I highly recommend taking him!

Best professor I've had so far. Really funny and genuinely wanted us to do well (he thought that our second midterm with a 73% average was disappointing). If he's not available one semester for linear, I would wait to see if he is teaching later because it was such a great experience.
