He is super fair, sweet and caring. The main difficulties in his class are the tough finals and heavy homework. His midterms were super easy but unfortunately nothing to do with the finals content, but he curved at the end which was good.
Very fair tests and decent lecturer. Honestly, if you did the homework you'd be just fine during the midterms. The biggest issue was the final, which was incredibly difficult.

He was a great Prof during the year. His tests are pretty straightforward. His class is a lot easier than the other Profs and I learned this when I took the final. This final was impossible- so much harder than any of our tests. It was clear that Burkhead made the majority of this test. Kumar is a great prof, but use Burkhead's material to prepare.

Lectured very well, and was quite straightfoward. He made sure that the class was understandable and easy to follow as possible. Yes, he did give a lot of homework, but when asked to lower it a bit or provide extensions, he did. The major problem was the final exam, but his midterms were easy, so study with other classes in prep for the final.

He's a sweet guy but his lectures rarely made sense. Pretty much had to teach myself everything. Midterms were fine. There was a lot of homework but it was helpful. Reason for the super low rating is because the final, which is worth 40% of your grade, had literally nothing to do with his class. It was very obviously made by another professor.

Midterms in the class itself were alright. Very straightforward as along as you keep up with the homework.The final however was a final(worth 40%) with the other sections as well and was extremely difficult as Kumar does not prepare students for these questions at all. If you want to do well, ask students in Burkhead's sections for practice DAILY.
HIS FINALS ARE SUPER HARD!!!!

So his midterms were fair and quite easy. I got 94s. His class was way easier than Burkhead's. He doesn't teach us some stuff that Burkhead did. This is fine. However, he decided to use Burkhead's final. this messed a lot of us up. My grade went down by 10 percent after his final due to how unprepared he made us.
Midterms were fair, lots of homework. Sweet guy, final is quite hard!

Dr. Kumar was a very caring professor who encouraged feedback and questions. While there were some issues of seeing the board, he went through each sections theorems and did examples which is a much more helpful method compared to a lot of other calc professors. The exams were straightforward and fair, but there is lots of HW. I highly recommend!

I had him for MATH233 but this isn't an option. His lectures are very good; he follows a format of explaining theorems and then SOLVING problems, which I think is what a lot of professors forget. A lot of homework every week but ultimately it helps in the end to learn the material better. Take him and you won't hate your math classes as much.
That's right
Very hard class, practice exams are no where similar to the actual exams and you don;t feel prepared going into the exam.

If you ever become sick in his class, your grade will feel it, he gives pop quizzes every single week on random days and doesn't do make ups. Lectures are boring, and he expects you to know everything in the course.

Knows the material, can't teach. Basically a self-taught without recorded lecture or notes. Being in class isn't helpful either, since he mumbles and assumes knowledge of future material. Exams are 80% of class grade, but aren't too bad. Little to no practice available, only the homework and maybe a 10 question review without answers.

I do not think his lectures were boring. I found them very engaging, and he covered good example problems. The tests made up almost the entire grade but they were extremely fair if you study. It is crucial to do the homework and make sure you have all the material down. I liked Sawon a lot. I would really recommend him for math233.

sawon is so kind and this class was not too difficult, but the lectures were painstakingly boring and hard to follow. he was kind of all over the place and the most monotone lecturer. however, the two midterms were easy and the final was doable. just do the edfinity and read the textbook and you'll be fine. GREAT guy bad lecturer

Dr. Sawon is very nice and clearly knows a lot. HOWEVER he doesn't curve anything, doesn't drop a single thing, and exams are almost 90% of the final grade. Cannot stress enough how frustrating this class was.

Tests were all very fair and not difficult if you put in the effort to study. Unfortunately, Sawon definitely lacked enthusiasm towards class and his lectures were often hard to follow. I appreciated him going over homework problems in class. Exams make up pretty much the entirety of your grade, so be aware of that before taking it with Sawon.

Sawon seems like a very smart guy, often to his detriment, as he's not great at explaining the concepts to people who have never seen them before. Mostly teaches in proofs, followed by examples. I often understood, but it could be explained better. That being said, Sawon is a nice guy and grades his exams generously, so the class isn't too hard.

Sawon has the harshest grading policy of any 233 prof at UNC—90% of your grade is based on exams. No midterm replacement, little weight on homework or recitation. Other profs give more free points. The course itself is easy, but take someone else if you want a lighter grading policy.

I really appreciated his accessibility and personality, but his lectures were often somewhat difficult to follow. While the midterms were fairly easy, it left me relatively unprepared for the final. If you're okay with putting in extra hours to learn material yourself, you'll be okay; however, make sure you're extremely thorough.

Overall, a great experience! Lectures were always well documented, and the notes were uploaded afterwards onto Canvas. The midterms are also not super challenging, and I always found myself confident while taking them. I hope to take more classes from him later on!

Sawon is super chill and makes the easiest midterms. He basically writes proofs/thrms at the beginning of each unit and then goes through practice hw problems. His midterms are very simple, literally the same stuff we have done in class, some q's even easier than the hws. Hes accessible in office hrs too.

I can tell he knows a lot about math, but he doesn't seem to particularly like teaching it. Puts minimal effort into his lectures, teaches very fast. I was better off just reading the textbook. But he did do homework questions in class & was semi-helpful in office hours. Midterms were really easy, but 20% each, and the final is 45%.
Easy course, 4 solutions and attendance are all you need to get an A. Suggested for students in majoring in Mathematics.
Had him for three lectures when my professor was travelling to Italy. Honestly, one of the best at teaching!
This professor was an incredible lecturer and is great to talk to both in and outside of class. Take a class with him if you can.
Best math professor I've had at UNC. He explains concepts clearly and makes math feel genuinely learnable. Attending every lecture really sets you up for success.

The workload is very similar to other math classes. If 80% of grade being exams is a problem, you should probably stop taking math classes. However, the textbook sucks and lectures are tedious. Mistakes are not tolerated because on exams he uses vague wording to trick you, and if you read the question wrong, you will get 10% off. He is chill though

Overrated. The prof is a decent lecturer, but the overall experience was poor. The homeworks were extremely long, and 80% of the grade comes from exams. Also, grades below a C- are converted to Fs. Although his online real analysis lectures are good, I would recommend avoiding MATH 523 with him. Many students I spoke with had similar experiences.
It always feels like teaching this course is his second task.
Homeworks are ridiculously tedious, including longest homework due during LWOC.

Prof. Rodriguez is probably the chillest professor in the math department. He may initially come off as dry, but he's really understanding and has a good sense of humor. After taking 521, 523 isn't anything to be scared of and it seems a lot of defs are easily translatable. Complex numbers have some really nice properties. Very interesting class!
Super chill
Great professor, makes things clear, holds office hours, tests are fair and similar to hw, good elective to take
Such a chill guy, prepares for his lectures, and very helpful during office hours.
Exams are worth 80% of your grade...

I came into this class with high expectations given previous reviews. However, homeworks are assigned weekly and are extremely tedious with so many parts to complete. Very distant and cold to students in class. Professor does not even show up to lectures, and we have had a substitute in place of him. I wish I took a different 500-level math class.

This has been one of the least enjoyable 500 level math courses I've taken. Homework is excessively long and overly proof heavy, while lectures feel rushed, though there are well drawn visuals at times. Compared to other 500 level courses, it has felt unnecessarily difficult despite its reputation for being easier.

This class was tough. Homeworks were impossible without office hours. Few examples in class and terrible textbook. Not many resources for students who weren't already familiar with the material. Midterms were reasonable, but the final was really hard. I like Casey, but didn't love this course
Call me the Piola-Kirchoff stress tensor the way I stay making references.

The way he taught us real analysis was far better than reading Rudin. His lectures helped me thoroughly understand the fundamentals of mathematics. He developed the problems thoughtfully and guided us smoothly through the material. He is truly one of the best professors I've ever had.

The way he taught us real analysis was far better than reading Rudin. His lectures helped me thoroughly understand the fundamentals of mathematics. He developed the problems thoughtfully and guided us smoothly through the material. He is truly one of the best professors I 've ever had.

Funny engaging lectures that make so much sense compared to some of the other professors here, and the exams are very fair as well. He made it super clear what would be tested on any given exam. There was a very fair amount of homework assigned as well. If you can take any class with him (especially Math 521) i highly recommend him.
He made MATH521 as enjoyable as it could be. His lectures are very engaging and he walks through the material very clearly. If you have to take 521, highly recommend him/
Goat

he's kinda awkward but seemed to really care about the class, and would always try to re-explain tough concepts if you missed them. midterm 2 was pretty difficult (especially compared to midterm 1). i thought the final was on the harder side but if you take the time to do all his practice problems they prepare you well.

Maybe discrete is just hard to understand but Tosteson didn't really make it easier. I never understood the more difficult concepts in class when he explained them because he would kinda just write the proofs down and not explain it in a way that makes sense to someone learning for the first time. Hard final, lot of self-teaching required.
takes points off for the smallest mistakes, confusing

Really cares about the content and is a nice but awkward guy. Lectures were okay but if you didn't understand how he explained it the first time, he struggled to explain it in a new way during office hours. Midterm #2 and the final were both pretty challenging, despite putting in hours of practice and going to office hours. Not the worst, not best

Can tell he cares about teaching, but he's a bit all over the place. Would go over time every class & doesn't put any grades in Canvas. But homework is fair & good practice for midterms. Practice exams very similar to the actual one. He encourages questions and does a good job teaching a hard class. Overall, much better than most math profs.
Super nice professor, really dedicated to his work. He wants students to ask questions and is always willing to help students. Homework is really good practice for exams.

he's a really nice guy, albeit a bit awkward, and you can tell he's really dedicated to his field! office hours weren't super accessible timing wise (few hours, during class times for me) and he does sort of just read off his notes but he's not bad. i didn't read the textbook but i def would recommend it. hw and practice problems are helpful
Caring, and puts efforts into his lectures, covers all the content, what can you say.

Took 381 with him I was dual enrolling at UNC, he covers not only the concept and the theory behind the course, but also gives detailed examples  (office hours were also quite in-depth). Tests were easy if one actually attended the lectures, and those complaining are a bunch of unmotivated com sci majors forced to take the course.

Professor Tosteson was good overall and is knowledgeable about the subject. He has frequently related the subject to uses outside a theoretical context. He teaches straight from the textbook, but I still found attending class useful because of the dense content.

The exams are 60% of your grade and very fair as they come straight from the hw problems. Lectures are boring as a non-math major, but Tosteson explains concepts fairly well (although he makes a lot of small errors). Attendance isn't mandatory but is important to doing well on the exams. There are weekly hws, but they only take 1-2 hrs.

His lectures can be a slog, and there were even a few times I walked out of class early due to sheer boredom. However, most of the information is not posted on Canvas so attendance is vital. The class is boring but the test questions are basically straight from the homework or in-class examples so they felt VERY fair. Not fun, but relatively easy.

My GOAT! Truly an incredible professor. He makes learning discrete math weirdly fun. His tests are fair and his explanations for topics in class are clear. Discrete is by no means an easy class, you need to train yourself to think in certain ways which just takes practice. His test questions are often similar to stuff discussed in class and in hw.

I've seen a lot of reviews about his stutter, and it DOES NOT affect his ability to convey the material. I thought his lectures are good and the homework sets you up to do well on the tests. He is very nice and willing to help outside of the classroom.

He's a good guy, and clearly understands the material very well and is very helpful and responsive outside of class, even if his lectures aren't engaging and can be pretty hard to follow. You may have to teach yourself for a fair portion of the class, but this is aided by the fact he applies heavy curves on the midterms (not so much on the final).

There were two midterms which were curved, I'm not sure about the final. Tosteson was a great professor overall and the lectures were recorded. There is a lot of homework and it can be a pain but I think the online homework was good for practice. He made a lot of mistakes during his lectures which students had to catch and seemed scatterbrained.

Be prepared to teach yourself calculus. Homework sucked and took a long time. He did drop 10% of homework at the end of the semester. Each test was curved heavily because our class average was so low. I made a 54 on one and ended with an 80. The final was not curved a lot which sucked. You can not fall behind in this class.

A very sweet guy but pretty hard to follow: stutters heavily, overcomplicates concepts, makes little mistakes when working through problems (students would have to correct him often). Homework would often take hours to complete and rarely ever lined up with class notes/examples. The two tests we had were HEAVILY curved; the final exam was not.

He was a really nice guy, and this was his first semester teaching, but the lectures were to follow. To understand the material you would need 8+ hours a week to teach yourself. The two tests were hugely curved (because class averages were so low), but the final was not. A good amount of homework. Do yourself a favor and avoid!

Chill & sweet but VERY scatterbrained & not a good teacher. Lectures were a pain to sit through & he sometimes had no idea what he was doing. hella hw that took HOURS & is nothing like class examples/tests. There's only two tests & they were heavily curved but the final was BRUTAL & not curved. Attendance is not mandatory and you can join on zoom.

Professor Tosteson really did try to set all students up for success. Although sometimes he made mistakes in lecture, he used guided notes and all his lectures were recorded. The homework was challenging but if you used it as practice, you would do well on the tests. There was leniency in grading including good curves and dropping lowest grades.

Tosteson is super sweet but I think he still has a lot to learn with teaching, hopefully, it comes with time. He struggles during lectures and often makes math mistakes that go unnoticed. moves very quickly, no time to process anything. If you have the time to spend another 10+ hrs/wk teaching yourself, you'll be okay...otherwise you will STRUGGLE

Tosteson is a chill person but not a good teacher. His lectures were hard to follow, and I had to teach myself everything on my own. Exams were very hard, but he curved them nicely (this was prob the only reason why I passed this class). He also extended due dates on homework often. I would still def take this class with another professor though.

This was Professor Tosteson's first semester. However, he is a very genuine and nice guy and wants to help you especially if you go to office hours. I have also heard no good reviews from any calc 1 students about their professors so I would argue Tosteson was the best because of his HUGE curve on the exams. Use The Orgo chem tutor to review!!

Where should I start? He makes mistakes in every lecture that the students have to catch, creates very hard exams, class examples don't help with homework/exams, rushes through lecture, hard to follow in class. If I taking this class with a different professor, I would have done significantly better. AVOID!!!
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS THE LECTURES ARE AWFUL AND ONLY TWO TESTS.

This was Prof Tosteson's first semester, so granted at times the class seemed a bit unorganized. He's a super nice guy and is very responsive to questions/emails, but I think at times he's a bit scatter-brained and overestimates our abilities in a calc 1 class. His lectures were him solving problems and his tests were hard but did have a nice curve

She explains everything as complicated as possible and goes so fast. I went to every class and still had to teach myself everything. The edfinity homeworks took forever and were much more difficult than anything we saw in class or on exams. On the plus side, she's nice and the tests were all very easy.

She's lovely but her lectures tend to be a little boring. The grading was kind of fair, with 3 midterms (30%), 3 homeworks (30%), attendance (10%) and a final group project worth 30%. Be careful with the second midterm cause it was so hard for some reason.

Don't know why so many people give her bad comments. I enjoyed her lecture and easily got an A. If you go to the class everyday, it's easy to do well in this class. The practice exam is almost exactly same as the real exam. And there's no homework other than edifinity. I love her.
Lectures could be a bit boring but this class is SUPER easy. Def take this is you want an easy A

Lectures were disorganized, difficult to follow, and somehow felt rushed even though she was going slowly through the content. Exams were easy. If she continues to use Gilbert Strang's textbook, then I highly recommend watching his lectures on MIT OpenCourseWare (18.06SC)—he explains everything much more clearly and makes the class a breeze.

Editing this review bc it was too harsh when I first wrote it. Lectures are confusing, but you can still get an A if you work hard outside of class. Yifei wants us to do well, and I'm sure the course will improve more from when I took it (Yifei's first sem at UNC). I didn't have the best experience, but I still learned a lot abt linear algebra.

She wasn't a tough grader and was very lenient with the syllabus, dropping a midterm that she originally had counting for credit. She wants to help your grade. Lectures aren't the best but material isn't bad and it's not set up for you to fail.

Lou is really nice and explains things very clearly. The workload is manageable, and the exams are about the same level as the sample exams. However, she sometimes talks a bit too fast, so you need to stay fully focused throughout the whole class to keep up.

Show up to class and work hard, and you'll get an A. Her other reviews are so low prob bc only 20% of students actually went to class. There are 3 midterms (avg = mid 80s) and a final which are v fair and based off the HW + practice tests. Her lectures sometimes were fast-paced and confusing, but I expect she will improve as this was her 1st sem.

I actually really liked her. I'll note I believe this was her first semester at UNC, which it was also mine so I understand the adjustment and I think she did well for it.
She definitely talked a bit fast, but I was engaged in her lectures and liked them. She did take constructive criticism of what to focus on in lectures like less proofs.

Dr. Lou is extremely nice and caring, but it was a bit difficult to understand her lectures, especially later on in the semester. The exams got progressively more difficult, and I had to supplement lectures with a lot of YouTube and online resources to explain things more clearly. Would highly recommend Gilbert Strang's videos.
had an A until the final and i got absolutely finished

I hope that she never teaches Linear Algebra again! Lectures were all over the place, and if you miss one, good luck understanding her lecture slides. Her practice exams are laughable compared to the real ones. Final was extremely hard. My advice: don't go to class but watch the Strang lectures instead. And don't forget to do the worksheets!

The content being taught is not incredibly complex, but her lectures are often disorganized and she makes a lot of mistakes. Make sure you are able to self teach if you take a class with her, especially because the online homework covers content that was never mentioned in class. If you take Lin Alg with her just watch the Strang lectures.

I have so much to say about Yifei Lou. First, I want to start off with how such a nice person she is. She is such a sweet lady and she has a great fashion taste. On the other hand she sucks at teaching. Like holy hell. She is not clear at what she's teaching. She goes crazy fast during lectures too. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. NOT WORTH IT.

She is really sweet and while the midterms ARE difficult, she gives example problems and stuff that are similar in difficulty so I was never surprised by anything. Doing examples with us in class was very helpful if you're that kind of learner. At the end, she offered to drop more things if ppl filled out the course evals.

She's so sweet and genuinely wants to help. She is willing to compromise with hours and will answer questions without complaint. She does work fast but she will stop for questions. Office hours were very helpful because you could just work in there and ask questions when needed so it felt like a a safe space.

Quizzes were in every recitation. The lectures were chaotic. The main difficulty of this class was the exams. 3 exams worth 15% each and a final worth 35% which would also replace your lowest exam score. She did let us get half credit back on one exam by doing test corrections on any exam of our choosing which helped my grade a lot in the end.

Yifei Lou feels like she's holding your hand through calculus. She is very lecture-heavy so if you're not paying attention in class you will have to watch videos instead on your own time. Her practice problems before each test are very similar but she tends to get creative so you have to know everything beforehand to get a good grade on the tests.

Let me start by saying Dr. Lou is a VERY nice and understanding person. HOWEVER, teaching is just not her thing The class was extremely difficult. I failed every exam and I'm praying for a miracle on the final to pass the class. She talks extremely fast, is hard to understand, and does not explain things in lecture. Hardest class I have taken here.
