I had absolutely no coding experience and even on LDOC, he just jumped right into R. It took a lot of work to catch up on my own.

Look, 445 is an evil class. But Ziya teaches it in a way that makes it doable. His lecture notes are exactly what is done in class, and self-studying for the last half of the semester really helped my understanding (complex explanations in class had me frazzled). I ended feeling comfortable with stochastic modeling and a B+ out of a 70% final grade

Prof Ziya has done a great job of making a difficult class understandable and enjoyable. He is really good at lecturing and gives a TON of review material for the tests that is super helpful. If you go to class and do the review material you will be fine. I would 100% take this course with him!

**FOR STOR 113 - only a few homeworks, tests make up majority of your grade 3 midterms and one final. I had taken Calculus in highschool so this class was easier for me, but if you haven't before I think it would make this class a lot more challenging (exam averages were normally around a 65). Very generous curve, kind person.

STOR 113 -- Prof. Ziya gets a lot of criticism on here, which is understandable due to his sometimes confusing lectures. That being said, he's very helpful if you reach out and this class really isn't that hard material wise, although exams are often harder than class problems. Very generous final curve. DO NOT take STOR 120 with him though.

STOR 113 The exams are challenging and make up almost 75% of your grade. Averages were quite low but most people did not go to class. If you go to class and his office hours you will be fine, Ziya is very accommodating if you can't make it to his office hours. The exams aren't curved but final grades are curved significantly.
Grades are very hard, and do not provide good advice. Very hard tests.
Hard tests, great curve.
For STOR 133 - not engaging, confusing lectures, and terrible exam averages. exams are majority multiple choice and conceptual. try and take with someone else if possible.

FOR STOR113
Not sure why ratings for this class are low. Professor Ziya walks through every step during his lectures and allows for discussion and makes sure to answer all questions you have during class. His exams are short and if you do the homework and practice exams you will do good. So much better than any other math professors I have had.

This review is for STOR 113. This is a very difficult course. The professor is lecture-heavy, but his lectures are not very clear, and he does not stop to explain what he is doing. The tests are much harder than the practice he provides, and the class averages are consistently low. If you have to take this class, try to find a different professor.
*THIS CLASS IS STOR 113*** One of the worst classes I have ever had at UNC. This class was so hard, averages were very low and tests were nothing what we learned in class. Do not take this class.
Loved Dr. Ziya, he was a great teacher for an interesting class. Everything is exam and no need to do homework really. Just do the old midterms and finals to prep. Great Prof would take again.
Not as good. He did explain things clearly, but the course pace is too slow in my opinion. He didn't even get to queuing theory because the slow pace. The course is boring for me overall.

Your entire grade is based off of tests for 445 but this is standard across department. Compared to other options for professors, Ziya is the person you want to take this difficult course with. I found that, although the material is tough, I enjoyed coming to class each day because the professor made each lecture seem like a set of puzzles to solve

Prof Ziya is a great lecturer and explains concepts well. I haven't read the textbook any and have done fine just from paying attention in class. The entire class is based on 3 midterms and a final. The first midterm average was a 55, but he curves the final so the average student gets a B+. Just study previous exams and hw and you'll be fine.

Prof. Ziya put this class on Auto-pilot mode. No HW and midterms were graded by the TA. He recommended some homework in the book, which is easier than the actual exams. His lectures are from the book, they were not very helpful.  60% for 4 midterms, and 40% final. The midterms are very long and complicated for the 50-minute time frame.

STOR 445 by Prof Ziya is one of the greatest STOR classes I've taken. He explains every concept clearly and he fosters thinking and discussion in the classroom. No homework so the workload is pretty light. There are 4 tests and a final and they are not easy. However, he does curve a lot, so It's not so difficult to get A/A-.

Useful class for industry. Attendance and hw is optional, but textbook is sufficient for learning. Reviewing hw and past exams is enough for exams, which were relatively easy. He drops the lowest of 4 exams which is helpful. Nice guy who is helpful with questions.

This class was hard. 4 tests worth 15% and a final worth 40%. The average on our fourth exam was a 52.33. However, he does curve the class and I do like him as a teacher. I just wish HWs were apart of our grade bc I studied so hard and still received a lackluster grade

Fantastic stats professor, explained things clearly and did not rush to fit in more content. Exams were similar to practice exams made available and open note, and he was helpful in office hours to explain answer keys further. There is no graded homework, so you have to motivate yourself to study and do well.

This class said it was beginner friendly, it was not. I could not drop or pass / fail a launch. Now my GPA is going to go down -1.0. I would not suggest taking this course if you have other STEM classes and you are a beginner coder.

As a course requiring no previous knowledge of stats or python, I expected the professor to do more than copy another professors lessons and provide no explanation of concepts. He admitted to never using python and had no problem with more than half the class failing the midterm. He is a very stubborn grader. The TA was the only helpful resource.

This class was advertised as a first year launch with no need prior knowledge of coding or stats. That was a lie. He never used python and just copied off his notes. Spoke in circles without answering questions in every aspect and found no problem that over 5/6th of the class failed the midterm. Overall, very stubborn grader but nice guy.

Only "teaching" that occurred was copying code off the board supplied by the other professor as he told the TA he had no idea how python works or how to use it-he did not explain any stats terms and expected us to know the significance/how to use the formulas. Class description says "no prior knowledge of stats or python needed" it lied. Enjoy!

Professor Ziya was fine, although fairly boring and can be very detailed with grading. He was fair in grading, he gave all the students one question right on a midterm exam because of poor wording. If you can code, this class will be somewhat easy.
Definitely in the top 2 STEM professors I've had at UNC. STOR 435 is very hard material but he is hilarious and great at explaining the material, and there are many office hours every week.
Great class. Teaches very well. Only issue was loads of homework.

Shankar is incredible! STOR 435 is a very hard class, but he explains things so well and makes the course as straightforward and clear as possible, and the exams are very fair. Lots of homework, but they are very helpful. He is also hilarious.

Highly recommend taking him for 435! Very fair exams and grading, and he allowed us to use a cheat sheet on the final. The hws take a while, but the exams were all variations of hw or practice exam problems. He's also very accessible outside of class and explains difficult concepts in 435 well. Definitely would have done much worse if not for him.
Amazing guy. Super funny and knowledgeable. If you have to take 435 with anyone make sure it's him.

Professor Bhamidi is an excellent professor and cares deeply about the success of his students. On multiple occasions I was able to meet with him outside of his scheduled office hours because I had class during his office hours. He curved the grades at end of semester. Also a funny lecturing that makes a hard class more enjoyable.
I had Dr. Bhamidi for 435H. He's a super nice guy, and class is very manageable if you put in some work. Take Probability with him if you can!!

Shankar was great. He explains the course material very clearly, grades very fairly, and the tests are written very clearly despite the difficult course material. His self-deprecating sense of humor was amazing and kept the class alive. Somehow got an A, thanks in large part to Shankar's clear teaching. My only wish is that he recorded lectures.

Prof. Bhamidi was great this semester! He made calc 3 seem super easy, and although there were a lot of HWs, quizzes, and labs each week (apart from worksheets in class to track attendance), the workload didn't seem unbearable. Be prepared to go to class since he uses the blackboard a lot, and uploads empty slide decks. Stay on track and it's easy!

Shankar made calc 3 very easy to understand by showing us how it is used in the real world. There are weekly homework's, quizzes, and labs. You need to go to class because he works out the problems on the board, and he tends to show super long proofs that may cause you to zone out, but a great professor overall.

Great professor, there are a bunch of assignments for this class that help to balance out your grade and it helps you understand the material well. Explains the material really well during the lectures and is very accessible outside of class. All around great professor.

One of my favorite professors! Coming into the class, I was really intimidated by the topics on the syllabus due to previously struggling a lot with calc. Luckily, Shankar is an excellent lecturer and explains complicated concepts in a digestible way. No surprises on exams; they reflected the difficulty of HW/quizzes. Super nice guy. Def recommend!

Shankar is one of my favorite professors at UNC. The exams were fair and always questions we had seen before in homework or class. You have lots of grade buffers to boost your grade. The final was harder than our other exams, but not unmanageable. If you don't go to class, you will do poorly. His lectures are very important to do well.

Probability is a hard subject, but Shankar's explanations are thorough and his exams are very fair. The class is accessible to people without much statistics background. The exam questions are easier, multiple choice versions of the homework questions. If you stay on top of the homework, it is not too difficult to do well in Shankar's class.

The content is very hard, but Bhamidi is a good professor. It is really easy to get behind. Please pay attention in class and stay up to date because it is so easy to get off track and never get back on.

GOAT. He was a very clear lecturer and explainer and was very nice to the class. He wants you to learn the material but understands the content is hard. His tests aren't too hard (most of my misses were bc reading errors). There is a lot of stuff to do and learn, but he makes it as easy as possible while still teaching you everything. Seek him out!

An absolutely amazing professor. It is very important that you go to lectures as I didn't halfway through and my grade suffered because of it. Regardless though, it was an amazing class and he makes a really difficult subject super accessible. Best STOR 435 professor out there.

Professor Bhamidi is a great lecturer, the reality is just that this is a really hard class and it is very easy to get behind. There is a homework and a quiz each week, and he allows a note sheet for the final (but not the midterms). Go to lecture and pay attention because he doesn't post notes, just slides.

Shankar gives you everything you need to succeed in this class. Homeworks are lengthy and can get difficult, but he is super accessible during office hours and explains problems very well. The lectures were good, and in case you miss lectures there are scribed notes for every class. Awesome teacher and awesome person with a great sense of humour.

I feel bad writing this rating but...the last rating is just not true. I got an A in the class so this isn't a "bitter student rating." He's a very smart man and nice but that's where it ends. He does not know how to teach students, he doesn't give good feedback, and disorganized. And the worst part was the exams and the format...
I love his teaching style. He always helps students to learn and think.

Ridiculously hard and lengthy exams and lectures are not at all helpful as he goes too fast, is very condescending, and is unaccommodating. Has homework due during university holidays. Plus, his textbook is extremely unintuitive to use. Avoid at all costs if you want any chance at saving your grade.
Nice guy, but posts no lectures and then has homework questions that he does no examples of in class. Seems counterintuitive.

Prof. Kulkarni is clearly very smart and knows a lot about the subject, however he does not teach the info. in an effective manner at all. His lectures were very difficult to follow, you really have to teach yourself most of the information. All tests are open note, but exams also make up the vast majority of your final grade. Attendance is graded.

This course was challenging but manageable. The lectures aligned closely with the instructor's textbook, which I liked. Solving the textbook's practice problems and focusing on key concepts are essential. The unknown grading scale made it difficult to guess the grade. My weighted grade was around 92, for your reference.

Very difficult class, maybe more suitable for grad students. Extremely proof heavy lectures with (almost) no proofs on final, so you don't get exposure to what you'll need for the tests except for in homework, which is ambiguously graded
Homework due the day after our wellness days due to the school shooting?? And office hours today, when we're supposed to get the day off for mental health

Kulkarni is a good lecturer. The class material is difficult so you definitely have to put in the work, and the tests are hard, but he gives a very generous curve. Tests are also open book/note. Also he wrote and provided the textbook for free and there are hundreds of practice problems. Grading scale a little unclear. But he does curve.
Difficult class but lecture is fair and the textbook is really good - grading on tests can be hard but the class is curved

Cares for his students sets you up to succeed. Before each class, there was an easy poll everywhere pertaining to material from the last class. Then he goes over it at the start of that class which gives you a chance to see the thought process and ask questions. The exams were open book/notes but he made them long to balance out the difficulty.
Very kind and funny, listens to class feedback well, and flexible. A little bit of a slow lecturer but good overall.

If you're thinking of taking STOR 120 over STOR 155, I would take 155 instead if you have little to no coding experience. Weekly labs and homeworks take about 2-3 hrs each. His lectures consist of him doing the code and you copying it down but fairly quick. He is a nice guy but overall goes quickly and lots of homework.
Professor Pipiras is a very impressive man with plenty of knowledge and accompanying wit. The class is difficult, but doable. You get out what you put in.

You had to calculate your grade yourself, which isn't ideal, but overall the professor is nice, and he helps a a lot.
This class, however. It's hard if you have little to no coding experience.  Stor 155 was better

Professor Pipiras was great. Although teaching seems very fast paced content coverage was excellent.
If you do put time in you will definitely get an A . Extremely easy tests and if the entire class is not doing good in it he reduces 0.5 points instead of 1 point for every wrong question. Very easy going grader .
Recommended for everyone.

This is a good class. It is a little difficult for those without much coding experience. However, the professor makes it easy to learn and as long as you are being diligent and learning, it's great. Grading is pretty chill and a lot of boosts come in later on. Prof. Pipiras is decently lenient on grading tests which helps a lot.

Lots of homework and lab assignments. Test are pretty difficult and require a lot of studying. I mostly taught myself everything in the course and went to the bare minimum amount of lectures required. If you have the option to take Stor 155 like if you are a premed definitly choose that.
Do not take this class, take 155 such a big mistake

Professor Pipiras is excellent and easy to communicate with! Sets clear grading criteria, has well-prepared documents, and gives moderately hard midterms. STOR 120 is not a very challenging class and you get what you pay for.
Professor Pipiras is very kind and understanding. He uploads a lot of useful material on Canvas for students to use. The class is well-planned.

Vladas seems to know what he is talking about but he doesn't have a great teaching skills; not engaging or friendly AT ALL at office hours. Gives zero help before midterms, he just tells you to reread everything you did up until the test and I had no idea what to expect going into exams. He goes fast in lectures. Don't take this as an 8am class!!!

So he is a good person overall but moves fast in lectures. I took this class with zero coding ability so there is a learning curve. The start is so easy and I had an A but all of a sudden that tanked with a plummeting homework average and a 63.5 on an in class midterm. All I can say is study the homework and labs, you're going to need it.
Start of class is easy but if you fall behind it's hard to catch up. Exams have in class and take home portion. Lectures are boring and sometimes confusing but is a nice person overall.
Very Easy class. Never went to lecture. Only big grade is group project that is also very easy. Very Easy A!

Easiest class ever as long as you do the work required. Attendance isn't required and there are no exams just a final paper and project. Overall would recommend Prof Li as you can learn a ton from her without a lot of stress.
She inspires me to kill myself, takes 50% off if your are even a second late to turn things in, avoid if you can

Great professor, very clear with lots of materials. None of the assignments were too difficult, and despite having a group project where some group members left much to be desired, and our final deliverable was suboptimal, it was very easy to receive a good grade in the class. Definitely the best of all STOR 320 professors, take it with her.
Super easy class, graded off out of class homework and a final project. No one really goes to lecture as she just posts them anyways.

It is very easy to do well in her class as long as you do the work. She outlines the requirements for each assignment clearly and is a fair grader. Lots of opportunities for extra credit and there are no exams in this class compared to other STOR 320 sections. She genuinely wants all the students to succeed and is a very kind professor.

Super easy. But as other review says, the class proceeds very slowly and only covers very little knowledge that is actually useful and interesting. Clear grading rubrics. Assignments, projects, and pop quizes are all easy. Most people lose attention during class and the class interaction is not good.

lenient and easy grading criteria, 40% homework, 20% pop quizzes with points that could be earned back through extra credit, 40% final project. lectures were dull at times but followable with motivation

This class is horrible. It has a terrible structure. We only covered about 2/3 of the planned material. Lectures are extremely boring, and the homework often includes content not taught in class. This class was so bad I could write 100 negative reviews. It kills my passion for machine learning. That said, it's an easy A with excessive extra credit.

Had her in Fall 24, highly recommend! No exams, so your grade depends on HWs, labs, and the semester long group project. Very fair grader and gave specific feedback on final presentations so you know what to fix for the final paper. Participation was a small portion of your grade, but if you participated more than required you got extra credit.

I took this class having done STOR 455, so I already knew a bit about coding using R. Only the last third of class ended up teaching me anything new, and you could complete homework, assignments, and labs without attending lectures. Main part of course grade is the group project, which was fine. Overall, the class is ok, but not too hard.

Didnt go to lecture much since theres a lab with lots of 1on1 opportunity to clarify concepts. Grading was very easy until the final presentation & project, where many groups scored extremely low on criteria that didnt seem to align with her positive verbal feedback. Acknowledging this tho, she gave all groups an extension to improve final papers.

I absolutely loved this class! It is not super difficult if you have prior knowledge of R Programming. There are no exams, but a final project. Professor Li is also a fair grader and very understanding. Also, there are tons of opportunities to do well in the class with extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend taking this class!

I honestly can not say enough good things about Professor Li and the way she taught STOR 320. Her section was Tu/Thu at 8am and I made time to attend lecture even though attendance isn't required (this was not a popular choice though). This particular section was taught in R, which isn't too bad but it's not easy. She gives SO much extra credit tho
Great class and easy grading.

Surprised by the comment about the lectures being too fast. The professor always stopped to answer questions and would pause if someone raised their hand. The slides had great visuals alongside the math, which made things much more intuitive. It would be a difficult class for sophomore students but, of course, it's a 500 level course.
Difficult course, but Budhiraja was a great lecturer and was extremely helpful in office hours.

Lots of pretty hard homework, but the tests draw heavily from it. The textbook also helps with homework, and he does practice problems during class. It's a hard course, with lots of work, but he's a good teacher for it.
To all future students, if you're planning to take STOR555, get out while you still can. Find another way to get credit for this class, because this is not the way you want to do it.
Nobel's lectures are clear and very concise. I compare to other lectures from the same classes of different schools, they are basically similar. He is very nice and approachable outside class.

It was the worst class I have ever taken. Long homework and harsh graded exams with no answer keys, no practice. BEYOND THAT, his lectures were awful, and he was too stubborn to listen to student feedback. He sees “poetry” and “story” in statistics problems and acts as if students are crazy for not seeing them.

cant find a 555 option, so im putting this under 565. its laughable how bad bro is at lecturing. tests are needlessly long. only thing that saved me from failing was decent hw grades. hard agree with the other person who said this dude says you tell me to every question.

I had him for STOR 555, not 565, but there is no 555 option (those two classes are completely different btw). I genuinely don't know how people ever succeed in that class. Any time someone asks a question, he will only, and I mean ONLY, respond with "you tell me." Like, dude, WE SHOULD BE TELLING YOU THAT. YOU'RE THE TEACHER, NOT US!

Nice person but he will make sure you suffer. Insane amounts of homework with intense deadlines (like 4 days). Lectures are very confusing. Exams aren't too bad but are graded harshly, and there will be no answer keys for anything. Good luck.
Overall, I'd say she was okay. The content was genuinely hard, but she allows a cheat sheet for midterms which was nice to have.

Dr. Zhong is smart and decent in teaching a tough 500-level course. The course is fast-paced, but the same for all ML classes. She curved very hard, both on non-exam components and overall. You will learn a lot if you keep up with the contents, while the curve won't make your grade too bad after all, since hw and projects are graded leniently.
Not a very good lecturer, but she is super nice, the final project was graded insanely easily, and homework makes up 45% of your grade, which is an absurd level for a 500-level course.

Seeing a lot of negative reviews after the first midterm but she clearly realized it was too difficult and made the second midterm easier - class avg went from 65 to 80. 

a lot of homework but no final and shes a really generous grader. will give you full credit on the final project if you put a good faith effort in.

If a professor sees the class average sitting at 60, that's usually a sign to look in the mirror. A genuinely kind one would probably throw in a nice curve or tweak the course a bit—but Professor Zhong doesn't really seem to notice there's an issue.

Not really any practice in class. Wish there was more homework to provide grade padding and practice, especially after a brutal midterm. She is clearly smart and kind, but lecture slides are posted last minute and lectures are hard to follow. I'm teaching myself the content with Google and YouTube videos. Don't stack many hard classes with this one

Dr. Zhong is honestly pretty nice and not even bad at lecturing. The class is super theory heavy and homeworks do take a long time and have a good amount of coding. What makes this class so bad is the super high expectations. Midterm was on things either barely talked about or out of our scope, and average literally was failing. Good luck...
I need therapy after the midterm. Take the class with anyone else
Brutal and exhausting...

The professor seems nice, but wasn't understanding of the students.The practice exam she gave was different from the real midterm,  much harder and way more complicated. It was discouraging because it didn't feel like she wanted us to truly learn the material. I tried my best, but it felt more like being set up to fail than being guided to learn.

Can't believe how the grading changed this much from last semester. It used to be project-based, now it's all super hard exams. Totally killing my GPA.  I honestly don't know how I'm supposed to graduate if the professor doesn't make adjustments to the grading policy.

Lectures are highly theoretical and often difficult to grasp, despite the professor describing the material as easy and intuitive. You'll need independent study to try understanding the content. I wish slides were consistently posted early to read ahead of class. The first midterm was brutal and different from assignments and the practice exam.

The professor is very smart, but the lectures are mostly pure theory and really hard to follow. I spend a lot of extra time studying on my own. The practice exam for the midterm wasn't very helpful, since the actual exam was way, way harder.
horrible midterm

Prof. Liu is by far the best professor to have for Stor 320. He is extremely approachable, encourages questions, and is a fair grader. When the grading TAs took off an excessive number of points for the midterm, many of us spoke to Prof. Liu, and he gave us points back. The group project is intense, though, so choose your group members wisely.

Dr. Liu is very knowledgeable in data science and has a light-hearted personality. His Jupyter notebooks were very organized. Take-home midterm, bi-weekly homework, and no final exam. The final group project was tedious and split into multiple deadlines throughout the semester, but he is a fairly lenient grader and lets you choose your groupmates.

He was a fine teacher, but one thing to be aware of and why he is not getting a higher rating. He assigned 33 assignments in 15 weeks and was horrible about grading. Grades for this class are due in 4 days and I still do not have a grade back for an assignment that was due in Oct. Giving us this much work and then not grading it is unacceptable.

Professor Liu genuinely cares about his students and challenges them in a way they can grow. Exams weigh significantly, so doing poorly on one exam can affect your whole grade, but Professor Liu is very willing to help you in ways he can. Lectures are very important in understanding the materials, and the course itself is quite fast-paced.

Second midterm was rough (class average ~50 %), but Prof. Mo curved hard so the final grade turned out fine. The Python labs add extra work compared to STOR 435. Attendance isn't required, but his lectures really make everything click.

Dr. Liu was a great guy and very smart. The course is pretty difficult, which is just the nature of the probability courses. Lectures were heavy and slides were posted, but attendance was required to understand them. Very available during/outside office hours. Exams are more difficult than other sections of 435, but overall grade is heavily curved

Professor Liu is very knowledgeable and very nice. Compared to other STOR 435 classes, his midterms are much more difficult, but as a result you learn much more in this class. If you want to take an easy class, do not take Mo, but if you want to be challenged, take him. Keep in mind most of your learning will be done on your own, outside of class.

The material is just hard in general, so he did a relatively good job at lecturing. Your raw grade is going to be pretty bad, but he curves hard so its fine. He said that if you attend the final, you are guaranteed to pass. Tests are all MC.

STOR 535/435 is a beast of a class in general. He's genuinely a nice guy and, although boring (like honestly really really boring), his lectures aren't that bad. Homework and tests are hard and coupled with his first year teaching year our class is going through it. Not his fault he's just inexperienced.

The class itself is so difficult but he's super patient and sweet. He lectures the whole time (can get pretty boring) but is always willing to help and answer questions. Exams are impossible, pretty sure the class average is an F right now but he says he'll curve the average final grade up to an A- so I'm just praying for that
Yeah just no
He was a super nice guy; I strongly recommend taking him.

Dr. Liu's lectures were pretty boring and didn't engage with the class much. However, his class was organized and the take home midterm, homework every 2 weeks, and no final exam was extremely lenient grading wise. There is a group project that you do the whole semester and can pretty annoying with subpar teammates. Probably the easiest 320 class.

Dr. Mo was alright for his first semester teaching at UNC. He patiently lectured, and the course was organized. The current lecture style isn't very engaging but it's the way the course is taught, so no choice I guess. Homework and the midterm were graded quite harshly so pay attention. Wasn't a fan of the group project but that's not his choice.

STOR 555 was the hardest class I've taken at UNC, but Jan was overall really good. The HW was brutal and lectures can be hard to follow, but Jan is really friendly and will help. Just make sure you go to office hours early, you're probably going to need it.

Jan is great person and professor. That being said stor 555 in my opinion is the most difficult undergraduate course in the department. HW were difficult but they did teach you how to do the course materials just be prepared to spend a few hours on them each week. Tests were much simpler. Material can be hard but Jan tries to makes class fun
The HW was very tough, but tests were made easier. He is very smart, so sometimes his lectures can get a little in the weeds with the math. Overall, he was a great prof.
Alright prof, a little boring and terrible at algebra. Exams were very easy, homeworks could be tough.

He is one of the best in STOR department. He explain everything well and really care students. His practice match with exam and grade easy. He is also approachable in OH, unlike those who does not care students. Overall, TAKE THIS CLASS.

I throughly enjoyed the lectures but do wish he spent more time on releasing material more than around 30 minutes ahead of class time. Myself, and I'm sure other students, prefer to work through lecture content ahead of time to be prepared with questions for class time. Aside from this, I enjoyed his lecture style and the homeworks hard but doable

Professor O'Neill is an easy going person. His lectures are decent and provide you the knowledge you need to do well on the exams. He is also very open to all sorts of questions during lecture, after lecture, and during office hours. As long as you take advantage of all of that, you will be in great shape for this course.

O'Neill is alright. Not a great lecturer, but a pretty nice guy with fairly reasonable expectations for the course. Easy exams, weekly HW. Wouldn't recommend going to class outside of exams; the lecture notes (the provided notes compiled by other profs) are a far better resource. You'll be fine, this is generally a pretty common sense course.

He is the ONLY choice for 415. I took 415 with Pataki and received a D+ due to insane grading and bad teaching. This semester, I retook the class and it was completely different. Although I had to learn essentially a whole different course, O'Neill made it possible. Exams were fair and he was actually a great teacher and taught the material well.

Good professor, lectures pretty clear and as long as you follow the material is not bad / 
Weekly homeworks that aren't too difficult, tests are pretty reasonable and just computational /
Great choice for 415

Really great lectures but tended to post course materials such as lecture slides or homework very last minute. Other than procratinating (he was also creating much of the content for the first time he said), this was overall a great course with a great instructor. One of the most open teachers I've had to questions and feedback which was a change

VERY hard but rewarding class. Long homeworks (10ish hours). HARD final exam - but curved. Lectures are great. Group project similar to the one in 320. Professor is reachable and knowledgable. If you are serious about a career in data science/ML this is your class. Clear grading and curves grades. Overall great choice definitely recommend.

HARD class. He moved up the final, so I started to prepare for it around the late of October. If your project schedule happens to be near around this time, everything could be really challenging for you. The homework is much harder than the quiz and exam. The professor is very nice, easy to talk, very accessible, and a very useful class!

Great lectures! I really learned a lot by just attending lectures, and you may have multiple uh-ha! times during his lecture. Prof Liu is very knowledgeable and very easy to access during office hours. He would adjust course material and exams by students' feedbacks (though I think there's no need to change). Overall a great course with Prof Liu!
Great lectures though a bit notation heavy at times. I enjoyed his lengthy but interesting homeworks but do think the level of difficulty on the exams was unnecessarily complex in comparison.
Best STOR prof I have had. Explains things very clearly. HW was a little tough, but glancing at the textbook and going to lectures make it doable. Very useful class.

Probably one of the most useful classes in STOR department. A must-take if you want a job in data science or quant research, or if you want to go to a top grad school. Even after graduation, I still reviewed his lecture notes to prepare for job interview. Study hard folks. Things you learn in this class will pay back in the near future.

Lectures can feel a bit boring at times due to the lack of class participation, but the topics covered are interesting and timely. I enjoyed the assignments, and grading was fair without being too harsh.
Fantastic！

Had for STOR 565. Homeworks can be challenging and are assigned monthly  but graded very lenient. Tests much easier than homework and also graded lenient. Decent lecturer but very inaccessible outside of class.

Do not underestimate the rumors that Todd is trying to make the UNC chem department one of the most difficult in the country. He's a nice guy, but lectures are boring, exams are more difficult than he really prepares you for, and he seems to enjoy your suffering a little bit.

Funny and kind person, plus Todd's a great lecturer for Orgo. He teaches the material very cohesively and ensures you're well-prepared for exams. In class, I noticed people in his section often did better than those in other sections. In Todd we trust!

Todd is GOATED. Y'all give him too much hate. This class is low-key overhyped in its difficulty. He tells exactly what you will be tested on it so if you put in the work and study, you can make an A. Austell  requires you to buy a $70 note packet w/ no electronics in class and access a $100 online textbook/warm-up software that he says isn't even good for teaching. todd is a nice person but some things he does is annoying. chem 241 is a very boring class and the midterms are

241 is not the most interesting class but Todd makes the lectures interesting and digestable. He's a great lecturer who explains concepts very well. Extremely unorganized and it made the class so much harder than it needed to be. Nice guy, bad lecturer and didn't explain content well at all. dont bother going to lectures. dude talks about swamp water
Great lecturer but that's about it. I loved going to his lectures but his exams are very difficult and they require a lot of out of class preperation. The online textbook is also pretty expensive.

Todd is a pretty engaging lecturer, but that's it. He makes you buy >$100 worth of his own course notes. He doesn't release any ANSWER KEYS which made exams very hard to study for. There is no doubt that Todd is a great guy. I enjoyed his lectures and he is very clear about his expectations and what content you'll be tested on. Dr. Austell is a wonderful, hilarious man who clearly likes teaching. Todd receives a lot of criticism. This is from people who shouldn't be chem majors. If you aren't willing to put in the work you will not like Todd. Todd is a genius and he is so dedicated to the department and every one of his students. Thank you for sharing my love for chemistry and being the weed out prof that UNC needs.

Exams are tough, but Austell is the GOAT. I feel like he's the best STEM teacher I've had at UNC so far. Explains complex topics very and is very fair. Also had him for 241. If you are planning on taking the MCAT/DAT, I would recommend taking Austell. Make sure to read the textbook before class.

Todd is a great professor. In Chem 102H, he understands that everyone in the class has credit for 101 and 102. Because of this, he makes sure that everyone will get an A or B in the class. His class was my favorite of the semester, he made Chemistry interesting and cared a lot about us inside and out of the classroom

Orgo is a tough class. If you want to do well YOU need to do the work. Practice, practice, practice. Austell is a wonderful lecturer, very passionate about chem and really wants you to succeed. Lots of Q&A sessions to answer questions, but you have to choose to go to them. There is only so much he can do to help if you dont put in the work yourself

Analytical is actually a pretty interesting class, but I would honestly recommend taking it with any other professor if possible. Midterms are pretty doable if you have access to previous exams, however, can seem pretty hard if not. The textbook used also isn't the greatest.

I love Todd! He was always so sweet to us and made sure we understood all the topics he was teaching. Lectures were great and always had us well-prepared for exams. The final was a bit hard, but the class was curved really nice and the lowest you could get was a B-. The class does have quite a bit of homework, but it helps you out in the long run!

I thought Professor Austell did a decent job explaining content in the lecture slides and keeping the lecture engaging. The exams most closely reflected the problems in the workbook so do all the possible assigned practice problems in both the workbook and textbook.

The UNC Chemistry GOAT. Todd is an institution and you either love him or hate him and I can absolutely say I love him. So engaging and caring. Made me excited for 8AM Orgo! Not easy! I'm upset I probably won't get the pleasure of taking another class with him. Orgo is his teaching specialty and if you get a chance to take it with him, do it.

I absolutely loved taking orgo with Austell this semester. Incredibly engaging for an 8am, hilarious, and taught the course content incredibly well. Textbook is very helpful for understanding content. Exams are very fair if you take the time to understand the "why" behind it all instead of strict memorization. Cannot recommend him enough.

Being my first semester, CHEM 102H was a great launchpad into what the school has to offer, especially in the chemistry department. Austell gives ok lectures but is very unhelpful outside class. Expect to spend all your free time on practice if you want to survive this course.
Professors try to grade 500+ tests all in one day which results in grade errors more often than not, and the way regrade process is set up getting a correction is hard even for obvious answer key matches.

AVOID taking CHEM 261 with Todd as he makes the tests extremely hard and not reflective of class content. This class was honestly relatively doable if you have access to previous notes/exams and understand the format. If possible, I would advise taking this class with someone else!

Todd is a very caring & knowledgeable man. No laptops, only notebooks/flat tablets. iClickers. If you prefer active writing and talking, this is the professor for you. Handouts & practice exams are EXCELLENT exam prep, MANY Q&As. Final much harder than midterms. He tries very hard to be accessible to everyone. My fav chem course I've taken here.

Dr. Austell is super communicative, friendly, and wants us to succeed! Such a kind professor. He sometimes goes on tangents, but that makes class enjoyable lol. Fair amount of work for a Chem 102 class! Would reccomend!

Professor Austell has a unique teaching style that works if you're willing to put in the effort. Exams can be tough, but he prepares you well. For study prep, I found unstuckstudy AI and the textbook really helpful.

Austell is a great teacher who really cares about his students. His assignments and exams were hard, which is expected in any orgo class, but fair.
Austell has a unique style of teaching without technology, but it works if you are willing to work with it. His exams are fair and he prepares you pretty well not really many surprises.

Todd is a great lecturer and cares for his students. Fast pace in lectures. Expects you to know gen chem stuff well. Tests are hard. Wrong sig fig = wrong answer. Offers extra credit but quite minimal compared to the overall grades. Offers lots of practice problems but doesn't release keys. You must go to Q&A sessions for uncertain questions.
In Todd We Trust

Todd isn't a bad prof and I thought that the first 90% of this class was actually pretty great-I was getting A's and B's on the midterms, but the final was insanely difficult and dropped my grade by an entire letter. The midterms were not too bad and were reasonable but the final was awful. I got As and B on the midterms but the final dropped my grade to a C+
Good for 102H, only gives B- though A grades for this class. No curves on exams but tests out of over 100pts so you can get Qs wrong and still do well. Funny guy, recommended!

Based on his ratings for 241, Todd definitely excels in the more personal setting of 102H. MANY resources provided to master the material and learn more if interested. Probably easier than regular 102 sections.

Todd is very good for 102H. Everyone is guaranteed an A or B and there is little emphasis on test scores. I've heard his 241 and 261 classes are much harder but I strongly recommend him for 102H, good refresher course of AP, including some topics (nuclear, lattice structures, etc) not covered heavily in AP.

Be prepared to read like an entire chapter of new concepts every class only to spend one day on it and then have complex exam questions that ask you to apply concepts you've only read/learned about for a second.

DO NOT take Austell for 241. He's super nice, but his class is unreasonable. Great guy, but a not-so-great professor. Definitely a weed-out class. Todd is a great professor. His pacing can be awry at times, but he gives plenty of opportunities to ask questions and learn. Exams are incredibly straightforward. If you do the practice he reccomends you do, you will be fine!

SAVE YOURSELF AND DONT TAKE. I had an A in chem 2 but NOW I'm failing. Grades are from 3 exams then FINAL. NOTHING else. BE ready to do 500 questions/week for Hw. I cant read what he writes on board. For gen chem, I felt Todd made it a little tougher than it should have been--he gets a little too into it being a "weed-out class" compared to other teachers. The tests were okay, but sometimes it felt like it didn't matter how hard I studied.

YOU CANT USE technology. lectures beyond confusing and won't help you on the test. Overall, he's a good orgo professor. He has a good sense of humor and always seems eager to talk to students in class or have every day convos about his life before class begins. He's good at explaining things that are very complicated. The only time I've seen him be rude is telling a kid to get out of his class for falling asleep
Very, very, difficult class. That said, Todd is a great teacher! Unfortunately, he doesn't give answer keys to worksheets, which is more than a bit annoying.

In my experience he was accessible in this class over the summer and had Q+A everyday and gave us plenty of practice. HOWEVER he assigns a LOT of problems. Todd is a super reasonable professor.  He gives his time to answer questions and is readily available.  He tries to share his personal life with his students that makes the class a little more enjoyable.  It feels like he cares.  Orgo was tough but with him it really wasn't bad.
Actually the sweetest professor. The test were very difficult and required a lot of studying.

Professor Bliem was genuinely amazing in a small class setting. She was funny and kind, making a connection to everyone. She is like a sweet grandma who wants you to do your best in chem. Very good professor. She also wrote the textbook so she knows what she's talking about. Exams were also more fair in my opinion compared to other professors.

The UNC chem department in general isn't awesome, but Dr. Bliem is a great bet for gen chem. She is kind, good at explaining concepts, and her handwriting is legible. She is 
Exceptional teaching and I really wonderful
Professor Bliem is the best professor I ever had.
I loveeeee her!

I had professor Bleim for Chem 101 and had a great experience however the same cannot be said for 102. She quickly fell behind on lectures in class and began to speed through important and foundational material if it was covered at all. The Chem department leaves a lot to be desired

Chem is a canon event. the class is rough. Professor Bliem is very kind and cares about her students. She is funny and her pace is slow but still gets through all the content. Even apologized after an unfair exam even though it was not her fault.
Good professor horrible horrible class
Professor Bliem was very kind and clearly cared about both chemistry and her students. Lots of studying is required to succeed on the exams, but overall Bliem made my 102 experience pleasant.

The chem department is horrid but professor Bleim was so accommodating to my needs and was readily available. She formally apologized to the class after the 3rd exam because it was that unfair, but if you need a prof for chem102, I recommend.

Professor Bliem is very kind and funny. Chem isn't an easy subject but she is really approachable and supportive of students. Gen chem is going to be hard, no matter who you take it with because the exams are made by the department. But Professor Bliem is by far the best in the department for gen chem. 102 is over 200 people, yet she will answer every single question, answer every email, and encourage you personally throughout the course if you talk to her.Take chem w her

CHEM at UNC is very difficult; however, Bliem knows her stuff and is very kind. Her lectures are very helpful for exams. I've had a year of gen chem with her, and my experience has been fine. Definitely a lot of work, but the professor for gen chem has little bearing on your grade. Just go to Chem Possible and use other outside learning materials.

the unc chem department is notoriously difficult, and there's no other way she could teach this class because of the curriculum, but her lectures were extremely helpful in outlining exactly what to look for in the exams. go to gpss, use peer tutoring, do chempossible, do the exam type questions and you'll be okay.

Just not a good lecturer. For the chems your professor doesnt matter that much, but I have heard that every other professor is better than her. It is easy to tell that she doesn't want to be teaching Gen Chem, just take it with Fostvedt.

Bliem is fine, i never rly spoke w her personally but she seems funny and kind. Good handwriting. Gives eccentric aunt vibes. I loved taking 102 with my table (shoutout carroll 111 active learning lab!) You MUST study above and beyond to be prepared for niche details on exams. I found 101 (test avg 98) much easier than the 102 exams (test avg 89).

The Chem department in itself is very difficult, and it was already highly suggested to attend GPSS and ULA sessions outside of class. However, Professor Bliem was very charismatic in the 6-minute meetings, and she does a good job attending to questions in GPSS.

Transferred in and took 102 my first semester. Do not use AI to help you with your smart work or you are so screwed on exams. you need at least two days to review the smart works and slides. I've heard people say Chad's Prep helps. You need to do all the problems on the slides before class. Pretend you're a ULA.

Bliem is a decent professor for CHEM 101/102, but she can be condescending. She gets annoyed when you ask about testing accommodations or midterm questions, even when you're just trying to prepare. She knows the material, but her attitude can make asking for help uncomfortable.

The Textbooks do not suffice for being a flipped classroom. I never was able to learn from Bliem's descriptions- find a good ULA and cling to them. You MUST attend the worksheet sessions and ChemPossible and do the practice problems. I never figured out how to crack the exams.

Bliem does an amazing job at explaining difficult concepts. Her lectures are interesting if you actually pay attention. Although chem is hard, I feel Bliem does a great job of making it easier and doable. The Chem department in general is hard, so even though you will have to put in a lot to succeed, it is very doable with her.

Professor Bliem is amazing and extremely good at her job.  The class is difficult and requires a lot of work but she is clear and doesn't confuse you in lectures.  Her lectures are a little mono tone but its chemistry.
Dr. Bliem is an amazing professor who wants each and every one of her students to succeed.  The content is not easy to learn and requires an absolute ton of outside studying.

She seems like a nice person, but the way she delivered her lectures were so boring. Fell asleep multiple times in class because of how boring the lectures were. If you have to take Chem with Professor Bliem, sit in the first 3 rows so you don't fall asleep during the lectures.

chem101 at unc is HARD, regardless of who's teaching it. Dr. Bliem is super nice though and knows what she is talking about, and I'm very glad I had her. Go to lecture, sit in the front row, actively participate, ask questions, do all of your homework, study hard, and you'll be alright! It's a hard class, but she wants to see you succeed.

Chem 101 is going to be a tough class no matter what. Bliem is one of the better chem profs imo and actually cares about you succeeding and understanding. Lectures can be boring and monotone, but I actually enjoyed them and thought she was really funny. Exams will be harder than you expect, be sure to study everything before and after class.

She was a very nice and caring professor and made us laugh at times. But sometimes her lectures were pretty boring, and I had to learn it after the lecture. The midterms were hard and the final was harder

Prof Bliem is a great person but chem at UNC just sucks. They expect you to know the content before lecture so the lecture isn't much help if you've never taken AP chem. Prof fostvedt's slides were the most useful in studying so I would try to take her. I also just stopped listening in lecture and began to teach myself and seemed to do better.

Chem is hard, and I don't blame my grade on Dr. B but on the organization of the dept as a whole. Bliem is as kind as it gets and made me feel very seen in class. I ended getting close with one of her TAs which significantly improved my experience. I made sure to enroll in her 102. she's a gem and deserves the world.

Professor Bliem is very kind. Especially with a hard class like chem, she is really approachable and I felt comfortable asking questions in and outside of class. She is also pretty funny. You do have to work hard in the class but I think that's because of the subject and I think Professor Bliem does a good job of explaining the concepts.

Dr. Bliem was very enthusiastic and kind all semester. A lot of the bad reviews are here because the tests are hard. It is a weed out class... that's just how its gonna be. I think she does a good job of explaining the content and makes lectures interesting. Chemistry tests get a 2/5 Dr. Bliem prepares you well and gets 5/5.
Professor Bliem did a good job explaining difficult concepts. This class was difficult but doable if you have the time to work hard for it.

Bliem is the best. She's straightforward and her lectures are very understandable. CHEM 101 is difficult no matter who you take it with but the best way to succeed is by leaning into the flipped classroom. Also be sure to ask the ULA's whenever you have questions. I would absolutely take 101 with Bliem again if i had the opportunity.

Dr. Bliem is a good instructor who has engaging lectures. CHEM 101 at UNC is just very difficult. If I had to take it again, I would take it with her. CHEM 101 is essentially only graded on tests, which are very tricky. My best advice is to keep up with the readings and do the homeworks without Googling the answers.
Really funny and engaging during lectures, explains chemistry in a way that makes sense. Coming from someone who does not like chemistry, she made this class enjoyable and understandable.
Gen Chem at UNC is horrific but Bliem is probably your best bet as a professor.

Ive taken chem101-adjacent coursework three times and I can honestly say bliem does an okay job teaching it. The main struggle comes with exams which are purposely made INSANELY hard for no reason. As a chem major who enjoys chem, exams are not an accurate reflection of your knowledge. Take fostvedt if possible, but bliem is still solid.
She is an effective teacher for a challenging class. Exams are quite difficult, but she doesn't make them.

Prof Bliem obviously cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. However, I found the class to be incredibly difficult and I will be retaking it. Sometimes I felt that she glossed over important topics or did a poor job in explaining them. Get ready to teach yourself most of the material.
She is the best CHEM professor you can get. Utilize her office hours because she cares and wants you to learn, chemistry is just a hard class.

Honestly, at least for CHEM101, I don't understand Prof. Mclaughlin's low rating. She gives great lectures and, despite being in a classroom full of 200 students, makes an effort to ensure everyone understands the topics. Chem midterms are difficult, but this is not Bliem's fault.

Bliem is a very sweet professor. Her lower rating isn't deserved quite honestly. The chem department at UNC is hardcore and she does not reflect that. She does a decent job at lecturing. She is funny and genuinely a kind person.

This class sucks, no matter who you take it with. The tests are brutal, the homework is long, and there's a ridiculous number of things you have to buy. Bliem's fine. She adds a bit of humor and some fairly clear lectures. Most of class is spent on practice problems, so use the opportunities you have to make friends to study with.
I love carribeth

Chem 102 as a standardized course is difficult, considering the majority of your grade is based on 4 exams, Bliem herself is a great, funny lecturer and really makes sure you understand the content. I took the launch section with a class of about 20 which made the experience more personalized, def reccomend for any freshmen with 101 credit already.

Chem 102 is hard and its easy to lose a lot of points on the tests. Bliem was always very kind and cheerful in class. She does kinda expect you to understand everything from the textbook, class is mostly just practice problems. The test questions are usually harder than in class questions. I wouldn't have gotten an A if I didn't take AP chem in HS

Professor Bliem is, overall, a good professor for CHEM 102, but you have to teach yourself how to use a lot of concepts outside of class. As long as you study the practice exams and LA review sessions you will do fine and she is clear about explaining concepts in the lecture.

Dr. Bliem is probably your best choice out of the 101/102 pool. I had her for both lectures and have done well in both because she explains things well. Chem is chem but hedge your bets with Bliem instead of someone else.

Bliem is a great professor who truly cares about her students. CHEM101 is challenging, but she provides the resources to succeed, like annotated notes. Attend lectures and use unstuckstudy AI for helpful study prep.

Professor Bliem while covering all of the topics provided vague and often confusing lectures. Most of the learning was done outside the classroom or by reading the textbooks and I often referred to other professors notes when looking back at the lecture notes. Although exams are the same get a professor who teaches in a more in depth way.

I loved Bliem. Chem at UNC is no joke, but Bliem definintely made it easier. She clearly wanted us to succeed and was always willing to help if I had a question after class. The important thing to know is that you will have to study to do good in this class, but the content itself really isn't that bad.

If you are looking for a Gen Chem professor, look no further. Dr. Bliem is a great lecturer and loves to interact with students. She takes her time explaining concepts in class and has no issue with explaining them again. Gen Chem is hard, but it doesn't have to be painful. My grade truly doesn't do her teaching style justice (or maybe it does).

Professor Bliem is very sweet. You can tell she truly enjoys what she is teaching. She also starts off class with her 'pet of the day' trend she does and it's absolutely adorable. Would recommend if you need CHEM-102.
I absolutely loved this professor and she always had a positive attitude and was very helpful. However, the course in general was just too much and I do not recommend. TAKE AT A COMMUNITY COLLEGE!
I took this class a year ago but she was the goat as of May 2023.

Chem sucks, but it wasn't that bad if you put the work in. Mrs. bliem was an okay professor very monotone. Get fosvetdt or however you spell it. Use her annoted notes they help a lot.  Also don't get behind or you're cooked.

Professor Bliem is a fantastic professor who truly cares about the students in her class. CHEM101 will be a difficult class, so you should prepare accordingly, but she gives you all the necessary resources to succeed. Make sure you attend lectures, and an iPad may help too.

Professor Bliem is a great teacher, Chem 101 is by nature, a very difficult class. She cares about you but there is only so much she can help you with. A lot of the learning is on your own. I say make good study groups with the people in your class and take advantage of the 6-minute meetings offered (no matter which professor you get).

Bliem is hilarious and a good teacher, but you have to work even more outside of class to go above and beyond to understand the concepts because she does not teach that in-depth. Smartwork assignments and participation points help boost your grade just like 101. If you don't spend time every week going through the material, you will fail the class.

Bliem was a great prof, and probably the best option for 101. I haven't heard any complaints about her, but I can't say the same for the other 101 profs. Definitely the hardest class I've taken here so far, and requires a lot of outside work to succeed. I think Bliem would be close to a 5.0 if the course wasn't so difficult.

Professor Bliem and the Chem Department get a lot of hate that is really unwarranted. I ended up pass/failing this class, but I would have gotten an A-. The UNC chem department is hard no doubt, but as long as you actually do the work, attend class and recitation, and go to an occasional GPSS if you have questions, you will be fine.

Dr. Bliem was a great 102 professor. She spent time breaking down the content into more manageable problems and Bliem does a great job of pointing out common errors. The content is difficult and does take time to wrap your head around but GPSS is available outside of lecture. She also cracks some good jokes during lecture :)

Dr. Bliem is a hilarious lecturer and a wonderful professor! She tries really hard to make chemistry accessible, but if you are struggling you need to go to GPSS while you're doing the material in lecture. Overall, I loved her class and thought she made the painful experience of learning chemistry fun!

She does not thoroughly go over any topic. She spends 1 minute on each problem and goes so fast I can't keep up. The textbook did not give enough step-by-step instructions. Info was scattered across lectures, study sessions, and extra help sessions. I spent 10+ hours a week and still did horribly on the tests.

Prof. Bliem is a great person but not very good at explaining. You either understand the content or you do not and then it is up to you to learn it on your own. It is clear she expects you to understand what was read in the textbook prior to class and will not spend time explaining in detail. She does detail problems on sides which is nice.

Prof. Bliem is a solid teacher. Chem 101 has a common curriculum, so she teaches the same slides and content as the other professors. Sometimes lectures can get dry, but she is very clear and there are a lot of resources to succeed in the class. Chemistry at UNC is tough, but she did a good job explaining concepts and supporting students.
tough exams and lots of hw

Prof Bliem is great and does what she can with the terrible UNC chem department. I had her for both 101 and 102. She is aware of how difficult this course is and makes lectures bearable. Overall if you have to take chem here, Bliem is a solid option.

Bliem is funny, kind, and a great prof. This class is super hard. If you plan to take it, take Bliem or Fostvedt. The other profs do not know how to explain content (at least when I went to their group problem solving sessions) I bombed the 1st midterm but if you lock in from the start you could make an A for sure bc there are a lot of resources.

Dr. Bliem was a great professor. The class sucked. Chem 101 was difficult for me and a lot of other students. Ratings for Dr. Bliem are not fair (she's a great professor, but the class is just hard). Three "midterms," where the lowest is 12%, and the two others are 18% of the grade. The final is worth 27% of the final grade. So VERY test heavy.
Honestly everyone warned me that she wasn't a great teacher, but she really is not that bad. It is a "flipped" learning style so if you don't do the reading before class the lecture makes zero sense

She is an ok lecturer and the class itself is relatively difficult. Her lectures are organized and give you sufficient time to practice she just doesn't offer anything unique. She has a dry sense of humor and can be a little rude at times but otherwise, she's a fine option for chem for anyone with a decent stem background and aptitude.
The worst professor I had in my 4 years at Chapel Hill

Bleim explains concepts poorly, and contradicts the textbook daily. When she asks questions to the class, she does not pass a microphone to students who are answering questions, and doesn't really explain why they are right or wrong.
Worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. Bliem is not helpful and contradicts the textbook daily.

Took in the fall. Please do yourself a favor and take a different professor for CHEM 101. She doesn't explain things that well. Will be retaking with Fosvedt. Regardless of the teacher I definitely recommend CHEMpossible, SI sessions, Peer Mentors, and Peer Tutors for this class. Very hard. Exams are a nightmare. It IS a weed out class.

I loved this course so much and Dr. Bliem is extremely helpful, intelligent, and can explain things on a great level! I think that this was the perfect introduction to CHEM.

YOU MUST PRATICE TO DO WELL.

EVERYONE WHO RATED HER LESS THAN 4 --- it is because they did not do enough work or use the resources on campus.

Overall chem is a very hard course. With any teacher it is required to read the textbook and teach yourself most of the material. Bliem did a decent job at teaching and connecting pre-reading to lessons. The prework and homework wasn't too bad but the tests were the most difficult.

She is an ok teacher although I feel as if she went too slow some times and it was hard to pay attention to her. My bigger issue was that she was absent for the redox reaction lesson and then a few questions of the redox reaction lesson were on the final and I along with multiple people I know were unable to answer those questions due to that.

Dr. Bliem is a severely underrated professor. She is very skilled at explaining new concepts and answering q's during lecture. 101 will never be an easy class, but she provides many resources for studying and asking q's to the point that any issues I had were more about the time and energy I spent using them. Also she's very funny.
As long as you read the textbook you will be fine. Just make sure to do the work and the notes and then the class won't be too hard.

Do not take this class with Bliem. Literally contradicts the textbook everyday in lecture and instead of explaining her reasoning she simply says "got it" and goes on. I have learned nothing from this class, thank God I was able to pass fail it. In the end I would have likely gotten a B+ but this class is hell and not enjoyable at all.
Good at explaining things and can always point out common mistakes and misconceptions. This class is hard but Bliem is a good bet to get through it.

She's respectful and funny and her lectures were always easy to follow (as long as i did all the homework and warmups, which requires some time). Make sure to not fall behind with the content and be ready to study a lot. That, together with following the lectures, prepared me for the exams better than just studying by my self the days before.

dr. bliem is a really sweet professor, but her voice made me fall asleep in her lectures. honestly, chem 101 isn't hard at all as long as you actually do the pre-class readings and learn how to apply the concepts properly by putting effort into your assignments. also since shes the boss lady she gives valuable info on what to expect on a test

Two midterms, equally weighted, one short presentation with a discussion post, one long presentation which spans over several months. On top of this, there is a cumulative final exam. Must meet with him in office hours for the presentation. Rates "engagement" but doesn't even remember who speaks and still takes points off because he can.

Really enjoyed this class. Content was very manageable and exams were straightforward if you studied beforehand. Large part of the class focuses on a chemistry presentation on your own topic, which was fun to make. Beaver was accessible outside class and was very helpful with presentation prep. Can't recommend enough.

Dr. Beaver is a great teacher during lecture and really breaks down the material in an enthusiastic way. That being said, his exams are very difficult and contain a lot of niche material. I gave him a 3 because he is quite rude and condescending to students who asked him questions on 1 to 1.

I loved Beaver for orgo 2, genuinely wants his students to succeed and get the most out of his class. Orgo 2 is a hard subject theres no workaround, but if you put in the effort it is very doable. Listen to his suggestions on how to study. Attend GPSS and do the ULA worksheets. Sit in the front, ask and answer questions in class.

man he's a good prof but unless you're confident you know the material he's not worth it. his exams are the hardest out of the entire department and the stress is unreal. i got out with an A but then my physical health genuinely declined due to the stress solely from that class. unless you want your entire life to be chem, dont take him.

Beaver is a great guy and probably knows the course content he's teaching better than anyone. Yes the midterms are very challenging but the final is much more fair in my opinion. If you got through orgo 1 with a decent grade, you know what to expect with Beaver. Study hard for the midterms and practice practice practice and you will succeed.

Dr. Beaver is one of my favorite chemistry professors at UNC. He genuinely cares, will listen to student feedback, and is amazing at breaking down difficult concepts. His GPSS is super helpful and his class is very engaging. I highly recommend taking 262 with him.

Dr. Beaver is really nice and truly wants you to succeed. Explains content well during lecture and provides a lot of resources to succeed, but the exams are HARD. You need to do all of the practice material he offers and understand everything fully, but that's probably true regardless of the professor for organic chemistry.

His lectures are great and he's incredibly knowledgeable about the material. He expects lot from students, but also cares about learning if you want to learn. I'd recommend if you truly want an understanding of organic chemistry, take it with him, but if you want the best letter grade you can get, take it with someone else.

I enjoyed 262 with Dr. Beaver. His lectures make sure you will know the content. There's just a lot. Exams always have a few trippy questions, but fair overall. Did amazing on the first 3 and poorly on the final due to other stuff. An A is certainly possible if you spend 1-2 hours a day practicing. He gave some extra credit too so can't complain.

Orgo is just a hard class, and it takes a lot of time to understand and memorize it. Beaver was a good lecturer and 100% cared, but he made his exams SO HARD. You aren't screwed when you take him, you just need to know 110% of the content to do at least OKAY on the exams. It isn't like you can know 80% and make an 70 on the exam, you need 100%.

Dr. Beaver definitely knows his chemistry and is good at teaching it. He just creates next level difficult exams that are hard to do well on unless you 100% understand everything in the class. My highest score on any exam was a 66% and I would study about a week in advance.... I did much better in Zurcher's 261 and found her exams to be more fair.

Organic chemistry is just such a hard and content filled class. Dr. Beaver was a nice guy and lectures seemed to be helpful but his exams were next level hard. He is not the worst professor but if there Is an easier option, go with that one. Office hours were only held in 8 minute increments and sometimes answered questions a little backhanded.

Man, first stem class I took at unc as a transfer student and it makes me want to switch my major. Required iClicker in class, weekly quizzes online, no required practice but you're screwed if you don't do the recommended. Hard exams, I thought I could study but it just got worse as the semester went forward. Probably will retake w/ someone else.

I took CHEM262 with Dr. Beaver over the summer, and I can confidently say it was one of the best classes I have taken. Orgo is a dense subject, but with how lectures are given, the support outside of the classroom, and with enough practice problems, an A is possible. I plan to take intermediate organic chemistry with him! Do recommend.

Literally the least accessible person on the planet. Ignores every email ever and didnt respond to any office hour requests. Went to one problem sesh and he made me feel stupid. Mid teaching style. Lectures weren't horrible, but him ignoring me made them horrible. Overall, came in with high expectations, left with a low GPA and anger in my veins.

Like other reviews are saying, Beaver is a good guy but his exams are awful. I did much better in orgo 1 with Zurcher and also prefer her teaching style. Beaver does want you to succeed and is nice in lecture. Can be oddly passive in office hours/1 on 1 interactions. Again though, his exams are SO hard so be warned

I took Orgo 1 with Zurcher and much preferred it to Beaver's Orgo 2. He has a tad bit of weirdness to him; gets very easily offended (became very passive aggressive the lecture after our second exam because students were less engaged and pissed at the exam difficulty). He wants you to learn, but its beaver method or death. Exams are hard .

Great lecturer, but was VERY standoffish 1-on-1 sometimes. Make sure he knows your name. Exams were EVIL & if you didn't know 100% of content exams will get you. I never got > a 90 on any exam but ended with an A thanks to Rogue Chem and solving every textbook problem. He was fair with points back and cared for his students-you WILL learn orgo 2.
Beaver wanted to see us succeed as shown by the 4 final EC points he provided. Be warned that he always tests the hardest parts of each concept and the "exceptions to the rule"

Orgo is difficult, but Beaver's engaging lectures and clear expectations make the class manageable and even enjoyable at times. He is tough, but honest and tries to connect with students and help them succeed. He knows it's hard and pushes you to get help EARLY. Keep up with your rxn cards, practice DAILY, and consider rogue chem for the final!!!

Please take any Orgo class you can with Zurcher. Beaver is not a horrible teacher; he is just condescending at times and creates the most diabolical exams you can imagine. 3 midterms (70 or below was the median on all) and just took the 70-question final. Class is hard but doable.
Dr. Beaver is an exceptional lecturer who really cares about his students.

Dr. Beaver does an amazing job working with the lecture hall, making the large lecture hall feel like a small classroom. You could tell he cares about what he's teaching and who he's teaching it to. His tests are supposed to be the hardest out of all the orgo professors, though. Also, his voice is very easy to listen to lol.
Dr. Beaver is great but the class itself is challenging. The material is difficult, but he makes an effort to give students the resources they need to succeed.

Dr. Beaver is truly a beacon of light in the UNC Chem department. While the class is difficult, Dr. Beaver made the material very accessible and was always down to help us out with material. He is a very effective and engaging lecturer. Sometimes he is a little sassy, but never condescending or mean. He also tries to be reassuring, which is nice.

Professor Beaver is a really great orgo instructor. The content is just really difficult. He is very accessible outside of class and makes an effort to learn your name and truly wants to see you succeed. I am satisfied with the grades I got in this course and feel that they were fair given I crammed before every exam.

Chem261 is a tough class, but Dr. Beaver was an incredible teacher. If you're considering taking orgo with him, do it. He's incredibly understanding and caring. He learned the names of everybody who participated in class and would say hi while walking around campus. Attend ULA sessions, don't be distracted during class, and STUDY! You'll do great!
It's a no from me dawg.

Liked beaver in 261/262, not as much in 460. 460 was v difficult & structured poorly imo. You must be VERY confident with orgo 1/2 content, esp orgo 2, even if you took it years ago. Majority of class did poorly esp on exam 1. Added 15 pt curve to exam 1, 10 pt curve to exam 2, & a curve at the end, which was v nice and unheard of in UNC chem dept

The class is definitely a lot of work, but Dr. Beaver's a good professor. He's very caring and explains the material well. Exams were also fair. Just make sure to keep up with the workbook problems and rxn flashcards.

Beaver's got good lectures and very accessible via OH so don't be intimidated. His LAs were just awesome! They single-handedly saved me in the class with super clear explanations. Study hard for the thermo exam, that by far is the hardest exam in the course. You've got this!

This class was so informative and engaging. Exams were hard but extra credit opportunities were given, and the final also had a take-home portion. Group presentations were a good grade boost and also enlightened us on modern orgo research. Dr. Beaver was also very helpful during 1-on-1 office hours.

CHEM 101 was horrible for me, so going into CHEM 102 I was terrified, but Dr. Beaver was a great lecturer and made the class interactive and easier to understand. The lecture was a launch so the class was only about 35 people. Dr. Beaver was respectful and his LAs were great too. The tests were difficult. Go to the LA review sessions!
this class was unnecessarily difficult with him. beaver is rude and condescending at times, and sometimes appears to have an ego issue. take with literally anyone else.

Chem 460 review. Lots of prerequisite knowledge required, make sure to brush up on orgo 2 before taking. Lots of pre-class reading, and exams were extremely difficult (be he did give a generous curve). The class has a large presentation component, which is fine, but just be aware.

This review is for 102. Dr. Beaver is a great professor. He made learning chem easier and made sure students understood as much as he could. Chem 102 at UNC is hard, and the exams are ridiculous. But Beaver is definitely the best professor I've had in the chem department and is passionate about what he does. I would definitely recommend him.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment.
