The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

Dr. Beaver was awesome. Set the best foundation for Organic Chemistry and his lectures were very informative. He is very smart and forces you to think through the course material. His lectures are also engaging and I would definitely take him again. The only slight is his exams are difficult, but I learned so much in this course.

I was pleasantly surprised by this course. Joshua Beaver was extremely professional and knowledgeable. He always came prepared and stuck to schedule, never falling behind on the course material. He was genuinely compassionate with his students as well, encouraging participation and making a point to remember people's names.

Great course overall. Orgo here is hard but getting a good grade is definitely doable. Beaver is a very caring and engaging professor. I can see how he may come off as condescending sometimes but he's very empathetic and receptive in office hours. Don't take Orgo with too many other hard classes. That was my mistake and I didn't lock in enough.

It's UNC orgo, it's going to be a lot of content. I bombed the first test before learning how to prepare for this class. Skim the readings before class, don't spend too long on them, there's a lot of unnecessary info. Keep up with the workbook, it's the key to the midterms. Go to the ULA session and at least one problem solving session a week.

I love Beaver. He was amazing, and the class is very manageable if you stay on top of it. He has q&A sessions and office hours to help and genueinly wants to see you succeed. Many people said he seemed condescending, which at first he kinda did, but as soon as I talked to him a couple times he is the best prof ever.

It's definitely possible to succeed by doing workbook +textbook problems, ULA worksheets, going to q&a sessions -- uncommon most students with other hard classes. Midterms are pretty fair, but Beaver is not super accessible; condescending and judgy -- gatekeeps info at his q&as, so go to those if possible (or todd). Has a buffer for graded work.

Prof. Beaver was a nice guy and could be pretty engaging during class. However, lecture slides were often vague. Midterms were significantly harder than the final exam, and final grades experienced a slight curve. When in doubt about whether you should have received credit for an answer on a midterm, submit a regrade.

Dr. Beaver is a wonderful lecturer and instructor.  Organic Chemistry is hard, and requires lots of practice and attention to detail; Dr. Beaver emphasizes these things daily in class, and puts a ton of effort into helping people correct their misconceptions.  Easily approachable, spent a lot of time making the class digestible. Curved final grade.

Dr. Beaver cares about his students but I do not think he is a good lecturer. The slides are a bit confusing and his explanations were vague so we could "teach ourself". The review sessions only helped if you knew what you were doing and had a few questions. Orgo is one of those subjects that requires consistent studying so don't fall behind.

Orgo is fairly challenging and requires a lot of practice. Attention to detail is key in the course. As for Dr. Beaver, I don't have much positive to say. You ask him a question, he will not only not answer your question, but he will make u feel like a fool for even asking. I got more clear answers on EdStem, the TAs do better than he does.

I quickly came to the realization that some people are good at orgo and others just aren't. I did the preclass, ULA sessions, the GPSS, workbook, and slides every week and still did bad in the class. Some people that didn't even do half of what I did would do better. Make sure you don't take any other hard classes bc this class is time consuming!
Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. Make sure you take his advice in the syllabus and you will do good in this class

Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. He cares about his students; however, he expects a lot from you. I would say do absolutely everything he offers, and you will do great. 
Overall, Doctor Beaver is one of my favorite professors at UNC, even though Orgo1 is hard!

Very intersting lectures and very nicely planned out lecture slides. Dr. Beaver wants students to do a lot of practice questions outside of class and I do not like the pre-class reading quizzes (Easy to get points but heavy reading and does not really help me to understand the content). Easy to get daily participation and graded work points,.

Organic chemistry is very difficult to navigate, but Beaver truly explains these concepts and ensures his students have a deeper understanding of the WHY behind everything. I am very glad I took this class with him!!

Organic chemistry is going to be hard no matter who you take it with. Beaver was a good lecturer and provided lots of problem-solving in class so lectures were never boring. The textbook for the course was actually very good and Beaver's slides were very helpful when studying for exams.

Extremely difficult course and main source of learning, his own written workbook has no solutions...so outside of the scaffolded answers he provides on canvas, ALL the other practice, good luck getting and if your schedule doesn't allow for you to go to office hours, sorry for you. Smart guy, fair but hard tests, and cares.

Lectures were engaging and easy to follow along, however the difficulty of the course was extreme at times, especially in the tests, tehy were nothing like the previous exam questions given for practice.

He does not know how to teach.  He is the most condescending man that I have EVER met and that's saying a lot.  He is also so misogynistic.  He is so self-centered, everything is about him and nothing is about the ACTUAL content of the class.  This class literally bombed my mental health.

Became an alcoholic, it was that bad. Honestly, the main issue is the problems done in class are infinitely easier than the ones on the test. That being said, he's a really good guy and cares about you if you put in the effort.

Dr. Beaver's approach is high structure active learning - it rewards students who practice every day using all resources (workbook, blank slides, worksheets, office hours). Was 261/262 hard? Yes! Does Beaver have high expectations? Also yes. This can be intimidating for some, but it motivated me to try my best. Orgo @UNC is high risk + high reward.

In 262, there's SO many rxns to know; prioritize this class. Keep an errors notebook. You need to understand WHY things happen. Beaver was more personable in 262 than 261, but still had high expectations of depth of understanding. Have him and the ULAs answer all of your questions, all the time. He is more willing to help if he knows you by name!
Do not take a class with him

The best chemistry teacher I've had.  You definitely have to put in the work, and go to his Q&As and LA sessions as much as possible.  Content is difficult but he genuinely wants you to succeed and will take student feedback to heart.  Test questions are pretty straightfoward and fair.

This is a very difficult class and Dr. Beaver is known for making hard tests, however, he genuinely does want his students to learn and succeed in the class. You will need to devote a lot of time to studying and practicing the material but you definitely can do well in the class.

Def a tough class and still harder than 261 (esp the second unit). Having a good foundation in 261 is KEY. Insider info: every test had a huge predict the products section, and acid-base shows up every time. Encouragement: first midterm=worst grade in orgo ever, last midterm=best grade in orgo ever. Midterm med were 77, 74, 77; final med was 79.

Dr. Beaver is a great guy! I had him for 261 and 262, and you can tell he really cares a lot about his students. Orgo definitely was not my favorite subject but he was always engaging and it was nice to come to class where the professor knows your name in a big lecture room. The course is hard but if you take his advice, you will do just fine!

Seems to be a genuinely good guy and a solid teacher. However, he expects all of his students to have a near-perfect understanding of all of the material. It comes across as if he thinks this is our only course.

Orgo 2 with Dr. Beaver is way better than orgo 1 (had him for both)! You NEED to do the legwork for this class - do the workbook/textbook problems concurrently with the lectures, study well in advance, and you will do fine. I got a B- in orgo 1 and I'm maintaining an A- in orgo 2! He cares a lot about his students - work hard & you'll be fine!

Beaver is a difficult professor no doubt but I accredit much of my ability to study and learn effectively to his guidance and mentorship. He genuinely cares about your well-being and if you show effort, he'll reciprocate. Exams are pretty difficult but not impossible by any means. Go to class, participate, do the readings, don't fall behind.
poo. avoid.

His exams were definitely the most difficult to take and understand by far. If you do not have a thorough understanding of the material, and fall short of 100% understanding, the exam will be challenging. They are not impossible; rather, they test your overall comprehension through every possible question that could be asked.

Organic chemistry very difficult in general, especially when you're taking it here! Dr. Beaver, however, is a very good professor and I really do think he cares a lot for his students. You have to do the reading, practice, study and work very hard!

Dr. Beaver is very knowledgeable and truly cares about his students succeeding. However, he has a very condescending demeanor when explaining concepts in office hours or review sessions. He expects students to learn at the rate he would which comes across very heavily. He is very organized and lectures really clarify the textbook readings.

Dr. Beaver was nice and clearly knowledgeable about organic chemistry. However, I felt that he did little to explain any difficult concepts during lectures. All midterm medians were in the 60s and there was about a 1% point curve at the end of the class. Exam questions are harder than lecture and practice questions.

I'll try to cover what the other reviews haven't covered already. I honestly thought Beaver was a great teacher and I always found his problem sessions helpful. I know it's hard, but try not to stress too much about your grade; there is a slight curve at the end. Here are my grades for reference: mid-80s on every midterm, low 90 on the final.

Beaver explains concepts well & learns names but orgo itself is a menace. CHEM 101/102 at UNC were pretty easy A's for me, but I spent several hours a day on orgo just to get a B+. Tho its possible to get an A- or A if you get in the 80s on exams bc they curve slightly at the end. Redo the slides, go to ULA sessions, do as much practice as you can.

Beaver is a respectable guy who deeply understands Orgo, making for a good professor, but he also has extremely high standards for students, so merely keeping up during lecture will not get you a good exam score. Tests medians were around 68, so you must deeply understand the material. This course is what you can expect of a Orgo course at UNC.

I don't know why everyone talks badly about Professor Beaver but he is a very caring man. He is straightforward and will say that a problem was "easy". However, don't take that to heart.  Attending his office hours is also great because he gives you tips on how to succeed in the course and he wants everyone to succeed.

Nice professor who learns your name if you participate. He can be pretty fun to learn from when he's in a joking mood, and is clearly passionate about chemistry. Chem classes here are what they are, but he does his best to help you succeed. You have to be the one to put in the hard work to succeed. Medians on tests were 66-68 so study hard.

I know orgo is notoriously the most difficult class at UNC, so I'm trying not to let that get in the way of my rating, but Beaver didn't help my understanding of the material. The workbook was helpful, but to get the answers you need to go to ULA sessions, and they only solve a few problems. I worked my butt off, and I'll still probably get a C+.

Dr. Beaver is a decent lecturer. Not the best by any means, but he was also not the worst I've had. Nonetheless, tests are very tricky and grading can be pretty cut-throat, so make sure you study and understand the material very well.

BEST CHEM PROF!! Made an effort to learn everyone's name. Commended individual students for improvement on exams. Explained the material so well. I did so much better in ORGO2 than ORGO1 w/austell. I absolutely adore Beaver. Extremely kind. iClicker for attendance. The exams were what I expected. I did devote a lot of studying time, but u should.

Dr. Beaver is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and tries to get to know everyone's names. He wants the best for everyone and always had great advice on how to succeed in the class. I would definitely recommend taking a chemistry class with him.

I feel like a lot of Chemistry professors get a bad rap because they teach a difficult class. CHEM 262 was definitely not easy, but Dr. Beaver explained content well and clearly wanted us to succeed. I wish he had written all of our exams rather than alternating with the other professor, but that is not his fault. I'd take another class with him.

Dr. Beaver was extremely kind and respectful. His lectures are interesting and engaging, and he's a very smart, fair person. The exams are stressful, but Dr. Beaver does his best to make sure you're not too scared for his exams. I recommend him wholeheartedly.

Pretty solid professor and a good guy. He seemed to truly care about his students and their success. He understands that the material is hard and does everything in his power to allow students to be comfortable with it. I enjoyed taking his class.

Beaver is a good teacher. The test were hard but fair and they are always good about giving us the partial credits. I believe Beaver wanted us to succeed and provided tips outside of class material on how to study.

Dr. Beaver seems to be universally despised for no reason. Organic chemistry is never going to be a cakewalk. However, Dr. Beaver was a funny guy who often told us many anecdotes. He did a great job with conveying difficult orgo 2 concepts to students. Exams were graded generously and Dr. Beaver actually (wait for it) wants you to succeed.

Orgo 2 is naturally hard, but I think Dr. Beaver gave us everything we would need to succeed. He is available for questions, has regular office hours and problem solving sessions, and responds to emails promptly. He overall hasn't done anything wrong in my book, even if he may not be the most exciting or charismatic guy.

Don't listen to anyone who says that Dr. Beaver is uncaring, manipulative, etc. They are just people who have become frustrated with organic chemistry - its a subject that takes a lot of work. Dr. Beaver truly cares about his students, is willing to help them in any way, and also is quite generous with his exams.

Orgo is obviously a hard class but Beaver is a good professor. His lectures are always clear and have lots of class participation, and there are tons of resources to get help and practice after class. He's also very generous with partial credit on exams

Dr. Beaver does a great job of making lectures engaging. He also makes a conscious effort to learn student names, and is really invested in helping students be successful. He is also a big help with study strategies.

Chem 262 is a hard class regardless of the professor. Dr. Beaver does a really great job of making the content on the tests reflect what was taught in class. He is very accessible outside of class and makes a conscious effort to learn everyone in the classes name.

The only positive thing I have to say is that she was generous with curves & EC. However, she is very petty, extremely hard to follow during lectures, creates ridiculously long exams, and gives very few practice problems that I did not think looked anything like the exam. I only did well because I am comfortable with stats and put in a ton of time.
Erin Baker graded almost solely based on midterm exam scores, and didn't assign much homework to practice lecture material.

She did change the grading scheme because of issues with AI which was unfortunate, but although the exams became weighted higher, I have never seen a professor give such generous curves on exams as her (even if average = 70s). She does problems slowly and in detail, and super open to questions. Exams are long but every 241 professor has long exams

very poor lecturer. was extremely difficult to follow along - expect to spend tons of time outside of class teaching yourself the content. 

tests weren't difficult but very long, so there was never enough time to check over work. 

but, if you are math-minded, you will find this class easier than other 241 sections because of its focus on stats.

Makes ARS absence accommodated students do a problem you didn't learn how to do (only blank slides provided) and submit it by 5pm the same day for credit. Admitted to people outside of the class that she made exams extra difficult on purpose after the AI issue. Punished class for some people's wrongs to be "fair." Taught unnecessary extra stats.

Different content from other 241s. Tests are based on lecture content (not textbook). Teaches extra math that won't be tested on, but she lets you know what will/won't appear on a test. Tests are long and seem hard, but curves are generous +EC. Didn't post slides afterwards & only wrote on chalkboard.

Overhated for AI imo - we were not faultless.

Dr. Baker seems sweet but the AI incident definitely left a bad taste in her mouth (She changed the syllabus to be 85% exams right after). Exams were long but she curved them all. The final was fair. I would take the other 241 sections over her's because she mostly teaches statistics, only the last 1/3 of class was actual chemistry.

I ended up getting an A after a near perfect score on exam 3 and replacing the lowest midterm grade with the final grade, however, her class was hard and not really reflective of what other 241 classes teach. Her lectures were confusing to follow, and my success at the end of the course came from reading the textbook, not from her. Kind of petty.

Covered half of what other CHEM241 sections did, which is unhelpful for the lab/MCAT. Said that the final would be a certain format, then changed it without informing students. Overcomplicates the simplest concepts and doesn't upload her slides/work half the time. The rare extra credit doesn't compensate for the stress you'll feel from this class.

Dr. Baker is rly nice and clearly cares about her students. That being said, this class was really math/stats heavy (big content difference from other classes or the lab) and the explanations weren't always the easiest to follow. Tests were really long but not terrible for UNC chem imo. Unnecessary hate.

I had only positive interactions with Dr. Baker. However, I found the most challenging part of this class to be that she wrote on the blackboard only and I struggled to read it a lot. I did appreciate the practice questions she provided and they were always very similar to exam questions. Once I understood her expectations, the course got better.

Go ahead and take her if you want extra premature balding. I genuinely did not comprehend a single thing this woman taught all semester, and trust me, I normally enjoy chem. I appreciate the extra credit but never have I seen such terrible grades as I had to dig thru everyone's exams to find mine. and don't even get me started on the AI situation

Acted like a child the entire semester. Held a grudge and retaliated against the ENTIRE class for ONE assignment that had nothing to do with the core curriculum. Was condescending and sent nasty email replies, if she ever responded at all. Told us she purposely releases exams after class, because she doesn't want to have to answer our emails…

Dr. Baker handled this semester's 241 class with complete immaturity and lack of professionalism. She doesn't know how to teach to save her life, her lectures are all over the place, she made her own crazy curriculum, and changed the syllabus and grading system in the middle of the semester. Her midterms were 40 questions long, longer than finals.

Her exams are extremely long, and the class is disorganized, but I feel she deserves some credit for how she tried to make up for the first half of the semester. Generous curves, extra 3 points on exam grades just for coming to the next class, and a very fair final exam. It is frustrating to have such a different experience from other classes.

Other reviews are unnecessarily harsh. She was an okay lecturer and her exams were very hard, but she was pretty clear about what was going to be on them. She posted review sheets beforehand and graded generously. Honestly if you can do the practice exams you'll be fine. Most stats heavy than the other professors, so avoid if not your thing.

While Dr. Baker is a brilliant researcher and kind person, she is not a very effective instructor. She struggled to convey even the simplest of topics, resulting in students needing to learn the majority of the material on their own.

While Dr. Baker isn't the best lecturer and doesn't cover some of the content that the other 241 sections do (which makes 241L more difficult), the other reviews are a bit harsh. She makes it very clear what will be on exams and she curves them + additional bonus points. She definitely has her faults, but the generous grading makes up for it.

Dr. Baker writes all her notes on a blackboard and doesn't post notes that you can go back to. Half the time she has to look at her paper to see the work she did before continuing on the board. The way she does problems is more complicated than it has to be. She is so strict about sig figs but messes them up on answer keys and lacks consistency.

Dr. Baker made CHEM 241 a terrible experience. She is incredibly immature and lacks professionalism. While some students used AI on an assignment, instead of punishing those who did, she punished the whole class. She did the same thing on participation grades. She is condescending and acts like she got her feelings hurt and needed to retaliate.

Nice lady, terrible prof. Do you want to succeed at UNC Chem 241 - don't take Baker. That's a fact.  Why would a professor have to curve and give extra credit for each exam?? Because most students did bad!!! It's a sad story; people fought to get into this class, just to be played in the end. This is the Carolina STEM experience.

Syllabus change, lack of partial credit, long exams, and limited practice. BUT she curved, gave extra credit for attendance so you could get >100 on exams, and is so kind and personable when you go to OH. Final exam almost all directly came from past exams or in-class slides. She's also famous but you'd never know just from class. Would recommend!!

Though this class was incredibly frustrating, I think Baker also had many saving graces in the class. Extra credit during certain class periods, curved every exam, and the very straighforward final after you make it through the class. Did I enjoy the class? No. Absolutely not. Very disorganized. But she makes it possible to get a good grade.

Extremely exam-heavy(85%)and unforgiving grading. Changed the grading scale weeks into the course. Penalized the entire class for "AI use" with no evidence. Rarely responds to emails. If you want a fair, transparent, or supportive instructor, avoid this class. Change your schedule around if you must, do not settle for Dr. Baker, you deserve better.

Yes, she teaches a different course than other analytical profs, and yes, she's not AMAZING at teaching. Keep in mind that half our class DID use AI to shortcut an easy paper, so take all you see here w/ a grain of salt. The content doesn't always feel like chem, but it's really not hard. Go to class, do the work, and go to office hrs. She cares.

Her exams aren't conceptually difficult but are very heavy on memorization. The course often felt more like stats than chemistry, but she didn't clearly explain either aspect. She seems friendly but her communication can come across as passive-aggressive at times, which made the class environment less comfortable.

Honestly, this was one of the worst classes I've taken. Partway through the semester she changed the grading scheme so that exams suddenly became 85% of the grade. On top of that, she barely taught actual chemistry and spent most of the time on statistics, which other 241 sections didn't even do.
just dont take her class or you will be played like a dog

Trash, absolutely trash. worst i have ever had. she changed the grading scheme in half of the term and made tests 85 percent of the whole grade. she canceled all attendance grade and a project grade which were easy for students to get grade on. she didnt even teach chem. instead she just teach you bunch of stats which the other 241 class does not.

Very passive aggressive. She goes on 30 minute tangents explaining the math behind something just to tell you right after that you don't need to know it. She accused the class of cheating and instead of reaching out to those students, she penalized everyone in class and made exams weigh more. She also took away in class participation a month in.

Very spiteful and immature. Obviously the AI thing (several students cheated on a participation grade using AI) was bad but instead of punishing the students who used AI, she made exams much heavier. Not only that, but there is very limited practice for her exams which are designed to be lengthy and tricky. No dedicated final exam review. Avoid her

Dr. Baker is one of the most condescending professors I've had at UNC, and I tend to like professors even with a bad rep. Her exams are insanely long (she had to extend time 30 minutes on all three midterms) and her lectures are super confusing. She messes up simple concepts while teaching them and makes them way more complicated than needed.

A few students cheated on an assignment and instead of giving those people 0's she took 12% of the whole class grade coming from attendance/easy assignment and added it to exams. Literally bad at teaching during lectures, unnecessarily long exams/not enough time, entire grade is exams. Not much HW. Stubborn + mean, not willing to help students out.

Take everything you read with a grain of salt, the AI thing was bad, but the ratings she gets are not deserved. If you show up to class and pay attention it is very manageable. She is clear about what we will be on exams, and they are fair(plus a curve to around a C+ average for each exam.

Wouldn't take at all. Her lectures are disorganized and often seems like she doesn't know what she's doing or how to solve problems. Very different curriculum from other CHEM 241 classes and seems to do things the ULAs don't even know. Does apply a curve but that's because the tests are difficult and lengthy (almost 40 questions long). Avoid.

I 100% agree with her response to students using AI to cheat but I want to focus on something else: her class is incredibly disorganized, but everything from the test comes from lectures that make little sense. Slides/textbook don't correspond with her lesson. She is generous with curves but it does not make up for her inability to convey content.

Her exams are extremely unfair. Both times she has made them 36 questions, with some being multipart and has had to let everyone stay at least 10 min more + barely anyone finishes. She also basically creates almost an entirely new course. Compared to the other analytical classes we learn things they've never heard of.

No annotated slides posted and lectures fall flat relating to math examples. This class relies more on self teaching than other UNC chem courses. While I understand her response to the AI situation to some degree, it also served to punish students that actually did put in the work. Removing attendance buffer was just further retaliation IMO.

DO NOT TAKE, like actually one of the worst profs at UNC, said half the class cheated on an assignment so replaced 10% of the grade into the exam category, making the class 85% exam weight? Then doesn't record lectures, doesn't drop any assignments or exams, no flexibility at all. Doesn't even fill in slides to post online. Lectures are scattered.

The material we are supposed to know isn't really explained to fullest extent that it can be. Often explains problems in the most complex way possible. Exams material isn't the hardest, but the sheer amount of questions given is too much. Lecture was mostly full even after extra time was provided. Keeps brining up the ai situation.

Don't take analytical with Dr. Baker - if you work hard enough you can get through it but it will be miles easier with any other professor. Her slides are disorganized and she is not the best lecturer either. She does not explain concepts clearly and will often go on material tangents and then say that we don't actually need to know any of it.

It's actually true that more than half our class DID cheat using A.I. That in itself is problematic. But the cringe reviews complaining about the fact that Dr. Baker actually did something to address the cheating? They really devalue the UNC brand. The school seems to admit a lot of cheaters, who retaliate when caught because they resent working.

please just dont. its october and we've barely even touched actually chemistry. shes obsessed with math so we've literally been learning statistics since the start of the semester. so unfair to give such a different experience than the other classes. her slides make no sense and her test questions are obscure (and first test was legit 36 questions)

Much easier than any other chemistry professor at UNC. While accusing students of using AI and changing the grading scale to weight exams higher was unfortunate, it shouldn't really change anyone's grade in the long run if they're coming to class and putting in the work. You can tell she truly loves the subject she teaches and curves exams to help!

Avoid Erin Baker at all costs. Right before the first exam, she accused half the class of using AI, despite having no proof, and proceeded to change the entire grading scale to make exams weigh more. She has been nothing but spiteful since then, using obscure test questions from unrelated topics in class and being condescending in emails.

Take take take! She is miles easier than any CHEM241 prof with extra credit and curves to meet 85% test averages. Super caring and sweet. Although beware she has her own syllabus that will not match with lab - you will have to learn most of that content on your own.

I highly recommend Dr. Baker! She keeps exam averages around 85% and gives extra credit if they're lower. Her exams are very fair and she only tests on what she gets through in lecture. Her grading isn't very exam based for a chem class (only 70% of grade comes from exams). Also very accessible outside of class, friendly, and a very lenient grader!

Extremely caring and passionate professor! Tests are long and quite challenging but review questions are very similar. Didn't cover all topics that regular 241 sections got to but she writes her own exams so it's whatever. Recommend!

I took the honors section of chem430 and loved it. We did a capstone project and got to present our work at the Undergraduate Research Symposium. I was able to learn new how to work with data and even apply some of what I did to my own research! It was hard at first but I learned a lot about myself and team science. This was my fav class at UNC.

Dr. Brunk is kind and clearly cares about her students. She is very busy, as most research faculty are but she answers questions when you bring them to lecture. The flipped classroom can be an adjustment, but it reflects med school style learning. Biochem is challenging (DUH). Homework load is heavy-it helps and can be a grade saver for exams

This class was really hard but really good. It changed my view of medicine and it changed what I want to do with my life. I love the real world applications and learning how to work with data. I loved the lectures on precision medicine and things that are really happening in science.

Took Brunk because Hogan's section was full - worst mistake ever. My friends in Hogan's section had a walk in the park compared to what Brunk put our class through. Prone to mistakes in videos/lecture, very confusing explanations when asked for clarification (which I had to ask at office hours bc she never responded to my emails!), tricky exams.

She is rarely available and actively makes it harder for you to find help. She doesn't let you email her so you can only get help from the TAs. I had to have my final exam rescheduled and she refused to help me out. Keep in mind it was an EXTREMELY easy fix. Don't expect any notes or videos to be posted, and her modules don't match with the exams.

Dr Brunk is very nice, but not a great lecturer. There were mistakes on nearly every assignment including concept check quizzes and exams. The lectures were quite confusing at times. I couldn't get answers for the exam problems I got wrong because she doesn't release keys to us OR the TAs, and I could never make her office hours.

Dr. Brunk has a unique style of teaching for her class that some like and others do not. In order to do well in this course I would suggest preparing to understand the concepts on your own outside of class.  Dr. Brunk is good at teaching but it just seemed like her style of teaching was out of date. Also took long times to return tests.

Genuinely don't know why she provides us with an email to send questions to. Also, you'd think having only video lectures would result in clarity and infrequent speech errors, but that's why you're the student and not the professor.

Professor is hard to reach, takes a few follow ups for a response, even with the designated email. Final exam date was told after having “TBD” in the syllabus up until almost two weeks before the final. Flipped classroom, 0/10. Tests included small details from DEs, practice exams unhelpful. Grading scale somewhat curved to help though.

This is why research faculty shouldn't teach classes. It seemed like Brunk didn't have time to teach the class and didn't care about the students in it. Very disorganized: never released answer keys for exams, incorrect answers on CCQs, lecture content often contradicted videos but barely able to get ahold of her through email to ask questions.

Terrible class. The content itself shouldn't be bad, but Brunk is incredibly inefficient in lecture while also not teaching anything. She was extremely difficult to get in contact with and to communicate with. The coding for this class had almost no guidance and Brunk was very unhelpful. 0/10.

Brunk teaches biochem fine... the class had its own issues. Quizzes had wrong answers that wouldnt get fixed. Exam content wasn't weighed well: class emphasized big on topics just for there to be 1-3 exam questions on it. Wouldnt drop a quiz during the snow storm. Coding projects (DEs) were annoying. I didnt learn any Python I could practically use

Data exploration assignments are accompanied by a quiz, where the questions are incoherent. They refer to the wrong section of the DE, they have demonstrably multiple correct answers for questions that are choose 1, and multiple answer choice is on for questions that specifically ask for 1. Canvas quizzes are frustrating beyond content difficulty.

Interesting method with adding coding into the material. Biochem is a bit tough but the layout is manageable. If you come to class and ask questions about the material from the lectures you will be fine. Lots of opportunities outside the exams to get your grade up.
Flipped classroom is confusing and no one likes it. Weird assignments, like python coding but its more like reading about how the code is made than learning coding.

Flipped classroom, meaning watch an 60+ min of lecture video before class and lectures are practice questions, they go incredibly slow because, well, she didn't actually teach the material. Writes small on whiteboard?? for some reason in a GSB classroom. No attendance. Believes in the flipped class too much, unorganized/a little incoherent in class

Dr. B, is incredibly sweet, caring, and fair. They create a supportive learning environment, encourage participation, and provide clear, engaging lectures. Their grading is fair with helpful feedback, and they're always available to assist students. An exceptional professor overall!

Dr. Brunk uses innovative technology in her teaching, which can feel challenging at first, but she provides all the resources needed to succeed. Her lectures are well-organized, and she explains complex concepts clearly. She also dedicates class time to discussions, giving students the chance to ask questions and deepen their understanding.

Dr. Brunk is not a great lecturer, but she cares about the class and tries to engage the students as much as possible. The course content is interesting, but the flipped classroom model really did not work for me and it was hard to motivate myself when we would just do a few practice problems after a 30-60 minute lecture video the night before
take the class with any one else. would take weeks to get exams back when she had less than a 50 person class. so so so boring. hated the flipped classroom and felt like I learned nothing

Exams were straightforward as long as you studied the lectures and did the homeworks. Textbook reading is not required at all. Pre-lecture quizzes are a hassle, but manageable. Also, class isn't as test heavy as usual due to a decent portion of the grade dedicated to protein modeling in Python, which was a grade boost and gave breaks btw content.

The class isn't based off readings which is nice, but the research assignments are difficult even though they were interesting. Overall, if you put in the work you should be fine. Just prepare to be frustrated if you need her help. Hard to reach, lots of question mistakes that she would end up docking you points for, gets worse as semester goes on

Dr. Alexanian is a sarcastic funny guy, teaching style (talking at us) was ok but the pace is fast and lots of review for nuances in reaction mechanisms is required to understand what was going on. He's doing his best but he is def a research prof.

So far Dr Alexanian is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He was slow during his lectures, but it did not hurt me. However, during QA sessions and office hours he was extremely nice. His exams are so much harder than Dr Eskew's; however, questions he asked were fair.

Would ramble in class about his lab -- unclear on what we had to know as fact vs fluff? The midterm he made was ?? (average was a 63), and our class's grades were lower than Eskew's, but no curve. Final was also not easy. Condescending to questions in class. Interesting guy though, with a dry sense of humor. Allegedly gatekept things at his Q&As.

Erik is maybe the most mid CHEM professor at UNC. He's pretty nice and funny during class, but if you like a fast paced class, he moves EXTREMELY slow. His midterms were not too bad, the second one was rough but the other two and the final were really easy. He was very dismissive of people that asked stupid questions, but I liked him overall

This class has pretty fair midterms. It goes pretty well for me until the final, which was insanely hard. Erik is nice and understanding, but just be ware of the orgo final, which was the hardest chem exam I have ever taken at UNC.

Taught content well and clearly knew his stuff. Would move a little slowly through lectures; we were always 1/2-1 lecture behind the other section, which would sometimes hurt us on the end-of-week assignments if we didn't get to cover everything. Was late to lecture by a few minutes consistently. Nice guy.

Alexanian is a pretty good teacher. His lectures were pretty slow paced and understandable but we did always get through all the content. At times his answers to questions during lecture came off as condescending. The midterm he wrote (other sections professor wrote other midterms) was significantly harder than the rest. Final was pretty easy.

Erik is pretty nice but blunt, which may come off as condescending. He's a decent lecturer but goes at a very slow pace. For the honors section he only had 1 online OH session, but he did reply to emails fairly quickly. He also assumed we were the "smart kids" and ended up not explaining some things that he thought we'd already know.

The classroom is purely flipped. Class sessions serve as problem solving sessions rather than instructional time. Office hours are useful for difficult course content. Exams are difficult but fair. Sizable (~5%) curve added to final grades.

P Chem 1 is going to be hard, but Professor Cahoon has designed this class to be as effective as possible. It's a flipped classroom, which is kind of annoying, but it's much better than the alternative, since you can pause and rewind the lecture videos. He offers plenty of office hours if you need extra help, and his explanations are always good.

I really liked Dr. Garland! Her lectures move veryyy fast and she seems a bit stressed sometimes, but she's passionate about teaching and is very good at explaining concepts. I think BIOL 103 is just a hard course so you have to put a good amount of time into it to do well, but she is a great professor for the course.

She is a good teacher, but her tests are more of a reading comprehension test than actually understanding the material. If there is another professor, I would take it with them, but she's not the worst option. If you take this class with her, know that your effort most likely won't correlate with your results.

Dr. Garland is clearly knowledgeable about biology, but is the most unorganized professor I've taken a class with. Her exams are majority select all that apply with no partial credit and she is difficult to reach outside of class.

Dr. Garland is very approachable and makes it easy to ask questions. She genuinely cares about her students as people, not just grades, and takes time to explain concepts clearly. Her exams are challenging, but they push you to really learn the material. Overall, a great professor who wants her students to succeed.

Dr. Garland is very kind and accommodating, especially when I had to be out of town. Lectures move quickly and cover a lot of material, so I rewatched lectures at home. Exams have many multiple select with no partial credit. Class is interesting, but be ready to look over bio 103 if you took it over a semester ago. Reviewing everyday helps.

I took this class first semester freshman year and didn't do as well as I wanted to. However, Dr. Garland is a very intelligent professor and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. Her midterms are designed to trip you up, but if you memorize the learning objectives (aka the study guides) you WILL do well in this class. Be prepared for busy work though.

I took this course as a freshman. I was a bit nervous bc the last bio class I had taken was 10th grade (AP Bio). Honestly a chill class and a good transition to unc! She's caring and always willing to explain a concept in office hours. Last 2 units are a bit rushed, but lock in (esp on first 2 units), and an A is very manageable.

No basic knowledge will be covered in class. Preparation before class is extremely important. The professor's lecture sequence is different from that of the textbook. There is too much content, and the exam content is very diverse and detailed. Lesson quiz, unit quiz, three midterms, and final are worth a lot.

Her lectures can be a bit boring at times, but there are definitely days with a lot of peer interaction that are more engaging. The homework can be relatively long at times, but her quizzes aren't too bad. Her midterms can be a bit more difficult as well due to being very heavy with "select all that apply" questions that offer no partial credit.

Definitely spent a LOT of time studying for this class, but she does try her best to make it fair. Go to SI sessions and study the lesson quizzes/practice exams. Often gives points back on exams for multiple questions if questions were vague. Had a 92.85 but she was kind enough to round everyone with a >.5 up:). Consistent review>cramming is a must

Despite her bad reputation I thought she was a good lecturer, but exams were definitely hard due to them being majority select all that apply and no partial credit. The material itself isn't super difficult if you study hard, but the exam structure made it difficult to score high (tests were worth 72% of your grade). Be prepared to put in effort!

A true sweetheart, seriously SO compassionate & roots for everyone. Tests are hard, with half select all that apply and tricky wording but not impossible when you learn her patterns. Rework quiz questions and ignore GRQs. DEF go to office hours - she shares really cool info that deepened my appreciation for bio. Garland is a QUEEN!
Great teacher, great class. Lectures are a small percentage of your grade but you can without a doubt still get an A without going to lecture.

Homework is boring and the tests are an exercise in reading comprehension rather than subject mastery and occasionally include trivia questions. Lectures are designed to not really provide much content, but slides are helpful for exams. I didn't make an A on any test the whole semester. Definitely harder than Ott.

BEST BIOLOGY PROFESSOR. Anyone complaining about her just didn't put in the work. Honestly, such a sweet human, such a great class. Garland did everything in this class to help us succeed. Nearly every midterm was curved, she let students debate her on questions on exams and that occasionally raised our grades, and she drops your lowest midterm.
She does not teach at all! She expects you to learn everything before class and barely goes over power points. Please do not take care. She is not a good professor. Wish I took Ott.

I had Garland as the main instructor for Bio117. The class format was great and very engaging as we had a variety of healthcare professionals as speakers. I learned a lot from this course and was glad I took it. Attendance and participation are mandatory, but you are allowed to miss up to 2 assignments and 1 class.

I hated the class in the beginning of the semester and it's definitely killing my gpa but the material is interesting and I feel like I've learned a lot this semester. I wouldn't expect an A unless you're a god at bio but I wouldn't avoid it
always screaming at kids for having their laptops open in class, which I KIND of understood because this class is a pass/fail and only attendance based, but she was kind of strict it was weird.

Dr. Garland is nice, a good teacher, and knows her stuff. The course content is not objectively difficult but the way the tests are written (select all that apply, trick questions, subtle nuances) makes the class quite hard and time-consuming. BUT, all in all, if you put the work in, you WILL come out a much stronger bio student. Worth it IMO.
Really fun class with interesting material, but a lot of work and reading. Lots of group work and the lectures are engaging, but the tests are tricky so be prepared to study!

Dr. Garland overall was a solid professor for BIOL 103. The class itself is a lot of memorization and not as much application. Her lectures are somewhat engaging, but sometimes she didn't explain concepts too clearly. Her exams are definitely a little tricky, with many select all that apply questions and little partial credit.

Midterms are so incredibly difficult because of wording and she always try to trick you. On every question. Also does a lot of "select all that apply" with no partial credit. Lowest midterm exam is dropped though! She is a very nice person, super easy to access, and always willing to work with students to help them succeed in the class.

Participation and Homework matter a lot, make sure you re read your answers after you submit. But overall good if you are going into healthcare and want to explore different fields. All you need to do is pay attention in the once a week lecture.

This class is definitely challenging but it is very worth it. Her questions are worded weirdly sometimes but after a while you learn the style of her teaching. Succeeding in her class does require dedication so definitely make sure you have time to really look over material. She is very nice and funny if you go to her office hours!

Would not recommend for freshman. I took this course in my freshman year and went through a massive learning curve. I feel the way she words her tests are tricky, otherwise this is a straightforward class, 100% doable.
Just no. If you want to pass this class, do not take it with her. She is text heavy with many select all that apply questions with no partial credit.
Don't take it with her if you want to protect your sanity.

Avoid for any biology classes if possible. Lectures are 90% talking to neighbors and the rest is spent desperately trying to keep up with her as she flies through slides. Exam questions are meant to trick you and majority are select all (no partial credit). Content wasn't difficult but it felt like we were teaching ourselves. Wouldn't take again.

Dr. Garland's canvas page was so unorganized, and it was hard to find class materials. Her exams were so difficult, and all the questions were select all with no partial credit. She doesn't seem to care about her students, breezes over content, often cancels office hours, and doesn't explain problems in class. It was impossible to take notes. Avoid

She's not a bad professor/person. She knows her stuff. BUT you gotta work your butt off. I procrastinated and always studied until the last minute, and it turned out ok, but if I could redo it, I would study much harder. Content itself isn't hard, but she tries to trick you on the tests. Hate the select all. Grade not revealed until very end.
I didn't like the format of her exams; select all that apply with no partial credit for most of the questions.

Tests are written to trick you and many questions are select all that apply with no partial credit. Her lectures are terrible; she does not explain things clearly or even at all and pads lecture time by making us talk to our neighbors an excessive amount. She grades slowly and has a poorly organized canvas page. She seems very lazy and doesn't care

BIOL 103 is hard because the tests try to trick you but if you really focus during the exams, I do think you can figure out what she is asking you. The content isn't terribly difficult. Definitely learned something, just always felt super unsettled before exams lol.

thought i would get a C in the class don't know how I managed to scrape by. the exams are HELL, so many choose all that apply with ZERO partial credit. She's nice but purposefully tries to trick you up. Not to mention all the prework we have to do and she asks questions BEFORE teaching us

I had Dr. Garland and Dr. Ott. Garland is much more respectful than Ott and goes over more of the content from GRQs in lecture, but her teaching style isn't great for an introductory course. She does a lot of hand-waving and only reads from the slides. Exams can be crazy difficult and Garland doesn't give enough application-based practice.

This class gave me anxiety simply because I did not know what she wanted. At all. Lectures were so quick, she barely taught, exams were all trick questions with no partial credit, and she does not drop or replace. Just avoid if you can.

Avoid if possible -- if you go into the exam having reviewed the HWs (not related to lecture) and lectures and with the mindset she's trying to trick you, you might do ok. Quizzes open for an absurdly short time with no late policy -- tanked my grade. Lectures are pretty disorganized and unrelated. She is a very sweet woman though

what the actual **** was that class, shes not a bad person dont get me wrong but she is the worst professor you can ever take. she talks too fast, she's too smart, and not in a good way, she doesn't know how to teach an introductory course, the way she words her exams is more like a comprehension test than a bio test and overall it was very unfair

Bio 240 is pretty rough with either professor and as any general bio class here the exams are tricky even if you know the content. Study smartworks more than you think, exam questions related more to those than they did to lecture I felt. Pretty decent lectures and class is pretty interesting.
Was in the Co-Taught section. The amount of select all that apply no partial credit questions on the final was ridiculous. She's not very enthusiastic during lecture.

I was in the co-taught section with Dr. Garland and Dr. Ott. They are both great professors, but definitely have different styles, especially for tests. Dr. Ott's are more application while Dr. Garland's are more memorization. Dr. Garland was very kind and helpful in office hours. The tests are difficult, so be prepared to study.

I ended with an A, but I quite literally had to kill myself for it. This class is HARD, and it feels unfair. Admittedly, I have learned more in this class than I have in any other biology course. You truly have to work yourself to death to get a good grade though.

I took the co-taught section of 103. While Ott was teaching (the first two units) I made high Bs on both exams. While Garland was teaching (the last two units) I made low Cs. The majority of her test questions were "select all that apply" with no partial credit. Seems like a fine person but her exams are WAY too hard for an introductory bio class.

Not a great lecturer. I took this class with Ott & Garland, so the structure got super messy. Dr. Garland was always behind in lectures, and didn't explain topics well. The tests are more of reading comprehension than actual biology content. They dropped the lowest midterm and gave EC on the final, which I appreciate, but the tests aren't fair.

never studied more for a class and gotten this little payoff. lectures useless but rewatching was a must bc she blew through content. never ever knew what to study bc the learning objectives were only tip of the iceberg compared to what's on the exams. INSANE amount of "select all that apply" type questions. process of elimination won't help you gl
This was by far the worst professor I've had at UNC. Please avoid I say it for your own good.
Every day I go to class and every day I left confused and feeling defeated. Take Ott. Do yourself the favor.

Genuinely made this class so much harder than need be. The most unenthusiastic lecturer ever, you would think she despises her job. Doesn't reply to emails requesting personal meetings, exams are all made to trick you and ridiculously hard. It gets to a point where there is no point in studying. Drop it if you can, P/F if you must. Worst bio prof

She seems like a good enough person, and was pretty caring to her students, which is why the difficulty of her exams confuses me. The majority of the exam questions were multiple-select with misleading phrasing and no partial credit, almost like she wanted you to get it wrong. Overall decent professor, but I'm not a bio major anymore.

alaina obliterated my gpa. studied for the class, did all the work, went to reviews/ta sessions, but the exams made a fool of me. knowing the content cannot save u from the hate she channels into each exam question. they're literally designed to trick you. hahahaha, u really got me with the tricky wording alaina! thanks for making me feel dumb!

dr. garland seems like a nice person but she sucks at lecturing. she moves way too fast. I literally gave up at coming to lecture halfway through the semester because I knew I would have to rewatch the lecture recordings anyways. I had to teach myself and I would recommend taking this class with dr ott because you will actually learn something.

Get ready to study all the materials by yourself because the lecture are useless. The majority of class she makes us talk to our neighbors and waste time instead of explaining it herself. Tests are ridiculous and half the questions are multi-select and no partial credit. She doesn't replace or drop any exams either. Would recommend with a diff prof

Doesn't provide practice exams or hardly any study materials for exams, reads directly off slides in lecture, uses niche Smartworks questions on exams but changes one word to "trick you", stops answering questions on Piazza the day before the exam, etc. Constantly asks you to turn and talk to your neighbors just to rush through an "explanation"
Genuinely ruined STEM for me. Should have been a better experience with the way the class is designed.

All of the bio classes here are super tough, but she does an okay job. The format of tests is really weird though, it's a lot of multi-select with no partial credit given and you have to read a full paragraph for the question. Super hard tests, and lots of lecturing.

Dr. Garland was personally very kind and I enjoyed talking to her and going to her office hours. I disliked how incredibly difficult and tricky the exams were. Every question was a trick question, and multi-select with no partial credit. The content was also so ambiguous and the class outlines were SO disorganized it stressed me out.

dr garland has misery in her heart. this class was miserable. tests were unnecessarily hard and had no may multiselect with no partial credit. she was always behind on lectures and the slides were very lackluster.

I studied for WEEKS and WEEKS on end and still didn't do well on her exams. She will deliberately add "multiple choices may be correct" and then have only one answer be correct - just to trick you. She does not lecture properly, is inconsistent, and does not have the best interest of the students at heart when making exams. AVOID PLEASE!!!

Please avoid her. Exams are heavily applicational, but no cheatsheet is given. You are expected to know EVERYTHING inside out. If you are not 100% sharp on any content, you will not be able to answer them correctly. It also doesn't help that questions are often multi-select (without partial credit) and worded vaguely. Please avoid her, please do.

She didn't even taught in class---No passion, bad explaining concepts, etc, so self-learning required as always. But her EXAMS are RIDICULOUS. Keen advocate for multiple select while most of her answers are questionable / arguable & worded weirdly. It's a pure battle in finding who is best at reading her mysterious mind. AVOID!!! Take Kevin Slep's.

changed exams from Gradescope w/ cheat sheet to closed-book,pencil-and-paper tests & doesn't drop the lowest midterms; since she didn't have a question bank, many exam questions were taken directly from Smartwork homework; also doesn't post quizzes on Canvas because of technical issues which doesn't make sense because it works for another class

If I could give her zero stars I would. I honestly think that is class would not have been bad at all if anyone else was the instructor. She has no passion and her exams are always messed up somehow. Also, she grades LC based on CORRECTNESS, so keep that in mind. If you can take this class with literally anyone else, DO IT!!!

The content was manageable but Dr. Garland takes the "flipped classroom" too seriously. She asks questions in class before even teaching the material as if we're supposed to master everything before class. She also loves to trick you on exams by changing one word from the practice she gives.

Does not post slides unless asked, does not make practice for exams, no study guides, exams have select all questions with no partial credit, does not drop an exam, sometimes stops responding on Piazza, goes insanely fast and expects us to take notes in milliseconds, makes us "talk to our neighbor" for majority of class. AVOID.

Good person, but not a good professor. Does not update grades on Canvas so no sense of where you stand in the class. The exams are like SAT style, meant to trick you rather than test knowledge. Also, the midterms have select all that apply MCQs, which do not have partial credit. No cheat sheets allowed, and Garland no longer drops an exam. AVOID!!!

Dr. Garland is one of the most straightforward and direct professors. She speaks very succinctly, makes her expectations clear, and provides ample resources to succeed. Her tests are challenging and she loves to ask trick questions, but she never asked anything outside of lecture content. Spend the effort and you'll do well.
Be prepared to commit a tremendous amount of time if you need to take this class

Just took first midterm, was not particularly hard but many questions (40%) were select all no partial credit, which may end up wrecking a lot of grades. Oops tokens in the class, homework (GRQ + questions) can take a very long time especially if you actually read. Lectures are important, have a lot of exam level questions or straight up exam qs.

Dr. Garland is so sweet and caring for her students! The course however was very difficult in my opinion since the majority of your grade is based on exams that are extremely tricky and typically select all that apply with no partial credit. I studied for hours on end and knew the concepts but would often be thrown off by the wording of questions.

Dr. Garland was a caring professor, but not the best lecturer. We learned material for the purpose of answering test questions, not understanding biology. Content was scattered and the GRQs were not  helpful. However, Dr. Garland is very accessible outside of class, so make sure to ask questions! To study for the final, rework practice/past exams!

Garland glosses over concepts at times, but she explains things very clearly and is willing to help when you ask her questions. I went through course outlines at least 2 times for each lecture to truly retain the information. She only tests on lecture slides. Take your time and read every word on exams! Ask questions in class to peer instructors.

Because of my background in bio, I did not find the content of the class to be overly difficult. However, her tests are unnecessarily confusing. She writes them with the intent to trick you and when asking for clarification during the test she gives none. She's very condescending and it genuinely felt like she didn't want students to do well.

Solid teacher but devious tests. The content itself is light work but every question was 3 paragraphs and purpose-built to trip you up. I felt like I knew the material well but only just pulled out an A by the skin of my teeth. Mandatory attendance at 8 AM was not fun either. Group seating was good though.

I retook this class as a transfer and despite already having credit for the material I found this class incredibly difficult. If you rewatch her lectures and understand her slides before you attempt quizzes you're usually fine. Her tests can be tricky but if you actively review her practice tests you can do well.

Good lecturer. Tests are very similar to practice + unit quizzes -- variations of same questions. Big grade buffer (drops 1 exam). Accessible in office hours + piazza. PM's + SI's pretty good. GRQs pretty useless -- don't waste your time on those or reading textbook. Lectures a bit unorganized at times. Preps you well for later stem classes at unc.

Exams were tricky and often composed of questions meant to confuse you rather than test your knowledge or application of knowledge. Spent the whole semester discussing how cheat sheets were not useful, but then let us have a cheat sheet on the final??

The quality of the lectures was not good, much of the time is spent waiting for learning catalytics questions, lecture material is intended to be used for a "comprehension" of the material, but tests are based on application for case studies. Most egregious thing is the GRQs that have nothing of use, and the exams frequently had errors.

If you can avoid Dr. Garland PLEASE DO. I have never felt so discouraged, belittled, and not prepared no matter how much i understood or studied. Her lectures aren't good, theyre very unorganized and all over the place. She doesnt explain and expects you to know, then proceeds to give the most diabolical tricky awful exams. Just dont take her.

I hated this class lowkey. Not very hard content but it is presented in hard ways. Lots of homework but most of it feels really mindless which does not help in the long run. The slides are incoherent and usually out of order so its hard to go back and look at them later to study. A vast majority of the diagrams shown are burry and unreadable.
She was super cool. Took the class at 8am so my attendance was awful but she was a very good professor. Class is hard I'd say

Homework matters for this class, it's pretty much just a sampler through guest lectures. She's very strict about not having phones and laptops out during class. I'd recommend this class to pre health people even though it is at a weird hour.

Healthcare professionals came into speak with us and prof. Garland had participation grades, writing reflections, and pre class assignments. This was an easy-A that allowed us to learn from different healthcare professionals.

3 guest speakers from varying healthcare fields + pre-hw + post-hw every week = great exposure to diverse minds. Can be tiring at the end of the day (5:45-7:15 pm) when your mind is on other things, but attendance determines if you pass. Can't use devices/do hw (out of respect for speakers!). Def recommend for those w/ genuine healthcare interest.

I took AP Bio (BIOL 101+L) recently as a HS senior, which helped. No more cheat sheet, but exams are reasonable--based on lectures/slides, quizzes, and practice exams. Lots of grades dropped, including lowest midterm of 3; seek help from tutors, TAs, and office hours. Group seating makes the class fun. Dr. Garland knows what she's doing!

***BIOL 117 IS IN PERSON NOW***

It's really what you want to get out of this class. Great for people who don't know what they want in healthcare, but dangerously easy to fall asleep in this class. Attendance is HEAVILY monitored in this class.

On one of the first days of class, she said 'this is a weed out class'. Pretty much sums up Dr. Garland's point of view - she only cares about making the class hard enough that people don't pursue upper level biology. One of the least caring biology professors I have had here. I don't know how she keeps winning teaching awards.

Dr. Garland is one of the nicest and most knowledgeable bio profs I've had at UNC. Exams are difficult, but quizzes and HW are representative of test questions. Attention-to-detail and close reading are vital. However, an A or B is very doable given the buffer points and the lowest exam being dropped. Stay on top of deadlines and rewatch lectures!
Pretty easy, just utilize the TA's

Tough course with exams that test more on reading comprehension than content knowledge. Lectures move quickly, so rewatching them is a must. Cheat sheets didn't help much. unstuckstudy ai was a lifesaver for practice questions to prep. Overall, a challenging class that requires consistent effort.

Her content was pretty simple, especially if you took 103 at UNC, but the tests weren't really based on the content, more like application.  You get to drop your lowest midterm grade and have cheat sheets for tests.  Don't be afraid of her - a lot of her test questions are ripped directly from quizzes and homework problems.

Wasn't a super hard class. Annoying for sure. Long GRQs and mastering. Dr. Garland is really really nice. Her exams are pretty hard but DO the practice exams. Learned my lesson after the first one. Also, she rounds. Overall, not as bad as people say. Just stay on top of things.

Heard bad reviews but took anyways. Test are not knowledge based and weren't knowledge based. Cheat sheets did not help at all. Nothing was thoroughly explained. A lot of critical thinking blooms questions that she never explained or taught how to approach. Avoid at all cost.

Dr. Garland is nice and good at explaining things, but her exams are extremely difficult. I was putting previous exam question variations on my cheat sheet instead of the actual content. The whole class is based on lectures, not GRQS. I knew the reviews were bad, but I still took her out of necessity. It's NOT worth it.

The content of this course was all over the place. The exams and quizzes are reading tests and do not test your knowledge. She flies through the lectures so you have to rewatch them after class because she likes to test on what she says rather than what is on the slides. We were constantly a lecture behind and rushing to catchup. AVOID her please!!

AVOID! I had only heard bad things about her before I took this class but had to sign up as it was the only section offered. She is a nice enough person but a HORRIBLE professor. This was definitely the most challenging class I have taken at UNC so far and I took a 400 level CHEM course with 240 this semester that was exponentially easier.

She's not as bad as some might say. Many of the questions on tests are reused from previous tests and practice exams. She posts the lectures but attendance is part of your grade. Overall, she's a great professor.

Professor Garland's exams are difficult, but she'll often reuse or rework questions we have already done on the tests, so practicing these is really helpful. You definitely have to put in the work, but she gives a lot of resources to help you
Exams felt like the SAT reading section. Very poorly written questions that are unnecessarily wordy. Avoid at all costs.

I have taken her for the past 3 years out of necessity and every time I think it'll get better, it doesn't. The content itself is learnable, but her exams are not. They're tested on reading comprehension rather than your actual knowledge of the content. The amount of review I had to do for this course was appalling. Please avoid at all costs.

I was excited for this class and Dr. Ott made it a nightmare. It feels like she expects you to do poorly which really grated on me all semester. GRQs are beyond arduous, and she did a poor job explaining the content. Take someone else.

Dr. Otto lectures in a very organized and it's possible to follow her train of thought. However, she can sometimes come across as a bit condescending. Her exams are very wordy and difficult. Reviewing the lecture slides is probably the best study method. Make sure you actually memorize and understand the material.
While initially confusing, class set up was helpful and she dropped an extremely generous amount of assignments while also giving extra credit. Best 103 option.

If the devil and Dr. Ott fought, she would mop the floor with him. I took the class with her a few years ago when she had personal issues going on. In most cases, I can sympathize, but she took her stress out on us with hard exams and a worse attitude. I would recommend taking this class with absolutely anyone else.

Dr. Ott is super smart and great at her job but can be a bit condescending. Going through the lecture slides is by far the best way to study. GRQs were long and not always helpful, but it was nice to be told exactly what sections of the text to focus on. Lots of drops for lowest quizzes etc. and lowest midterm is dropped too.
She explains the material well as a lecturer, but her exams and the way she writes questions are quite unusual. It's clear that she likes students to challenge themselves.
Do not take. Benighted individual. Not sure how she managed to get a position at a university.
Inerudite. Difficult exams and unfriendly.

Do NOT take 252 or 103 with her. Not nice. Convoluted explanations of material mixed with poor grammar made tests incredibly challenging. Was dealing with personal issues that interfered with her ability to maintain composure during lectures.

Lot of busy work that does NOT help you for the exams. Pay attention to the slides, practice exams and unit quizzes because the wording is similar to the exams. Just read the exam questions carefully she really tries to trick you.

Generally I actually really like Ott and I would say she's a very good lecturer too. Her exams, however, are SO weird. This content is truthfully not that hard but her exams made it hard. Poorly worded questions, select all that apply, etc. Her final was much better though! Also rounded grades up, and had some small extra credit available.

Lectures are interesting and engaging. Exams are doable, but many of the questions I found ridiculous. If you gave me 50 questions from anatomy professors around the world, I could instantly tell you which one Dr. Ott wrote. That being said, my advice is to study HER questions, not the content necessarily.
All of her exam questions are tricky. You'd never expect that after all that hard work studying her PowerPoint, you'd get a C on the exam.
Dr. Ott is really passionate about this subject, but the exams are difficult if you don't study in advance. She does give a cheat sheet on the final so keep that in mind!

Dr. Ott is so accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to learn the material. I have a hard time paying attention in STEM lectures in general so that is why her in person office hours are so helpful. Once you figure out how to study it is definitely possible to succeed.

Gets a bad rep, but was genuinely a competent professor. She drops a lot of grades so there's a bunch of flexibility and her lectures were organized and helpful. Study the lectures, SI session slides, and practice problems and you'll do good.

I really enjoyed Dr. Ott's class! The exams are very difficult, but there are a lot of resources to help you succeed. She can be a bit short with students at times, but it was obvious that she cares a lot about teaching and biology. Overall Ott was great! Don't listen to the haters.

The class was definitely challenging, but Dr. Ott provided resources to help. Between GRQs, office hours, and study tips in class, there are resources available. Yes, the class is hard and takes a significant amount of time, but I learned a lot. Lectures could be long.
loved her for 103, absolutely hated her for 252. take anatomy with another professor. she skipped a lesson, and her exams are very tricky. she has had to drop and clarify a few questions.

By far, the worst professor, ESPECIALLY for anatomy. I've never hated a professor this much. She teaches cell bio and honestly should stay in that lane. Her wording on exams makes not only the questions, but also the answers, tricky to select, even when I knew the material. She skipped a whole lesson as well. Take an anatomy with someone different.

I was not a fan of Dr. Ott in the beginning, but she for sure grew on me and I started looking forward to learning from her each week. Unit 1 was the toughest for me (I got a D on the exam) but I stuck it out and became super ultra locked in and by unit 3 exam, I made a high B. Dr. Ott gets unnecessary hate, yes the class is hard, but she does well

This class was more challenging compared to other 252 sections. The exams were sometimes difficult because some answer choices felt tricky and could be confusing, even when I understood the material. I put in a lot of effort, and it was frustrating to feel like I was being tripped up by wording rather than tested on my understanding.

if u want to be happy dont take her. all of her exam questions are tricky. she is so condenscending. i attended her office hours and she told me that she knew i wasnt going to do good in her class. wow i wish i could rate her lower.

I thought this course was very doable. I did the homework and made Anki decks from the slides she provided in class. Overall, very great and entertaining lectures, would highly recommend! Just study and definitely do the practice exams, she bases a lot of her questions similar to them, especially the final.

She is direct and doesn't take crap from students, but I think she's effective and generally understanding if you seriously have things going on.  Exams are hard, but all her questions come from class.  She also drops the lowest exam and is allowing us a cheat sheet on the final exam.

This class is unnecessarily difficult. I swear to god the amount of times I have been screwed over by the wording of her questions is unreal. I am sorry, but this class is absolutely not it. Avoid if you can.
Had her last semester and she was a horrible professor. First, professor to ever make me cry.

I feel the way Ott teaches some concepts makes them more confusing than they should be. Instead of explaining what each concept is, she instead goes through participation questions (graded for accuracy) and complicated examples, which are more confusing rather than helpful. Her lectures have a lot of group work though, which makes it interesting.
So tricky, she purposely makes exams super hard.

I don't even know where to start honestly. She's smart and good at what she does, but she's so rude and backhanded at times that it negates the former. I didn't enjoy lectures, homeworks, and DEFINITELY not the exams.. very difficult and she loves to include trick questions. The material was somewhat interesting but the experience... frustrating.

Solidified my love for bio. Cares so much for her students and makes lectures actually interesting. Witty and fun which makes it exciting to go to class. She gives me the motivation to learn and understand all the biological concepts. Class isn't hard if you don't fall behind and keep up with the readings and pay attention in lecture.
Don't do it

Despite personal struggles throughout the SP25 semester, Dr. Ott still deeply cared for her students and taught concepts clearly. The class builds in repetition to solidify important concepts. Practice exams and lots of problems are great preparation for exams. GRQs are not exceptionally useful. Dropped exam :))) But they are pretty challenging.

Pros: Dr. Ott is very thorough on content, lectures are engaging. The mastering HW was fine. 3 exams, Lowest dropped. Final was cumulative and hard. 
Cons: tests are very semantics heavy, not only do you have to know the material inside and out, you also need to decipher what Dr. Ott is trying to ask you. Her voice gets on some people's nerves.

There are three exams and one gets dropped; she does have “flexibility” thing where she drops a certain (1-2) number of assignments but they don't apply to certain ones so make sure to stay on top of due dates
Take 103 with a different professor. Lectures were so boring, plus we had assigned seats that made class even worse.

Dr. Ott can be condescending and rude at times and even though she takes the flipped classroom to the extreme, her lectures are very helpful for the exams. I also had Dr. Garland, and exams are hard no matter who you have, but I thought Ott's teaching style was more appropriate for an introductory course and better prepared me for exams.
