Good professor, questions can be tricky, definitely conceptual

Prof Claytor is one of the best in the bio department at UNC. His lectures are clear and concise. Exams are difficult but nothing ridiculous if you studied and do the practice exams. GRQs can be long and take a lot of time but do really help you understand content. Would recommend that people jump at the opportunity to take a class with Claytor.
super sweet but god did those tests make me question my sanity.

Overall great lectures, If you pay attention and do the homework you should be able to do pretty good. Test content is gone over in class, no curves though. A little homework heavy, quizzes are online on your own. Drops 2 lowest quiz and HW grades and your lowest exam grade. Probably the best Bio 101 teacher though.
He's a great guy, and gives great lectures. The tests feel kind of unfair at times, but that's to be expected in Biology classes.

I really enjoyed Dr. Claytor's teaching style and his ability to keep the class engaged. It was a massive lecture hall but I still felt like I was participating in the class through the active learning breaks he adds into his lectures. I would highly recommend trying to take a class with him at some point during your time at UNC.

Very good professor. Lectures everyday and homework due before class. I do not think he does a great job at preparing you for the exams, he will only give typical test questions every once in awhile in lecture. He will also talk about things in class that are not on the lecture outlines. Bio is hard but he is very nice and explains concepts well.

Dr. Claytor is a great professor. He is very hilarious and his lectures are EASY to pay attention to. I would highly recommend him, but the tests are much harder compared to the hw in class. Definitely go to BioCell or office hours to get extra help. Make sure to look out for Trixxy on his slides.

Good professor, pretty engaging. Young and personable, makes jokes, and has lots of tools to help you succeed. Drops one exam grade. Material isn't that challenging if you follow along in class and do the reading questions outside of class.

I loved his sense of humor and the energy that he brought to every lecture. His slides and teaching was engaging and he was always welcome to meeting after class or helping in any way that he could. I had a difficult time in my life at the time of taking this class, otherwise I would've likely gotten a high A, but even through it, he was very kind.

Dr. Claytor is phenomenal. He is a young professor which makes him able to relate to students a lot more. His lectures are engaging, but I have noticed in both BIOL101 and 104 that his tests are so tricky. Even when you really know material the wording/answer choices can seriously trip you up. Wish he would make his exams more clarifying.
Never take this professor's class, When you doing the GRQ and Master quiz at 2:00 AM, and its only calculate for 10percent of your grade, you will know what I said.

Have quiz each week and homework everyday for up to 2 hours! I just got depression from taking this class. He never teach in lecture. This class is 101 and shouldn't be that hard. IS FOR PEOPLE WHO JUST START THEIR BIOLOGY JOURNEY BUT NOT A PHD STUDENT! The quiz is extremely hard and the exam calculate for 70% percent of your grade.

I LOVE Claytor. He was such a good Professor. Bio 101 is pretty easy in itself, but Claytor made it fun. He's funny, keeps you engaged, and teaches the content well. He really cares about his students! Anyone I know who has had him has loved him.

Tons of Homework, GRQ and lecture that do nothing with the exam. YOU WILL BE COOKED SO BAD BY ATTENDING THIS COURSE. Impossible to get A since do one question wrong will dropped to B immediately. SAVE YOUR GPA

course is entertaining but the lectures are almost useless and everything relies on self-study. Each question is 3 points out of 20, and one mistake means losing all 3—dropping to a B. It counts heavily toward the grade. Covering 150 pages in three weeks all on our own makes the setup unreasonable, with a grading system that feels truly unfair.
Super chill and nice professor! He actually wants to interact with students! Simply do the readings, ask questions, do the work and you should get a good grade.

All my homies love Dr Claytor. BIOL 101 is not an easy class, but Prof Claytor is a great professor, and he tries to be understanding of students with the course content, assignments, and grading. Would DEFINITELY recommend for a good bio professor.
Just paying attention and taking notes during lectures and on the homework was enough for me to do good. I feel like some test questions were a bit tricky so make sure to read questions twice.

Class is easy if you're intentional about doing the readings when you're supposed to. If you read, GRQs are not only easy, but helpful in making studying for tests super easy. (Started studying the day before midterms and did well, but ONLY BECAUSE I LEARNED OVER THE COURSE OF THE SEMESTER). 

Claytor is super sweet, and lectures are lighthearted.

Super nice, chill guy and very good lecturer. You can really tell he cares about his students and wants us to do well. As long as you pay attention to the readings and lectures you will do fine. Only complaint is that GRQs were time-consuming and a few times felt like a waste of time, but all bio 101 sections have to deal with that.

Dr. Claytor was amazing, I would definitely recommend him for any intro course. The class itself was fairly difficult, and just know if you want an A it takes a good bit of work. Go into this course knowing that they will try to "trick" you on tests, and lean into it by working hard to figure out how to see through the deception. You've got this!

Goated BIOL professor, his lectures were never too difficult and I thought his exams were pretty fair. As long as you do all the required homework and readings, you'll be fine. GRQs were sometimes annoying but the homework overall wasn't too demanding. Claytor has a super chill vibe which gives the class a very comfortable environment!

Dr. Claytor has a really calm air about him. He's not stressed out about bio, so you're not stressed out about bio. His midterms are very reflective of the lectures and readings. Sometimes he even straight up tells you what some of the questions will be. Great prof.

Dr. Claytor is an amazing lecturer! He's a super cool and funny guy, and you can tell he cares for his students. The tests are somewhat challenging, but if you participate and focus on the Learning Objectives, then it's not too bad.

He is such a kind and funny professor although his exams could be considered challenging. I felt like there was trick questions often but he was a very good lecturer and always kept them interesting. Homework is very helpful, especially the GRQs, and I also found the textbook very helpful!

I loved 101 with Dr. Claytor, and he is very engaging in class, and encourages participation. The class content is definitely hard, so it's important to get help with the tricky content (there are so many resources for this class!! use them!).

Dr. Claytor is an AMAZING professor. He makes the lectures engaging and there is a lot of partner activities. The content can be tough, but as long as you complete the GRQ's, mastering, and go through the learning objectives it shouldn't be too bad! I highly recommend taking this class with him!!

I hated biology before taking Bio 101 with Dr. Claytor. He is very passionate, and even though there was a lot of work, he made me start to love biology. He gave a lot of opportunities to get help outside of class and just really wants his students to do well! Definitely take his class!!

I LOVED professor Claytor. I loved his lectures and teaching style. He makes sure to keep you engaged. If you pay attention in the lectures and pay attention to the readings/the GRQ's, you are set. Claytor is also super nice and funny. TAKE BIO 101 WITH HIM

It's clear that Claytor is super knowledgeable about subject matter and he breaks down content in ways that make it much more understandable. Homework and quizzes are straightforward but you need a really good understanding to do good on exams, especially because exams are weighted really heavily.
Great teacher, kind of reads off slides but def makes lectures as interesting as possible for bio 101.

Claytor is an interesting lecturer and a really cool guy. The lectures apply concepts you are expected to have a basic understanding of from the reading before class. I would strongly recommend actually doing the readings. The material is not difficult but the tests are worded in ways that feel like they're made to trick you, so be careful.

Dr. Claytor is a little dry and kind of just speaks off the slides. However, I do think he is a pretty good lecturer and definitely knows what he is talking about. For the class, you do GRQs before almost every single class, a few quizzes, and then 3 exams and a final. The exams are fairly difficult, but nowhere near as difficult as Chem 101.
Dr. Claytor is funny and a good lecturer. His exams aren't too bad in my opinion if you study the learning objectives.

I really enjoyed this class! BIOL 101 is definitely difficult but Dr. Claytor does a really good job at providing adequete review and going over questions. The class itself is going to be difficult because it is a weeder but he does a good job.
Super fun and conversational, wears fun costumes, exams were harder than rest of material

Dr. Claytor is really good at explaining hard material. He is also super fun and is accessible outside of class. However, this class is hard! Test are super hard and are meant to trick you. Claytor is a really good lecturer but the class is hard.

Bio 101 is very content heavy so it's pretty difficult no matter what. There is weekly homework in the form of guided reading questions that are hit or  miss on how long they take. Tests are heavily weighted so you HAVE to study. Claytor provides students with lots of resources and I found him to be kind and entertaining. I would choose him again!

He is awesome! While Bio 101 is difficult, Dr. Claytor provides a ton of resources to help succeed and is very accessible outside of class. Tests make up a large part of your grade but are not too hard if you pay attention in class and study the material. Take Claytor!

Dr. Claytor is incredibly kind and a great professor. I wish I had listened to his advice at the beginning of the semester to be consistently studying for the final exam throughout the course. He was a pretty perfect teacher.

BIOL 101 is tough in general. There's a decent amount of homework (GRQs and Mastering) assignments outside of class that are hit or miss on how long they take. The class is very exam heavy and questions can be tricky so take advantage of your resources and STUDY! I found Claytor himself caring and entertaining; I'd definitely choose him again!

Prof. Claytor did a great job of engaging the class despite it being a very large lecture (more than 300 people). He was very funny and his fits were always fire. Tests were fine, but sometimes had confusing wording. The lowest midterm is dropped, and there is no curve. Participation is required, but a certain amount are dropped.

Professor Claytor was an amazing professor. He is an inclusive and encouraging professor, and he never failed to keep me engaged. His tests are a bit harder due to them being application-based, but the course overall wasn't too bad. There aren't many busy-work assignments, and everything was informational. I'd definitely recommend Claytor!

I LOVE Dr. Claytor, he is such an amazing person and his lectures cover the material comprehensively. Homework consists of guided reading which is due before the lectures, but shouldn't take longer than 1h. There are also take-home quizzes and in-class tests which are difficult but as long as you do the GRQs (pay attention to them) you'll do great!

This was my first STEM class at UNC and having Dr. Claytor as my professor has raised the bar high! Absolutely loved him as a professor and he brought great energy every lecture; he kept the classes engaging and all material was interesting. As expected though, this class is very exam heavy, so be ready to study consistently to get a good grade

I took this class as a non-bio major expecting to not like it and struggle, but I actually really enjoyed it. The exams were definitely stressful, but him dropping the lowest one provided some flexibility. Dr. Claytor is an awesome lecturer. I wish I had a reason to take another class with him!!

Dr. Claytor is so kind and wants you to succeed. Although the content may seem straight forward, don't underestimate it and study for the tests. There are online textbook readings with online quizzes twice a week, but they are fine if you do the readings. Lowest exam is dropped and so are lowest 2 reading quizzes.

Dr. Claytor is honestly a great professor and cares for his students. He drops your lowest exam score which was nice. I recommend coming to class, doing GRQs and Masterings, and the quizzes. Take advantage of his office hours because that was very helpful. This course is exam heavy which sucks, but is expected. Y'all please take him he's funny.

i love prof. claytor (hes so bonita). even though bio 101 is a huge class he's super chill. tests are very heavily weighed though, which was a pain. lectures got boring sometimes because the class is structured to where we teach ourselves the concepts before going to class by reading through the textbook.

The syllabus is very clear. Do your GRQs, go to lecture, and do practice exams and you'll be fine. This course is really easy but for some reason I got worst exam grades than my other chem/bio tests. Almost didn't get an A, but I think I underestimated the class, the exams were kinda tricky.
This class was very boring, but ecology isn't really my thing. Just study lectures, practice exams, and peer mentor review slides and you'll do fine.

Dr. Claytor explained things well for what the class was, the worst unit was the phylogeny unit but honestly that wasn't his fault it is genuinely just a confusing unit.  Class grade is majority midterms and the midterms contain A LOT of stuff from lecture so you really have to show up to class.

Dr. Claytor was great, but nothing special. Honestly, the class could be completely learnt on your own, he was less of an instructor and more of a facilitator - but I guess that is just how a lot of the STEM classes at UNC are. The exams make up most of your grade, but are quite similar in difficulty to the practice exams, assignments and quizzes.
its obvious he cares about the subject and his students.

He was a super engaging lecturer and I loved his class. It was hard but all anatomy classes are hard. I would take it again. However, it is super test heavy (78 of your grade) so doing bad on one tanks your grade.

I have taken 4 levels of anatomy at UNC and by far this has been the MOST difficult. Didn't do well on the first exam no matter how hard I studied, went to office hours and he told me to drop the course and take the F. Only graded on exams which are 100% unnecessarily difficult. Please please please take with someone else. I'm begging you
He's nice, but it is very easy to do poorly on the exams since there aren't that many questions. I would recommend taking this class with someone else.

By far the best lecturer I have had at UNC. Exams were tricky, so if your GPA is more important than learning the subject definitely take it with someone else (this class ended my 4.0). Nice guy but definitely doesn't mess around and will not budge on grading policy, due dates, etc.

Dr. Shemer is tough, this is the first bio class I really struggled in. I really enjoyed his sense of humor and he is a very king and caring person. Since he doesn't drop exams, it is very difficult to pull yourself back up from a poor test grade. He was very enthusiastic about the material and it translated to the students. Plus, he holds OH a lot

I unfortunately don't see the Shemer hype. Before taking this class I was told by everyone I HAD to have it with him, but I think I would've been fine with someone else. I found his tests unnecessarily tricky at times. He seems like a nice guy and his analogies and commentary in lecture are helpful, just be ready to put a ton of work in.
Good lecturer, tough tests, gets to know students (especially if you participate!)

Dr. Shemer was an amazing 252 professor. Even though his exams were tougher than other professors' exams, if you put in the time, they will be totally fine. His lectures are very engaging, and he breaks down the content in a manageable way. I learned so much in this class, and I definitely feel like his lecture and exam style made this possible.

This was my first bio course at UNC and I was worried. This class is tough but doable if you study and go to review sessions. Shemer is incredible and his lectures are engaging. Beware your grade is solely based on your test performance, no extra credit or curve. He makes you truly understand the material, just be ready to dedicate lots of time!

Dr. Shemer is an awesome teacher that is a genuinely caring and funny as well. His lectures are the best way to learn because he explains the concepts in a way that is easy to understand, and is very open to questions/feedback. The exams are straightforward and don't try and trick you, he actually helps you learn a lot. Great guy and great teacher.

Teachers like him make it hard to want to stay in science. Don't get the whole cool teacher thing that many students have going on with him when he seems to look down to some students, clear bias. If you can take the class with someone else, regardless of who it is, get ready to read and review review review.

dont fear dr shemer- took biol 103 and it was sooo hard but hes rly great 4 220. tests seem to have way more straightforward questions and he tries to make funny analogies (lectures are way less jam packed with time to discuss). The peer tutors and SIs really shined this semester as well! just listen to what he says verbally as slides r sparse
Dr. Shemer is an amazing lecturer, very engaging. He presents material well and actually checks to see if people understand what he's saying. Super nice person, great lecturer!

Dr. Shemer is the best professor I've had at UNC. Took Garland for 103 and 240 and never quite understood anything, got C's in both. Something about Dr. Shemer's teaching style just made everything click for me in 220. Would definitely recommend taking classes with him.
Dr. Shemer is tough but such a caring and funny professor. Makes an effort to connect with students and make the material relevant. Super interesting class and great prof!

His lectures are amazing, with good analogies and a straightforward way of teaching. Very deadpan, so his sense of humor that falls flat sometimes. His exams are hard, but he allows a cheat sheet, which balances things a lot. Pay attention to lecture and actually do the questions in class, and you'll be fine. Much more forgiving than other profs.

This class is so exam heavy and he intentionally makes them very difficult. There's no curve and very few opportunities to get your grade up if you do bad on an exam. He's a good lecturer but that doesn't do much when one bad exam tanks your grade. I expected more from all of the reviews
DR. SHEMER IS THE GOAT!!

Dr. Shemer is such a great professor for A&P! The class is very lecture-heavy, but he keeps the lectures engaging, and is excellent at creating analogies to help understand complex topics. He keeps his questions pretty straightforward, without really trying to trick you.

Overrated. Lectures are good but densely packed, requiring rewatching. Exams are overly difficult—small mistakes are heavily penalized, and effort doesn't always translate to grades. Median unexpectedly high due to large pre-med group. Consider easier alternatives if aiming for a balanced workload.
Loved this class with him! Absolutely phenomenal lecturer and makes it really engaging. Tests are really heavy for your grade though so make sure you spend time getting familiar with the material.
He is probably my favorite professor at UNC. His lectures are well structured, and he helps us understand with a lot of helpful analogies. He is also funny and kind. He wants us all to succeed.
He teaches very well, but his exams are 100% application and almost no memorization. To do well 100% rewatch every lecture, watch youtube videos, and do MANY MANY MANY practice problems

This honestly is the best class that I have ever taken at UNC. Dr. Shemer's lectures were more of a story where he made sure that he brought everyone along each step of the way. You can tell that he is so passionate about the material, and it is infectious. His exams were also fair. He let you bring in a 2-sided cheat sheet, and no trick questions.

If you do not like lecturer type professors please save yourself and take a/p with someone else. He makes the content 10x harder than it should be and has me questioning everything because his questions are worded in a tricky way. He might be better for 220 (I have not taken it yet), however, I think there are better professors for biol252.

I had Dr. Shemer for fall 24 and he is one of the best professors! He explains concepts in a way that makes you understand the full picture and how everything is connected. Exam content mainly comes from lectures, as he addresses scenarios that are similar to those on the exams. HW is light too. As long as you are attentive you will do great.
Professor Gideon is intense but worth the effort. The material is challenging, so use all resources - lectures, office hours, and unstuck study. With dedication, you can crush this class!

As much as I wanted to like Shemer, I wasn't a big fan of him this semester. His exams are crazy difficult and no matter how hard you try you always get a mediocre score back. There is no buffer in his grading system either. 75% are exams which puts a lot of stress on the exams. He is a decent lecturer but he needs to look out for his students more

Gidi is a really great lecturer and I enjoyed this course. Such a kind professor, he makes it obvious he cares about his students. His tests are challenging, but if you use all the resources and rewatch the lecture videos you can succeed. Dr. Shemer is the best professor I have had at UNC. This class is really a chore and I did not find it interesting. Gidi seems very busy given how big the class is and his other many responsibilities managing the department. I don't think he is as good as other people say. Many things that appear on the exam are not covered by the lecture. Really good lecturer and he makes genetics more interesting than it already is. He's very available outside of class and genuinely cares about all of his students.

Excellent lecturer. Exams are very fair but weighted heavily (75% of grade), so make sure you make a genuine effort to study if you do nothing else. Many things he says in lecture are not on the powerpoint, so it is very important to go to class to get everything. He records lectures. Outside of class assignments are easy and short.

Dr. Shemer was one of the greatest professors that I have ever had. He is engaging, funny, and deeply passionate. His explanations were very helpful and every assignment had a clear purpose. I have seen a lot of reviews saying that his tests are very hard but don't let that scare you. They're fair and just require some studying. Gidi is the best!

Dr. Shemer is such a good professor and puts harder concepts into real life examples to help his students better understand. Great class and professor, reading the text along is helpful, but Gidi covered everything in lecture. Content is difficult, however, the guided notes allow for a much easier time.

Dr. Shemer is INCREDIBLE! His lectures are so engaging, funny, and genuinely interesting. He has been my favorite professor at UNC thus far. Don't get me wrong, this class is difficult and test heavy, but he makes it worth-while - and genuinely wants to make sure you understand what you're learning at a deeper level. Take his section if you can!!

I absolutely love Dr. Shemer. I had him for 220 and 252 and while the classes are hard, he makes it easy to do well. His lectures are great and he explains things in a way that makes them really stick. Exams are weighted heavily and are hard; the final is hardest and can change your grade a lot so beware. Would 100% recommend for both classes.

This class is difficult, but Dr. Shemer gives you all the information and resources you need to succeed. It is up to you to study and pay attention in class, but if you put in the effort you should do well. Dr. Shemer really loves what he teaches and it shows in his lectures and lesson plans.

I adore Gidi. He is incredibly talented at teaching, he really cares for all of his students, he's very loved by all of us. Cancer biology is a FASCINATING class. I highly, highly, highly recommend this course!!!!!!!! The 200 level courses at UNC and experience working in a research lab help a lot with succeeding in this class. Take 445 if you can!

As a senior bio major, I had somewhat fallen out of love with the subject due to my experience with the 200 level classes. After taking this class with Gidi, my love for biology has honestly been restored. I have never had a professor so passionate and caring who can also teach his ass off. I will miss his lectures and stories dearly.

Dr. Shemer is great! Exams are 75% of your grade and they are difficult, but if you study well, you'll do fine. Shemer is the best lecturer I've ever had and his jokes keep everyone engaged. Gidi is amazing! His class is very difficult and forces you to go beyond the basics, with many challenging concepts that take a while to grasp. That being said, he is super accessible outside of class and willing to work with you to help you succeed. Go to his office hours regularly and exam revision sessions and you'll be fine!!

Good prof and so nice but very hard class. You get a cheat sheet on every exam and 4 on final. Lectures were dense and detailed - completely flipped classroom so come in knowing the content. GRQs due every class. Exams were heavy on application, tricky, and made you THINK. Minimal-no partial credit. Don't miss a lecture, don't get behind.

Great prof, very engaging and is passionate about what he teaches. The only thing is lectures can be fast paced because of how dense the material is and his accent may require more focus to understand. Overall, the exams were very fair; mostly application based and had very little "tricks". Go to his exam review sessions!

Pros:
- Amazing lectures!
- Gave us extra credit on occasion
- ULAs are gifted teachers

Cons:

- Exams were tough
- His accent is thick and hard to understand at times (Love Gidi tho)

How to study: Go to ULA sessions and Gidi Office hrs

a usual bio class, cheat sheet allowed but ofc not v helpful bc tests are 'conceptual'. annoying to get an A- but it's alright. he's a very sweet professor. attendance not mandatory but he's very into what he's teaching which makes it fun. i appreciate it. wish there were a little more buffer grades.

The GOAT, class was difficult but he does a great job lecturing and has done actual research on the topics he discusses. Would highly recommend. I look for his name for any Bio class I will take in the future.
He's VERY difficult, definitely more difficult then i expected, he's a good prof tho

I only have amazing things to say about Professor Shemer! He cares so much about his students, is a passionate and engaging lecturer, and gives fair exams. If you have a choice I would most definitely choose him as a professor :)
Good lecturer. I wish his exams weren't as detail focused. His notes have good examples, but he can miss the main point sometimes, brushing over it. Overall good, do reccomend.

Dr. Shemer is amazing. He uses lots of analogies to help ensure that his students understand concepts while also pausing after every concept to ask his students their questions. He truly cares about each student and encourages students to come to him with any questions or concerns.

Dr. Shemer is one of the best biology professors I've had at UNC. His lectures are entertaining, and he uses analogies and jokes to connect the material with students. He makes himself very accessible during class time to ask 1on1 questions, and his GRQs for homework are relevant and fairly short. Take his classes!
all the homies love gidi shemer

Dr. Shemer is absolutely amazing. He uses lots of analogies to help ensure that his students understand concepts while also pausing after every concept to ask his students for their questions. He also encourages critical thinking during lectures and encourages the use of our many TAs.

Dr. Shemer is the best professor I've had. He cares deeply about his students and is always willing to help if you are struggling with concepts. His lectures are interesting and interactive. Dr. Shemer teaches hard topics well, and returns to the big picture often to help students understand. He is understanding, and responds to emails about problems with assignments quickly. Definitely recommend a tutor and go to class! Take notes! Start studying for exams well in advance. 75% of the grade is from the exams. Dr. Shemer is a great lecturer and definitely knows his stuff. Gidi is the GOAT. His lectures were so clear and informative, and he is really funny. I found all the exams very fair. He doesn't give too much out of class work (especially compared to BIOL 103). Gidi was AMAZING! For all exams you can have a double sided cheat sheet and he posts the lectures after class for review. 75% of your final grade is tests so it is difficult in that aspect, but he makes the course as easy and fun as possible.

Although this course was difficult, it has been a pleasure to be a part of. Dr. Shemer is such a great teacher--and even friend. He cares and will uplift you outside of class. Totally recommend, despite not receiving the grade I wanted.

Dr. Shemer is fantastic y'all. He has amazing lectures and his homework load is super light (like maybe 5-15 GRQ questions). It is traditional classroom with him teaching the class. Deserves every bit of the praise on here and then some! A fantastic lecturer, whose humor, anecdotes, and slightly outdated pop culture references made lessons engaging! Very no-bullshit, though mostly fair. Goes out of his way to provide extra material and reading to help students. Dr. Shemer is one of the best professors at UNC. He is hilarious, an amazing teacher, and deeply cares for his students. However, the exams are very difficult and worth a large portion of your grade. Regardless, I would 100% recommend Dr. Shemer if you have the opportunity.

this class is making chem 101 feel like a cake walk right now. its genuinely so upsetting. thats it. dont do this unless you want to feel constantly defeated.

listen to her lectures over and over again. she tests on what she says. lowk i dont think there are great options for biol 240 at unc so she might be your only option. i didnt buy the textbook, it was $$ and not super useful.

Never take her. Take anyone else. It's literally been three months and she can't even manage to grade a single homework. Everyone I talk to feels the same way about her, and there's a reason her 240 class still has available seats in her Spring 2026 section.
take anyone else besides her i beg you its for your own good
she's just yapping bro idek anymore i just want this sem to end purely bc of her class

Too many people give this professor too much hate. Yes, sometimes we fall a little behind, but she actually does a great job at teaching content. She's a really really sweet person but cannot teach for her life. Tests are more reading comprehension than anything. Dr. Rea is super kind, wants everyone to succeed, and a big bio nerd (in a good way). However, she isn't a good professor. We are very far behind and content is very crammed at the end of every unit. She's an ok lecturer, and she is a nice person to talk to, but she does go off on tangents when you ask her questions sometimes. Her assignments and her exam papers are like night and day. Never saw the man but allegedly he was the man in charge of the lab. 252L is literally wrote memorization but spending like 2 days naming everything before every exam got me A's on all of them. You do not need a very deep understanding of the content to get a good grade. I found 252 lecture with Dr. Ott much more difficult, and interesting.

Dr. Johnson is an amazing lecturer and person who makes difficult subjects like anatomy reasonable.  His class is definitely exam-heavy, like most STEM classes, but his questions are always fair! He's also hilarious and makes us laugh at least twice a class.

Haven't finished the class yet but Dr. Johnson is by far my favorite Biology professor that I have had so far. He is really funny and very willing to help you if you are having trouble understanding a concept. Explains content clearly. Responds to email way faster than the average STEM professor. Class isn't easy but is doable with some studying.

This class can be very difficult if you don't make it a point to study the Anki in between every class session. If you do use the Anki and go to open labs, the exams aren't too difficult but are definitely still challenging. There is a lot to memorize in this class, but it is definitely doable!

Dr Johnson is really caring and very knowledgeable. He is easy to reach outside of class and is super accommodating to all of his students. His exams aren't super difficult if you go to class and study the material, as well as the only work outside of exams is a Mastering due before each class period. Would highly recommend!
I absolutely loved Dr. Johnson; he was a great teacher and had very fair exams. Would definitely take again.

Should not be a 1 credit class. It's hard but not impossible. DO THE ANKI and practice provided and you'll be pretty prepared. Is all memorization with some application -- the application depends on what you memorize. Review sessions, open labs, and LAs are excellent resources. Hope for a good TA they can make or break the class and your graded

The GOAT. Material is straight forward from lectures. He records all lectures, and attendance is lenient. Talk to him in office hours, he is so very understanding. Would not have taken this course with no one else.
Absolute beast. The most straight-forward UNC STEM class. I learned a lot too.

Dr. Johnson is awesome! He is an incredibly effective lecturer and funny. His attendance and homework policies were extremely lenient, leaving room to miss class and turn in homework up to a week late. His exams are extremely fair and consistent. Take 252 with Dr. Johnson, you won't regret it!!!

The best STEM professor I've ever had. I wouldn't say the content is easy but his exams are very clear and very reflective of what you learn in class. He definitely wants students to succeed and gives every resource possible to do well for exams.

my fav prof of all time without doubt. genuinely has the students in tears of laughter multiple times a lecture, and WANTS us to succeed. the course content is hard, but i find it so easy to understand with how his lectures are set up and the jokes he makes. i have a 97 in the class rn and the final should be a breeze. def take him for a&p!!
Corey J is THE GOAT. A simple guy who doesn't make his mission to make his students miserable. Not a ton of grades but exams are relatively easy if you study. Best Bio class at UNC. He is hilarious

Dr. Johnson is THE BEST professor I have ever had. The course material can be hard, but he teaches in a way that makes everything so easy to understand. The only assignments are GRQs through Pearson that you have unlimited attempts for. He also provides practice exams to prepare you for each exam. Could not recommend him enough!
So much memorization. Worse than the actual anatomy class.

Dr. Johnson is truly one of the best professors I've had at UNC! He is very kind, understanding, and easily approachable. He genuinely wants you to succeed! With that said, the class is tough, but it is fair. Put in the work and it pays off!

Take Johnson!!!!!! Best anatomy professor here. Made me actually enjoy the content, and gave fair exams. He is a Hilarious guy who keeps you laughing throughout the lecture, and you can tell he has a true joy for the teacher. Give him a raise!!!!

Most of the class is the TA; but overall this class was really easy. Start studying the Anki about a week or two out from each exam, do the labeling exercises, online exercises, and take GRQs/PLQs seriously and you'll get an easy A. The exams were some of the easiest exams I've taken at UNC, I didnt take more than 45 minutes on any of them

Professor Johnson is ABSOLUTELY the professor you want to take Biol 252/253 with 100%. He is a great lecturer and gives exams that are solely multiple choice. Provides practice exams and tries his best to teach at a pace that gives you time to process and understand concepts. Attendance is just PollEvs. I would 1000% take a class with him again.

Professor Johnson is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC. In both 252 & 253, he breaks down difficult concepts & makes them feel clear and approachable. It's obvious that he truly cares about his students' success and puts in the effort to help us do well. He makes lectures genuinely enjoyable - I always look forward to going to his class!

Had him for 252, and I'm so glad I have him again for 253. His lectures are super well organized, he's great at explaining tough concepts, and I feel the exams are very fair. You can tell he really cares about his students and implements their feedback for the class. Plus he's a really funny guy.

I cannot express just how amazing Dr. Johnson is! By far my absolute favorite professor. He takes time to get to know his students, ensures you know the material, engages students in lecture, and genuinely loves what he does. I like his group office hours, where he has spent both group and one-on-one time with students. Take his class if you can!

BIOL252L is a tough class, but with the right study approach, you can definitely succeed. Consistent memorization and using resources like Unstuckstudy alongside the lectures and textbook make all the difference. The exams are challenging, but the TAs provide great support.

I cannot speakly highly enough of Professor Johnson. He's understanding, encouraging, and a delight for any student. He does not allow cheat sheets but his tests are noticeably easier than other professors who do permit cheat sheets. Professor Johnson is an incredibly lecturer, and just a good person in general.

Dr. Johnson is the best bio prof. I have had so far at UNC. He actually teaches the material. He also provides practice exams before each exam that are extremely comparable to the actual exams. The textbook and homework are helpful. If you attend class and study you will do well. He's also super funny.

Corey Johnson was a great professor who genuinely cared about his students. Although the lecture sizes were large, he made the class interesting. I think the tests in his class were extremely fair, which is one of the reasons I liked this class so much. Would definitely recommend taking his class over any of the other anatomy professors!
He was very understanding and helpful with grading!

Best STEM Professor I have EVER HAD at UNC. Dr. Johnson is the best; he is very understanding, and his lectures are fantastic. He always takes his time to make sure everyone understands the material. His exams are practically based on the information he discusses in the lectures. Rewatch his lectures before each exam, and study your notes!

Johnson was an amazing professor! I was scared for this course, but Johnson eased my fears. His lectures are great and he is funny, inserting jokes whenever he can. His tests are very fair, ranging from straightforward to application questions; he only tested on what he taught. Take him if you're able. I heavily recommend him for this course!

Best professor. Easy to follow and entertaining lectures are recorded, class structure is clear, homework light, tests are all multiple choice and easy. Very accessible outside of class and seems to care a lot about student success. Anatomy isn't an easy subject by nature, but he makes it really approachable.

Dr. Johnson is a great professor and would highly recommend taking a class with him! His lectures are easy to follow, and he injects a lot of humor and excitement into them. He clearly cares about his students and is fair in his expectations for class and grading. The exams are all multiple choice and are very manageable if you do the assigned HW.
He is a great professor and lecturer. You can tell he enjoyed the subject he teaches. In my opinion, he is the best professor for the anatomy and physiology course.

Dr. Johnson is a great professor and is so funny during lecture. In my opinion his tests are significantly easier than the other anatomy professors. They are super straight forward and are straight from the reading and lecture

This class really depends on your TA but Johnson gives you lots of materials to be successful. There is so much practice provided and the lectures are pretty thorough. Overall just be ready to memorize new things and you'll be fine. It's hardly the horror it's made out to be.
Dr Johnson is an entertaining lecturer and his tests are super fair. He gives lots of opportunities for practice and is easy to reach outside of class. My fav BIOL professor so far!
The goat. 253 is more focused on physiology which was nice. Exams are difficult but you can do well if you prepare. 253L was MUCH easier than 252L.

Dr. Johnson was great; I don't know why so many people complain about 252L. Yes it's hard, but you have to lock in and spend hours studying and you'll get an A because it's just memorization based. The GRQs and quizzes are all graded for completion, and the exams are super easy. It's the TAs that do most of the instruction though.

This course can be very time consuming because it requires a lot of memorization. However, there are plenty of resources that you can use to study for exams. This course is also very lecture-dependent and it's helpful if you get a TA that explains the content well.

Dr. Johnson was one of my favorite professors at UNC! The content is difficult, but he is a great lecturer and explains things well. He provides a practice exam before each exam, which is really helpful. This class is mostly physiology rather than anatomy, which was very nice. Definitely take him if you can.

Exams were taken on paper, open response, pure memorization, and the photos of the models were so poor in quality. The last 2 exams were on paper, and it was harder to see the picture than it was to recall what it actually was.

There is just SO MUCH content. Each lecture is a flood of material that you are expected to memorize. To make it worse, 50% of the questions on the exams are random application questions that are most times not even mentioned in lectures. The format of this class is lazy, making the students do all the work, an unrealistic amount of memorization.

I spent more time on this than on the actual BIOL 252 course. This is unforgiving, relentless, and extremely poorly designed for it to be a 1 credit lab. Honestly, it wouldn't be much of a problem if it didn't have the RANDOM application questions that makeup 50 questions on each exam. No teaching is done, this is purely a test of your memorization

Each exam is worth 20%, there are 2 non-cumulative exams. They consist of 50 identification open-response questions (no word bank) and 50 application questions (random and open-response). By each exam date, you should have memorized roughly 150 terms, this class only consists of memorization. The final is cumulative and 30% of your grade.

I aboslutely love Corey Johnson as a professor, I wish he taught more classes. Don't let the no cheat sheets scare you, he knows his stuff and can properly answer any question you have. Also, the exams are much easier than you'd think because of the lack of cheat sheet. Best professor I've had by far.

He is good at making things clear and posts the lectures so you can go back. The only reason I wouldn't take him again is because for both 252 & 253 the other profs allow cheat sheets and he doesn't.  Not really fair when students are all applying to med/pa/nursing school and some students had to study twice as hard without a cheat sheet
it felt like a bulldozer was crushing us each week. class was doable but at the cost of students leaving the room crying. so I guess pick your own battles.

Clear lecturer, easy exams, and provided practice exams that had questions from the real exams on them.  There were warmups and readings due before class, but it's no issue to skip the readings, as all the information on the exams comes from the lectures.  Also one of the best dressing STEM professors I've had if you care about that kind of thing

Lecture is very TA dependent, but you can learn everything on your own because exams are based off the lab manual. There are A TON of things to memorize, but there are a lot of resources they provide, like an Anki deck and practice questions, so it is doable. Nothing is really difficult to understand, just takes a long time to memorize it all.

Dr. Johnson is amazing, and I learned SO MUCH. But I feel like his section of the class was harder than the other profs. Other sections were allowed cheat sheets on exams and had a non-cumulative final, which was not the case for us. Exams were fair though. Worth the trade-off though because this was one of my favorite classes!

This is definitely a difficult class and Johnson does a good job at explaining things and doesn't mind if he needs to reexplain. Weren't many things to grade in this course. Exams are a large percentage of the grade. Attending group reviews and office hours help. Provides practice exams. He seems like a nice guy that wants to do his job well.

I honestly really enjoyed this class with Dr. Johnson. He was super accessible and friendly and his tests were super fair. As long as you put in the effort in this class you'll do fine since the textbook isn't super complicated and his tests don't include anything he doesn't talk about in class, definitely recommend Dr. Johnson's class!

Anatomy is a hard class at UNC, but if you have to take it, take it with Johnson. He was so nice and caring. His tests don't allow a cheat sheet, but I preferred that because the questions were easier.

This class is DIFFICULT but has nothing to do with Dr. Johnson. He is very knowledgeable on the content and is good at explaining. The test questions are all pulled from lecture content and are either application, basic knowledge, or a super specific detail. Taking notes during lecture is necessary because he does not annotate slides but records.

If you're taking this class, be prepared to study regularly throughout the semester. It's all memorization, so do whatever is best for you to memorize things. They give an anki set which is semi-useful for identifying different parts, so use that. You do not need to spend 10 hours a week studying... just use anki early on and read the lab manual

Take BIOL 252 with him if you can! Any anatomy class is going to be hard, but at least he made it fun, and interesting, and the test questions were straightforward for the most part. The final was a lot harder than I expected and it ended up pulling me down a letter grade, but overall at least I learned a lot in the course.

Dr. Johnson is the way to go for BIOL252. His class wasn't 'easy' but it wasn't hard. The exams were fair and represented what we had learned in class. Read the textbook beforehand (don't take that many notes) and go to the lecture and you'll be good. He was also funny af and was nice to everyone. Take him!!!

Anatomy lab is really hard. You have to commit at least 10+ hours a week if you really want a good grade. All memorization and you'll get 0 points if you use one wrong letter. They put stuff on exams that isn't in the slides and can only be found in the lab manual. Also don't rely on study resources because there are mistakes and spelling errors

I LOVE COREY JOHNSON. He is the absolute best and the only way to go for physiology. I'm sad I wont have his class next semester. Best professor everrrrrrrr!

By far, he is one of the best professors at UNC. I would highly recommend that if you is teaching 252 or 253, to take it with him. He actually cares about you as a student and wants to see you succeed! His tests are straightforward and he tests directly on what he says within his lectures (re-watching lectures is honestly the most useful tool).

Dr. Johnson is one of the best professors I've had. The exams are very fair, include material straight from all the lectures. Nothing he doesn't lecture about is on the exams. Lectures are interesting and he's pretty funny and overall a really nice guy.

Everyone seems to love his teaching style but I don't. This class is worlds harder than any class I've taken at UNC, harder than chem 101/102 for me. Lab surprisingly is way better than the lecture. I leave class more confused and the tests are ridiculous

Amazing. He is a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. He makes lots of dad jokes, it's funny to hear during lecture. His tests are very fair and if you study for the exam you'll do good because he really is just testing to see your knowledge and not to trick you like other professors. Definitely recommend!

Material is very similar to BIOL 252. Exams are fair and based entirely in what is covered in the slides. Go to office hours if possible; Dr. Johnson is super accessible and kind so if you aren't understanding something or need help, talk to him directly.

Lab was VERY hard for exams; even if you understand the material you have to be extremely specific or you will get no credit. Corey Johnson is a great professor and his material is fair. This lab is only as hard as you make it. All the materials you need for the tests are clearly given to you. Dr. Johnson was accessible outside of class and seemed like a very nice person through his emails. However, the level of difficulty in this class was ridiculous. Dr. Burch is just confused about a lot of content within the course. We ask her questions to which she says "idk." Her lectures are very dull and you never really walk away with any insight on what will be tested. Good luck!

Dr. Burch is a fair professor and makes a difficult class a bit easier than it would be with other profs. I think Dr. Burch gets too much hate for the job she did in her classes, she keeps things organized and digestible for students, I think she's' a solid professor.

Do not take this class unless you have no other choice! Avoid this class, highly unorganized especially the syllabus and assignments. Attendance is mandatory but it makes it hard when the class is so unorganized and boring. I spent 80% of the semester not knowing the purpose of taking this class. Luckily, I took this class for fun. I had 0 fun though.
Do yourself a favor and avoid her like the plague. Not worth your time or energy.

I took this class thru Burch Infectious Disease in London and it was very doable. Dr. M cares most about you enjoying the city, but still do all your work. Ann was the absolute worst professor I've had at UNC. She was very unprofessional when students asked questions and got loud with them several times. Just need to go to office hours for quizzes and for exams. Past exams are the best ways to study.

Dr. M is not as bad as everyone says. She is very caring and funny. She has a great sense of humor. She is actually very inspirational. It is not an easy class, but it is doable.

Dr. Slep is one of the most boring lecturers ever. This class is so terrible and I would not make my worst enemy take it. Tests are extremely difficult and if you think they get better after the first exam you are telling yourself one huge lie. DO NOT TAKE.

Took w/ Slep + Roger, regret it, only option that sem, lectures useless, doesn't show up to his own office hours, even TA didn't know how to help, exams 80%, expected to have orgo and biochem background, flop on one test? no chance for grade to recover. DO NOT TAKE

Do not take Biol 240 with Slep & Rogers. Exams are worth 80% (4 exams- 20% each) and quizzes are worth 20%. Focuses on things in class that are not on the exams.

Dr. Slep (paired with Dr. Stephen Rogers) are the two best professors I've had at UNC. Whoever wrote "How to study: I do not know" is correct. Practice exams were nothing like actual ones. Professor Slep genuinely tries to promote class engagement. He is kind and is willing to answer any questions about course material. His lecture slides and teaching style are easy to follow and he tells jokes throughout lecture! Overall, I think his test questions are fair.

I've never written a review EVER, but I have to after this recent exam. Huge information overload! You must learn way too much quickly (each unit covers a semester of information in a month). Note: I took 240 with garland but sat in on Sleps lectures and he literally teaches CHEM430 lite. The textbook for 240 does not help. Go to Dr. Hogans office hours for help, this is not cell biology, this is biochemistry.

Pros: A jokester at times. Overall nice guy.

How to study: I do not know

i understand kevin may be your only option to take biol 240 but i will just say be prepared to be taught by monotone dr. evil. speaker's notes on the ppts are the only help you will get. final isnt cumulative and that is the only good thing. hidden cost of this class: the chegg subscription you will inevitably get.

Don't get me wrong, professor Slep is VERY kind.

HOWEVER, when my doctor asks why my blood pressure is so high at my age, I'm going to tell them that it's because of this class. There was WAY too much content to memorize and at such a high specificity, and the exams were a brutal reminder that no matter how much you studied, it was never enough.

Prof. Slep's lectures are kinda boring, but he teaches the material in a pretty comprehensible way. The exams are lecture heavy, so definitely pay attention in class (even though participation didn't count towards any of our grade).

Professor Slep is very lecture-heavy, he just went off the slides for a lot of the lectures which made the class boring but he did engage with the class more than Professor Rogers (they taught the class together). I recommend reading his speaker notes and going to the review sessions held by the TAs. Exams were worth 80% of your grade so beware.

He was the worst professor I have ever had at UNC. My grade was .04 away from the next letter grade, and he wouldn't change a thing even though I felt I deserved credit in the class other places as well. Take any other professor besides Slep. Also, be prepared to fall asleep in class.
Okay I feel bad for falling sleep in Slep's lecture but truly they are just not very exciting. Yet, he really tries. A for effort.

Dr. Slep is a very intelligent professor who really knows what he's saying, and although some people are saying his lectures are boring, I didn't find them boring at all. He was a fair professor, and his lectures were very clear and understandable.

Dr. Slep is a very intelligent man, and that came across very well in his lectures. He taught the second half of this class, and while his lectures were pretty long and he was often monotonous, they had very valuable information and matched up very well with the tests. His exam questions are quite complex, but doable if you look over the lectures.

Dr. Slep taught the second half of 202 and although he gets a bad rep I really enjoyed him, he is a bit monotone but he does his best to make the class enjoyable and funny. The tests are pretty straightforward if you study well. The slides he posts after class have extra explanations and are VERYYY helpful for the exams

The class I took with Dr. Slep was team taught with Dr. Ott, and while his lecture style is different from hers, I think he's much better at explaining the basic concepts and pacing the difficulty of the practice in lecture. His tests are very fair and if you practice what you learn in class you'll do well.

Professor Matute is not a proficient lecturer and is quite disrespectful. I did very well in this class, with 100's on both midterms and an A+ on the exam. I am pretty well vetted in the topics of this course, and I would never take Professor Matute again. He is very unenjoyable. The class is great, though, and I would recommend it, just beware.

His lecture slides do not include anything except pictures so ensure that you do not miss his lectures. He goes into a lot of depth and has you read a lot of biology jargon filled articles just to ask questions like 'what is population genetics?'. So definitely pay attention when he lectures. Be sure to get general ideas and you'll be fine!

Oh hell nah. When he taught his part in IDST 113, I was so confused, and his slides are basically pictures and graphs, which did not help anyone study for exams. Pier and Terry were chill and gave insight on exams and what they covered, but Matute did NOT. He was super strict during test-taking and was sort of rude.

In IDST 113, his slides made no sense and his exam questions were hard for no reason. He was also extremely rude to students on exam day and talked to them like they were kids. When the two other professors attempted to prep the class for the final, he gave no assistance on the bio section, which is always the hardest part. Would not take him again

Matute was kind but I wouldn't recommend for IDST113 unless prepared for long readings, confusing graphs, and random lectures. Some of it was fun and If you pay attention and do the readings it's not hard to get a good grade plus he does post the lecture slides (but they don't contain much information so they honestly aren't helpful for studying).

Hands down the best course I've ever taken! I loved the way he sets up class. Every day we would have a topic and have two students give low-stakes presentations on two of the most important papers within that topic. It was such an inviting atmosphere because he genuinely wanted everyone to participate and ask questions. Learned a lot and had fun!

Dr. Matute is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. He is knowledgeable in his field of study and genuinely cares about the topic. He also genuinely cares about his students and helps them to succeed. Take a special topics, small, discussion-based class with him!! The reviews in the triple I, large lectures do not do him justice.

Dr. Matute's score is artificially low because of the triple I. His 490 course is the most engaged in a science class I've ever been. Very chill layout where students present papers and we discuss as a class. I didn't think I'd care much for evolutionary bio but he changed that. So kind & is rooting for your success. I would 10000% take him again.

Dr. Matute is such a kind and considerate man. He truly cares about his students. Yes, his accent can be hard to understand at times but that is absolutely the only negative comment I could ever consider leaving about him. He is extremely intelligent in his field and ties in humor to every lecture. Our whole class loved him!

Best professor and best class I have ever taken at UNC. The accent is hard so he gets a lot of bad reviews from the big lectures but he knows that and he is more than happy to repeat anything! He genuinely wants what is best for his students. Every conversation I have had with him you can see how much he cares and how intelligent he is.

This is the first review I have ever left because I saw how low his rating was and felt it was totally undeserved. His IDST class does not show what he is actually like as a professor. Matute strongly cares about and respects his students. His class has been so enjoyable and I would 100% take another class with him.

Such a goat. Light hearted and such an easy way to make a connection with. Presses on ideas that he thinks you know but doesn't go too far. One of the best professors I've had at Chapel Hill. So knowledgeable in his domain and he is open minded when he doesn't know. Great man.

I took Evolutionary Genetics this summer with Matute while studying abroad, and he was easily one of the best professors I have had in college thus far. He converses with students like colleagues, and fosters intellectual curiosity & engagement. He teaches you how to dissect a scientific paper and challenge everything you read. Great class!

Matute is hard to understand, gave confusing lectures, and was often dismissive/rude to students. The exams in the class are very multiple choice heavy with very specific/difficult questions so it takes a lot of studying to eek out an A. Other IDSTs def easier

Professor Matute was the worst of the three professors in IDST113. It was always hard to understand the takeaways of his lectures as they felt like a mishmash of ideas related to genetics which he then tied to race. His slideshows embody his disorganized teaching style. Don't bother doing any of his long readings because they don't help.

Gives very heavy lectures, with slideshows that are for his own benefit, not yours. It gives you a look into the "college" lecture style, but it was just kind of unnecessary. Somewhat rude to students who asked questions about exams. Has a very heavy accent, so it was sometimes difficult to fully understand what he was saying. VERY FUNNY THO

This is a disorganized class and the modules don't come together. Matute at least treated us like college students and not kids. Genetics is cool and he knows his field. No tolerance for people on the phone tho
Weird class. Guy acts like he doesn't care but when I emailed him about some issues, he followed up and help me out a lot. Attendance is not mandatory but if you attend class the exams are easy.

Matute created lecture slides with only a few photos + barely words, which made studying for the exams difficult. In exam review sessions, he'd solely tell us to go through the readings (which barely followed the premise of his lectures + were each 45+ pages) and gave no further info. I didn't skip a single lecture + still found him challenging.

You can't miss a lecture and there are like six grades total for this course and he does not make it any easier. Long readings that don't connect to the class and the slides that are available literally have no words on them and are pictures. If you take this class do not miss this dudes lectures.

I have never felt less seen by a professor in my entire life, not only did Matute constantly degrade students it is very obvious that he does not care about actually conveying information but more telling you that he is qualified I have never had the displeasure of "learning" under someone so unprofessional before.
He doesn't explain things, but he is really funny. The class grade is determined by 4 things, the midterm, the final, the essay, and 3 discussion posts.

Matute's lectures were pretty pointless but entertaining sometimes. He's definitely charismatic but the class isn't hard. I would just say his lecture slides are pretty pointless because they're just pictures. You can definitely get by without doing the readings and there's barely any homework -- just 3 graded discussion posts and one longer essay.

Doesn't teach, slides are awful. FULL of random, unrelated AI-generated images "for him". Would assign the longest, densest readings, then never talk about them. Asked about what an acronym from his readings meant. Boosted ego. Even if you go to his lectures and write exactly what he said, there's a good chance nothing will make sense. Good luck!

I'm still not entirely sure what his lectures' point was. He would preach about multiple things during a lecture and then they would never show up on the exam, he would also have students argue a point and then respond to their point by saying "I don't care".

Matute was the worst idst113 professor. The class would have been bearable if he wasn't one of the professors. He did nothing to make the class easier, assigned dense readings, and his lectures didn't even connect to the readings. His test questions were very particular and unclear.

Out of the three professors, he was my least favorite. He was okay but sometimes was short with students and didn't make lecture info accessible if you missed class. The class did only reading homework and 3 discussions. The lectures were often boring for all teachers. Make sure to take good notes in class because they're essential for the exam.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS and especially with this professor. Matute is mean, disrespectful, very unclear, and it's hard to understand him. This class is so disorganized no one knows what the final and midterm material will be on. Save yourself and take a different IDST.

Don's take course with him! Just don't. Heavy Spanish accent, English understandable only for native English speakers.
Not respectful. I don't want to say profanity words, but good luck taking his course.
Useless materials. Luckily he decide to test general questions for final, or I'll write a letter to complain about his unrelated midterm MCQs.

Dr.Matute is very knowledgeable about genomics in biology, however, in the Triple-I format, I found it difficult to connect his topic with the other professors. The readings he would give out did not seem to conform to his lectures which left me confused on what I was supposed to be taking away from them.

Matute assigned long readings for his portion of IDST113 that got pretty confusing without any prior knowledge of biology. He's a really interesting lecturer and I would love to just listen to him talk, but his teaching style doesn't translate to the triple-I curriculum and made the class unnecessarily difficult. Don't take this class.
While the class was fine, I found Matute to be very rude in his interactions with students, and gave students no real material or structure to help them learn.

Matute was a really great lecturer and made the topics really entertaining. His tolerance for students not doing what they're supposed to is definitely lower, and he will shut down an activity if he sees people misusing the time. No need to be afraid of him though.

Professor Matute is passionate about his work and works hard to engage students with the material. That being said he is rude to students. Even forcefully shoving through rows of students and shouting at students during our final, needlessly spending lectures cold calling students, and fighting against test feedback after asking for it.

An incredibly immature professor. While hopefully he is a more reachable and engaging professor in his smaller courses, Matute was unreasonable, irrational, and showed no empathy for his students. Extremely discracting- screamed at a kid mid final and crawled over full row of students. Refused to listen and fought back when given feedback.

He would just sit at the front of the room and tell random people to answer his questions about a 70-page reading due that day. He also refused to use a mic and so it was impossible to hear/understand him. That being said, he is very passionate about what he does but I don't think it translated well to this course

Take home exams- as long as you go to office hours, he will help you get an A on all of them. As long as you participate in class every so often, you will do fine. Definitely a bias grader, helps if he likes you and you seem interested. Going to office hours is enough to get an A in the class.
Absolutely horrible. Worst class I've taken at UNC
Super smart professor and challenges the way you should think and approach problems. Take home exams were tricky, but going to office hours helps.
Very smart researcher. Absolutely horrible professor. Doesn't give feedback. Doesn't teach anything. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET.
Do not take this class with this professor, whatever you do do not take this class. Exams are hard and are overly graded. This class is worse than Orgo.

Though the seminar itself is hard (advanced biology, genetics) the class is very manageable. Grades mostly come from take home exams and participation. Attend class, come to his office hours with exam questions and you'll be just fine. He just wants people to be interested in what he's so passionate about.

The MTs and finals are open note, collaborative, and Prof Bloom will help you out if you go to office hours. His main thing is that you show up to class (he doesn't take attendance, but he notices who is there), ask questions, and pay attention.

I had Dr. Bloom for Biol59 - A FYS about Genetics. It was unnecessarily hard, we barely had any information on how to do well on the exams and were graded so harshly on topics meant for advanced molecular biology students. I learned a lot from this class, but if you're looking for an easy seminar without background knowledge, STAY AWAY!

Kerry is a very passionate teacher and knows so much about what he teaches. The class grade is very heavily weighted toward the take-home exams, but he is very willing to help you out if you go to office hours or work in groups. He does pay attention to who is in class, so participation is pretty important.

Professor Bloom is truly incredible and his passion for science is clear in the classroom. Throughout the semester the class requires students to lead to presentations. Your grade is composed of very few things but exams are all take home and collaborative. Professor Bloom is also accessible for exam questions during office hours!

It is a genuinely interesting FYS to take. Dr Bloom maintains a good balance between lecturing and student participating in his classes. 3 take home exams and participation were the only things which were graded for. The exams were questions which you could discuss and encourage you to think and apply knowledge. Would recommend.

The expectations for assignments are never clear and it felt like we were expected to read his mind. He was unable to explain things in terms that we could understand. The syllabus was a  lie and Dr. Bloom was incredibly disorganized.  Unless you have prior knowledge of molecular biology, I would not recommend this class.

Do not take this class if you have no pre-existing knowledge of biology. Dr. Bloom is incredibly unorganized and he is very unclear about what is graded in the class. There are very few things graded and the syllabus he provided is complete lies. If you want a challenge take this class you will learn a lot but be ready for some BS.

Dr. Bloom was a very understanding and caring professor. It is very apparent that he cares about the material and his students, wanting them to learn and be able to think on what was learned. Exams were collaborative and critical thinking about real world circumstances was facilitated. I hold him in high regards.

Dr. Bloom is genuinely one of the kindest souls at UNC. The midterms were take home and consisted of 4 challenge questions. He encouraged students to go to his office hours and consult each other. He curated such a collaborative learning environment that challenged students to think critically about the implications and applications of genetics.

I am unsure why Dr. Sockman has bad ratings- he is literally one of my favorite professors in the biology department. Did he go on a lot of tangents? Yes. Were they hilarious? Yes. The class material is super interesting and the quizzes are easy they're literally online. Don't get the textbook, just write down everything he says. Curve is HUGE.

Took Avian Bio in Maymester. Dr. Sockman is passionate and wants active participation (heavily weighted). Tests are lecture-based with a curve, but he grades tough. Slides are vague, so note-taking is key. Textbook not needed. Loved his experimental design teaching style. Class is a bit unorganized but very engaging.
His exams are really hard but he curves. However I enjoyed his class a lot mainly because I enjoyed the content he taught and his awkward jokes are funny.

He makes lectures worth going to, he is really funny and makes the subject fun. You really should take notes during lectures bc thats what the tests are based on. But also the book helps alot, he also gives videos on canvas covering stuff from that lecture. The tests are curved huge! all open ended questions and memory based. Quizzes r quick n easy

The quizzes are very easy, but they are quick. Its really just finding correct phylogeny trees with the groups names he gives you. If you look at the book the night before and draw the tree out it will be the easiest thing you have ever done.
Funny guy and makes lectures so interesting.
The best bio class ever taken.
Tests were all memory based

From my experience with Dr. Sockman, I would advise anyone who wants to take a class with him to be careful and, if possible, look for another course. The professor is very condescending towards students. The content itself was interesting, but having him as a teacher was horrible. If you take this course, your best friend is the required textbook.

This was a hard class, but it prepared me for med school. I am a current M1 and his teaching style, pace, and the lab were all similar to my current classes. He taught me more than any other professor at UNC. If you want to do well: study earlier, write down everything he says in lecture, study in groups. Reading the textbook also helps orient you.
He can be disrespectful and harsh against students. He was also tone deaf about certain sensitive topics.
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

I took this over summer so the structure was different, our exams were on lecture material and all the textbook, versus only lecture during the year. 

Pro: structured class so you know what's due.

Cons: Grading system is harsh so you never know your score leaving an exam. I felt better on midterm 2 but because of the curve did better on final.

I completed the Maymester BIOL 476 course (Avian Biology) and Dr. Sockman was ok. His tests were fair given that they followed lectures, however you have to take good detailed notes to do well. No one understands how he grades participation, everyone in my maymester course participated A LOT everyday, yet he made the avg a low 80, worth 20%.

Just finished Bio 476, Avian Bio, in a Maymester summer session. The textbook was useless in this course and there were no resources to help study outside of the class beyond peers and his slides, which had little text on them. He was not responsive to emails and would frequently mention a curve which was not installed by the end of the course.

This class was challenging but worth it. Very interesting content and I found Dr. Sockman's lectures to be engaging and memorable. He obviously cares a lot about the subject. His grading policies were tough but fair, but he communicated his standards clearly, which was nice. Read the textbook and pay attention in lecture and you'll do okay.

Love Dr. Willet, he is sooo incredibly kind and willing to work with you! However, grades are extremely test-heavy, and the tests are worded vaguely. Boring lectures :(. Class was harder than it had to be, and exams didn't reflect lessons. Beware: he input grades the day of the final exam for me (B to C+ in one hour).

Lectures make it very difficult to not only learn the material, but also to stay interested in the course and go to class. Cheat sheets were allowed on exams however exam questions were worded very vaguely making it not what you know but more of a test on how good you can interpret what he is attempting to convey/ask. Take 260/240 instead.

He was a sweet professor, but could not teach. The content itself is super boring, and the lectures did not help. Exams were difficult, but could use cheat sheets. Did not enjoy the class. Honestly, wouldn't recommend this class.

Willett is a good guy but unc bio is just a pain. you miss two questions on exams and youre already at a 90. Records all his lectures and always available on email to answer question. Exams are more like reading comprehension tests. Cheat sheets allowed

I literally wanted to be an evolutionary biologist but Willett was just sooo boring and not engaging that I felt turned away from the field. his lectures are about random studies and i never understood the purpose of his tangents. i literally couldnt take notes bc he was all over the place so i stopped attending class. snooze fest!

Girl...this class was soooooo boring. If you want the class to be engaged, you need to be an engaging professor. He has also provided no guidelines on the types of questions that will appear on the final (worth 20%), and he has yet to grade...anything...so I don't even know where I am standing. By far one of the worst classes I have taken at UNC.

He obviously knew his stuff, but was not great at explaining much. I found the examples to be helpful if you actually understood the concept he was talking about, but most of the time he would just start explaining a paper with no information on what we should actually take away from it.

Very interesting content and Dr. Willett uses a lot of case studies, papers, and real examples to march through the content. But I agree that this class is test heavy, and he does not drop or down-weight any of his exams, although he allows the use of cheat sheets. Two midterms each worth 19% and a final that is worth 28%

Midterm 1 median was 77, Midterm 2 median was 74. Attendance taken through poll everywhere. Prof Willett was flexible, he is available outside of class and uploads recordings of all lectures. Exam medians surprising, cheat sheet allowed, all exam questions are based off of lectures. I didn't read, just went to lecture and made cheat sheets.

Like the content and Dr. Willett is very knowledgeable about the topic, but his tests, which make up a large part of the grade, are designed horribly. Tries to trick you on test questions, questions don't align with practice exams, and never any partial credit. Test grades do not reflect knowledge of content. Studied more than for chem and got a C.

Willett is a good guy. He might not explain concepts the best during lecture but he's always available after class and during office hours. The class is super interesting and it's clear he enjoys evolutionary biology. Test heavy but go to review sessions and you'll be fine.

The half-semester research project was the main portion of the grade with a paper and a poster being made with your group. There was one midterm based on the weekly readings and in-class lectures but it was fairly easy if you paid attention in class. We did have to use Rstudio but it wasn't taught very well and was kinda confusing but it was doable
i know people didnt like him but i thought he was cool. had his unique interests and was a little quirky. he just isn't good at answering questions during class lol. he def belongs in the field
