Knows his stuff, but he's kinda boring and doesn't explain things well. I taught myself a lot of the content, the textbook and slides are more helpful than the lecture. Tests are math and memorization heavy (especially important terms!), use your cheat sheet for that.

Boring. Monotonous. Not engaging. Don't take 201 with him if you have another professor. Clearly is forced to take the course because of his knowledge from his lab. Doesn't care about students really, patronizing as well.

He is not good at (and not willing to) explaining things so be ready for teaching yourself. Textbook is useful, take it as a supplementary resource but focus on the lecture slides. Allows cheatsheet which makes your life much easier.

Dr. Willet is passionate about evolution, but lectures could go off-topic and have the class fall behind before the midterms. The lectures were interactive, which was nice, but some of the mathier concepts were a little unclear after class. Recitation, the GRQs, and the Peer Mentor sessions were helpful, though!

The evolution half of BIOL 201 was boring for me personally, Prof Willett didn't make it very engaging compared to ecology. Overall, it's pretty easy just be sure to attend recitation and pay attention to the math.
He's not a bad professor, a little boring but he knows what he's doing. The only issue I have is sometimes he doesn't know the answers to the questions students ask.

It is clear in his lectures that he is not a teaching professor. Im sure his research and experience in that field is great, but his lectures were so unorganized, ambiguous, and downright lacking. He will say large words and list concepts but never explicitly explain them, yet turn around and test you on them like you are an expert.

I loved this class with Dr. Willett. He is an awesome teacher who is happy to answer questions students have. He does require some work to be put in but this just involves reading the textbook. Some students are putting in bad reviews since they probably aren't reading but all of the exam questions are straightforward and come from the textbook.

Dr. Willett is a really nice guy who is passionate about what he does! However, he does not teach well. His lectures are unorganized, and while the content isn't too hard I just feel like I haven't learned anything through his teaching because of how chaotic it is. Just be wary before registering for a class of his!
Get your grade up before he switches with Dr. Maddox. He is an amazing teacher. I wish he taught the entire seciton.

Dr. Goldstein is one of the best professors I've had. His exams are almost all lecture content, but he explains it well if you pay attention/ take notes. Grades are 100% exams, but the median for our 1st exam was a 98. He truly cares and makes class fun. If he is co-teaching with Dr. Maddox, keep your grades as high as possible before her section.

Dr. Goldstein is probably my favorite professor I've had in UNC biology. His lectures are engaging and interesting if you're really there because you want to learn cell bio, and his tests are fair (if you take the practice exam and attend the review session, you'll do well.) It's a shame that he co-teaches the course with Dr. Maddox (AVOID HER)

He really cared about students and had several opportunities for students to ask questions and feel prepared. His practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams and he lectures in a way that feels like a story and makes things easy to retain. Got hundreds on both his exams!

Dr. Goldstein cares a lot about his students, evident by the time he puts in for the class. You must go to class to get a good grade, and grades are only based on tests, but his tests are very fair. Dr. Goldstein is a very good lecturer which makes the information much easier to retain than in some other bio classes.

Bob truly cared about his students. He included interactive days to keep us engaged and held VERY helpful review sessions in preparation for exams. He tells funny jokes and interesting stories during lecture. He was helpful during office hours and is overall a great person. If you have the opportunity to take this class with him do not hesitate.

Professor Goldstein cares a lot about the subject and his students. His half of the course is entirely made up of two exams, but questions are straightforward. He makes it clear what you should know and there are no curveballs. If you keep on top of the reading the pace of the class is very manageable. I would take him again if I could. Great guy!

Prof. Goldstein is a gem.  He offered review sessions outside of class before exams and stayed as late as students had questions.  His section of the course is 100% exams, but exams were very fair and he doesn't try to trick you like other bio profs do.  Extra credit offered and genuinely cares about student well-being and learning.

Prof. Goldstein is one of the most fun and informative bio professors there is. He indulges curiosity and celebrates questions and learning! His section of the class is graded just on 2 tests, which he grades very fairly and offers extra credit. He really made this class fun and I hope to take a class with him again!

Dr. Goldstein is the GOAT. What I love most about him is that he emphasizes learning for the sake of curiosity. He even had interactive days where we would do hands-on activities rather than listen to a lecture. Truly an incredible professor who is knowledgeable in his field. Textbook supplements lectures, and exams are fairly straightforward.
I will return in Avengers: Doomsday

This class almost took me out. It was the worst class I have ever taken and lectures did nothing for me. The tests were awfully worded and made to be confusing. The TA does not even really understand most subjects and it is extremely difficult to learn anything. If you have any dignity or self value you will not take this.

Dr. Rogers seems nice but he cannot get a sentence out to save his life. Class is purely lecture-based and is a non-stop snooze fest. Exams are weirdly worded and get progressively harder. They also act as though it is their first time working with canvas (or ever functioning in modern society). Take it with anyone else if you want peace.

Class was 80% exams, and Dr. Rogers just read off the slides. Difficult exams with convoluted questions. He was nice, but his teaching was not interactive and most of his lectures were very dense. Avoid this class if you can.

Dr Rogers is one of the most intellectual professors here. Loved taking this class with him, he really knows his material and his passion shows when he teaches. Spent just a bit during office hours with him during finals season and you can tell how much he cares about his students- he's willing to go way above and beyond. Take the class with him!!

Dr. Rogers (paired with Dr. Kevin Slep) are two of the best professors I've had at CH. Each professor is so knowledgeable and clearly care about students having positive experiences in the biology department. If you have a chance to take 447L with Dr. Rogers and Slep, please do. I haven't had a class like 447L. 10/10 course, 10/10 professors.

In his lectures, Dr. Roger would basically read off the slides. It seemed like he was not prepared for them and treated it as a review for himself more than for us to learn.. The slides did not have enough info to prepare me for exams, and the practice exams were nothing like them. The TA was not helpful as she could never answer anyone's questions

Rogers seems like a nice guy. But he is not a great lecturer. Or a great test giver. For our final we were given 8 practice problems that only pertained to one section of the material and 2 of the answers ended up being wrong. Rogers had to correct himself twice on one of them. Unnecessarily complicated class.

Pros: Nice, Exams are fair, compared to Slep... this guy is goated
Cons: Lectures were insanely boring and I love biology. The grade scale also sucks because its 80% exams and 20% quizzes 
How to Study: Never figured it out

dr rogers has the apologetic air of a field mouse entering a snake's nest. he is nice but not engaging or enthusiastic whatsoever. i will say that if you take this class w him and slep, his test questions are MUCH easier. he actually tries to be nice to students, even if he isnt the best lecturer. 20% each test (4) and 20% quizzes (18).
Prof. Rogers teaches the material well, but his lectures are not all that engaging. The exams are lecture-heavy, so definitely pay attention in class.

Professor Rogers is very lecture-heavy, he tends to just read off the slides instead of engaging with the class which made the class boring. I recommend reading his speaker notes and going to the review sessions held by the TAs which those will help more, and the workload was not bad.
Dr. Kieber is a legend and signal transduction was the most useful course I have taken in this university.

He is a great person, but the lectures were way too fast and contained little information related to exams. It was very hard to study using materials given. Class was extremely challenging and the grade was completely from exams. Hard to succeed when there is little outreach/homework/class materials. Sweet guy just not the best teacher.

Class is 90% exams. He moves way too fast, and his powerpoints have basically nothing but diagrams on them. He asked very specific questions on exams, which were very tricky and confusing. In office hours, he was condescending at times. Regretted taking him the whole semester.

this class was really, really hard and ive heard from grad students that we were being taught at an above-mcat level. with that said, professor kieber was one of the nicest and most understanding stem professors ive had at unc. he knew that it was an honors class and made it hard because of that, but he also curved the grade up to reflect that.

Idk why his rating is so high tbh. Lectures are scattered and moves too fast so its hard to take notes on everything you need to know. Tests are too long and written to confuse you, with answer choices like "all of the above" and "two of the above" tagged on the end of mcqs, SAQs, that he grades like you broke into his home and stole his valuables.

For 220H. One of the smartest and nicest teachers I have ever had. Difficult class but genuinely enjoyed coming to his lectures and hearing what he had to say. Talks fast but is more than happy to go back and go over content again. Only issue I had was that he is hard to reach outside of class as his office hours were rare and at difficult times.

Kieber was a chill guy w/ dad humor and the content was very interesting. No homework outside of class so exams were purely based on lectures which are sometimes fast-paced. However he'll repeat things if you ask him too. Content was difficult but manageable. All exams were free response, but he frequently mentions during lecture what he'll test on
Lectures are all over the place and hard to follow. There are no textbooks only based off powerpoint. Does not put anything in the grade book for you to know why you got xyz grade.
Great professor! Take him!

My favorite professor so far at UNC. His exam was so easy and was straight from the study guide. His lectures were interesting and he sometimes brought his dog to class. This course is taught with two other professors and he by far was the easiest one.

This is one of the best professor's I have ever had, he really cares about his students and is very passionate and knowledgeable about this course and topics. Definitely take this class, very easy and super interesting.

One of the best professor ever met! He really supports and wants student to learn how to do research and understand sustainability related topics. Grade is not a concern for this class (he's grading fairly and  leniently) but understanding science & research is the goal.

Dr. Bruno was an amazing lecturer, and super kind! The questions in our quizzes from his lecturers were often difficult, so make sure you take detailed notes on some of the exact numbers discussed in class. He has a really cute dog he brought to class as well! Super cool dude!

Dr. Bruno was by far my favorite lecturer on the FoF teaching team. His lectures were insightful and easy to follow, and he always brings his dog Mr. Lizard to class when he teaches. He gives an in-depth synopsis of the fishing industry and the fraud within it. He is also accessible outside of class and offers advice who show the initiative to ask.

Dr. Bruno was the best professor in FoF. He made lectures very interesting and was always knowledgable on what he was doing. Hes funny and is always very kind to the students. FoF as a class wasn't too hard but the quizzes were very detailed so I reccommend at least reviewing before. Everything else was graded easily, including the final paper.

Dr. Bruno is one of 3 professors in FoF. His passion for his field of research reassures me that there are people out there who care for our planet. You must take notes during lectures to do well on the 3 quizzes. There's a simple semester-long group project and final paper. Attendance not taken, but lectures aren't posted.
BIOL 221 was an amazing class. The TAs were great and so was the Professor. I genuinly enjoyed going to this class and it tought me a lot about research.
Professor Bruno was the best part of the future of food. The quizzes were difficult, but he made the lectures very interesting. He also always brought his dog to class, which was fun!

Prof Bruno was the best part of the future of food. While this class was challenging at times (mainly quizzes, but if you study and mostly pay attention in class you'll be ok), He was super funny and actually cares about what he is teaching, and wants students feedback and participation. Super cool dude, and brings his dog which is a huge plus.

idst 130 future of food was the worst class ever. they teach super basic things that are honeslty common sense and say we don't need to memorize anything. then its quiz day and the quizzes are based solely on important dates and specific policies that we were supposed to memorize. the group projects are a waste of time. no practice for quizzes.

Future of Foods was my triple I and Dr. Bruno was the best Professor out of the three. The class itself doesn't have any exams and your grade is determined by a few essays and in class assignments. Grading is done by TA's but mine was very nice and gave good feedback. If you put any effort and go to class at least half the time you will get an A.

This is a review for IDST 130 Futures of Food. Please do not take the class, super boring and the structure is awful. Dr. Buno is the only saving grace. Super cool guy plus he brought his dog to class regularly.

A knowledgeable and approachable professor who pushes you when she knows you're capable, which I value. She truly wants the best for her students and treats them accordingly. Beyond being an excellent professor, she's a remarkable woman you can learn a great deal from.

I took Dr. Gordon over the summer abroad. She is such a wonderful, knowledgeable and caring professor and I can't recommend her enough. The class was a series of paper presentations by the students, and sometimes she would lecture afterwards more in-depth about the topic. Every paper was fascinating and the workload very reasonable.

This course was a refreshing break from 200-level classes. Dr. Gordon is understanding and a fair grader. The class focuses on stem cell papers, with online, open-note tests that are straightforward if you keep up. Be ready to present, as one group presents each week. Also participation is 30% of your grade.

Dr. Gordon is one of the smartest, most kind professors I've had here. She genuinely cares for her students' well-being. Her lectures are amazing because she explains tough concepts in ways that are easy to comprehend and comes up with great analogies. Her exams are challenging, but they are fair and she is generous with partial credit.

Gordon is amazing and so enthusiastic about what she's teaching. This class is definitely challenging, but she is very pleasant to work with and will take time to explain difficult concepts if you ask. The tests were all on the long scientific papers and could be quite difficult. Overall, I would recommend Gordon!

Dr. Gordon is amazing! She's really sweet and incredibly smart and will go out of her way to explain a topic that is a bit challenging with demonstrations until it is understood. Class is not graded by much except few quizzes and midterms which are very straightforward if you understand the material, also no cumulative test. 100% recommend her!

Absolutely loved Dr. Gordon. Most exam questions were choose all that apply kind of questions, so that was a little more difficult. However, Dr. Gordon prepared us super well with lectures filled with demonstrations and props. You could tell she really was there for us to learn. Super knowledgeable! I would take any of her classes in the future!!
Gordon is passionate, it's obvious. She tells you to focus on the big picture. This is a big conceptual class and can be tricky but she does a good job simplifying the topics.

You'll get out of this class what you put in, so engaging in discussions, asking questions, and keeping up with the work will result in a comprehensive understanding of the subject matter. Dr. Burmeister is very fair and interesting to listen to. She asks challenging questions in class, but it's all to help you learn. Favorite class in my 4 years!

I am literally crying as I study for my midterm a couple of hours from now I have not slept. Amazing class, great content, great professor, REALLY challenging. dont take if youre juggling other stem classes, I might fail..

Her teaching style is very rough, especially for it to be covering a first year seminar. She is very vague in her lectures and the tests are very difficult. The lecture slides only cover the rough aspect of what you will see on your tests. She's also very difficult to communicate with, even came off as quite rude when communicating through email.

For a first-year seminar, this class was extremely difficult. She is unclear with instructions and barely gives rubrics, so you must go to office hours for clarification. Tests are extremely hard, but she offered test corrections which greatly helped. You can do well if you go to office hours and put in effort, but I don't recommend this class.

Dr. Burmeister was not helpful throughout the rest of the course She grades things at the last possible minute, does not provide insightful instructions, and also does not record her lectures. When questions were asked in class she was very condescending to students and was not effective in office hours.

Dr. Burmeister is a really smart prof and the class content is really cool. There is a textbook which you can use as reference as almost all the lecture content is based off of. There are pop quizzes every couple classes that can be quite challenging, but if you complete the assigned reading before the class then it should not be too difficult.

I was skeptical taking this class given the RMP. It was hard (which is expected for a 400's level biology class at UNC) but it's definitely doable. The setup of this class has been my favorite of all bio classes at UNC so far. There are 5 exams but each are worth 10% so unlike other classes it wasn't detrimental to your grade if you did bad on one.

Worst class I have taken at UNC. Hard to not fall asleep, she does not care to explain her though process when drawing figures on the board. Her exams were incredibly hard and partial credit was not consistent between peers. You and your peer may have the same answer but you will not receive the same amount of points for whatever reason

Loved the material for this class but there were several tests that relied heavily on being able to turn material we covered in class into graphs/images and it was hard to do that as a non-visual person. Wish there was more flexibility there. Slow replier to emails and it's impossible to pass without attending class in person

This is an interesting class for sure. I loved the lectures and course material, but when it came to tests, I still don't know the best way I could have studied. It was impossible to say something exactly the way she wanted it. Best advice: don't overstudy, memorize the main ideas. Course structure: 5 exams, lots of GRQs/reading quizzes.
Lab class. He was very knowledgeable & was good at explaining things. Recommend!

This lab is super chill. All the assignments are very quick. It's easy to get lost trying to understand the content but they guide us through everything. I don't think about this class other than when I am actually there

Great guy! We did some group projects and he was definitely on top of things throughout the semester, prepared. If you aren't interested in the subject matter, don't take the class, but if you are it's a fun time.

Super interesting content but lectures were a bit boring. He was accessible for meetings and was very helpful in answering questions about the content. Two group presentations but no rubric, however I assume were graded easily. Exams test heavily on conceptual thinking. I would recommend taking if you have an interest in biotechnology!
Great professor, learned a lot. Nice guy and clearly knowledgeable.

Professor Reed is very smart and a kind professor. Yes, the content is boring but I also expected that going in. He does the first couple lectures then it switches to students doing them (one of your three grades). Biggest problem was his final exam was nothing like what he told us to expect, he had us study general stuff then tested on specifics.
Dr reed is super sweet and passionate about what he teaches but if you are not very interested in plant nodulation I would not take this seminar. It was very boring but it has been easy.
Great professor, clearly very knowledgeable and I had a lot of fun in his class. Learned a lot.

Interesting subject and relevant curriculum, but way too heavy courseload. Assigned 2-3 heavy articles every week and group projects which were graded harshly and indiscriminately of who you were partnered up with. Class is open for grad students for some reason, which skews curving so that most people are likely to get a bad grade from this class.

Prof Reed is a kind person but I did not enjoy his class. The lectures were boring and monotonous. The content was interesting but the grading criteria was not clear at all. The tests were extremely difficult. We did not have a single grade in the grade book until the final grade. Personally would not recommend unless you are a biology genius.

Me, loving animal's wanted to take this class and even after reading the bad rate my professor reviews on her exams I still took it. One of the biggest mistakes I have ever made. The information itself is fairly simple but her exams are quite literally the definition of unjust.I had a 75 by the time of the final, somehow clutched. Don't take.

Instead of taking the bus to get to class, I should gotten UNDER the bus. 

Exams are ~80% of grade, so many studies, exams/quizzes meant to trick you (A + B only, only C, all choices). Test 1 average was 60. Very kind lady so writing this sucks, but absolutely don't take. Barely scraped by as someone who studies lots. Don't buy book for the 1 HW.

Dr.Lohmann is a wonderful lady but man this class is almost impossible. Your entire grade is pretty much three exams, all of which I studied for two weeks beforehand, and still ended up failing them. Her questions are designed to trick you but in the most unnecessary way possible. Do NOT take this class unless you absolutely have to, extremely hard

She is kind and really does love animals, however her lectures are insufferable. She fills the ENTIRE time with case studies. U learn like 7 studies every lecture (which is SO boring.) Midterm 1 mean was 60. Should be higher test grades for what this course is. Easy info, but it's so much for no reason. Doesnt add ur letter grade until after final.

Professor Lohmann is super nice and approachable, and the class and lab are really interesting if you're into animals! BUT you need to know that the class's 3 exams are pretty much your entire grade for the semester, so you HAVE to do well on them to do well in the class. Study the case studies and know them like the back of your hand!

Studied for the final for about a week and still got a C, exams are super tricky and on the tiniest details from lecture. She can be nice and is a good lecture but the exams will tank your grade. Wouldn't take it if you don't have to

I don't understand why Dr. Lohmann has such a low rating. If you go to class, you learn the material because she is an enthusiastic and engaging lecturer. She is always fun (even dressed up in a turtle costume). Her exams are based only on the lectures and aren't bad if you study.
all ive got to say about this class is BRUH. dont take unless you literally have to.

Fun class and not crazy work! The tests make up most of your grade (2 midterms at about 26% each and a final at around 36%), so little ways outside of that if you don't test well. The textbook is only needed for one homework, highly suggest borrowing from a friend. Dr. L is super kind and caring, and wants you to succeed, go to office hours.

She started teaching the class halfway through the semester. Reads verbatim off the boring, dry lecture slides. Rambles on about things that aren't specific to the exam. No need to get the textbook and no work outside of class. Be prepared to study a week in advance for the exams and study 20+ case studies for each unit... Can be rude and snappy.

Don't even bother getting the textbook, her tests are based on her lectures. She does cover a lot of material but, if you're good with memorization, you'll do fine. Some of her test questions are tricky but I really don't think they were as hard as I had heard. Tbh, one of the easier stem classes I've taken at UNC. The material itself was simple.

Do not take this class. Her exams were not fair at all. She is a nice person but if you take this class with her, expect to not do well on the exams even if you study an insane amount. I've taken a lot of STEM classes and this was by far the worst class I've taken at UNC. Avoid this class unless you want to lower your science GPA!

She is okay and nice as a person. BUT THE EXAMS? Be prepared to fail. the final is worth 40% of your grade and you only have 2 other midterms: no other assignments or things to boots your grade. This is a bad class so try to stay away from her.

Honestly Dr. Lohmann as a person is really cool and she clearly knows her stuff. It's easy to get participation points and she explains stuff well in class, but the exams are insanely specific and require you to memorize minute details about case studies done on animals. Not... bad? But needlessly difficult.

BIOL 545 was one of my favorite courses at UNC, largely in part to Dr. Shiau's teaching.  The 3-hour class structure was sometimes a little hard to sit through (not her fault), but she did her best to make the entire lecture engaging.  Literature-based teaching style was great and I would definitely take the course again.

Dr. Shiau was clearly passionate about the material, but lacked organizational skills. The class material was incredibly interesting and the small class size was great, but I often felt like she emphasized small details rather than the big picture. Overall, she is a great person, but the 3 hr lecture format of this class was not ideal.
Dr shiau was nice and helpful when needed but the class period was long. Class was also generally interesting with lots of topics. I think she treated students equally

Professor Shiau is a very nice person, however her teaching style can be difficult to grasp. Her exams are very straightforward and directly off the slides, and while long, her GRQs do prepare you well for class. She genuinely cares about her students, but her lack of practice exam questions can make studying for the first exam difficult.

This class is a challenging class. The way that she taught was very different from the first professor in the class, which is why her first exam is so hard. She is very lecture-heavy on exams, while I prefer textbook heavy. She also makes every class worth a bit. I don't think she is a bad professor, just different from the first half.

Nice and knowledgeable, but exams were tough. Required you to know very specific details and processes from her slides, but she said that she wanted us to remember concepts from her class moving forward, which makes sense. Use GRQs to get a sense of the topic, and then gain more information in class. Not a lot of content, just a lot of specifics.
All I can say is I do NOT recommend this professor. Shoutout to the first half of the semester for my grade.
Reading chapters is a terrible way to learn the material. I guess her slides are your best bet to do well in the class.

Dr. Shiau is an incredibly caring professor and is well-versed in developmental biology. Lectures were consistently interesting, though the material was often dense. Exams are difficult, but they're taken from her slides, so they're doable. Overall, great professor.

Previous ratings of Dr. Shiau are so misleading. She is a great professor. GRQs take up a lot of time if you really want to understand the material but worthwhile. Sounds like a you problem if you are not understanding the material. This is not an easy class but she managed to cut down on the material we need to learn for each exam.

Dr. Hedrick is very sweet so it saddens me to write this. If you are taking this class for an easy A (GPA booster), please don't. The course is graded 30% exam 1, 30% exam 2, and 40% final exam. The exams are genuinely very difficult and you will not do well unless you study hard for 2+ days. Try the first exam and pass/fail it if needed.
Friendly and funny made class very enjoyable. Not very difficult and no homework, grades are just tests.

One of the best professors I've had for a science course. Dr.Hedrick knows how to break down complex biological concepts in a way that sticks. Lectures are well-organized and never feel like a waste of time, and they genuinely care if students understand the material. Office hours are helpful—take advantage of them if you're struggling.

Dr. Hedrick is one of the nicest profs I've had at UNC, and his class isn't super hard. All lectures are recorded and well-structured. However, your entire grade is two midterms and a final, and the exams can be a bit tricky. I took this class as a bio minor without taking A&P first, which I wouldn't recommend, but was overall a good elective

Dr. Hedrick is one of a kind and truly amazing. Yes - there are only 3 grades. BUT, the exams are very fair. Take good notes in lecture (not just on the slides but the things he says) and put into a quizlet. That's all. Also grades on improvement. Attendance is not required and lectures are recorded. He is 10/10 amazing. Loved this class so so much

All of the lectures were recorded and attendance wasn't mandatory. I recommend watching the lectures before the exams though, as a lot of the questions were based off of stuff he said rather than just what was written in the powerpoint. The exams were a lot harder than the practice exams, so be prepared. CURVES HEAVY on exams and the final grade.

Dr. Hedrick is by far one of my favorite biology faculty. His class is so accessible despite only being graded on 3 exams. He is very knowledgeable and even showcases comparative physiology in action through gratuitous videos! Additionally, the exams tend to be curved. If you are looking for a great >400 bio class, this one is fantastic!

Super interesting, entertaining. I love the lectures- I actually go to class even though all the lectures are recorded. Only 2 midterms and 1 final are what you are graded on. Tests were hard but he curves

Dr. Hedrick is a great professor and truly cares about his students. He explains lecture material really well, and has his lectures recorded so that you may rewatch concepts that are at first unclear. This class is only graded on 3 tests, but as long as you take good notes during class you will preform well

Prof Hedrick is easily one of the best Biology professors I've had at UNC. Lectures are easy to follow and recorded and although the class is only graded with three exams, they're very straightforward from the lectures and he also considers improvement if you were to do bad in one of them. Very kind, funny and chill professor, definitely recommend!
So, I didn't actually take BIOL89, I took BIOL79H, but that wasn't listed as an option. I loved this professor. He was so funny and he really cared about all of his students.

This professor is very sweet and understanding. He is obviously very interested in what he does and his class isn't overly difficult. The only thing is that he is a tough grade and sometimes does not give clear instructions. But regardless random class field trips and cdad jokes and to be expected.

Dr. Hurlbert is fervent when it comes to the topic of citizen science, a field I have quite enjoyed to gain insight on. The projects in this class did take some effort but we were provided clear expectations on what to do in order to do well on them. If you are looking for an easy gen-ed class, take this one.

I loved Dr. McCoy. She is super fun and very knowledgeable about the material covered. This was a pretty easy 400 level class. She is very generous in exam preparation. A lot of in class group work that is graded just for participation, as well as an in class debate. You do have to do one 10 minute presentation. 10/10 course

BIOL 260** Dr. McCoy is awesome. A little disorganized but if that doesn't bother you than 10/10. She is very generous with exam preparation. Weekly assignments that go with lecture graded off participation. Course content was not terribly difficult. Study and you well do well.
She published the Exam II review slides.

Dr. McCoy is a sweet professor. If you need a fairly easy 400 elective, take 466. Most work is graded for participation so do the work & you'll be fine. Only thing I will say is she is often forgetful about posting assignments/grades in a timely manner but is flexible and will move dates if need be. Overall, enjoyed her class & would take again.

** BIOL (260) I really loved Dr. McCoy, she was a very caring and nice professor. The test material was straight from the lectures, and as long as you paid attention you could easily make A's, despite a few mistakes on the format of the tests. In my opinion this class was just a better version of 104, so I HIGHLY recommend.

(BIOL 260) Dr. McCoy was the GOAT! I loved her class, and as a junior, I'd say this is probably the easiest biology course you'll take at UNC. Her tests were definitely based on her lectures—no required pre-reading—and she encouraged students to collaborate on all assignments. She was excellent at breaking down ecological concepts. 10/10.
Soooo disorganized. Basically inaccessible outside of class. Doesn't respond to emails. Don't take

dr. mccoy is a very kind person, but she's really disorganized. with every single assignment or test, there's a mistake / something wrong. our first exam she had a bunch of repeat questions, our second exam she forgot to print half of the exam. it was kind of hard to follow along in lecture just because she'd contradict herself so many times.

Bio 260* Dr. McCoy is kind and approachable, but her lectures are confusing & the class is disorganized. The material of the class isn't too difficult but lectures are spent on examples that are unnecessary & confusing, there is no time to apply the content, & assignments are posted late/wrong/or there is always some kind of issue. So frustrating!

I've gotten A's in gen chem, orgo, physics, you name it and this was the class to tank my GPA. Prof is extremely confused during lectures, always says things backwards or just wrong. 69 on 2nd exam due to select all that apply where you can lose more points than you earn and random pics from slides to label. Extremely frustrated and disappointed.
Dr Mcoy was great at teaching and her exams were very manageable. She also had to deal with Dr M and Burch breathing down her back while she taught and was always kind to them and students.
Lots of papers to keep track of, but he cares a lot about his students.

I don't know what is with the teaching style, but it is very dull to the point where it is uninteresting to learn. The material is fascinating, but the teaching style just isn't it. The prof talks to himself rather than to the class. The course is PAPER HEAVY, so be prepared to take notes on each research paper since they WILL show up on the tests

SO MANY PAPERS. Remembering all of them was insane. Tests were all on the papers. Exams make up the majority of the final grade. Participation matters. Must take notes on each paper, and ask for help, because it will show up on the test!! Prof was solid. Recommended to have previous dev bio knowledge.

Article DENSE class, tests weighed a lot and mainly focussed on articles. Analytical and evidenced-based exams. It was a decent class to handle and understand only because of my previous developmental biology background.

Helps to have dev bio background. Research article dense class, be able to analyze, infer, expand, dissect papers and feel confident in providing evidence based answers on tests. Lecture content can only get you so far, so you must know papers well to do well since tests weigh a lot combined. Prof is great and helps build on bio 205 material.

Dr. Conlon was genuinely amazing. If you put in an ounce of effort, you will get an A. 3 exams, got a 76 on the first one, & still ended with an A+. Group projects every week, but we did them the night before & they took our group (not exaggerating)
The best class I have ever taken at UNC. Dr. Conlon makes you want to come to class because the material is so interesting you don't want to miss out. You get really close to your group b

Dr. Conlon is great! The class includes three exams (75%) and group presentation participation (25%), but Conlon grades generously, gives partial credit fairly, and offers plenty of test resources. The course material was genuinely interesting and Conlon showed enthusiasm when he lectured. I definitely recommend this course as a 400+ BIOL elective.

Dr. Lohmann is extremely kind and is an amazing lecturer! The classes are extremely fascinating, and it is never a dull moment in his class. The class is test-heavy, but the questions are fair, so it's not bad; it is best to attend class to learn all the content. Dr. Lohmann's office hours are helpful, and he wants you to succeed.

Really good high-level bio class, especially for a lab requirement. Made learning about invertebrates engaging and fun. I enjoyed the unique test questions - instead of boring recall questions, he writes creative and absurd ways to test your knowledge. It is heavy on memorization but I think it builds upon itself well, the beginning is crucial.
I love this class. The best class I've ever taken here at UNC, made me consider changing my major to marine biology.

Dr. Lohmann is the BEST professor in the biology department. Hands down. Amazing course content and really interesting topics were covered in class. He was always understanding and will do everything to help his students succeed.

Awesome professor! Teaches everything in a clear manner which is easy to understand. Exams are fair and not tricky. If you know the content, you'll do fine. Great course and easiest >400 course I've taken.

Prof. Sekelsky was a caring teacher and engaging lecturer.  He was accessible outside of class for questions and went out of his way to be helpful.  Problem sets were given far in advance of deadlines and content was from class lectures.  His exam was also exclusively on content from lectures and very fair. 
 Bonus points for his genetics shirts.
Great professor, designed handouts for students which is better than any textbook. The exam is fair, and the course materials are very straightforward.

Professor Blaimont was pretty great. I genuinely enjoyed her lectures and was interested in the content even though I am not a Bio major. Just try not to miss any homework or quizzes because she won't let you make anything up unless you get hit by a car or something. Overall pretty epic teacher.

Blaimont is awesome. Her lectures are interesting and she is great at explaining things. Expectations for assignments are clear and exams are fair. She is very knowledgable and you can tell she cares. I definitely recommend taking her!

Blaimont is an amazing professor. She is very kind, very enthusiastic about the subject (she is young and relatively new), and very straightforward about what she wants from her students. She is also very accessible outside of class for questions, help, and anything else. 100% the best option to take for 220!

God-tier of a professor. Definitely take Dr. Blaimont for BIOL 220! Very fair exams and grading on assignments. Patient on answering questions. I wish she would answer questions more directly, but she is already doing an amazing job for her 1st semester at UNC! Study the ppt and journal club, then you will be fine!

Dr. Blaimont was amazing! This class had a lot of content and work, but her lectures and teaching style always prepared me. Her exams were difficult in the right ways, testing things in an understandable manner from lectures and work. 220 had a lot of content, but I feel like she made it as manageable as possible. Take her if you have the chance!
great prof. the exams were fair and aren't meant to trick you. lots of content to memorize but lots of review and ways to boost grade.

Dr. Blaimont is the best Bio prof I've had at UNC! 220 is generally not regarded as an easy class, but her lectures were so clear, and I always had a good sense of what would be on her (very fair) exams. You can tell she loves to teach, and I would recommend her to anyone!

Dr. Blaimont was probably the best 220 professor ever. I was so terrified for this class and she was the nicest person ever. Her lectures were clear and engaging, and didn't mind explaining something slowly in class when I asked for help. Office hours are great, exams are fair, and she is hilarious! Don't miss the chance to take a class with her!

i think Prof. Blaimont's lectures were extremely helpful for the content on the exams. she's also really helpful in outlining good study strategies for exam content. really enjoyed being in this class.

This class was awesome. Dr. Ahmed was super layed back and the entire course reflected that. Your grades off of 2 midterms and 1 final (not cumulative) and 2 group presentations. It's very much show up do the work and an A is almost guaranteed. I don't think anyone got under a 80 on any exam or presentation.

This class was very easy in comparison to other bio courses. All midterms and final was take home and were graded very fairly with clear feedback. Only two group presentations and you get to choose your groups. Overall, I highly recommend this class to help boost your science GPA.
Great prof, never showed up to class and only showed up when it was my turn to present. Take home test and finals. He also records lectures and host it on zoom. Easy BIOL 400+ class!!!

I actually took 546, but it was an easy class, as long as you take enough notes to understand the material, all you have to do to succeed is rewatch the lectures and write down what he says with your understanding on the open note tests. He clearly wants everyone to get an A and grades group presentations nicely. Helps if you go to office hours.
This man does not tip servers when he goes to restaurants.

Dr. Mitchell is awesome! Take Biol 490 - best class I have taken at UNC! He is knowledgable and encourages collegial scientific discussions every class. This prepares you for presenting and inquiring about scientific work in a professional setting. Presentation based of journals and textbook chapters. I learned a lot in a low stress environment.

BIOL490 Disease Ecology and Evolution. Dr. Mitchell only teaches a class every couple of years, so if you see his name on the course offerings I would make the effort to build your schedule around this class. A discussion based class that was graded mostly on participation, barring a few assignments that were graded generously.
took BIOL 490!

Dr. Mitchell, my glorious king. I barely had to put any effort into the class because it was heavily discussion based but still learnt so much from it. Very accommodating if things come up for you. Attendance policy was pretty chill. Please take this class.

This class was easy and discussion-based—few lectures, just student-led conversations on the readings. He was clear, responsive to emails, and very understanding if issues came up. The discussion format was super valuable, and I learned a lot in this class. We could ask questions about anything—bio, research, even current events. Highly recommend!

Dr. Mitchell is one of the kindest professors I have had - seminar style class with students rotating leading. Come to class, read a section of the textbook/article, and ask questions. He wants to see that you learned something new, and is very flexible and gives a lot of grace with grading/presentation topics/leading discussions. Highly recommend!

Discussion-based class. 2-3 readings, come in and talk about it. Very kind and understanding professor, very fun class. Understands not everyone has a strong background in the content and is open to questions. Highly recommend.
Riddell is a good lecturer who cares for his students. It consisted of a lecture with many group discussions in each class. I loved this course and the material.

This class was great and very interesting since Dr.Riddell cares about what he is lecturing on. There were three exams and no final only a 10 article literature review(On an approved topic of your choice) plus a short and easy presentation to the class. I even had questions about environmental science careers and he made the time to speak with me.

Professor Riddell is very good at keeping lectures engaging and fun. He encourages group discussions and helps students when reading scientific literature. I took Global Change Biology (464) and the content was so much fun to learn about- it even had me reading the textbook. Get ready for some fascinating conversations about phenotypic plasticity.

He is a wonderful professor who will always make sure that you are taken care of and will extend deadlines whenever you need it! Take Dr. Riddell's class, it is a wonderful class with an amazing professor.

Dr. Riddell is calm, warm, brilliant, and an expert on global change. I frequently wished that classes were longer or that we had more of them because he had so many interesting things to say. Quizzes were not super hard. The textbook was a useful, but not totally essential supplement to in-class material. Take this class.

Professor Riddell's lectures are clear, his tests are pulled straight from lectures and quizzes, and there are lots of opportunities for basically free points in this class as long as you actually go.

Dr. Riddell is great! His lectures are engaging, and he really cares that his students succeed. Exams are very straightforward, so if you come to class, pay attention, and study the slides and quizzes, you will do well. There are lots of opportunities for credit in the class and ways to cushion your grade if you aren't a good test taker.

Dr. Riddell is a really nice professor. The class is very straightforward – most exam questions come directly from lecture or quizzes and prof doesn't try and trick you at all. There are two projects, a group project and independent project, and 3 exams, so make sure to be on top of time management. Overall really cool guy and would recommend!

Food Science & Fermentation. Easily the highlight of my semester. Fun to take even if you don't drink. Group research project & hands-on lab (molec bio & kitchen). Might not recommend if you will stress about getting an A; take it to enjoy it! Dr. Jones is a fantastic guy, very kind and funny, & cares a lot about his students.

This class is one semester long group project, with the deliverable at the end being worth 75% of your grade. Dr. Jones is fun and caring, and he really is excited to see what students can do. This class is good for people who can work in teams, set deadlines and stick to them, and who like data analysis and research.

The class is very chill, and he's a very fun and laidback guy. The only qualm I have is that he doesn't tell you your final grade breakdown, it just appears in CC. And there are no midterm grade evaluations, just one grade at the end of the semester, so you have no idea how you're doing until the very end.

Dr. Chen is very kind and responsive to emails. Lectures were mandatory but I wish they were more interactive. Exams are open-note and based off the lecture slides. Homework was light and did not take long. Overall a decent 400+ level class.
he was amazing!!

Dr. Chen is a charming and obviously knowledgeable professor, but he is not the best lecturer by any means. That being said, the exams are all open note, and he provides review slides that directly reflect the content on the exam. Overall, the class was pretty easy, but really boring since you have to go back and teach yourself the content anyway.

Class was a lot of content and for me it was hard, but the exams are open note. He really tries his best to get students to ask questions if confused. He does really great at answering questions.TA was also really helpful and kind to everyone. Would recommend, but I wouldn't say it is an easy A. 2 midterms and 1 final.

Dr. Chen is very knowledgeable in his field. You will learn a lot about paper-reading and analysis through well-prepared lectures and GRQs. The most manageable bio course ever with no tedious work. As long as you read and participate, you will get a good grade. However, lecture is monotonous and can be more engaging. A balanced and safe optiion.

He is soft spoken/quiet so it is kind of hard to hear what he says. But he is a great professor, has a lot of opportunities to give or receive credit. Probably not an easy A but definitely more manageable than other unc biology courses. Also, open note exams!
This class is awesome!  Dr. Z is very knowledgeable and super kind.

He is super nice and so interested in CRISPR! There is 1 midterm and you get a cheat sheet. The average was a B+ and he gave us 2 questions back that people missed. Otherwise, the only other grades are a semester long group project and the "final exam" which is a prompt that you get ahead of time and can prepare. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Nimchuk has been by far the best biology professor I've ever had at UNC. This course was my absolute favorite this semester and I always looked forward to sitting in lecture. He is very knowledgable with the CRISPR-CAS9 system and has so much insight to provide. Everyone should take this class and witness how marvelous Dr. Nimchuk is!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Very clear on his expectations and willing to explain difficult concepts. The class material was interesting for people interested in genetics and molecular biology. If you read and understand the papers, you will do well.

Loved Dr. Z! His lectures were engaging and entertaining to learn from. He sent out a weekly email that outlined the class we had that week and showed how much he cared about us. This was a 1-credit seminar, but he's teaching a full course on CRISPR next semester which I would highly recommend!

Great professor and person. Very knowledgeable on the subject matter and cares about the students. Seems as though he wants students to succeed and learn from his class. I highly recommend his course on CRISPR if you're a science major and interested in genetics. Final project was a lot of fun.

David is kind, funny, and passionate in his work and teachings. He is EXTREMELY fair in terms of recognizing fault; he eased up on our second exam after understanding what students didn't like from the first exam and offered extra credit. He's also very helpful outside of lecture to thoroughly explain topics that I didn't understand well in class.

Dr. Pfennig is an amazing professor. The class was amazing and very discussion based. The structure of the course was amazing for learning the material deeply. There was one presentation, a grant proposal, and a few weekly assignments. All were amazing and things I looked forward to completing. 100% recommend.

Great teacher and great class! graded by 4 things (HW, which is a 100, participation, a grant proposal, and a presentation you work on with a group). He gives you great feedback but also grades leniently. Highly reccommend!

Great professor who made lectures incredibly enjoyable to attend. He is passionate about the topic and transfers that feeling to the class. Lecture slides contain the exact content you will be tested on. Only difficulty is the tests can be a time crunch, so you have to know your stuff.

Dr. Pfennig was fantastic, and the relaxed nature of this course really worked for me. There was a lot of reading, and everyone had to do multiple group presentations as well as a significant amount of individual/group writing, so the workload is somewhat high, but it seemed like the work was very applicable to what would be done as a scientist.

I highly recommend taking this course, it's one of the best bios I've taken. Showing up and participating is the biggest thing with a few homework assignments, two exams, and a presentation/discussion leading. Dr. Pfennig is very clear and thorough in lecture and truly care about students success.

Dr. Pfennig is the kindest professor I have ever had here. She is passionate about her research AND teaching, which makes a huge difference in the quality of the class! She only wants you to succeed, and it's not hard to do in this class! As long as you attend class and participate in discussions, you should be on track for a good grade.

Probably the best above 400 level biology class at UNC. Can't recommend the class more, even if you don't really care about behavior. Available outside of class and wants you to do well on exams. Exams are online and timed, but questions are based on what is discussed in class.

I took BIOL564 with Prof. Yitbarek, and he's a really nice guy who obviously cares a lot about his students and what he is teaching, but he does not explain things in the most intuitive way. It's often hard to follow what exactly we're learning in class. Easy grader though tests are hard. Not many assignments besides tests.
Kind of a disorganized class in BIOL 564 but Dr. Yitbarek is very chill. I enjoyed the class, but be warned that there is a ton of math and plenty of basic calc.

Dr. Yitbarek's lectures were very engaging, and he was always willing to give feedback in office hours. He also offered multiple extra credit opportunities because he wanted all students to succeed. I really appreciated how the class was project-based with lots of opportunities to interact in groups. Take this class for your upper level bio!

Dr. Yitbarek is caring and obviously wants you to succeed. His class is strictly project-based, and you will do well if you put in the effort. The topics of the projects are flexible giving the freedom to do what you want. If you are interested in ecology, this class is a fantastic overview of many ecological subtopics. You will learn a lot.
Absolutely loved this semester with Paul. He is a super caring guy and extremely smart. The class was a little disorganized, but I didn't mind because he was so kind. This was BIOL 649.

Paul is an expert on microscopy, and his lectures were super interesting! He also assigned a group project as a final project and encouraged students to run creative experiments for it. However, he was impossible to reach outside of class, and the structure of the class overall was disorganized, which made it more stressful.
Online course. strict attendance.
Dr. Laederach is very knowledgable and the class runs on a project for a lot of the semester. Would definitely recommend.

Alain was a fantastic professor. Great attitude and loves to help. Assignment criteria can feel "vague" at first, but assignments are easier than they appear. Use all available resources (including generative AI), and work with your peers, and this class rocks. Course itself is not super bio-heavy; focused on computational methods/programming.

Alain is so great! Learned a lot in his biol 528 class about coding and learned how to use Chat GPT! Took more away from this class than a lot of other classes at UNC, and he made coding fun somehow! Highly recommend!

She gave back 0 grades, and didn't use canvas. Not even the syllabus was on it. She never gave feedback. Impossible to know how we were doing, until the final grade was entered. She also rejected my final exam reschedule request, and implied I was lying? Avoid unless you are a public speaking pro.

I think this was her first time teaching. It shows. The first day of class she divided us into groups and we stayed in those groups the entire semester. Presentations from the groups every other week. It was interesting to learn about neural engineering but you're basically teaching yourself.
Dunked him in a dunk tank for a cancer fundraising event... oh and he's a good lecturer, pretty funny.
Very passionate and entertaining. Attendance is important

It was a fine class. Easiest stem class ever. If that's what you want, then perfect. He was clearly invested and interested in what he was teaching, so lecture could be interesting. I don't love it when teachers use powerpoint so heavily. I wish it was a little bit harder, I probably would have enjoyed it more. The material was also interesting.

He is super passionate about what he teaches, which makes the class fun and engaging. The class is very organized and the workload is not bad. There are quite a few midterms, but they aren't super difficult.

This is an amazing class, Colin Wallace is a great professor. The grading is based on attendance, homework, lecture tutorials, 3 midterms, and one final exam. There is a lot of information and it can be difficult if you do not pay attention to lectures or do not do readings, but if you really participate it is super understandable and so fun!!

Colin Wallace is an amazing professor. This is a great class to take for anyone regardless of prior knowledge on astronomy. Graded on attendance, homework, lecture tutorials, 3 midterms, and the final exam. There is math involved but it is very easy if you are paying attention to lectures and doing the readings. (Its not actually about aliens)

He brought a lot of excitement to class everyday.  Attend lectures and you'll do well on the exams.  ExpertTA work was not relevant to lecture and was not tested.  Good teacher and many opportunities to answer questions in class.

Dr. Wallace is great for PHYS 115!! I struggled in 114 so I was nervous coming into 115, especially since I heard it was harder. However, I have had a great experience in 115. Dr. Wallace's lectures are engaging, he has a great attitude, and he genuinely enjoys physics. His exams are also clear and straight to the point.

If you want the easiest gen ed class ever, but also don't want something super boring, take this class. I would have preferred it to be harder, honestly. I studied for about 30 minutes before each test.

Dr. Wallace is the goat of the physics department here at UNC. You can tell he loves what he teaches and also wants you to genuinely understand the course material. For me I found 115 to be harder than 114 conceptually, but practice and get old exams if possible. The studios are also much easier than 114, and the TAs are great and there to help.

Dr. Wallace is such a beautiful light in the physics department. I can tell her really loved trains as a kid. And planets. He has a zest for physics that no one else on earth has. He lectures beautifully and in another life was a game show host. His exams are fair and he truly wants you to succeed.

Professor Wallace was great. Class was engaging (he uses Poll Everywhere), and the workload is manageable. He is a very clear communicator, both in class and online. He emailed the class updates regularly. I really appreciated his attention to detail in his welcome email in August as well - you will come in feeling well situated on day 1.

I am not a science person but the professor performed a miracle and actually made me enjoy science. He had inspirational quotes at the beginning of each class and played music. He is an amazing lecturer!! I was always interested in what he was teaching. Just a cool dude and a great teacher.

Took to fulfill focus capacity, ended with an LP because I knew I wouldn't get a good grade. Don't listen to the people saying it's an easy A. Ts was hard asf. Wallace is super nice, but unless you're really into physics, astronomy and have enough time to dedicate to this class, it isn't worth it (ESP FOR PREMEDS.)

Professor Wallace is amazing and so passionate about astronomy. Lectures are mandatory (highly recommend doing the pre-class reading) but he keeps them engaging and breaks complex topics down so they're easy to understand. Lots of outside-of-class work, but he drops multiple lowest grades at the end. Practice exams were similar to the exams.

There was a lot of material and a lot of graded things to keep up with outside of class like warm ups, homework, and lecture tutorials. Attendance is graded and exams were harder than anticipated just because of how much material there is. Be prepared to memorize lots of concepts, but you can tell Prof. Wallace loves what he does.

Dr. Wallace is honestly REALLY good at explaining material, I was happy every time he lectured. I just wish more of 115 was taught by him. Some of the harder content was taught by another co-lecturer. Final was difficult, but doing good on midterms really sets you up well.

Professor Wallace is beyond incredible! He is able to break down complex physics material into such simple ways that make immediate sense. And this is coming from someone who absolutely flopped in PHYS 114. The course topics are super interesting and the exams are very fair (except for the final... that was a bit sick and twisted... but we ball).

Dr Wallace is an amazing professor. He is very patient and always willing to help students to grasp the challenging materials. His engaging lectures broaden my understanding over physics, and I would highly recommend taking physics with him!
Professor Wallace is a super nice guy. You have to pay for 3rd party websites to submit hw on, it was only like $50 though. Lectures are important but not too boring.

Colin is the goat. Best professor I've ever had. He teaches the content VERY clearly and prepares you well for the exams. His class is a weird format: he asks PollEV questions, you respond, he explains. LOTS of homework assignments, lecture tutorials, warm-ups, etc. Very easy to miss deadlines, but overall interesting + easy content (I'm not stem).
Awesome guy both teaching and as a personality

ASTR 100 with Prof. Wallace is amazing! His lectures are super informative and very easy to follow, and his passion for the subject enhances them! Tests are straightforward, all MCQ. Practice exams are very similar to the real ones, so no big surprises. Not hard to get As if you go to class and do the work. Highly recommend, fantastic class!

This class was fairly okay until the end. My god, the final was atrocious!!! With a 59 average, words can not express how much that exam needed to be curved. The questions were quite difficult too. I also do think that having three lecturers for one class is a bit ridiculous

Fair class up until the last minute when the final absolutely tanked my grade. Unclear and misleading grade reporting in emails; I calculated the mean and median myself and they were 57 and 69 respectively. Some major content not taught by main professor and these lectures were impossible to understand even in the recordings.

One of the best professors you could take, especially if you're a non-major that needs filler hours or FC credit. Very manageable workload and exams (all multiple choice) that you can very well get high 90s on if you follow his pacing. If you attend class and complete all the work assigned, you will do well. ULA and TA's are super helpful too.

he explains concepts very well and always tries to make himself available when he can to help students. He genuinely wants students to succeed and hes very enthusiastic about physics. The class is hard and lectures can become dry sometimes, but he is a good lecturer.

THE best prof at UNC of all time. Even though Astronomy could get tough at some points, Prof. Wallace wants his students to succeed and cares about real progress. Very engaging lectures with a clear-cut breakdown of what's needed before, during, and after class.

Professor Wallace is really great, his class that he teaches however is a really difficult class for me personally to understand. I am not a stem major keep that in mind, however he is really passionate and good at what he does. He provides practice exams for everything.

I love professor Wallace. He is sometimes a bit unprofessional but that's what makes him a vibrant professor. He has a good personality and genuinely makes me excited to come to class. There are lots of pauses in class and lots of discussion. There's not too much work outside of class, and is fairly easy.

This guy is awesome. I had no passion or interest in Astronomy coming into this class, but Wallace genuinely loves what he does and cares for the students and their success. He is full of energy and knowledge, and such a sweet guy. I would definitely recommend taking this class. He's also hilarious, and always has jokes or funny side comments.

Dr. Wallace is so amazing. I don't plan on taking any more astronomy classes but if I did I would a thousand percent take him again. He really wants his students to do well and he is extremely passionate about what he is teaching. The work load is not bad at all and as long as you study the exams are not bad.

Im not sure why he doesnt have a 5. he has been an amazing professor. he is so passionate about this class and is so engaging. he makes our whole class laugh and genuienhly wants his student to suceed. he is very responsive over email and has so many TA's that office hours feel like they are a constant. i highly recommend taking his class,

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had. He is so sweet and funny and you can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to do their best. The class isn't the hardest, but there are definitely parts that are challenging, but Dr. Wallace is amazing.

He is rude, unprofessional, and he is not understanding of his students. We emailed back and forth about extra credit that would bump up my grade from a B+ to an A- (I was at an 89.86), and he would not budge. He didn't send out a clear announcement about the extra credit (which was geared toward another section btw), and he was rude when emailing.

Dr. Wallace is one of my favorite professors at UNC and his clear and enthusiastic teaching style encouraged me to enjoy learning physics. He is very considerate when asked questions and generally is a gem in the physics department.

I had Wallace for PHYS 114 and he was amazing. Most fair exams I have ever seen at UNC, no trick questions. PHYS 115 content was more difficult and it was co-taught with a bad professor. Exam 3 and the final both had averages in the 60s and no curve for either. No rounding for grades anymore. Great lecturer but worse course structure now

Wallace's PHYS 114/115 videos have been removed from YouTube!!! Why??? The physics department is trying to make us students fail!!! 

I am tired of re-watching the recorded lectures, which are filled mainly by pauses for PollEvs and would much rather watch the YouTube videos!!!!

The professor is a strong lecturer, but there was a serious breach of student privacy. After mistakenly giving the wrong final score (the average was an F), he made the situation worse by publicly stating it actually belonged to the student with the last name below one's on the roster. This constitutes a clear FERPA violation and requires attention

His lectures were very clear, and I learned the material best from his teaching both in 115 and through his online videos from 114. The class is a lot of work and some topics are hard but I think the structure with the studios/homeworks helped me get a lot of practice before exams. Dr. Wallace was also great at answering questions outside class!

Dr. Wallace is a great lecturer and I learn very well from him in class! He listens to feedback from students as well. Exam 3 and the Final this semester were written to be a little more difficult than they should have been in my opinion, but Exams 1 and 2 were easier than expected.

I found Wallace to be entertaining and funny. He's a great lecturer, a major improvement from the mess of 114. Exam 1 and 2 were written fairly and were relatively easy. Exams 3 and the final were much tougher. Physics is a hard subject, but if you are willing to contribute time to studying you will pass easily. TAs graded fair with partial credit.

Whenever wallace would lecture I always understood the concepts more. He is very clear and good and at explaining physics concepts, I wish he would have taught more lectures. Phys 115 is a hard class, make sure you really understand all the equations and studios to do well on tests
Just because you got the same grade as your neighbor doesn't mean you're correct, Collin.
I received a good grade in Collin's 115 class. My experience was filled with frustration. Wallace contributed to instruction disparities, and the way he handled student concerns was unprofessional.
Final exam average was a 65% with no curve. Says a lot more about the course than the students.

I liked this class better than 114 but overall a super hard class that if you can take somewhere else I would. Wallace made an error sending out the wrong FINAL GRADES to students and he had no sympathy at all. Claims he cant bump grades up (ex. 79.9 --> 80) because of the department policy even though he is the head of the department.

Colin is a great lecturer, but the class is co-taught (my other prof was Tsui, who wasn't very good) and felt disjointed. The final exam average was 65% with no curve. There was also a grading mix-up where we briefly saw other students' scores—possibly a FERPA issue. Colin was solid, but the course had structural issues.

One of the worst classes I've ever taken. Everything about the structure makes no sense and I would recommend people don't come to UNC because of the chem and physics departments being as bad as possible.

If you have to take a STEM class, take it with him. He's very passionate about the material and explains everything super well. This is a hard class but lectures were always better when he taught them.

Great lecturer, goes into good depth while explaining well. Was fortunate to have him for 114, feels like he really knows how to communicate lessons to students. Office hours with him were very useful. 114 is not the easiest class, but he teaches the concepts very well. Very kind man as well.

Great Class. I found the topics covered to be very interesting, and Professor Wallace taught the class in a way that made it very engaging. The material is somewhat challenging, but if you are actually interested in the subject matter, this course won't be hard.

Dr. Wallace is very passionate about his field, and he makes his lectures engaging. The class content is also very easy; if you have even a little bit of experience in anything STEM-related, you will do well in this class. The homework assigned is busy work but is definitely manageable. Attendance is required and can affect your grade.
Really interesting lectures! Uses PollEverywhere frequently for student engagement but doesn't grade based on accuracy, only on participation (PollEv is used for attendance)

TAKE THIS CLASS! 

Professor Wallace is one of the most caring educators I've ever met. He's enthusiastic about what he teaches and will always be sure to explain topics when you have questions. Beware that this class does require a lot of studying, especially if you are not familiar with introductory physics formulas. Worth it!
Gave clear and engaging lectures given the nature of the content. His tests were similar to practice problems, study those and you should be fine.

This guy is super chill, definitely take him. Only reason I got an A- instead of an A is cause I missed a couple lecture tutorials early in the year, which are 20% of the grade so don't let that happen.

I really like Professor Wallace as a person. He is super nice, funny, and extremely understanding. He really does care about his students and wants to help. However, despite always feeling like I grasped the concepts from lecture, the homework and test questions were usually different and much harder, and despite studying hard, I got bad grades.

Professor Wallace is an excellent professor and I would highly recommend taking one of his astronomy courses at some point. He is very passionate and explains things very well, although some of the physics concepts may be confusing for those who aren't super good at math. He gives good preparation for exams, although the homework can be difficult.

Colin is an amazing professor, he's passionate & interesting to listen to. A lot of people get disappointed by this course because we only talk about aliens for ~a week's worth of lectures. However, the other content is fundamental to understanding how we can find aliens. Not a lot of work, & the topics are pretty easy to grasp. Math involved!!

No grade buffer for hws/studios which brought me down. Exams harder than lectures, but on par with studios. TA's great for questions. Doesn't round at all (89.9 would be a b+) which is aggravating, could come off as elitist when asking questions and mean in post-exam announcements. Final was pretty bad. Co-instructor hwan was much better.
Honestly a pretty easy class. Missed some homeworks early on which messed up my grade. But if you just do the work on time and cram before the test, you'll get an A ez.

Colin was a great professor and was very consistent with the syllabus. I am just not great at the course material, but that is a reflection of me, not Colin. Colin teaches what you need to know, however, I do note that there are Lecture Tutorials, and you don't know if you are doing the majority correctly because there's no key. Good class overall.
Do not take this class if you do not have a stem background. I was able to understand what Prof Wallace was teaching on the slideshows in class but on the exam it seemed like every

Prof. Wallace is nice and enthusiastic however the content is really hard to conceptualize for non stem majors. I took this to fulfill a gen ed and I wish I chose something else. I studied for hours for each exam and consistently got bad grades. He also includes trick questions on the exams which is annoying

Took this to fulfill my Natsci credit and Professor Wallace was the thing I liked most about the course. It's clear he loves the topic and wants you to like the topic. I didn't know there would be pretty much every type of science incorporated in the class, so look out for that if you sign up. Overall, love his energy, but the class was mid.

Prof. Wallace's ASTR100 class is well-structured with engaging lectures and manageable homework. The content can be math-heavy, but using resources like Unstuckstudy alongside the textbook makes studying more efficient. Overall, a great elective for fulfilling science credits.
Collin is far too happy to be teaching physics. This man is always grinning but then writes some odd conceptual exams. Not a fan, but it is nice to see how passionate he is about physics.

This class is not it. The title makes it sound so much more interesting than what it actually is. Feels like a trap class. I took to fulfill a FC and I am regretting my choices as I cram for the final. Do not take unless you truly enjoy astronomy.

Professor Wallace is hands down the best lecturer at UNC Chapel Hill, and maybe in the world. While the astronomy topics may not always be seem to be the most interesting, his classes are always informative and engaging, and he does a great job at thoroughly explaining the concepts. His excitement is super contagious, and you'll love the class.

One of the best professors I have had here! He structures his lectures very well and tells you exactly what you need to know for exams, with lots of practice included in lectures. I took both PHYS 114 and 115 with him and it is so clear he cares very much about his students and their success - definitely recommend!

This class is so much more holistic than just aliens! Learning about atmospheres, rocks, using formulas. You'll enjoy this class if you want to a little bit of physics, chemistry, biology, math, geology, etc. Sometimes I didn't feel that his lectures prepared me for the work, but overall, he was an enjoyable, engaging professor.

I LOVE Prof. Wallace. He is an incredible professor who is exceptionally passionate about the material. On top of that, he is the most understanding professor I've had at Carolina, which I think is so impressive because this class had roughly 300 students. He makes resources heavily available for studying and is accessible outside of class as well.

He makes it very clear what you need to know for the midterms by marking each slide. There weren't any surprises content-wise and as long as you generally keep up with the material, its an easy class. If you're a stem major it is not hard at all. i was .10 from an A and studied the night before all midterms and final.

Professor Wallace is a great professor who has a good sense of humor and explains topics thoroughly. He is very accessible outside of class. The class isn't hard at all, but don't forget to submit lecture tutorial checks. Would recommend to nonmajors.
One of the most organized and caring professors. Explains thoroughly and wants everyone to understand the content. Knows his audience. For the class: devote yourself and you can do well.

A really great and caring professor. My grade should not scare you aware. You can perform well in this class if you put in the work - there's a lot of it. I definitely recommend taking ASTR 100 with this professor!
Dr. Wallace is extremely clear in his lectures, fully explains all concepts, and gives very fair tests. He is a wonderful professor who is very receptive to his students.

Mandatory attendance (you get 3 absences), daily homework/reading, 3 midterms, and a final. Overall, easy class if you keep up with the daily small assignments and pay attention in lecture. It's math and logic heavy at times so it's hard if that's not your fav. As a math major, it was a breeze. Interesting and a great elective for lab credit.

Great and easy lectures. Homework can be hard at times but barely affects your grade if you get a few questions wrong. Midterms and final are easy if you study the material.
