Just make sure you keep up with all the warm ups, lecture tutorials, and homework. (he drops a few assignments) overall easy class

Clear and great lectures. Exams are not easy-- don't be fooled by them being weighted low because the final is worth a lot and it will bring you down if you aren't prepared (my grade went down 10% after the very difficult final). Pay attention during studio because concepts may be on exams. Wallace is a great prof and best prof I've had for phys

The class is structured extremely well. He gives a short lecture and then the rest of the time is spent doing the in-class homework and practice questions on PollEv. I didn't find any of the content too difficult and the homeworks don't take long to complete. Highly recommend if you're looking to fulfill a science credit.

I really enjoyed Professor Wallace's lectures and you could tell he really loved teaching this class. You do need to review a lot for exams and pay attention during lectures. I am not a STEM major nor have I ever taken any class like this before but I think if you are willing to put the time in it is a good course.

Great guy and gives good lectures. Academically easy for anyone with a STEM background but it had so many random requirements it was hard to keep track of everything and easy to forget things that impact your grade. Requires multiple textbooks, 3 different websites, and an annoying app for attendance. Overall alright class but I regret taking it

I am not a STEM major, and I'm not great at math. I took this class to satisfy a science requirement. If you are a STEM major this class will probably not be very difficult for you. Prof. Wallace is a good lecturer, and the material is interesting. There is quite a bit of math and physics involved, so be warned.

The midterms were fair, but the final was awful!!! In most stem courses, the final helps or it at least doesn't hurt. The final took me from a B+ to a C+. I will say that this is a hard class in general, and he might be the best option.

I learned a lot in this class. There was a lot of work but it was mainly HW, Warm-Ups, or learning checks and no big project. Wallace is super passionate about Astronomy and wants you to be too! Tests weren't easy but were very similar to practices. Had a lot more math and physics concepts than I thought. Good class, but certainly for math people.

Honestly, he is a really nice guy, and he loves astronomy, but as a non-stem major, I did not enjoy the class. Before every class, you must complete a warm-up, sign in for attendance on the silly app, and then submit lecture tutorials and homework. I definitely could've done better in the class if I had tried a little harder, but I got bored.

ASTR100 is a tough class. I wanted an easy FC-Quant and this wasn't it. If you're trying to fill that requirement, take some easy math class like my friends did. Colin Wallace is a good professor though. Had him for Triple-I. Just a hard class. Lots of HW and tests difficult
Great.

Professor Wallace is a nice guy and is easily accessible outside of class, but if you are not a stem major and this is a class for the quantitative reasoning fulfillment, don't take it. The material is difficult and there are probably easier classes you can take to fulfill that requirement.

I LOVE Prof. Wallace. He is one of the nicest professors you will ever have. I took this class out of interest. Definitely work heavily, but it is just frequent small assignments. Lectures are extremely engaging, and even though it's a large lecture hall, he cares SO much about each student. I wish I could take this class again. He is amazing!!
Offers 2h office hour every week. Very nice and patient. Gives clear explanations. Enthusiastic lectures with good pace.

Professor Wallace is truly amazing. He makes the lectures clear and does not assume you enter into class with prior knowledge. There are lots of polls throughout class to gauge your understanding and he is extremely helpful during office hours. He has slides clearly marked with what you do versus don't need to know for tests.

ASTR 100 is very easy for anyone that's taken any sort of STEM class before. Prof. Wallace is perfect teaching this class, as he explains concepts very thoroughly, and brings a fun vibe to the lectures. Easy homework/classwork every class, and the exams are all multiple choice. If you go to class and answer the pollev, exams are nothing new.
Best lecturer. He's incredibly entertaining and very knowledgable in his field. Cares about all his students.

The astronomy/physics that he taught was easy. I don't enjoy his lecturing, to be honest, but most do. I disliked their inconsistency in unlocking homework and warm-ups (sometimes two weeks prior, sometimes one or two days before it was due). There was extra credit for the second quiz and the final exam.

Although he didn't teach Phys 115, he was the coordinator. He was really helpful and communicated well. He was very accommodating after the two lockdowns and cared about the students. Gave us two extra credit opportunities. Got grades back quickly and was fair.
Super knowledgeable in the material and always ready to give assistance. Had to take this class for a first-year requirement, so it wasn't something I'd intentionally do, but I still enjoyed it.

Class is curved down in a way that high grades are not attainable without extensive understanding. To anyone considering taking this class to satisfy their science credit, this is equally as hard/harder as UNC Chem or Bio, you have been warned. The assignments are relatively easy, but the tests are difficult.

I had to work so hard to get an A in this class after a no-effort A in 118. Dr. W is an fun and silly professor who's very understanding. I feel like overcoming this class caused me to ascend. Be prepared to work AS HARD AS YOU CAN; Dr. W knows that people who don't do well tend to get upset and not improve, instead of making changes in studying.

I like Dr. W a lot!! She's kooky and fun in lecture and ran 119 very well. Exams were hard (average about 65), but it's not impossible to do better than that if you put in the work. About 25% of each exam is take home as well. Studio is a nice grade padding especially with the extra credit. Not as hard as people warn.

Theres a worksheet due before each class. Go to the office hours of the TA's, you need to go a certain amount of times to get credit. It's a theory heavy course, so don't worry too much about the math aspect of physics. Also, make friends in the class and start working on labs early. You'll have to do a couple of labs with other people.

119 has the potential to be my worst course in college. The lectures are droning and boring (though Muxin is much nicer than Dr W) and hard to stay engaged with. The tests consistently average low 60s and are confusing for no reason. Dr W is extremely passive-aggressive, in person and online. The instructors have no concern for difficulty. BAD.

50 min mandatory lectures twice a week, but are incredibly simple and not helpful for homework or tests. Unreasonable grading of labs, and no communication with TAs on how to actually support us in labs. Don't reach out over email and expect a helpful or caring answer. The class is fine if you know what you are doing, the professors are lacking.

I LOVE JENNIFER WEINBERG-WOLF. When she started talking about shooting neutrons into an apple, I was inspired. She completely changed my perspective on life. Imagine shopping in a grocery store... LOOKING for the perfect apple to shoot a neutron into, ultimately turning it into a Hulk Apple.

She is a nice person, but this is a hard class to take as an introduction to physics, especially for people like me who aren't physics majors. The class requires a lot of time outside of class to understand the concepts and examples in order to answer the questions the way she intended them to be answered on exams.

Physics 119 is obviously an extremely difficult course, but Dr. W does her best to alleviate this pain. She is consistently available outside of lecture, provides clear testing expectations, hosts review sessions, and reaches out to congratulate individuals who improve throughout the semester. Since this class is probably a requirement, good luck!

Difficult course to take, especially if this is your first physics course ever. A lot homework and every lab you have to complete on your own time. Very slide heavy for the lectures, but some very cool in class demonstrations. She does give lots of partial credit on exams and gives lots of preparation materials which makes it manageable.

Although Dr. W was not my main professor for this class, she gave very useful feedback during our one-on-one post-midterm 1, and it helped me improve my test score greatly. This class is extremely tough, but it is clear Dr. W wants to help you succeed.

This class is difficult for a physics course for non-STEM majors. I wouldn't recommend taking it to fill a FC unless you have some physics background. Dr. W is very accessible and does a great job explaining material in lectures and office hours. Lots of textbook readings, assignments, and labs graded on accuracy.

This was the hardest and worst class I've ever taken. It took over my life the entire semester and ruined my GPA and my mental health. Every time I tried to communicate with Dr. W she was so passive-aggressive and rude. My final grade was 0.3 points away from a B- and she refused to round up and was straight up mean when I emailed her about it.

Only take this class if you can spend all your time focused on it. The number of assignments is absurd (51 in gradescope), and there is lots of required reading. The tests are almost impossible to complete in the allotted time. With that said, Dr. W is very nice, but there is so much material the lectures tend to scratch the surface of the topics.

This class caused me so much stress. As someone who has taken physics classes, this was the biggest mistake of my life and ruined my gpa and mental health. I am having nightmares about the clock I had to build. As someone who works hard to maintain his stem GPA do not take this class RUN AWAY. this is not worth it at all take something else.

I think Dr.W is very nice but I hated this class so much so I highly recommend dropping it! It was interesting for a bit but really not worth all of the assignments and labs that occur outside of class. She would give us equations without teaching us how to use them. I don't think you should take this class for a FC credit; don't tank that GPA.

nightmare class, no correlation between content in class, exam practice and exams. I'm convinced she doesn't write them. Effort will not translate to grade purely because the class is so disjointed. INSNAE amount of work - don't do it.

I have nothing against Weinberg-Wolf. She isn't the main lecturer as there are 2 for the class, but her office hours are helpful for specific problems. For learning concepts, studios/labs are best for that as she doesn't explain the complex concepts very easily. If you put in the hours to practice problems and study, you'll be fine.

I have nothing against Weingberg-Wolf. She is cheerful about the class, but she does not actually teach the lectures very often. She is helpful during office hours for specific questions, but not much for learning the concepts in my opinion (TA's and Studio is better for that). The class is very hard, but it clicks if you put the time into it.

Dr.W is literally born to be a professor. She is incredibly caring and wants you to succeed, the content is very difficult but she is so so willing to work with you and help you. For the content of the course Dr.W made this class the absolute best it possibly could. She constantly asks for feedback and again she is super willing to work with you
I think she might be evil.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE A NON-PHYSICS MAJOR AND JUST NEED AN IDEA CREDIT. I wish I would've listened to the 1 star reviews. Insane amount of work, exams are unnecessarily hard, labs are stupid, and lectures only scratch the service level of understanding. Spare yourself unless you want your semester to revolve around an INTRO LEVEL CLASS!!

I took this course with absolutely no physics background and was quickly humbled by it. Dr. W seems like a great person, and she definitely does care, but just be prepared for the heavy workload and difficult exams.

If you want to take this class solely to fulfill the FC-Create requirement, please reconsider. There's an ungodly amount of homework & labs. There's interesting demonstrations during lecture but the focus on concepts for exams was considerably less, attending SI session and doing lots of extra studying is really the only way to get by on the exams.

PHYS 100 was the worst mistake of my life. It says it's designed for non-physics majors, but it is extremely difficult and time-consuming. It may be 4 credits but it takes up much more time than that. Labs are difficult without clear instructions, and midterms are very hard and graded strictly. She is disingenuous and doesn't care about students.

Writing this while studying for the third midterm. For the love of god, don't take this  class. This is the most needlessly difficult class I've taken at UNC and even though I underloaded, this class took up basically all my time. So many homework, labs, and impossible exams.

Please spare yourself from this class if you can. Took this class to cover a focus capacity and have regretted it ever since. Lots of assignments, often due at once, midterms vary greatly from homework and lecture material, and Canvas page is a labyrinth to coordinate in addition to Gradescope which, for labs, contains few instructions.

Please, please, please, never take PHYS-100 with this professor if you're not planning on being a physics major. It was advertised as a class that required no prior knowledge and DESIGNED for non-physics majors. Worst mistake I've ever made. I should have dropped the class when I had a chance. This course will consume your life. Tests are awful.

The workload is reasonable and the lectures are interesting. But please, make sure you submit your homework properly on Gradescope. You will NOT get any of those points back, so DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE AS ME! I definitly lost a good chunk of my grade from that. Otherwise, study hard and you should do fine.

Genuinely please never take this class. I took it to cover one of my focus capacities and it WAS THE WORST MISTAKE I've ever made. It's not worth it. The midterms are so confusing with barely time, theres like a million assignments every week and don't even get me started on lab 3... Don't take this expecting an easy intro physics class.

Amazing professor, especially when she teaches it with another professor (Dr. Branca). Test-reviews often weren't helpful, but the lectures were very relevant and is generally a good professor.
This is just a difficult class with so much to learn, but she will do everything to help you succeed.

Literally do not take this class if you are trying to get ur create credit or anything, it may say meant for non physics majors but this was a pain and I would pay to have never taken this class. Would not recommend to anyone, egregious workload and midterms graded very harshly

I would never recommend anyone to take her PHYS 100. She makes the lectures very easy and the practice exams. She then makes the exams so hard. I was in a tutoring session and a graduate level TA said he did not know how to solve one of our problems. This class requires no baseline knowledge by the way. I would never ever ever take this class.
She is a great professor, but it takes a great studio group and a ton of work to get a good grade. Tests were fair, but studio assignments were just as hard

Dr. W seems nice, but a lot of it seems really disingeniuous. She talks about how "we don't want to trick you" and gives some of the hardest exams known to man (the 2nd midterm with a 55 average, the final). Warmup, HW and long studio assignment for every module will really drain the life out of you. Take during the summer if you can.

Dr. W is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. The class was very difficult -- lots of group work in studios, multiple homeworks due each week, several lab reports, confusing topics, and three midterms. However, Dr. W provided lots of resources to succeed. Go to office hours and pay attention in studio and you'll be fine!
The course is hard but there are so many resources available to succeed. Dr. W is a very likable person and taught her portion well.

You work more with TAs than Dr.W, but she is still there if you need help. Course is challenging, but you CAN do well with some effort. Performed 7 labs, wrote 6 lab reports, did 3 presentations (one being the final), along with small hw assignments. Extra Credit available for all labs. Start lab calculations and report writing ahead of time.

She is super nice and understanding! There is a lot of homework for this class as well as three midterms, a semester long project, and 6 at home lab assignments. The class was fun and interesting. She replaced our lowest midterm grade with your final grade. Just go to class and make sure to study. Lots of math!!

PHYS 119 is probably the hardest class I will take at UNC. Although the actual concepts aren't too difficult, the way they ask will be extraordinarily difficult, in a way different than other subjects including math and stats. If you actually want a good grade, prepare for this class to become your life and something you study daily.

Physics 119 is very hard and math heavy and it's very helpful to already have taken calc 3 before. Dr. Weinberg-Wolf is amazing and wants you to succeed and is very encouraging, and makes sure your grade is not only reflective of your performance on tests.

pretty fair professor. Follows the syllabus, if you miss a deadline for some things makeups may not be accepted. Class itself is challenging but if you're good at math it shouldn't be too hard. Midterms are tough, especially the third one. Equation sheet is your friend, make sure to use it. Homeworks aren't very hard, but the studio's a pain.
She actually WANTS you to succeed. Midterms were difficult but fair, and not worth that much. The final was pretty easy compared to the midterms.

Dr. W is incredible. It's apparent that she cares for her students and tries her best to help them succeed. This class was possibly the hardest class I've taken here at UNC, but she makes the class as manageable as possible.

Felt like she wanted us to succeed compared to 118 instructors. Fair tests especially including the take-home portion. Will be hard but Dr. W is very good. I didn't do the readings but focused energy into homework, review sessions, and practice exams and did well on tests. space out learning each module at a time. would not recommend cramming here

Dr. W is a very caring professor, she really wants her students to do well, even though the material is difficult. I took this class as more of STEM person and it was definitely more conceptual than I expected. I notice physics in real life all the time now, so if you want to feel smarter than your peers and challenge yourself, take this course.

Informative lectures with cool demos. Great teacher who is passionate about physics. Also very nice. Medium workload - 20ish min guided readings for almost every lecture + occasional hw and take-home lab. MakerSpace training! I did well in physics in high school and found the class easy. Tests were not hard, difficulty came from time constraint.

This class is the hardest thing I have done at unc, the homeworks take all weekend and feel almost impossible, the exams throw things that are hard to comprehend in a short time; if you take this class, your entire life will be physics. However, Dr. W is super caring and really wants you to suceed, she and the TA's are the only positive.

Dr.W does a great job administering a hard course! Her and the instructional team are really fair in my opinion. They provide all the resources and more to succeed. It is up to you to take advantage and stay on top. Don't underestimate the calculus pre and co-reqs.

Knowledgeable teacher but a lot of work. If you are taking this class for the fc create credit I am sure you could find other options because I really do not think this is worth it just for that credit. This class makes you do more work than other courses.

PHYS 100 has a LOT of work, but it prepares you for the lectures. Dr. W fairly understanding about struggles to meet deadlines for labs, and if things become too much, you can always talk to her and she will help you work out a solution. This class has very little math, being made for non-STEM folks, and as long as you come to lecture, you're fine.

Dr. W is a great professor, and I'm glad I took physics 100 with her. That's saying a lot considering I broke my finger doing one of the labs (don't do labs when you're in a hurry). If you took physics in high school, you should find the workload very manageable. If not, it may be challenging. Dr. W is a great lecturer, and her tests are very fair.

Dr. W is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. In addition to being a great lecturer, she truly cares about her students and structures her class to help you as much as possible. The Phys 119 material is really tough, but you can still do well if you put in the effort in studio and go to office hours
Extremely difficult course. Dr. W makes sure to explain concepts thoroughly. Very fair with partial credit.

This so-called "physics by firehose" class is extremely difficult, but Dr. W does a great job of enabling the success of her students. You probably won't enjoy the content at all, but you'll enjoy your professor.

Dr. W is a very caring professor and teaches a tough concept very well. She is very willing to answer questions both in and outside of class which is essential in such a difficult class. Don't be too discouraged by the low midterm grades, the studio section will help your grade.

Dr. W was honestly great and 119 covers some extremely interesting content. However, as so many others have said, this class is flat out ridiculous in terms of the amount of work required and the number of topics it covered. 

Summary, Dr. W fantastic, PHYS119 interesting but ludicrous.

Physics is going to be difficult no matter what, but Dr. W explains things well and is extremely responsive and accessible; she genuinely wants her students to succeed. There is an exorbitant amount of homework at times, but the expertTA questions come with an extremely lenient late penalty. Overall a very tough class but a very good professor.

If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. W!! One of the nicest profs at unc. She takes the time to learn everyone's name and check up on students throughout the semester. It's a notoriously hard class, but compared to other profs she seems invested in student success. Definitely study w/ practice problems and stay on top of deadlines.

He does not seem to care for our success. We do much of the learning ourselves so he is essentially the placeholder that contributes relatively little to our understanding. The actual learning is done during the 3-hour lab sessions. Would not recommend the class but there is a very limited selection of instructors here who teach this, so no choice.

Dr. Deardorff was a bad explainer so I mainly had to learn through Studio labs, my peers, or Dr. Hansen. Practice exams and exam prep sessions are the most helpful when studying. Exams were quite long compared to the 50 min we had, so making a mistake could cost you time.

First time taking physics, but it was manageable with freshman courseload. Gives multiple homeworks/warmups a week. Office hours and the online vectorious worksheets helped me most to prepare for exams. Exams were hard, but Dr. Deardorff offers extra credit for improved performance. Studio takes a lot of time. Final was the easiest exam for me.

He was ok. I preferred the other professor (Dr. Hansen). Participation is SUPER important so go to all the labs/lectures. Labs were hard. I failed every exam, but I was able to get a 70 at the end with help from CramBetter and practice problems. If you're not doing well, it's ok just try to get as many points as possible.

Exams are only 50% of your grade so studio (25%) really helps bring your grade up. Partial credit is generous, but the class is very self-taught. Manageable as a freshman. 70% of the class got a B or higher, ~75% class average on exams. Utilise practice exams, Vectorious problems, and Friday exam prep sessions.

The exams are graded well (lots partial), so it is possible to get an A. However, Deardorf is one of the most condescending and rude professors I have ever had. Would not be kind to students when they answered incorrectly in class. When 9% of the class got a question right on an exam he told us we needed to study more...
He was fair. The class is hard and he understands that, he wants you to succeed but you have to put in the work for that to happen.

Good professor, sometimes has a bit of an attitude but overall the exams were very fair. Hw was harder than exams and the practice exams he gives out are very similar to the actual midterms so just focus on those. Use exam preps and Vectorious as well. Would recommend to time yourself taking practice exams to get urself used to that 50 min limit:)

Lectures aren't helpful, definitely a self learn class. If you work hard in studying/keeping up with content the test questions are pretty fair, but the 50 minute time limit isn't nearly enough to finish. No curves nor rounding grades, the class is fast paced but very organized. Duane is nice and responsive to emails! I was super close to an A- :(

I didn't go to class so can't say much abt the professor. The class was hard but not impossible. Attend vectorious review sessions consistently, do the homework, and do well on studio assignments (they really cushion your grade). Attendance matters but we could also sign an attendance sheet at the end of class, so I just did that the entire sem.

Very smart professor but it hinders his lecturing ability in that he expects you to understand everything at the same level as he does. The class is challenging but navigable if you're willing to devote the time to it; the units build on each other to an extent. Studio and Vectorious sessions are super helpful, just find a group you work well with.

If you do not have a background in physics the class will be tough. I also advise against taking this course with a stem heavy semester, you will have to teach YOURSELF ALL of the material. You don't learn in class, in fact he says that. Instead, you learn in lab how to do the problems and if your group mates aren't willing to help you learn, GG's.

Dr. Deardorff is not a good lecturer, but he genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. But the class is extremely organized, and he is extremely responsive via email concerning absences and excusing missed work/class. The exams were a little unfair but doable. I was super scared of taking physics at UNC, but it wasn't bad with Deardorff!

Dead serious this guy is the worst professor Ive ever had. I would not take him if again if my life depended on it. This guy is horrible at teaching. I learned absolutely nothing in his lectures and had to basically use ChatGPT to teach me everything. He makes friday exam prep session mandatory but they just make everyone in the class feel stupid

Writing this as I actively crash out abt how unprepared I am for the final. The lectures don't go into the depth that you are asked to apply the material on the homeworks and exams. Thankfully the midterms are only 10% each, otherwise I'd be failing. Wouldn't recommend taking this class at all if you have no prior knowledge bc you'll get no help.

This dude stinks. I was in the ER with a university-authorized absence, and I couldn't make up the missed attendance and lab. Lectures are not helpful; you can tell he is very intelligent, but his ability to teach students is nonexistent. You will be fine in this class with a strong math/physics background (take calc first, you premeds!).
Awful lecturer, mean to students, rushes through lectures, and never shows up in Studio. His co-lecturer, John Hansen, was much better.
He is the worst lecturer to ever exist. He reads exactly what is on the slide, shows no work for any questions, and moves on. You have to teach yourself the entire class.

Not too bad but his atitude and approach to teaching a physics class rubbed many people the wrong way. Seems like Dr. Hansen put more effort and actually cared about teaching the material where as most of the time I felt Dr. Deardorff just read from the slides and briefly explained some things. Study the material/ do practice exams and you're good.

duane would be a great professional juggler. he is not a good professional professor. extremely condenscending in both emails and lectures and manages to make simple concepts confusing. had a different lecturer for two months and the class did better than previous semesters on the second exam.

I think Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person, and he seems very sweet outside of the context of PHYS-114. He is very condescending and snappy in lecture, and is not the most effective at teaching the material. Most of his class is self-taught with the help of TA office hours because the TAs seem very sympathetic about how the class is run.

Deardorff does not explain the material at all and is very condescending. He acts like the material is all common sense and expects us to solve problems in seconds and answer them in class (where the majority of the class then answers wrong). He seems like a decent person but is truly a terrible professor.

Get ready to self-study the whole class. The content itself isn't hard but he cannot teach, and then gets mad when we don't do well on exam prep sessions. Only surviving because I have prior physics experience. Only positive is that the style of questions on the practice exams are similar to the midterms.

I've never felt a need to rate a professor before until taking this class. Professor Deardorff is extremely condescending and passive agressive in lecture and emails. He speeds through slides without any explanation and expects us to know the answer and gets mad when we are not doing well on poll everywhere or the Friday exam prep sessions.
Don't take this guy. Very condescending

Deardorff didn't actually teach, so this is just about 114 in general. The course has a lot of content, and it's important to stay up to date. However, if you can manage to do all the assignments, readings, and studios, the course is actually relatively easy. The hardest part is just staying on top of things. Be disciplined and you got it!

Professor Deardorff doesn't actually teach; he is just the coordinator. That being said, he is still responsive to emails and kind enough to help you if you need it. However, this class can be quite difficult if you don't have physics knowledge upfront. It is fairly difficult, but I appreciate the little bits of EC provided.

Professor Deardorff is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He truly wants his students to succeed, and goes the extra mile to help. He's super flexible and willing to meet with you outside of class, and also offers extra credit opportunities. About half of your grade is based on assignments, which takes some stress off of exams.
Professor Deardorff is pretty good at teaching physics to beginners in the subject, but he can be a little condescending, especially if you don't answer lecture poll questions.
Tests were generally fair and partial credit was generous. Duane's lectures were bad. I only went to lecture for attendance. The homeworks and studios is where you'll do all the learning.

Not a bad professor, but not a great professor either. This may be due to the fact that it is a large lecture. He essentially would read off of the slides and that was that. Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person though. Very kind and accommodating, but personally I would have liked more engaging lectures.
Tests were fair but lectures were confusing and did not help me learn content. You learn most from figuring out problems on your own in studio.
He is alright.

I put in hours studying for an exam and ended up with a stellar 39%. The cherry on top? A grueling fourteen-page practice test covered concepts that played hooky on the actual exam. In class, the instructor's "Only twenty percent got it right" prompts are met with crickets. It's like a silent comedy show, starring us as clueless characters!

Professor Dolan really teaches this class, and she is very difficult to understand as she just reads straight from the lecture slides! Note: Physics is probably a very difficult class not matter where you take it. The exam grades are not curved, your raw score is what will enter the grade book. Try to avoid taking this class at UNC if possible.

Dr. Deardorff did not directly give lectures. He was more of a coordinator, but he was very responsive to email even with a large class size. I don't think you have any other professor choices when it comes to introductory physics at UNC, but this class' difficulty is reasonable that any hardworking student can get an A in.
He is one of the meanest professors I have ever had, and he didn't even teach the class. He did the behind the scenes work, such as responding to emails, and he was so rude. AVOID!

Not bad, though he only lectured for the first (syllabus) lecture. He seems like a good guy the four times I have interacted with him. The class is difficult but if you pay attention to the slides, homework's, practice exams, and Vectorious, you should be good! Also, don't forget to do the warm ups, they are easy to miss.
Take it at CCCC, Dolan and Deardorff are the absolute worst. Insane homework due everyday, studios are intense and exams murder hopes and dreams.

Exams are quite unfair. This is one of those classes that makes you wonder why you chose UNC. Professors appear more concerned with making their department seem competitive than you learning introductory physics. Exam 2 class average was 52 and median was 50. They did curve, but those raw scores are absolutely insane for an intro class. Avoid.

exams are extremely difficult and often so unlike anything we have seen or are given that studying becomes futile at a point. says it is to better challenge us to understand the content conceptually but if that were true our other assignments like HW and studio would reflect it. does curve slightly. also rarely lectures, it was usually Dimitri
Do not take this professor. Professor does is not very helpful, not really good at explaining. Take this class with someone else please.

Very blunt and straight to the point (probably why people rated him so low)
But very helpful and does give great teaching if you go to his office hours!! Doesn't come off as very friendly but is always willing to help you out.
Key note: very, very blunt!!

Puts his heart into the class, which I appreciate. If you want to learn how to program micro controllers, this is the class for you. He provides plenty of opportunity and incentive if you screw up as well. Downside is the lack of grading and some labs are a bit wordy, but that's about it.
Unclear grading rubric for most assignments and very little feedback since 75% of assignments are still ungraded almost a week past LDOC. I would not describe him as open and inviting.
If you want to be verbally abused then this is the prof for you :D

he is a narcissist. wont answer your question directly. writes paragraph responses to you but it makes everything more confusing. disorganized. unclear. einstein said "if you can't explain it to a six year old, you don't understand it yourself". dr j does not understand physics or anything really yet believes he knows everything

PHYS231 can be a lot of work, but I liked it! Uses a points-based grading system that's very forgiving; I didn't do well on exams but did enough extra labs, etc. & came away with an A. Dr. J is pretty disorganized, but he's nice & happy to help outside of class. Would recommend having solid skills in either physics or CS -- the class draws on both.
He is a genuine professor who explains things well. The studio lab determines a weirdly large part of your grade considering its heavily dependent on your lab partners.

(BTW math person).PHYS-118 is hard, but it is possible to do well. Tests are weighted 10% with final weighed 20 so it is very easy to at least get a B. Dr. J is helpful but comes across as rude, unsure if intended. HATED office hours but his forums were helpful. Studio attention/hw comprehension is vital. Learned course from TAs in studio.

Dr. J is a pretty cool. He will give lots of help over discord and can help with many things not related to class itself. The class itself can be challenging at times, but is manageable. As long as you are engaged in class, you will do just fine.

This course is very difficult. Class averages for midterms/finals are failing. If you already have a good knowledge of physics you might do well in this course. This course requires a ton of homework. The labs are long and boring most of the time. Pr. Jeglinski is very rude over email and doesn't offer much help. Reach out to your TA's for help.

The most unhelpful professor ever. The coordination and curriculum of this class is awful. If you're still in highschool I'd do whatever you can to get a 5 on your AP Physics test or try to get credit any other way so you can avoid this class.

Held unhelpful review sessions and was very condescending towards students if they were at all confused or didn't understand the material. The way he talked to students made me scared to attend his office hours or ask him questions. The expectations he sets for the class are unreasonable as the average for our 3rd midterm and final was an F.

He is a nice person outside of class but is unhelpful in any way, shape, or form. He refuses to give easier explanations to problems even if the student doesn't understand it and fully expects you to have the same understanding of physics as him.

This was one of the worst experiences I have had in a class, the class was ungodly difficult, and they did nothing to try and help us succeed in the class. The Sakai site was awfully organized, and he never answered questions thoroughly and was incredibly rude to the students. If you don't have to take 118, don't, and avoid this professor!

This class was extremely challenging with Dr. J. It is impossible to get a straightforward answer from him. The class was unorganized, and no grades weren't received until weeks before the end of the semester. He's not a bad person though, he was gracious when I had a person emergency. This class will be very hard if you don't have CS experience.

Dr. Mann is a great professor and he genuinely cares about the course content as it is VERY applicable if you are looking to do any observational astronomy in the future. His homeworks are long and difficult, but his and the TA's office hours are very useful! Overall, his lectures are great and he throws in a lot of humor to keep you engaged!

This class is far too difficult to be a gen ed. Classes are solely lecture, and when he would ask practice questions, even if 50% of the class got a question wrong he would move on anyway. I took pages and pages of notes every class and studied countless hours but still got 50s-70s on all exams. If you struggle with stem classes at all then avoid!!
Dr. Mann is amazing!! It's obvious that he loves his field and that enthusiasm comes through in the way he teaches. Great guy and would take another class with Dr. Mann in a heartbeat

Dr. Mann was great, and I managed to get by without having to attend class. There's so much going on though - with HWs, lecture tutorials, warmups, etc. Just a lot to keep track of, and I missed so many that I tanked my grade. If you're on top of all of these then it's an easy A. Very fair exams - just keep doing the practice tests!

Dr. Mann is an impressive prof. While he is passionate about astronomy and extending his knowledge to students, he doesn't take himself too seriously like other UNC STEM profs. Really enjoyed this class and Dr. Mann. Shoutout to his cat, Bandit.

Not an easy gen-ed, but easy for a stem class. It's mostly physics-related math but fairly simple and you don't need to memorize equations. There's so many little assignments, so keep track. Tests are easy if you understand the practice tests which are very similar. Dr. Mann is very caring and there's lots of opportunities for extra credit & help!

Professor Mann is a very nice guy, i took this class for my lab credit and I'm a poli sci major, but steer clear of this class if u cant put the time into it, its also easy at first but gets really hard as u get into the physics part. The homeworks are short and a good grade booster but the exams are difficult! Easy for stem, hard for anyone else

Dr. Mann is very funny and wholesome. The class is super easy for a STEM major but harder for humanities oriented people. The content was interesting, but the way things were graded and due dates were sometimes confusing, especially since there is a small assignment due almost every day.

Lot of little assignments that can be annoying. very test heavy with 3 exams and a final. the material is not super difficult but there is math involved. I felt like the concepts were not always explained super well in class and a lot of time is spent doing "Lecture tutorial" assignments in class (where you only get feedback on one question)

Dr. Mann is the man! He is an amazing lecturer who can engage the students in the material. He's very accommodating and gives a lot of opportunities to get the grade you want. There are a lot of assignments, but they are all very small. The material is really interesting and for the most part easy. His cat Bandit is so cute!

This is a super easy class to fulfill the science course requirement. There is a TON of busy work/small assignments, but keep track of dates it's fine. He gives a few drops on every category. Exams are like practice exams and in class questions. If you pay attention a lot of it is intuitive, and he's a nice guy. Class gets harder as it goes!

So many deadlines throughout the semester. All of his assignments are super short, which is a good thing. His exams (3 and final) are exactly like the practice ones he gives. The content seems a little all over the place but is generally interesting. I would recommend him, but make sure you can keep track of due dates (there is a lot)!

Dr. Mann was great! This was a difficult class but you could tell that he really wanted everybody to succeed. The midterm averages were a bit lower than he had wanted so he let us rework a problem in class to get points back. He was always so sweet, funny, and accessible outside of class, and I would 100% recommend him!

I believe Dr. Tsui is too smart to be teaching this class. Man has been at UNC for over 25 years. He's a physics genius and he's asked to teach introductory, non-calculus based physics. Kinda feel bad for him. He does an okay job but I really can't put much blame on him. He's a good guy, but I'd probably take physics with someone else.

Dr. Tsui is a very unclear lecturer and is not engaging at all. He mainly reads off the slides and barely explains practice problems. If there are two professors teaching the section and he is one of them, you should do alright because the other one will most likely be a better teacher.

He is a very nice guy just not the best lecturer. Some times the way he explains things is confusing and he can go on tangents sometimes. Phys 115 is a hard class in general so its hard to grasp the concepts when they arent explained too well in lecture.
Very kind man who wanted students to understand the material

He knows his stuff but the lectures are incredibly boring. Just reads off the slides and spends 15 minutes explaining the easiest question while skipping over harder ones. Not bad but definitely didn't ignite a love for physics within me.

He was a very kind, caring man but I do not feel he explained content amazingly. He seems very intelligent and 114 might just be a bit too low-level of a class for him. Great person, but might not be the best professor unfortunately.

Terrible lecturer. Dr. Tsui did not explain things well and made the class content much more confusing. He did not answer the student questions in a clear manner. He talked to the board and assumed all students knew exactly what he was teaching.

Took PHYS115 with Dr. Wallace and him. Really glad that they alternate on lecturing because Dr. Tsui is not a good lecturer. Lectures are boring and often times no/minimal explanation is given for answers of in-class practice problems. He is a nice person though.

Dr. Tsui is a very knowledgeable man, and his teaching style takes some getting used to. He expects his students to put in effort to understand the material, but if you do, you'll be rewarded. He grades fairly and holds office hours so you can ask any question, though he is not direct with his answers because he wants you to figure it out.

Took a mentored research class with Prof. Lu, which is a more chill setting than a traditional class with lectures. He helped me learn medical imaging physics, assisted with work on an impactful research project, and connected me to one of his PhD students for help with the project. Definitely a memorable, chill class.

Dr. Lu was a pretty fun and engaging lecturer. PHYS 118 naturally is a hard class, but I thought he did a decent job explaining the concepts. The only minor issues were that he has a bit of an accent (which isn't his fault) and didn't get what students were asking a lot of the time.

Dr. Lu is not a particularly good lecturer, especially for such a difficult class. It will be hard, you'll get through it, but there could certainly be a better teaching professor teaching the content.
Nice guy with decent lectures. Only like 50% of the class was graded by exams with lots of partial credit. This class takes up a lot of time tho with the studios, lectures, and homework.

There is so much content in this class, don't start skipping. Midterm questions are hard, use the past midterms as much as possible. I didn't find studio too helpful for learning, but it was a good grade boost. I recommend skimming the textbook, reviewing slides and using youtube.

He's a nice guy but sometimes he'll be bad at explaining something. Make sure to read the textbook; it helped clear up a lot of confusing topics. Class is extremely accelerated, so don't fall behind, especially if you don't have prior physics knowledge. The class was difficult, but the studios make it so you're pretty much guaranteed a B.

His slides are made by the department and set up to be taught well, but he just read off of them and did not explain well at all. Most people in my class did other work instead of listening. Studio is where you will really learn, so be sure to participate there.

He clearly knows what he is talking about, but the course is not set up optimally for learning. You are paying for three lectures a week but only two days are actually lectures, the third is an optional Q&A. The course is a sprinting race through 27 modules even though a full day that could be spent fleshing out concepts is wasted every week.
He was a good professor who seemed to care, but his thick-ish accent combined with the microphone system made it difficult to understand him. The slides explained the concepts well enough tho.

Difficult if did not take AP physics in HS. Must put a lot of time into studying. Very interesting if you like physics. Those who memorize formulas fail. Those who understand concepts intuitively do great. Will change the way you understand math and the way you approach problem solving.

Lu's lectures aren't all that helpful, but you get the basic idea for every topic from lecture, which you will absolutly need for studio. If you didn't take AP Physics in highschool, you absolutuly CANNOT fall behind in this class. You'll need to study super hard to do decent on the midterms, go to office hours, vectorious, and Q&A sessions.

Dr. JP was very nice however, if you have never taken a physics class before be prepared to struggle. The lectures were very hard to understand and the slides did not help study for exams at all. The exams were also extremely hard and I would study for 20+ hours for each one and still do poorly on them. I would avoid taking this class at all costs.
Professor Lu is humorous, and he explains concepts clearly. It is enjoyable for me to take his course.
Lectures are the most boring thing ever.

Lectures, textbooks, homework, and studios are kinda redundant -- I went to studio and did the homework, but I normally skipped lecture and never read the textbook. I did fine. 

(attendance is theoretically 'mandatory', but they replace participation with your final exam grade if it's higher. that provides an 'out' to skippers who perform well.)

Dr. Henning was a great professor for PHYS118. He and another professor would rotate lectures. His lectures were very clear and he was open to answering any questions. This class has mandatory attendance for lecture and studio. Exams are 50% of your grade. The class has very clear expectations for its students. Study hard and you'll be fine.

As someone who took an algebra physics class in high school, 118 was manageable. Studios were annoying but TAs were happy to check answers. Henning only lectured about half of the classes and he was fine. Exams were fair if somewhat tight for time. Can earn up to 1% bonus to course grade for surveys throughout the semester.

PHYS 118 is not an easy class by any means, but Dr. Henning teaches it well. Lectures were easy to follow for the most part, and he did his best to demonstrate the concepts when possible. You can tell that he has great passion for what he teaches. He is transparent about the logistics of the class from the start, so nothing comes as a surprise.
118 is a hard class and definitely takes up a lot of time, so be prepared for that. But if you're willing to try, Professor Henning makes it very doable to get a good grade in the class.

Physics 118 is very difficult, especially if you are not knowledgeable about physics. Pr. Henning only covers the basic physics concepts. The problems on the homework and tests are much harder than the ones he does in class. The class average for midterms and finals is an F and there is no curve. Don't take this course if you don't have to.

Phys 118 is hard, but the course is set up in the best way for you to succeed. Warm ups followed by lectures followed by studios followed by homework allowed for a very cyclic learning process. I feel like it may be a little much with all the busy work you have to complete and time you have to spend, but Dr. H truly did his best.

Lectures are fun and lively, and to be honest I think the tests are easier than homework and studios. The relativity part was the hardest, however, the rest were not hard if you are prepared with basic AP physics1 knowledge even if you skip the lectures, however, they are for grades. BTW, studios are boring and longer than they needed to be.

he's actually not that bad of a professor, but the tests are so much more difficult than the homework/studio work.  the average on the second midterm was a 60% and it wasn't curved!  just absurdly difficult for an introductory course.

His lectures are not good whatsoever. Expects you to understand everything he presents with no explanations or proofs of anything. Says he doesn't curve exams because this introductory course is graded on mastery, yet the extremely low exam average is more a testament to his inability to teach than the students "inability to master."
Love Dr. Lopez. He is very caring and willing to answer the questions for students outside the class.

He takes forever to get to the point and his lecturing style is not the best. I also have a very hard time deciphering what he's trying to say bc he has a thick accent. Also for whatever reason he taught the hardest concepts for PHYS 115 which was very frustrating since it is already so difficult to understand these topics, let alone understand him

i was always a bit confused and lost in lectures. If the class doesn't understand a concept, he doesn't stop and just pushes on, which was a bit annoying because then I wouldn't understand the rest of the lecture. Sometimes made somewhat rude comments about how it was easy and we should understand it, or things like that, but he apologized.

One of the co-professors for PHYS 115 and I swear every time we walked into class and realized he was holding a lecture that day, there would be a cumulative sigh. Not good at explaining material at all. Everything comes seemingly intuitively to him and his explanations are over-complicated. Friendly! But I don't want friendly, I want competent.
He doesn't know how to lecture. Accent is too thick and it's hard to understand him.
The absolute worst professor I have had at UNC. Class average was a 69%. Is not accessible and will belittle you for asking questions.

Makes the class way harder than it needs to be, both in how he lectures and writes exams. Acts nice at times but also does insensitive things. He showed quiz grades and names on the projector, and the first day he told the class of juniors and seniors that some of them weren't cut out for physics. Thank goodness Griffiths writes a good textbook.

He's a nice guy, his tests were just very hard. It was difficult to know how to prepare well for the midterms, and always felt crunched for time. This was a major blow to my grade, but I did learn a lot and I enjoyed his lectures.

The people who struggled the most in this class had a hard time with the math - the physics itself isn't crazy hard. Make sure you can set up the problems, the tests are pretty fair, but don't leave much guessing room. Most common grade was a C+; afaik just one student replaced their grade with the final so don't rely on that if you're struggling.

Dr. Lopez is a very caring professor. However, he will NOT curve very much. Your final can replace it all, but the average final grade was around a D. If you pay attention in lectures, show up to office hours, you will do fine. If you just coast through the lectures and look up homework solutions you will struggle; the tests are very unforgiving.
The best physics teacher I've ever had.

Dr. Erickcek is knowledgeable and does a good job covering the material. The material is difficult though, and your grade comes down to how well you do on the midterms so study accordingly! Still, they are fairly graded and often were curved slightly (including the final) if she saw the majority of the class struggled on certain sections.
She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. The content of the classes are super challenging. she doesn't downplay the difficulty. She delivers excellence in her teaching and expects excellence from her students. It's intense, but worth it

Dr. Khveshenko is one of the worst professors ever. His lectures were useless and completely unrelated to exams. Anything he wrote on the board was impossible to decipher, and his accent is difficult to understand. He cannot answer any questions, and talked to us as if we are PhD students in physics. Please avoid for your sanity.
DON'T take physics with Dmitri he's hard to understand and doesn't show his work. He just clicks through the slides. Bad lecturer.
just a bad lecturer, will just read off of slides and click through how problems are worked out. 50% of the time when students ask a question he answers a completely different question

I wish I could give him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is obvious he does not read the slides before class, nor does he care about teaching the material. No work is ever shown and explanations are always unclear. Take this course with a different professor, or at a different institution. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!

I wish I could rate him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is very clear that he does not read the slides before he comes to class, nor does he care about teaching it. He shows no work when solving examples and provides unclear explanations. Take this class with another professor or take it at a different institution.

I have never disliked a teacher enough that I have been compelled to leave a review until now. Do not take a class with this man AT ALL COSTS. He does not read the slides before the lectures, so he encounters them for the first time along with the students. Genuinely the most confusing and hard to listen to lecturer I have ever encountered.
i wish i could rate him a 0 but it is not an option. Avoid at all costs

Lectures were easy to follow and went by the textbook layout identically. Hints at certain problems that might be on exams. The course was fair, and homework + lecture + reading was enough to prepare you for exams.

He's a little bit of a dry lecturer, but course is pretty clear cut. Especially after being traumatized by E&M I, this class felt very fair. Exams were hard, but nothing unexpected. He graded very generously, and homework assignments weren't too bad either.
Doctor Wu is super enthusiastic about physics. He is really caring and understanding. The only thing is his expression sometimes is not clear enough. Overall, he is good.

The TA teaches, grades and creates homework for the lab section. Professor simply gives the recitation lecture. In those lectures he is a slow speaker, does not get through all the material in a timely manner. He is also a poor communicator outside of the classroom. He once forgot to tell us about an assignment and then tried to blame us.

Lecture plus supplemeting with textbook make the material clear and manageable. Fun lecturer and engages with students. Grades exams rather strictly, (i.e., you want textbook work) but is very lenient when it comes to getting points back. Akaa wants you to succeed, and he was very forgiving with final rounding. Put in the work and you will do well!

Great professor. The midterm exams were both a bit disorganized, but he was honest and fair when grading them. Doesn't take attendance traditionally, but gives pop quizzes throughout the semester as a substitute. Overall very understanding and a funny guy in lecture.

Professor Akaa is a caring instructor and wants us to do well. He goes through lectures very diligently and they are easy to follow. Pop quizzes are nice to help provide extra practice problems outside of hw and midterm reviews.

He's a very decent professor. He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he is talking about, and he expects that from you as well. If you put in the work, you'll do just fine. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I was lazy.
Made mistakes on each of the exams. Strict grading scale. Provided a lack of practice for final due to poor lecture/hw planning.

Changes exam grading criteria during the exam, grades were always over a month late, consistent mistakes in derivations, didn't appear to truly understand material. Slides copy and paste from textbook. Homework supposed to be consistent over semester, ended at spring break. Disorganized, better off skipping to study and do practice problems.

I took 281L with Dr. Ayangeakaa, and again I found that he was a caring professor that only wanted the class to learn and succeed. Homework sets are a little disorganized and can be long, but the lectures are well-structured and clear, and include examples to work as a class or in small groups. Tests are fair and he prepares you well with examples.

Akaa is amazing. Great lecturer and you can tell he really cares about you and will do anything he can for everyone to succeed. He does not want anyone to fail his class and he really shows it. He's able to take difficult material and break it down for students to understand.

Lectures were good and enjoyable but hard to follow for me because he almost seemed too smart for his own good. Make sure to learn python before you take the class. Beginning of the class was difficult because this was my first time programming.

10/10 class, and 10/10 professor. It was certainly not an easy A, but most definitely not unachievable either. Quizzes, final exam, and final project were all very fair and was the perfect amount of challenging. Highly recommend.
Best class - the TAs and prof really cared. So much fun

I loved professor law and his TAs they are all very kind and helpful, but if you are not good at astrophysics do NOT take this class. The description is very misleading as we didn't start actually talking about aliens until halfway through the semester and there was a lot of math to do with this class.
Overall, he's a great professor and a great guy but the class was pretty rough and hard to understand. Confusing concepts and lots of math. This was a rough semester for him in general though.

dr. law & his TAs are fantastic. i'm a humanities major & really struggled with the class content, but they truly care & are more than willing to work with you. the class & especially the tests are tough but law is great. i'll also add that he was fantastic during the shooting incident this year. i wouldn't have wanted to be in any other classroom.

law is such a sweetheart. as a person who came to unc with no love for physics, I'm starting to get interested in it and will be minoring in astronomy because of him. he's very supportive and his TAs are amazing too (s/o to lawrence, doctor procter, will). they all go out of their way to make sure you understand the content. 100% would recommend.

Great professor and lecturer, but this class is very misleading. The class is labeled Alien Life; however, the class is 3/4 Astrophysics. I did not expect this when signing up for the class. The last lectures are very interesting because they are about aliens, but the rest of the class is about material that is difficult to understand.

Prof Law is passionate +nice! He really cared for our mental health after the 2incidences this semester as pollev+ lecture tutorials weren't mandatory +he removed 1 exam! But the exams are difficult. They're mainly math word problems +the lectures are mainly concept based. We did some math in class but not enough or in the same depth as the exams

This was a great class and the lectures were very interesting; however, the exams killed me! The material is not difficult but the questions on the exams are worded unclearly and most of the grade is based on the exams.

Prof Laws lectures were always so interesting. You can tell he has a great love for the subject. The exams in this class are crazy hard. Didn't enjoy the homework or lecture tutorials but he was great. I'd give the class itself a 3/10. Not my major i just took it for the credit hours so that's probably why I didn't like it. Not really about aliens.
Professor Law is caring and kind. However, I don't know why, I just feel kind of sleepy when listening to him.
Professor Law is a great lecturer!!! You can tell that he is passionate about what he's teaching. You learn a lot of cool stuff in this class.

You can't really hear him during lectures to the point where people dozed off, talking to themselves because it felt pointless. I do think he would be better with a public speaking class for sure. Overall, the class itself wasn't bad, just practice and get old exams.
African Blackneck Spitting Cobra, Electric Eel, Y. Qiu. What do all of these things have in common?
DO not TAKE HIM

This is for PHYS115 but I agree this guy needs to take a public speaking class before he can lecture.  I can't imagine him teaching his own class don't take him if you don't want to raise your cortisol levels.

This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.
He's an awful lecturer, and reads off the PowerPoint word by word. He also just doesn't explain things even if someone asks him to.
He is awful

He needs to take a public speaking seminar before teaching again. Also he needs better awareness instead of staring down, as I saw a girl with her hand up for over 3 minutes without him so much as looking at her.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.
Writing this review as I'm sitting in class. Awful lecturer, reads off the PowerPoint word by word,  sounds sleepy a bored doing it.
Jesus christ, this guy is an absolutely HORRIBLE lecturer. Thank god that he's not the only professor for this course

So so nice! It is clear that he is passionate about what he does. Basically gives you what is going to be on the exams. I would say to make sure you know what time assignments are due so you don't miss one, he doesn't make them due at 11:59 and there are very few of them. Also can be a little condescending if you answer a question wrong in class.

Professor Zhou is a great instructor. He's passionate about what he teaches and his tests are verbatim the concepts taught. There was little homework but that meant that the class was test-heavy. The content was interesting and we were able to go to the labs! You needed to be present in class to understand concepts as his slides were confusing.

Dr. Zhou is such a king! You'll probably feel intimidated at first but he tries so hard to make the topics interesting and make jokes during class. Very few grades and he doesn't really use canvas so you won't really know how you're doing in the class. Slides are not detailed so go to class and pay attention and the exams won't be too bad.

Dr. Zhou is a great professor and taught some really cool things about nanotechnology and science! Class is pretty chill with few homework assignments, a midterm and a final for the year. I just wish lecture slides could be more detailed, but if you pay attention in class, you should be fine!

Dr. Zhou is a character. The class feels a little just thrown together, but the material is not difficult at all. Very little homework while is nice, and as long as you payed attention in lecture you will be fine. Incredibly laid back class that I would recommended for your first year seminar if this sounds interesting to you.
midterm + final are on pieces of printer paper! it is mostly a lecture-heavy class and you can make friends within the class. unclear on grading, however, pretty lenient on the final grade

Professor Zhou is passionate about what he's teaching, and he makes the material rather interesting. Most grades are participation/completion-based, plus a midterm and a final. The review he gives you is basically what's on the exam. He also takes you on little field trips to the labs!

Dr. Zhou always seemed interested in the course and always promoted participation. He made the course suprisingly interesting and was very knowledgable on what was taught. The course is graded on attendence, homeworks, midterm, and final. Detailed grading but as long as you pay attention in class you should be fine (lecture slides lack a lot).
THIS GUY IS AWESOME. JUST PAY ATTENTION AND YOU WILL LEARN. TOOK HIM FALL 2023 AND THE THIS GUY KNOWS HIS STUFF!
There are no grades except one midterm (was given on three pages of blank printer paper, and he just said write this information if you know it), a final, and a final project

I loved this class. Dr. Zhou made it the least stressful physics class I've ever taken while ensuring we still learned a lot (which I did). Not worrying about the class made it easier to learn and enjoy the material. Highly recommend this course to anyone going into the medical field or a physics field.
Clear lecturer, minimal studying required

Dr. Gruszko was extremely accessible and answered questions thoroughly. The class was difficult, but don't let the midterm scores discourage you as the studio grade will bring you up. If you find the time for it, go to the review session before the midterms and the final, they are a great way to remind yourself of the many concepts covered.

Lectures are a MUST. You will not glean enough information by simply going through slides. Work the problems out in class, do the homework, and pay attention in lab. This class was sneakily difficult for me, but if you practice, pay attention, and work to do well on the final, she will take that into account. She is also super nice and accomodating
AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! Always listens to students, if you have any questions ask and she'll always be there to help you. Office hours are incredibly helpful and she knows what she's talking about.
has an accent, but it isn't bad and she explains things very well in the lectures

Dr. Branca is the best. She was very caring and accessible through Piazza and O.H. and really cared about helping as many people as she could. For someone that has never taught PHYS 119 before she did a really amazing job. You will definitely have to put in a lot of effort on your own, but she really does want to help along the way. Great professor

dr. branca taught phys 119 pretty well for her first time. there were times where we didn't cover the last little bit of the lecture but that was remediated by the studio work. tests were reasonable except for that second one D: lots of help available and the hw is great practice.

Did not provide complete slides and some of her solutions were blatantly incorrect.

She chill tho

This course is very very hard, It is for physics students only. These are concepts that are super hard to wrap your head around.There isn't enough visual learning to justify taking this course in person, all you do is read of the board, the homeworks are very difficult. My understanding of the topic increased minimally.

Very funny guy. The class is hard regardless, and he did a pretty good job of making things go as smoothly as possible. Always asked for feedback and for questions, and worked with students' requests quite a bit. Definitely recommend him.
The best professor at UNC.

All around wonderful guy. Class is made up of weekly homework and quizzes with a large semester project at the end. Attendance isn't required but you're better off going to most lectures (or attending on zoom). Grades leniently and cares for his students.
He is a great guy!
Very passionate and easygoing professor!
Chill teacher, really is passionate about what he teaches and makes class accessible to all!

Professor Hill is a great guy; he is passionate about his subject and it showed in every lecture, along with a lot of humor. If you keep up with the homework and quizzes, you'll do well. I found some of the content hard but asking clarifying questions during lectures helped. Both midterm and final were take-home, open book, and open note.

Brad is the goat. Exams and homeworks are a near carbon copy straight off the slides. If you are at all interested in Astr, take this class as he is def the best professor. Very engaging and loves what he does. All exams are multiple choice and they are all very fair questions, not suppose to trick you like other professors.

Awesome professor. He gave amazing lectures that were genuinely interesting and enjoyable. Possibly the best lecturer I have ever had. Class was relatively easy with exam material clearly outlined beforehand and minimal work day to day. Highly recommend
The literal greatest professor/teacher I have ever had. I actually looked forward to ASTR101 on Tuesday and Thursday.

I looked forward to this class every time I had it, Professor Barlow gave me a newfound love for astronomy. He is hilarious, and keeps his students engaged at all times. The 3 exams + final are based off of the homework and in-class quizzes, and require studying. He cares about his students immensely, and is fun to chat with after class.

Dr. Barlow is truly one of the best professors you can have. He cares deeply about his subject and you can tell. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO IT! His office hours are extremely helpful and he will explain things down to whatever detail you need and make sure you understand it. He is extremely kind and willing to help.

Class itself is easy. Learned content from outside resources and then reviewed the slides to understand the class. Topics aren't hard and plenty of opportunities to ask questions in ~3 hours a week of office hours.

I did good in this class because of Youtube learning. His lecture slides made no sense, and they had errors on them. I learned absolutely nothing from Rodriguez. Shows up late and unprepared, and he doesn't care about teaching. Grading/tests were not as bad as I was expecting, but If I didn't have Youtube or ChatGPT, I would have been cooked.

Literally awful. The content of the class is presented on slides that he just repeats it. Nothing makes sense. I was taking 383 during this class and I literally didn't learn or comprehend a single thing unless it was something that we had gone over during 383. If u haven't taken linear algebra and a proof based class (like math 381), do not take.

Professor Rodriguez is a great professor. He will take time to explain things that you do not understand and enjoys teaching. PHYS331 is a tough class if you have not taken linear algebra and a proof based class. There are tons of proofs in the homework. It seems they need to update the prerequisites for the class. Otherwise, it is a great class!

He's a great professor. Low stress high learning environment. Unfortunately, class was at 8 am, so made it hard to pay attention, but that was no fault of the professor. Highly recommend taking a class by him: he's clearly a very smart, very experienced individual. Lucky to have him as a professor.

MSA is the GOAT!!! She leads amazing lectures and ensures that no student is left behind. The HWs prepare you well for the midterms. Attendance is crucial b/c she covers all content in class. Legit just using calculus to prove common sense (ex: prices rise --> quantity decreases no way lol). Understand derivatives thoroughly and you'll be chilling!

Very caring. Sometimes felt like she could have gone faster and finding "tricks to memorize" the concept instead of understanding it deeply. Midterms and final are majority of the grade and you need to be doing well on all 3 to get an A. Very manageable. Need to be very comfortable with derivatives.

So nice and really funny, BUT her flipped classroom model taught me NOTHING. I went to office hours, all lectures, and watched all the videos and still didn't learn anything. The tests make up a majority of your grade so you can't do bad, and you are expected to intuitively know econ or you're cooked. The TAs and ULAs were also bad at explaining.

Amazing, best econ professor, literally study the exact way she tells you by grouping practice problems and you will be fine, flipped classroom is annoying but it works, no other econ professor compares, if you did well in calc you will do amazing in this class

I had the pleasure of taking Professor MSA for both ECON 410 and 415. ECON 415 builds on the concepts from 410, but she does a great job of reviewing the fundamentals needed to succeed in the course. While 410 was a bit trickier, both classes were very manageable as long as you stayed on top of the material and completed her practice exams.

Without question the best professor I have ever encountered. She is welcoming & considerate & leads lectures extremely well and efficiently, giving students plenty of chances to ask questions and absorb info. She is accessible via email and office hours (DEF RECOMMEND GOING), knows how to teach in a way that students will understand...0 complaints.
MSA is a great teacher. This class is not very hard if you are good at calculus and have prior exposure to a lot of the math beforehand. Very fair grader and wants students to suceed.

I like everything about how MSA does ECON 410. She is warm and caring but commands the room and lectures with confidence. She provides a wealth of helpful resources and gives fair exams. If you can get the math down (hardest concepts are exponent rules and partial derivatives), then nothing is more difficult conceptually than the stuff from 101.

MSA is hands-down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. I love her! Somehow, she is able to explain every single micro concept clearly and do it with patience and care. She is very generous with weighting your best exam heavier, dropping homework grades, etc. If you are going to take 410, take it with her!

MSA is amazing! ECON410 is a heavy course, but she has an insane amount of resources. This class is also a flipped classroom (but I never watched the video and did fine, just gotta grind a lot later). Looking over 101 materials/taking it the previous semester can definitely be helpful. Grading is fair, though she doesn't curve or give extra credit.

MSA is an awesome instructor, as she was able to explain abstract concepts very clearly. As long as you strongly lock in September, you'll be fine the rest of the semester. Many resources are provided throughout the semester.

Econ 410 is not a breeze. Content picks up pretty quickly, math intensive (calc 1), etc. However, MSA made this class extremely feasible. She was always there to help before/after class and in office hours. 2 midterms, a final, and HW are pretty much your entire grade. A is def possible if you keep up w the course videos and ask questions!

She has the magic of explaining complex stuff in the easiest way to understand. Very kind, interesting, approachable, and generous about grades. Exams are extremely similar to the homework. I personally feel the pace of the course is slowed by the class size (~200 people) and many polls during class (each could take up to 10-15 min of class time)
She's lowkey hilarious.
