Not a safe learning environment. He over-simplifies the concepts like its review. Can't ask questions because he will make you look stupid in front of the class.Slides are unorganized making it even harder to understand the concepts. I'll pass but the emotional trauma is so real. It's his first time teaching this course but he has no grace for us.

Respectfully, he always plugs his other class he teaches, but I would never consider taking it as long as he is the one teaching it. I always go to lectures because of the polls, but I cannot say I learn anything. Why are his slides different and riddled with mistakes??? If I do not pass this class, this man will truly be the bane of my existence.

Prof Hill is so bad that he worth me to waste 5 mins on writing comments for him. Sometimes to be polite, we might say an econ prof a good economist and a good person, but not a good lecturer. Prof Hill, in my opinion, is a disqualified economist, below-average person, and an horrible lecturer. Just dont take him and you'll enjoy your life at UNC.
Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Literally edits errors in his slides during lecture and has yet to actually explain how to do a problem in class.
Lectures and course materials are useless and confusing. Do not take unless you are intrested in learning all on your own even though attendance is mandatory.

The exam materials are completely useless, chalk full of typos and incorrect work. I feel bad for the ULAs because even they can't decipher a single thing he is talking about. The whole class is a jumble of random topics in no discernible order, and it is never clear what is actually going to be tested. Stay far, far away.

Probably the worst Econ prof at UNC. Edits his slides as he's lecturing. Useless slides in general. Does not care if his students are following or not. Illegible handwriting. Says we'll get a 0 if we copy-paste Stata outputs on HW but then pastes Stata outputs on his slides. Unprofessional, careless, lazy teaching. Honestly a joke. Save yourself.
instead of taking his class, go to econ aid or watch youtube. This guy clearly have no idea about teaching.

Completely useless lectures, you will have to teach yourself everything. Definitely should have dropped the class after the first day. Absolutely take this with another teacher, this guy is the worst.

This guy is a joke. The homeworks are worth a ton and are very difficult. The only thing he lectures about is derivations of things and never actually does an example or explain how to do a problem. The material in this class is tough regardless but nearly impossible with this professor.
The worst.

some homework problems are not related to the lecture at all, WILL require you to learn by yourself. Might be an oversight, but one concept in the latest homework was never covered in slides, recitations, or review sheets. Lectures are ok and there are review sheets available but resources outside of his class are far better and more helpful
Don't take his 410 Class, or you bet study on your own for hours per week. The homework has nothing to do with the lecture. He just supposes that everyone knows how to do the problem naturally.

Professor Hill is nice and wants his students to succeed. His midterms were very easy, but his final was far harder. You have to follow along with what he writes on a chalkboard, he expects a pretty strong basic understanding of Econ concepts. Overall a good class. Don't skip.

Hill is a good guy and is friendly. But it felt that the econ department kind of forced him to do this topic. Everything is on a chalkboard, so it is quite challenging to go over notes. Midterms were fairly good, finals were very difficult. I have mixed feelings.

Lectures off chalkboard and doesn't post notes, so you have to go to class in order to get everything (or copy off a friend). Super clear in lecture and answers your questions to clear any confusion. Exams and Homework were very fair and not designed to trick you, but there are only a few so you have to do well to get a good grade in the class.

Graded 50% midterm 50% final, not sure what he teaches is economically/historically/politically correct but he is entertaining... holds office hours from 6am-8am lol. Exams are so stressful but there's no work other than that and you just have to regurgitate his opinions. But ik a bunch of people who did REALLY bad so proceed with caution!

Ignore the poor reviews. This class is absolutely worth taking. Extremely knowledgable professor who has taught this course for 50+ years. Part of the UNC experience is getting to listen to individuals who are highly knowledgable and connected in their fields, this is certainly that case. By far one of the most interesting econ electives.

If I could give Rosefielde a 6/5 I would. Best econ class I have ever taken. Extremely interesting and relevant lectures. Teaches precisely to the test which allows for a deeper grasp of the material. The class is graded on midterm and final which are essay style. He prepares everyone perfectly as long as you attend class. 10/10 experience.

I was skeptical at first, but Prof. Rosefielde proved me wrong. He's a brilliant, caring lecturer. The class is lecture-heavy, but the exams are fair. He teaches objectively, critiques all sides, and welcomes open discussion. Many bad reviews reflect implicit liberal bias—not the quality of this insightful, unique, and well-taught course.

Most problematic professor I've had at UNC—creepy toward female students and prone to weird comments about students' ethnicities. Frequently makes inaccurate claims about Russia's political system and espouses centrist/conservative views. He's critical of "wokeness." The class is easy for a 400 level elective which still makes it worth taking.

This professor is discredited by his peers, generally considered incorrect in his publishings, and anecdotal at best in his knowledge. You'll be graded on two papers which he grades based on to what degree you agree with his (again discredited) opinions. As a result of the fact that no other scholar agrees with him, all textbooks are his own.

I thought the class sounded interesting but was hesitant to sign up because of some of the critical "reviews" on Ratemyprofessor. While I see reviews that are spot on, I remind myself that I have also been possibly surprised sometimes. This was one of those occasions. He is great!

Dr. Rosefielde is the gem of the UNC Econ department. He cares for his students and gives them every opportunity to succeed. He tells you what will be on the exams. The course grade depends on a midterm and final, both free response. As long as you take good notes and go to his lectures you will have no problem. Tough but a very fair grader.

Even though this is the only Econ class without math/numbers, I would not recommend. Your grade is fully determined by the midterm and final. He says all of his information in the exams is from his lectures, but this is not true. Have to read multiple of the textbooks he wrote on the topic to do well. He also says some questionable things in class.

Rabid Russophile who says off-color and uncomfortable things for 45 minutes each morning and grades two closed-book two-hour final exam papers as if it should be full of cited statistical figures and grades on paper organization despite claiming all semester it is content-only. This is 100% of the grade. Only people who got A- cheated & used notes.

Prof. went to Harvard, claims to know Putin. Too smart for his own good yet horrible at teaching, mostly rambles about random stuff, also just a weird old man. Didn't learn a thing and then was expected to write a 5 page essay in 2 hrs for the final which was worth 100% of our grade. Incredibly harsh grader for not teaching anything.

If you are good at writing essays, take this class for an easy A. If you are slightly unsure of whether you can churn out a quality essay in 2 hours that throughly answers multiple questions (twice if you take both the midterm and the final), avoid the class.
Way too hard of a grader, way too harsh of attendance policy for an 8am. This class isn't even worthy of being in your shopping cart.

He went to Harvard and is a genius, so if you're anything less than perfect on the two essay exams you will perform poorly. Don't worry though, the exams are only part A and B. Sike its part Aabcdefgh and part Babcdefg, also you only have 2 hours to complete it. Wrote 2000 words in 2 hours but got a failing grade and literally no positive feedback.

Professor Rosefielde is a really nice professor and his lectures are great. There are only two exams that make up almost the entire class. It's important to pay attention close to the exams because he will tell you what he wants to see on the exam. Sometimes he's hard to hear so I recommend sitting closer in the class. Really interesting class!

He is an easy professor in terms of content. He rants the entire lecture and tells you whats on the exam. But he grades poorly and ambiguously, and SAYS WEIRD STUFF. If you are a woman or not white, expect him to call on you and make WEIRD references the entire class. People ignore it because hes 100 years old but its weird.

Material is not hard, but incredibly harsh class policies. Attendance is taken in first minute or two of class. If you are absent or 5 minutes late twice you drop half a letter grade, 3 times a full letter grade, and 4 times you fail. Mental health is referred to as needs in quotations. Got my grade because I didn't put in minimal work. Prof is a d

Easiest ECON class but he's an awful grader. I dont even think he reads the essays thoroughly. I'm giving him a 2 because of that but i would take him again just because its a non quantitative econ class that teaches to the test. Also he says sketchy things often in class and is bound to be reported to the dean one day

This class has made me not like economics anymore. The lectures aren't that helpful, the exams are rushed and include topics that we have not learned in class, and the homework isn't returned on time. For the amount of busy work she gives, it is not reflected in weights of the grades. "Just understand everything" isn't useful advice.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. The class can be hard to follow at times but she really wants you to do well. I wouldn't take this class with anyone else and I wish she would teach a 500 level class.

As a professor, she seems caring and willing to help. Exams are long and include topics that are not covered. She curved each midterm, which was nice. Lectures are helpful and the memes made them less boring.
Her teaching was extremely poor. It had no connection with the exam content at all. It required a lot of self-study time. Moreover, she inexplicably made the exam extremely difficult.

For the Econ 420 class, the lecture is ok, but not very clear. The exam is long and difficult. The exam time is less than 75 minutes, which is too rushed for students to finish in time. Although she curves a lot on the exam, it still makes students feel unprepared for the class. However, Professor Chao is a very nice person, caring about students.

The exams are completely different from the lectures and homework. To make it worse, multiple-choice questions can have up to two correct answers. I fail to see the educational value of setting up assessments this way.

She's nice, but she can't teach. The course is unclear, quiz answers on Canvas conflicted with the answer key, there was basically no feedback. The slides aren't helpful, and the exams were so hard and too rushed. She rarely grades homework on time.
She is kind but be sure to see her outside of class for the best understanding of things because her lectures can be confusing

Having exams worth 70% of your grade is unreasonable when lectures are unclear, the slides are filled with AI and memes, and the textbook offers little support. The exams don't reflect what's taught.

She is kind and accessible outside of class, but I don't think that makes up for what you'd get out of it.

she probably isnt bad for Econ 101 b/c the content is straightforward, but she is not equipped to be teaching Econ 420 at all. she seems nice but she cannot answer questions clearly and her lectures rarely stay on topic. the exams are not bad if you use outside resources, but in general her lectures offer little help with understanding the content.

She is the sweetest lady, don't get me wrong. But she can't teach. Most of her slides are AI memes and she deviates so much from the content. She doesn't grade the homeworks till more than a month after it is submitted.
What you are taught in class is NOT what you are presented with in the exam. And you're not allowed to ask questions on the exam..

The majority of the slides were AI generated pictures of herself or random AI pictures/memes. The lectures were not very helpful and most of the learning is done outside of class. I think she's really nice and knowledgeable about economics, but it didn't really feel like a whole lot of teaching was going on.

Truly such an amazing teacher. I would take many more classes with her. The material was not necessarily easy, but her lectures and demeanor helped deliver it clearly. The class never felt like a struggle to follow. She is so welcoming for office hours and coffee chats.

Econ 101 at UNC is not the easiest but professor Chao most definitely made it really easy to learn. Her slide shows are posted and are easy to learn from, her lectures are pretty funny and engaging with the effort that she puts into teaching the class. Make sure you work hard on the first and second midterms because the final is pretty difficult.
Dr. Chao is the sweetest! She really cares about her students and made economics interesting. If you can, take ECON 101 with her she is AMAZING.

Dr. Chao is my favorite professor I have had so far at UNC. While the tests were definitely hard, the problem sets, review exams, help sessions, and care she put into the class made them manageable. She made lectures engaging with the images in her slideshows and really tried to see what students were not understanding in order to help. Great prof!

Ying is super caring and a great person; however, she isn't the greatest lecturer and I learned most of the material on my own time from class slides. If you want to do well, you have to commit time outside of class to really understand the material and come to office hours with good questions. Generous grader, but exams were still very difficult.

Dr. Chao is amazing, and such a kind professor. That being said, this class is HARD. Exams are much harder than content learned in class and the final exam was almost impossible, even after days of studying.

Professor Chao is the sweetest instructor I have ever had. She makes sure to remember your name, brings snacks and candy to class, and gives genuine feedback on any questions or concerns. Lectures can sometimes be a little messy, but if you are able to follow along, you will learn! Econ is a hard class, but Chao makes it very possible to succeed.

Dr. Chao is an amazing professor who cares for her students deeply. She actively sends messages of support if we seemed down in class, was engaging through the lectures, and had snacks in class if we were hungry. Rare to see a professor like this, definitely sign up for her class!

As a person, Dr. Chao is extremely nice. However, her teaching style is not for everyone. She tends be disorganized with her lectures and tends to do things in a more complicated sense. The final was pretty rough but I think that econ 101 is just a tough class. Probably the best out of the 101 teachers.

Dr. Chao is literally the sweetest professor ever! She tries to make lectures enjoyable and is super accessible outside of class for extra help. She genuinely cares about her students and wants each one of them to succeed. Econ 101 is challenging but she breaks down hard concepts really well. There isn't too much busy work outside of class either.

Chao was lovely for Econ, truly cared about her students and their success. Much less work outside class than Staub but still had to work hard and study lots. Sometimes was kind of confusing while teaching but is mostly due to the speed at which econ 101 needs to be taught.
shes genuinely so sweet and caring- econ101 was lowkey tough but she makes it easy to learn if u put in the work

The best Econ professor you can get. The lectures are very clear and Chao is very caring, breaking down concepts that are difficult. The tests are very manageable as long as you complete the practice. If you are taking Econ101, I highly recommend Chao as a professor.

Take Econ with her! She is the BEST Econ 101 professor. She is so caring and even provides snacks in class! Dr. Chao offers to meet with students individually because she genuinely wants you to succeed.

Hands down the best ECON prof. at UNC. Super sweet and wants her students to do well. Super responsive to emails (fixed a problem with my grade in 5 mins on the last day). Homework is very manageable, midterms and final are definitely tough but not impossible (multiple choice only). Grading is very fair, midterm 1: 15%; midterm 2 and final: 20%

I LOVE DR. CHAO! If you have to take Econ take it with her I am begging you. She is extremely sweet and actually cares about her students. She knows that we care about our grades and gave us bonus points on our final. I feel like the difficulty of Econ 101 is exaggerated; If you read the textbook chapters and do all the practice, you will be good.
Genuinely one of the most caring professors ever!

Chao is genuinely the sweetest person I have ever met and she wants to get to know you. I didn't love her teaching style- I struggled focusing. 2 midterms worth 15% and 20% and a final worth 20%. Content is very hard- exams are very challenging but she is the best option to take it with. Does only multiple choice and is so accessible anytime.
Amazing person. She is incredibly caring about her students and truly wants what best for you. Econ 101 is a hard class, but she is definitely the person to take it with.

Her teaching methods are not the best but she is understanding and the lecture is small enough you can ask her to explain or go back. There is a solid amount of work in this class that's always due Sundays at midnight (no late work accepted) but is completion grade. Do not leave it til the last minute. Definitely the best of the 3 ECON 101 teachers

Professor Chao is amazing. ECON 101 is a tough course, but she's 100% the teacher you should want to take it with. She has note outlines for the lectures and has set weekly office hours that make her very accessible. She's very willing/enthusiastic about getting to know you on a personal level. Go to class and PAY ATTENTION!

Chao is the goat. Econ 101 is a hard class conceptually, but she makes it enjoyable enough to want to come to class. She is very personable and is very accessible outside of class and really cares for her students as people. This class is legit though so you will have to put effort into it to do well, but she is definitely the best choice

She's such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about what she does. I highly recommend her class. Although ECON 101 can be pretty tough because of the material itself, she does an amazing job of providing time outside of class to study it and explains things very clearly.

she is so amazing and makes me econ fun. Her tests are not super easy, but also not hard if you study. She gives you handouts to do every day that will help you study, and I would say that attendance is kind of important. She cares so much about her students and I don't know anyone who doesn't like her

Absolutely phenomenal professor! Very caring and genuinely wants everyone to do well. She gives so many resources to prepare for tests and assignments and she is always willing to meet at any time to help you understand. 10/10 recommend if you want to take an Econ elective, take it with her.

The class was difficult for me, but the resources she provides are amazing. The homework and exercise problems are great preparation for exams. She is very sweet, caring, and accommodating, always ready to help if you have questions about a topic.

The class is somewhat difficult but as long as you study and go to class you will be okay. Vaidyanathan is clear on what can be covered on the test and the practice exams prepare you well for the exams. Overall she is a great professor and wants to make sure everyone understands the material. Just don't slack off.

The content, in my opinion, gets harder and harder, so it's better to get high score at the first two midterms. She applied curves at the end. Really good class, but takes good effort to get an A. Also the final in non-cumulative.
Enjoyable class, learned a lot. Great teaching style. Only complaint is can cold call and if you don't know the content she's asking about thats a hard situation to be in.

Professor Vaidyanathan is by far my favorite professor in the entire Econ department. Her lectures are easy to follow and the homework sets you up well for the exams. The content is not easy, but it is intuitive if you put in the effort to understand the concepts. Professor V is also incredibly accessible outside of class and willing to help!

Dr. V is an amazing professor. The material is interesting and not too difficult to understand. Dr. V likes class discussions and tends to cold call, but if you don't know the answer, it isn't a big deal. The homework and exams are pretty on par with the course material. Just study and you will do fine.

Dr. V is great. Tests are fair (2 midterms and final), and homeworks are not bad. She drops the lowest three HWs (out of 8), and if you just go to her OH with completed homework before it's due, she will go over the whole thing with you. Lectures can be a bit boring and she does occasionally cold call on people, but she is a great teacher overall.

Dr. V is a terrific person who cares so much about instructing students and making sure they understand the material. Sometimes, her lectures can be confusing and she doesn't often post her work to in-class problems, so you've really got to pay attention in classes. Her exams are difficult, yet fair, so be sure you have everything down.

Great professor, my favorite in the ECON department. Very caring and understanding, the lectures get a little harder to follow as the year goes on but there are a ton of resources to practice. The exams are difficult and cover almost everything in class but the final isn't cumulative and the practice tests are helpful.

Geetha is a great professor and explains pretty complex topics in a way that makes them easy to understand. Her lectures are a little boring but if you pay attention and work through the homework/practice problems its decently easy to get a good grade. Only complaint is that the actual exams can be significantly harder than the practice ones.

got honor courted by the ULA and the class was very hard and test heavy. Did not do well on exam 1 and then ended up doing worse on the harder exams (2 and 3). too much material to cover and there are many resources. hard to pass the class and one of the hardest econ classes ive ever took!

Took in Fall 2022. [Good] She is unbelievably extremely caring! [Bad] If she mentioned something outside PPT once, you will one multiple choice about it in exam. I thought she was disorganized firstly, but the truth is that she wants to test all the things, although something is very trivial. She said ECON460 is easy, but I respectfully disagree!!!

Sets clear expectations for tests and assignments and provides a list of topics that will be on each test. There's always an in-class review before the test, and Verdier always paused to make sure everyone understood the lessons. Clearly wants you to succeed, and if you study well, you will easily finish with an A in the class.
Very good teacher. Lectures are engaging and useful. Tests are honestly pretty easy if you study all of the materials; generally, the test averages were ~92%.
I guarantee you guys that all your effort will pay off. Not a challenging class, if you study hard, u will get an A.
Goat of Econometrics. Take class with him and enjoy an A
Approachable and explain the lecture in detail. It's easy to follow up if you forgot what u learned in the past.

Went more in-depth mathematically than most students were prepared for, forcing him to spend a lot of time explaining things. Ultimately skipped the last 4-6 weeks of content as a result. Explains concepts and questions thoroughly and clearly. Exams were easy, and he was clear about the structure in advance. Plenty of EC opportunities on psets

Ended up getting 105 percent. He is the best professor in teaching Econ 470. Lot's of extra credit in the homework and the midterm to help your grade. Also he teaches way less content than other professors, which make this course easier. It's a math and prove based course, Do the work and you will be fine.
Great class and professor. If your looking to take 470, do yourself a favor and take it with Verdier.

He is one of the best professors I've had at UNC, I am taking him again for 571. His lectures make so much sense and there are plenty of opportunities for questions/clarifications. There are bonus questions on almost all problem sets and exams. Grading is fair and expectations are clear. Practice exams prepare you for the real thing.

take him .he is the best professor I have taken in UNC.he will give you the exact structure of the midterms and final.and he will also give you the practice exam of the exact same structure of the actual exam .the things you are tested in the exam is exact the same as which in the practice exam ,he gives extra credit for all homeworks and exams
One of the best Econ professor in UNC

Content can be difficult but he stops and to make sure everyone understands every step of the way, very open to questions and encourages all types of answers. Exams very similar to practice and homework. The assignments and exams are all split up well giving you adequate time to complete them and to study.

Prof. Verdier is a really nice, caring professor who wants you to do well. He is also a good lecturer, and as long as you attend lectures and keep up with your work you will most likely succeed in the class. Highly recommend.

The content of the class was pretty easy but he's such a bad teacher it made it more difficult. Genuinely learned more from the TAs.
He is a nice guy, and grades pretty fairly, and he added a pretty big curve at the end though.

Gary is a VERY nice guy. However, he taught us like we were phD students and I took nothing away from this class. All lectures were power points and there was 0 practice(besides extra textbook questions which were unhelpful). Help in the aide center was not helpful in any way either. If you want to learn 410 or even get a good grade, do NOT take.

Funny and knowledgeable guy indeed, but a bad professor. He literally taught us the same way he taught his phd students, you can't understand anything from his lecture. Do yourself a favor and take msa's econ 410 plz.

Very tough class. Tests make up 90% of the overall grade.

The homework was barely useful and the lectures were hard to follow.

The professor lied about adding curves and completely changed how he weighted the exams in the last few weeks. Also, I did not see a single grade posted until the final grade was posted in ConnectCarolina.

Great professor. Pretty funny guy. The exams are not too difficult but the grading is ROUGH. Believe this is partly from the TA who pretty much took over the class when it comes to grades. Class averages on exams were usually in the mid 60s, and the curve was around 3 points. Would have been a much better class if there was a different TA.

Great guy, bad teacher. Very disorganized slides, few examples, mostly explained math but not how to apply it, still you had to go to class or you'd be completely lost (attendance not mandatory). HW assignments are only worth 10% but very long and only 1 problem picked at random is graded. 90% of grade is exams. Very arrogant TA, as clueless as us.

Gary is a very knowledgeable and smart individual who greatly struggles to convey information to his students. Lectures consist of him yapping in doctorate level terms about concepts that he introduced 30 seconds ago. Reads directly from poorly designed powerpoint slides. In class examples (of which there are few) and HW's do not translate to exams

Absolutely terrible professor especially for such a challenging class like Econ 410. Get ready to self-teach yourself everything in this class because the slides and his lectures are absolutely useless. The 3 exams made up 90% of your entire grade.

Jawn was a grind, bank on riding the curve. Slides were never useful (majority of class). If he does a problem on the board though, it might be on an exam. Useful things: recitation, finding book answers online for hw problems and learning from those, old exams, review sessions. Dude also definitely has adhd

I really do not understand why so many people write awful comments about Professor Biglaiser. Microeconomics is such an awesome field that he has the mastery on. The lectures were inspirational  to the point that I was enthusiastic ( as a freshman) to go to the office hours and talked about microeconomic concepts. 
He is also a very funny guy !

Gary teaches the class as an honors class, uses poorly developed slides, and threatens to beat us with a stick. Homework accounts for 10% of your grade. The TAs do not understand the assignments/problems,the homework is completely irrelevant to the exams. The TAs would say "I do not expect any of you to get this right, I barely understand it."

This guy is a threat to teaching. In fact , there is no teaching only very disorganized slides as well as one bad TA that is arrogant (hashem amireh).I had to self teach myself everything and he gives the honors version to normal ECON410. Furthermore, multiple students have threatened to commit suicide since 30 % of the class is failing.

Gary is a terrible professor. He is nice enough, but his class is extremely disorganized and he makes it way harder than it needs to be. The homeworks take hours and are basically completely irrelevant to the content of exams. The TA's are also disrespectful, which is a shame because recitation is the only time you do problems similar to exams

Worst class I've taken at UNC. I'm a math and econ major and found Calc 3, Linear Algebra, and Discrete Math all easier than this class. Horrible at explaining concepts, does practically no practice problems in class. do yourself a favor and AVOID.

Professor Gong was a great professor because she actually put effort into teaching rather than the flipped classroom style of some other econ classes. Problems challenged us and really tested our understanding of the material without being "trick questions." I loved this class and thought it was relevant to contemporary policy problems.

Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.
Easiest Econ elective, very few homeworks. Fair exams.

Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.

Excellent econ professor, wants you to learn and that's it. This was the easiest 500-level econ class ever; great choice for an easy semester but still worth taking seriously because the material/skills are important and Dr. Gong really cares a lot.

I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

Only thing that I found slightly annoying is she does not take any questions during exams at all, not even clarifying ones. However, overall this class was one of the best econ ones I have taken. She is not trying to trick you at all where it feels like a lot of econ professors try.
Makes it very easy for you to succeed, if you go to class do the 3 problem sets and do the practice exams this class is barbecue chicken

The nicest econ professor I've ever had. She told us on the first day she wants us all to get As and she makes it very manageable to do so. The problem sets are for completion except one randomly selected question for correctness. The tests are never cumulative and exactly like practice and old tests. So funny and nice!

Super nice lady, she really takes the time to explain everything clearly in case you ever forget the basics from Econ 101 or Econ 410. You have the option to take the class form zoom instead of showing up in person.

Agree with others - best ECON prof at UNC. 552 is a readings/policy-based class, doesn't really involve typical econ math, just understand and apply data analysis. No tests or exams, assignments are reasonable and build towards a final paper that is a decent amount of work but Dr. Gong is super accessible and helpful.

Going to class is pointless. Didn't learn a thing. Taught myself the whole course. Fairly easy content. First two exams were easy, but final was ridiculous. Absolutely nothing like the practice final or the homeworks, and it was 40% of grade. Walked in with an A, walked out with a B (after days of studying). But I guess that's the UNC ECON depart.

90 Percent of ur grade is test and the other 10 percent is homework. But she gave answers on homework after you completed on line so almost everyone get it. Test was not hard but people can easily fail by failing one exam. Simply put, two midterms are 25pts each and final are 45pts. This means u loss one percent when u lose one point on the midterm
LOL easy class. just study by yourself, no need to go to class.

It was straightforward and largely reiterated the material from ECON 420. Most students didn't attend lectures since the textbook covered the content just as well. If you take 246 at all you will have to take his difficult tests no matter what, so I highly recommend taking Sturgill for the wealth of knowledge he provides. Though he is very slow on emails though which makes regrades frustrating.

CSC 246 is a hard class, but Sturgill is very passionate about the course and it is evident in his lectures. Lectures are mandatory because there are small quizzes at the end of them. Outside of that, you'll have 1-2 small coding exercises a week and then a larger homework assignment due every 2-3 weeks. Exams are tough, but not impossible.

After taking CSC246 with Sturgill, I regret not doing the same for 230. People told me not to take him because he graded harsher / harder tests than Balik, but I honestly disagree after seeing it for myself. Sturgill is a MUCH better professor, way more knowledgeable, I enjoy attending his lectures versus Balik's were absolutely worth skipping.

Sturgill is heavy on the lectures and while attendance isn't technically required he provides daily quizzes at the end of the lecture which forces you to attend. Exams are hard and detailed. To give credit where credit is due he does try to make the course doable. But he provides very little help if you are stuck and will not help debug anything.

Class is well organized and informative. It moves very quickly and covers a lot of material so you need to show up and pay attention. Tests are very difficult and require lots of studying, but it's curved pretty fairly. Projects aren't too bad. You can tell he cares about you understanding things. Overall, pretty good.

He actually seems to enjoy the material and teaching. Curriculum and projects are well-designed, and he has several office hours a week for questions.

Leave more time for debugging in C than with Java, but generally his grading seems reasonable. Anything I missed on an exam was something I probably should have known (but I did have to study).
Great professor, and very enthusiastic about a class at 8:30 AM. Harder tests than the other professors, but by far the best lecturer. Make sure to start projects early, there are 6 of them.

Yes, if you take Sturgill's sections for C and Software Tools you will likely get a lower grade. This is irrelevant. The class was engaging all the way through, and it is clear that he knows both the course content and the inner workings of C significantly better than the other professors. Project heavy -duh. Get started early and you'll be fine.

One of the best lecturers I've ever had. VERY knowledgable about what he's talking about, and tries to be engaging/entertaining in lectures. His tests are hard, but I studied really hard and was able to score above the average for both midterms. If you take him and put in effort, you can leave with a good grade and a lot of knowledge.
This is a difficult class, but worth your while if CS is your major.  There's a lot of work, but if you do it you'll come out knowing your stuff.

Great lecturer however some of the technical aspects of the course were quite lacking. Jenkins feedback was not available for the first half of the projects, and he was very behind on regrade requests. Has end of lecture quizzes that cannot be done online or made up. Tests are very difficult but Sturgill is also very good at teaching the content.
NGL, Sturgill is harder than the other professors who teach this class. He's also better. Take his classes if you really want to learn.

Quizzes are very hard sometimes and he forces you to go to his classes by having quizzes. Exams are insanely hard too. He makes the materials not fun or enjoyable by asking you very tricky questions on exams.

Difficult class. Do not take with Sturgill if you want a good GPA. He is very hard but I still respect him since he is intelligent and knows what he is talking about. It just feels unfair taking it with him since its so much easier with other professors, so I will not in the future.

Great teacher, great at teaching but super heavy workflow, he will not give u answer but hint in office hour, get early at lease a week early to do the project. it is super charllenge, but you learn a lot, like a lot!!

Dr. Sturgill is an awesome lecturer. He expects a lot, but almost everything he explains is something that you will end up seeing in the professional world. Tests are difficult but manageable with a good study routine. The homework requires some thought but is fair. I would rather take a B in a Sturgill class than get an A in a different section.

Dr. Sturgill is a good guy and he knows the material very well. Lectures can get boring, but the content is very important (CSC 230 is a grind). He assigns handout quizzes at the end of every lecture which can be annoying if you miss class, and his tests are really tough. Doing well on the projects can help you stay on track in the course.
Awful, wasn't accommodating to extenuating circumstances, and even yelled at the class. Very unprofessional.

Sturgill knows his stuff. He is willing to help students outside of class and even holds night office hours sometimes. You have to pay attention in class and the tests are very tough, but you come out really knowing what you are doing.

The weekly projects take a lot of time to complete but aren't necessarily super difficult. Prof Heckman is a solid lecturer and I felt like I learned a ton in this class. Just stay on top of project deadlines and you'll do very well in this class. Exams are relatively easy and offer lots of partial credit.
She is a really nice professor. However, the exams are hard and projects take a very long time, so make sure you actually lock in and study.

She seems nice, but I do not like the lectures. Fast-paced, lots of info presented, and not getting enough from them. Projects take a lot of time, and they have components with deadlines during exam week. I wish I had started P1 sooner. Thankfully, we were allowed a partner for the final project.

If you go to every class and take good notes then you can stay on top but if you miss even one class be prepared to do a lot of work to catch back up. The projects are not hard but the instructions are unclear, so you will often spend many hours rewriting code, because the instructions and the staff test code expectations can be different.

Easy class with two lab projects constituting bulk of the grade. Midterm and final were each 15% only. Dr. Heckman lectures a lot with several participation activities in class. Attendance is mandatory.

Dr. Heckman is a good lecturer but she moves really fast. However, the class is really just hard. There's project milestones and lab deadlines on the same week as an exam.

Project directions also contain typos, confusing language, and broken links. And not to mention the MILLION research studies they keep hounding you to participate in.

The course has been difficult to follow because the lectures rarely align with the lab work, leaving many concepts unclear. The instructor's explanations feel scattered, and her interactions with students often come across as curt, which makes the class atmosphere uncomfortable and discouraging.

The instructor's lectures are poorly structured and don't connect to the labs, leaving students confused. Her teaching style is unhelpful, and she is often rude and dismissive when students ask questions. This has created a frustrating learning environment and makes understanding the material difficult.
Solid lecturer but nothing exceptional. Go to class and don't wait until the last minute to start the projects, and you will succeed.

Dr. Heckman is overall a great teacher. Lectures are very fast-paced, so be prepared to spend time outside of class looking over old slides. Projects make up 50+ percent of your grade, but are very good coding practice. Overall, not an easy class, but Dr. Heckman made it a bit easier with her enthusiasm and knowledge!

Dr. Heckman was very knowledgeable and a great lecturer. She went over notes and information in lectures and gave us tips for how to do things more efficiently. The projects take a long time, so start early! The projects will usually take longer than the projected time she gives. The class is time-intensive, but Dr. Heckman makes it bearable.

Dr. Heckman is a great lecturer and very enthusiastic, but the class overall is rough + fast-paced. The exams are more difficult than they should be, especially the final (too much writing code by hand). The projects take up lots of your time but are great at giving a hands-on experience, unlike the slides. Beware of the min grade requirement!! -HY

She loves teaching and is passionate about computer science. Tests are fair and it is easy to do well in her class if you stay on top of project deadlines, go to office hours when necessary, and study well. All in all, a great 216 experience and prepared us well for 316. Will surely take her again if given the chance!
216 is awful. Tons of work and long hours. Dr. H made it much more bearable with her helpful TAs and great digestable lectures. I still suffered greatly in this class but Im glad it wasnt worse.
Amazing teacher, absolutely loved her. Would take her class 10 times over again. You can tell she really loves computer science and it shows in her lectures.

The best CS professor I have had, you don't need to attend the lectures to do well but attendance matters. Class overall is pretty easy but start the projects early because they can take a lot of time.

Dr. Heckman is the best professor you can take for 216. She is really passionate about Java data structures and techniques (especially iterators), and prepares you the best she can for the numerous projects and coding assignments. Start Part 2 of the projects as soon as you can--you will spend more time than you expect debugging.

Dr. Heckman is a good lecturer with fair tests and projects. The projects are important and take a long time so start early! Tests could be difficult and involved a lot of writing code by hand but are graded fairly. Dr. Heckman also makes sure there is a lot of help available to students at most days/times.

She is a good lecturer and a nice professor. Majority of the grade is projects which were great for working with the concepts covered and enjoyable to work on as well. They do take a while so start early. Tests were fair, got to bring a note sheet for the midterms. Have to hand write a lot of code on exams which I didn't like.

Dr. Heckman is one of the best professors I've had so far in CSC. She is very approachable and knowledgeable. It's clear she wants us to understand how to write good code for industry. If you're taking her for CSC216 make sure you start on the projects early and study lots for the tests. The final has lots of code writing on it.

She's fine - your options are limited in this course anyways. Attendance not mandatory. Tests trivial, vast majority of grading focused on projects. Soooo boring though. I skipped at least 30% of class towards the end. Lots of focus on practice, processes, etc. They assume you can code at this point.

Dr. Heckman does an outstanding job of explaining everything needed in a way that is clear and understandable. Not only is she one of the most approachable and nicest professors I have ever taken a class with, but she also doesn't put an effort to fail students. If you're taking CSC216 in the future, START PROJECTS EARLY, INCLUDING THE GUIDED ONES!

Once again a hallmark class by one of the well respected professors in the Computer Science Department. Class was a clear demonstration of what a typical software engineering job would look like. Very much a team based class so pick the right group of people. Exams were fairly easy as a notesheet is allowed. Very project heavy but not too difficult

She's super nice and her lectures are very appropriate. Cares about the course and the students. Tests are super straightforward and a very fair class. Projects are a massive pain and headache I would say (mainly that first one). SO if you start early and work hard for the work heavy class you will do great. Material is pretty enjoyable :)

Dr. Heckman is a great professor who knows what she's talking about. Her teaching style is definitely one that a hands-on learner may not do well with though but she's knowledgeable about it so you do end up learning a bit about the concept. Watch out though for Project 1, that one can take a toll on you, it did for me even starting it early.

Heckman's CSC 326 not only assumes that everybody wants/needs full-stack engineering skills, but grades you based on superficial criteria that doesn't apply to the work itself. Too much emphasis was put on "process" which took away from the engineering side of the class.

Great lectures and a well structured course that gives lots of practical experience in software engineering. The class is a lot of work, but it all feels relevant for the most part. Heckman is a great lecturer who clearly cares about her students and gives lots of real world context to the material.

Make sure you have good group members.

She's a great lecturer, but I thought that CSC326 was a huge waste of time (and she has the control over making it mandatory as the director). I do appreciate that the class let me realize I have no desire whatsoever to get into Software Engineering.

Dr. Heckman was nice but the class is fairly boring and mainly just depends on doing the lab and projects. I rarely went to class as you don't have to physically attend lectures to be counted a present.

Dr. Heckman is incredibly relaxed teacher with student-focused grading policies. However, the material covered in the lectures are not always related to what is covered in lab, so be sure to spend extra time learning lab concepts on your own.

Dr. Heckman is a very knowledgeable and capable instructor.  The course concepts can be hard, but she does a great job explaining them, and she knows what she's talking about.  A lot of the grade, however, is left up to your performance on projects--start earlier than you'd typically do, because they will take up dozens of hours usually.

Great professor. Engaging lectures and fun projects. She doesn't have the ability to connect one-on-one with students due to the class size, so she does the best she can through the TAs. Would take again in a heartbeat.

SE was a blast with Heckman, incredible lecturer. The course project has switched from previous years and is a fresh new experience. Evident that lots of care has gone in to make 326 a great course. Definitely take lab sections with people you know, though, as you'll be working on a project with them all semester.
She is a fine professor, but the professor you take for this class doesn't really matter that much. It's more about doing the work. I did find her to be a bit overly enthusiastic at times...

I rarely asked the professor for help on assignments since I usually received help from TAs. But Dr. Heckman is a great professor. She teaches the material well. For projects, start them early. Usually you will be debugging code errors. If you know you're going to need help, go to office hours ASAP. They get filled up quickly near the deadlines.
A great lecturer who explained concepts very effectively and enthusiastically. You will need to start working on projects early or else it is very easy to fall behind.

If you are taking CSC216, she is not a bad option. She does tend to speak pretty fast during lectures but she is knowledgeable in what she is talking about. Expect to spend a lot of time for this class, and definitely start the projects early. Also try to get help from TAs whenever you can.

I failed 216. I love Dr.Heckman though. Her lectures are by far the best I have taken at NCSU. Be ready for a lot of work in projects (especially project 1). For lecture test, I would recommend doing a lot of practice-it problems. Lots of the data structure test answers are from the lab so Make sure you know them by heart.

Heckman has very organized lectures and is overall a great instructor. CSC216; is NOT a cakewalk. Start projects as early as possible, and seek help when needed; or it's very likely you could fail. Expect to spend around 10+ hrs a week on 216, IF you're not a gifted programmer.

In CSC326 basically the only contact you will have from Dr. Heckman is the lectures. She clearly cares about students and does her best to make the very dry material from software engineering engaging. A solid pick for 326

Balik provides everything you need to be successful in this course and it's clear she genuinely wants everyone to do well. The only downside is that the lecture is a bit slow and dry but if you make sure you are caffeinated she moves at the perfect pace for you to take notes and actually absorb information during lecture.

lectures are required but its so hard to learn from them, she is unorganized, doesnt record the lectures, and makes the slides impossible to study. 
waits until last minute to grade big projects so theres nothing you can do for your grade if it drops. confusing and unorganized project requirements. exam two is a GIANT jump of topics after the first
She just sucks as a teacher and person. do not take her class and nc state should of fired her 500 years ago
I didn't wear a seatbelt on my way to class. If you can infer what I mean.

The lectures were dry but fortunately the class itself is pretty easy so it doesn't really matter. Tons of homework and a mandatory online textbook. Cares a lot about her students but the tests/projects are graded really harsh. I would recommend Balik if you are new to Java, but if you are already familiar you'll be very bored.

If you haven't taken Java/coded before she may not be for you,bc it's mostly powerpoints: great for reviewing java, but not learning it.However, if you have, she's a much easier time than other csc116 professors, with hw and tests being pretty straightforward, and her group project is simpler than other profs.'.Focus on projects, they take time!

Despite providing practice tests, her tests, which require you to HANDWRITE CODE WITH PAPER AND PENCIL, are horrible. I went into this course with previous Java knowledge and 3 weeks to the end, I BARELY have a 90. The lectures are useless, but attendance is graded. The class is way too difficult for an intro level course.

Dr. Balik knows her stuff, but she teaches class as if it's a review, since for a lot of students, it is. If you're new to programming do not take her. The review feel of her class makes it very hard for a beginner to learn the material. Otherwise, a good teacher. She gave practice tests that looked just like the test, and helps when you ask for it

Dr. Balik gets a lot of hate, but I had a good semester with her. Yes, lectures are boring, but you're forced to complete an online interactive textbook which helped me learn everything needed. Her tests are also VERY similar to the practice tests, so just start projects early and always maintain high quality in them as this class is very demanding

Alright, listen. Yes, lectures are dry, name tags for attendance is a bit weird, but the slides are great and you should come to class anyway. Just pay attention. She's kind and wants you to do well, put the laptop away and synthesize what she's saying. Ask questions. There's no reason to avoid her, she will support you if you put in the effort.

Do you want a college professor that treats you like a middle schooler? If so take this class. We had name tags for attendance and we had to get them one at a time to ensure that no one "cheated the attendance system". Lectures are dry but the tests weren't awful.

Lectures weren't very interesting or insightful. The only benefit of class time was to ask her and the TA's potential questions. zyBook was the homework and I found it to be pretty redundant. Grade was comprised of coding activities, homeworks, projcets, and tests.

I found coming to class useless, slides were read with no added given context / personality. Self studied, ended up with an A- with not too much effort. She seems to have good intentions, seems like a really nice person... I just wish she'd take into account feedback from her students.

Just read the slides as is in class with a lot of information that isn't conveyed in a manner that is not easy to understand or intuitive. it's just unfortunate that this class is difficult and is coupled with a professor who shouldn't have the responsibility and doesn't have the competency to educate students.

She reads off the slides so her lectures arent necessary but attendance is graded. She is passive aggressive if lecture is interrupted but better than past classes from what I heard. Gives time at the end of every lecture to work. Project heavy: start early because these are long. TAs are nice and helpful for projects GO TO OFFICE HRS!

Absolutely terrible teacher. She is a good person but should not be teaching. This was my first programming class, and I will never take one again. The projects caused me migraines and took up weeks' worth of my time. I only ended with a good grade b/c I got help from the TAs and spent extensive time outside the class getting help. Not worth it...

If you have experience with Java or coding in general and can organize a schedule well, you should be able to do well. Anyone else who is new will need to self-study hard from the Zybook textbook and projects/daily exercises since her lectures are meaningless. Lots of work but at least gives some extensions for projects and better due dates

One of the worst professors I've had at NCSU. I don't think I learned anything from the lectures because she reads only what is on the slides and adds very limited context to the information. She never even opened an IDE to show us how the code works, and has the TAs do most of the work. You might as well not go to class and learn it on your own.
The final is so hard, but the exams are easier than Sturgill's.

Dr.Balik is not a good lecturer. She reads through her slides without giving you any context of the topic. She talks slowly but somehow she is able to finish most of her lectures in 30-40mins(It is a 75 mins lecture) because she does not lecture you but reads the slides for you. Overall, she seems like a good person but not a good professor.

Balik is rude and lacks connection with her students. Her lectures are very boring and fast-paced. She lacks empathy and acknowledgement of college student feelings and struggles. I am very interested in Computer Science but after her class I feel bitter about the subject. I would recommend not taking Balik for CSC 116 if you can avoid it.
She gives a lot of homework and overall is not a very thorough good teacher.
Arbitrarily difficult and tedious sums up this entire class. You would genuinely be better off in every way going to a coding boot camp.

I did not enjoy Balik's lecture style at all. It is extremely boring and non-interactive. However, she does cover all the necessary concepts and provides decent powerpoint slides. DO NOT take Balik if you are planning to pursue Computer Science. She does not teach or implement GitHub or allow you to use an IDE.

12 Weekly coding workshops will take anywhere from ~2-5hrs. Very straightforward instructions. His slides are good for studying. Tests are very similar to workshop-written activities. I struggled initially, but got the hang of it. Semester project (proposal, coding, reflection), but it is spread out nicely. He is a cool dude who uses Kahoot a lot.

Dr. King is a caring professor teaching a challenging course, and student frustration with the material is sometimes unfairly directed at him. While his lecture style wasn't my personal preference, he is a good professor who puts real effort into making DSA engaging. This is an important course, and the effort you put into it will pay off.

Dr. King is a solid lecturer and provides recordings of all the lectures so you can watch them at any time. The workshops can be a lot of work but are manageable and helpful for studying. The class moves quickly, so it's important to stay on top of the assignments. The tests are long for the amount of time given, so you need to work efficiently.

Dr. King is a good lecturer and very knowledgeable, but is overly strict especially about academic integrity. The class is very fast-paced with lots of content to learn. Exams have too much content and not enough time, so memorization is key. Workshops will take up time but will be your best friend. Beware of the MGR and form good study groups. -HY

Very fair professor, knows we have an insane amount of content and does give a lot of work. But the assignments aren't super hard and aren't strictly graded. And we get late penalty waivers. Tests not too hard and they are fair. Great class organization. You must put in a lot of work, and I caution taking with CSC 230. But King is great for 316.

Dr. King makes the best out of an extremely vast and complex course. His lectures are interactive (although some topics can be boring), and he's very responsive on Ed. The course is tough, however he (and the TAs/textbook) offer plenty of help with the material. The exams are a time crunch, so focus on the point-heavy questions first!
King makes good lecture slides and weekly workshops. He makes it very easy to skip lecture, read the slides, do the workshop in a few hours, and come away with a strong grasp of the material.

CSC 316 is a challenging course. You have to put the work in to get the results. Dr. King's lectures and explanations make data structures and algorithms interesting and easy to understand. Weekly coding and written workshop assignments (5 - 6 hours/week). Exams are dense, but fair. I ended up enjoying this class quite a bit!

Best teacher I have ever had. Made data structures an enjoyable class which is insane. Tests are extremely reasonable and test you on knowledge rather than trick questions like other teachers. 10000/10
The GOAT of 316 🐐

CSC316 is a theory class (no new Java) but also has weekly coding assignments that take 3-7 hours and have clear instructions. The tests are open-note, but they move so fast that you NEED to have most of the material memorized or be able to find it almost instantly. Drawing and visualizing the steps of the algorithms and tree operations is vital.

His class is manageable if it's your only CS class, yes, that's how much time you'll spend on it. Beware of the midterms + final, they're open-note, and that's why they're way too long. The exams are also much more difficult than what you normally see. In general, you need to keep up with his pace for success. He's also super responsive online.

Dr. King taught this class well. The class is organized and structured quite well which is nice because you know what to expect each week and lecture. He gives late penalty waivers to allow you to submit assignments 2 days later with no requirements which allowed me to balance my classes way better. Just get ready to study and do a lot of work.

I love Dr. King! His lectures are some of the best I've ever attended. This class is a LOT of work, and Dr. King knows it. If you keep pace with the work, start early, and prepare well for exams, you will do great! This course is extremely important to the field of computer science, and Dr. King is a fantastic teacher of these tricky topics.

Terrible lecturer, way too rushed. Assigns a lot of work that has surprisingly little semblance to real world work. Cares more about overly strict rules & artificially hard policies on cheating than improving the course. Zero help inside or outside of class, which hurts for how needless & hard the workload is. Rly wish there was another 316 prof.

Dr. King is a totally fine professor. He isn't the most enthusiastic by any means, but he lectures well and does his best to make the material entertaining (it's just not the most exciting class). The workload is a lot, but he posts deadlines in advance and he clearly puts a lot of thought into this. Be ready for a lot of work, but don't be afraid!

Hes a good teacher who really cares. His lectures are very well put together and organized, but you have to pay attention. If you slack off for even a little bit, you might get behind, but that's not his fault, it would be yours.

He's a great teacher if you actually apply yourself and lock in.
now, is not his falt as the collage requirt him to teach so many thing in one class, and too many student at once.

he has the best slide and class. As a student who has been in ncsu for both undergrade and grade, I have to go back to see his slide when i take OS for my master. Don't blame him on no helpful on out side of class, as there too many student and too few TA, and school is reciving too much student for money, but not hire enough teacher as they should

This class is a LOT of work and can be very hard.  That being said, King makes it well known in advance when stuff is due, and he is also very responsive on Ed.  He's not the most engaging lecturer but his slides are good and it's worth going in-person to class.  Everything is well planned; this class just requires you to be on top of things.

Good lecturer, but there is a lot of content throughout the semester. Make sure you study the content the entire time, otherwise final review will be a lot. The tests are open note. Very serious about academic integrity. lectures are online and in person, with small quizzes for the topics.

Genuinely unhelpful outside of class. Will take hours to respond to even the most basic questions and is not willing to make any adjustments. Will not mention deadlines in class, the students are left to check every little thing themselves.

For the difficult class it is, he does a good job teaching, especially in-person. Attendance is optional, but I suggest going to class as the default. He explains concepts well, the slides are well-made, but his questions he asks mid-lecture are often confusing and a bit awkward. He's also incredibly specific when describing terms. Pretty solid.
Dr King is a nice guy and he tries to make this class easier but 316 is just very difficult. The lectures were somewhat helpful but you need to put in effort outside of class to do well.

This was my favorite class last semester; he cares about what he does and is passionate teaching. Couldn't have asked for more. Does set tough standards, but if you put in effort it's a piece of cake.
Great professor for a very hard class, was very enthusiastic about the material and is clear about what is required to succeed in the class.

Engaging lectures with online option. Has review kahoots in beginning of class. Theres lecture questions but theyre reviewed in class. He checks Ed online forum for questions everyday so he responds very quickly. Coding workshops can be long but easy for most part, can collab on written questions. Exams are online and open note. Would recommend!

Dr. King really is a pretty good professor, the class gets a bad reputation due to the workload. This is mostly unavoidable for King though, as the class and content is important (seriously!). The lectures are engaging if YOU engage. Don't just sit there and look at the lecture slides. Overall a fine class albeit dense.

Great professor, I never personally had any issues with him or his teaching. The lectures can sometimes be a bit boring but that is also just how the material is. Just be aware that this course is VERY time consuming, I took this course w/CSC 230 and at only 12 credits I felt like I was working constantly on projects and assignments.

I took CSC316 with Dr. King. He is a really good lecturer and he can explain material well, but god forbid you go to his office hours if you are stuck on a piece of code (at least he makes this known). King also is an extremist about academic integrity violations making many people retake. Exams are long and difficult. LOTS of homework each week.

Class is pretty standard, but exams are quite long. Projects/workshops are easy, but the class is too focused on tree data structures to be of any value for the average student. You don't really cover DP, greedy algorithms, or really any competitive programming topic aside from the basics of tree traversals.

King is a good lecturer and very organized. This course is interesting and very useful. It's set up well for EOL - Moodle is fully utilized, everything is available on time, group work, open note online exams, etc. My only gripe is there is a bit of a "witch hunt" mentality when it comes to academic integrity violations. Overall difficult but fair.

Dr. King does not teach, he just talks. Most of my classes were extremely difficult because this class took so much time to do anything. Be careful what classes you take along with this class, and don't take 230 along with it if you can help it. Expect to take twice as long on any given assignment and you'll be okay

You aren't allowed to go to office hours for help. The average response time is largely inaccurate and posts get resolved with the "help" being one of three 1) generic/pasted answer from a different q 2) threat of ban due to asking public/private pair questions 3) an actual response?! -usually short and nondescriptive or refers to a different post.
Sometimes I wonder if King is sponsored by red bull because you will need one to make it through lectures and absorb everything

Her class is flipped class style which I personally do not like but she is a good professor. Especially if you have any background with coding, you'll be just fine throughout the course. Projects took some time and there was weekly quizzes but overall it was an easy class.

This class was more time consuming than it was difficult. Weekly labs are very long and can require further work outside of class. Its a partially flipped class so she puts a lot of the learning on you. Content still gets covered in class and is explained well. It feels like a lot of work for a 3 credit class, but it is conceptually fairly easy.

The flipped style of the classroom renders the excruciatingly long and boring lecture period for the class to be entirely unnecessary. No one pays attention during lecture. Also, in our class, Dr. Battestilli wasnt great with technology aside from Matlab.

Dr. B genuinely cares about her students. The lectures are long and labs are longer, but the work given is good practice and prepares you for exams. It is helpful to come in with previous coding knowledge, but is not necessary. The exams were fair, labs and weekly "graders" were helpful, and projects were difficult but you can work with partners.

She loves to say that flipped classrooms help the students learn, but all the material she gave us was pointless. The labs and the TAs were the only reason I understood the class at all. She tries to be motivational, but no one pays attention during lectures because they get nothing out of it other than participation. Attend the online section.

Dr. B truly cares about her students and has awesome TAs. The labs are long and boring, but they're relatively easy. Projects are significantly harder, but you can work with partners if you want. With it being such a big class, it takes a long time to get grades back, but that's not a huge deal to me. Lectures are boring and not too helpful to me.

I have no personal issues with Dr. B, however the class setup for CSC113 is egregiously mind-numbing. Despite it being a 3 credit hour class, the amount of work you have to do outside of class (projects, online learning, mini coding work) takes up your whole week. Projects are long and can be hard. I feel she expects too much for a beginner class.
Lectures are absolutely mind-numbing. Attend the lectures online via zoom if possible. Class is saturated with micro-assignments that consume quite a bit of time but are worth nearly nothing.

She assigns way too much work for the course. Projects are due and expected to be done while you are still learning the material that you need to know for the project. She treats it like a hybrid class even though it's purely in person and is NOT hybrid AT ALL in the enrollment wizard. I recommend going to lectures on Zoom as well.

Every lecture: 
30 x "are you with me?"

While I respect Dr. B, I found her lectures to be pretty boring. Her personality is very calm, which can be pretty numbing at times. I have more gripes with the course than Dr. B herself. 

Unless you enjoy Comp Sci, the course feels very long. The Tuesday lectures approach 2 hours, and the weekly labs can last up to 3 hours.

A kind professor who is very accessible through office hours (even though I never went to one). To succeed in the class, I would study the function reference sheet that's provided for each cycle. She gives opportunities for test retakes if you didn't do well. My only gripe is that class time kinda feels redundant (it's a flipped class)

Dr. Battestilli is a great professor. She makes it very easy for students to get the help they need outside of lectures by keeping a calendar for office hours and holding office hours all throughout the week. It did bother me, however, that we would be asked to watch online lectures at the beginning of each week to learn the material before class.

Overall a pretty easy 3 credit hour class if you pay attention and study. The content is not hard, the tests are not hard. Her class is very well structured and organized, it is easy to see what you need to complete and when. You don't have to go to lecture because they stream it to zoom. I came in with minimal coding experience and had no problem.

Dr. B is the only instructor to teach CSC 113 as of today's date. She has long lectures that I didn't find too useful since most of the learning was online before lecture, but the test review lectures that are in-person only are worth going to. The lab sections are great if your TA is passionate about MATLAB, I learned more from my labs tbh.
The class isn't very hard. For the projects do them early for free points. For the tests just do the practice problems and you will be fine.
Excellent professor for Senior Design.

Pre-class lectures = comprehension questions, goes over material again in lecture w/ more explanation and practice. I barely knew coding going it, but even if I didn't I would've been fine. Labs have 5-6 problems, TAs are great, good test prep, and I left in 1-2 hours. Lots of extra test practice. Projects are easy w/ early submission extra credit

The lectures are genuinely useless since all of the material is recorded online and mandatory to watch the night before, but attendance is mandatory. The labs are well done but time-consuming and at annoying time slots. The class is a good intro to coding and not overly difficult. Just find something to keep yourself busy during the lectures.

I did not like Dr. B or this class very much. It has a lot to it, and requires a good amount of time and effort. The lectures are pretty useless - the most useful resources were the TopHat videos (recorded lectures) and projects, whereas the labs and graders felt tough and easy to neglect. Keep track of deadlines, make friends. You can do it!

I had her for "Well-Being Strategies for College and Life". I personally learned a lot, and if you take the assignments seriously, you will definitely find something that sticks with you. Dr. Battestilli clearly cares a lot about her students and has done lots of research to create this course as a great intro to practical strategies for wellbeing.

Good professor. She cares about making the class perfect. The tests allow you to use the MatLab grader to do it which allows for the tests to actually test your knowledge. The lectures aren't super helpful, but you should still go. The lab portion is honestly perfectly designed. Overall a good class and professor.

I appreciate how Dr. B gives real-world advice to her students. She may not be the most personable, hundreds of students are being funneled through her class, but she leaves little easter eggs of wisdom which I think are nice and speak to how she does care about her students. She tells students to believe in themselves, and that's key.

The lectures are futile, frankly. One time she took a poll to see if the students wanted to do "breakout rooms" on zoom, it was a unanimous no. She sits there.. "hmmm I don't know I think I kind of like break-out rooms" ? We all just said no? Makes you wonder if she takes into account the substance in the hundreds of surveys she pushes.

The class followed a flipped classroom style, so lectures were just three hours of examples.  Lectures were very difficult to get through, but the content wasn't too difficult to learn with some effort.  The labs were very engaging, and the projects never took too long to complete.

Reverse classroom, 2 hour lecture, and 3 hour lab for a 3 credit class is absolutely brutal. Lectures felt useless because you learned everything prior, but there were some good examples. 3 projects, 3-5 weekly homework problems, 2 hours reverse classroom, 3 exams, no final. Lot's of time needed for this class but it's easy and enjoyable

The class is a reverse classroom, where you learn the material outside the course with a few practice problems and then during lectures, she would review the material and dive deeper into practice problems. Lectures were boring though. 3 projects, pretty easy and fun. If needed, she would explain concepts differently to get students to understand.

I hated coding before this class but it was my favorite to take; she really caters her teaching style to what is best for the students. She uses a flipped classroom which I initially hated but the way she does it is so helpful, I rarely struggled and when I did both she and all the TAs were extremely helpful. Love Dr. B!

Labs and projects are great. The weekly lectures are a snooze-fest and felt like a waste of time since the TopHat questions are so basic, and she asks for questions for 5 minutes after everyone understood the code. The class itself is very easy. If you've coded at all before, MATLAB has a rather frictionless transition into grasping its syntax.

Her lectures are insanely boring and almost completely unnecessary since she makes you learn everything outside of class anyway. She really only goes over examples in class and doesn't actually really teach anything. I'd say this class is heavily self taught, just zoom the lectures and go to lab. Do the work and you'll be fine.

This is one of the only sections that requires you to buy the $100 textbook for your grade. If you're shooting for an A+, you need to buy the textbook. Getting an A without the textbook is doable, but I strongly recommend finding a different section.
Very useless class. Very easy though. Nothing against the professor that much, she and Dr. Adams were occasionally funny. But just work on other assignments during the lectures.

This class was really good. And you will learn a lot about DSA that is directly relevant to LeetCode problem-solving. He provides generous grading and curving. Best of all, he teaches really well, and if you follow the class (no mandatory attendance policy), you should be able to get an A grade easily.

Extremely high-quality class and one of the best professors at NCSU. The tests make up most of the grade and they are definitely not easy but with curving and generous grading its more than fair.  Take thorough notes, especially when he steps through an algo in class and be familiar with algebra and simplifying terms like 2^log_2(n)

The professor is very passionate about the subject, and extremely clear about the grading, homework, quizes and final exam. It's an interesting and scoring subject if you study regularly. The professor even gives mock exam papers with solutions before mid term and final exams, so the students can prepare and have an idea on what to expect in exam.

Prof Heber is really passionate about the subject which can be seen through his enthusiasm and teaching style. Would definitely recommend taking CSC 505 under him in the Fall semester (some other prof teaches it in the Spring semester).

He Included a lot of mathematics in the course that was kinda unnecessary but overall really helped clear some of the basic concepts for CSC505 and liked his teaching style, also liked the fact that attendance was not mandatory and I could just watch the recordings.

Great lectures. Study throughout the semester and pay attention to quizzes and assignments. Exams are easy. Professor loves this subject and can be seen by the way he delivers it. Worth attending lectures!

Very good lecturer, but the homework assignments are just the worst. Be prepared to write 10-20 pages of proofs and explanations on multiple algorithms for each assignment.
